awareness:1.en: At the edge of the highest island, the wind carried a strange hum. Old Helm closed his eyes and listened. 'Pay attention,' he said softly. A slow *awareness* spread through the troupe — the map was not pointing outward. It was pointing down.
awareness:1.cnHint: 在最高的岛屿边缘，老舵手让大家保持____，因为地图指向了意想不到的方向。
awareness:1.hook: Below the clouds, something vast was waiting.
awareness:1.line: 'Let your *awareness* grow quiet, and the map will speak.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the highest island, the wind carried a strange hum.
sentences.cn: 在最高的岛屿边缘，风携带着奇异的嗡鸣声。

sentences.en: Old Helm closed his eyes and listened.
sentences.cn: 老舵闭上眼睛，侧耳倾听。

sentences.en: 'Pay attention,' he said softly.
sentences.cn: "注意听，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: A slow *awareness* spread through the troupe — the map was not pointing outward.
It was pointing down.
sentences.cn: 它指的是向下。

introduce:1.en: Bell unrolled a new fragment on the stone table outside the dock. It showed an island none of them had seen. 'Allow me to *introduce* our next destination,' she said, tracing its outline with one finger. The shape looked like a sleeping bird with open wings.
introduce:1.cnHint: 小铃在码头外的石桌上展开新地图碎片，把新目的地____给大家。
introduce:1.hook: The bird-shaped island had no name written on it.
introduce:1.line: 'Let me *introduce* you to the place at the edge of the known world.'

sentences.en: Bell unrolled a new fragment on the stone table outside the dock.
sentences.cn: 小铃在码头外的石桌上展开了一张新的碎片。

sentences.en: It showed an island none of them had seen.
sentences.cn: 它显示的是一座他们都没见过的岛屿。

sentences.en: 'Allow me to *introduce* our next destination,' she said, tracing its outline with one finger.
The shape looked like a sleeping bird with open wings.
sentences.cn: 那个形状看起来像一只展开翅膀的睡鸟。

expense:1.en: The market on Windmere Street was busy and loud. Old Helm bought three jars of cloud-salt, a rare seasoning that keeps food fresh at high altitude. The *expense* was steep — two full word-fragments traded away. He tucked the jars under his arm without a word.
expense:1.cnHint: 老舵手在市集上以高昂的____购买了云盐，用两块地图碎片换取。
expense:1.hook: Two fragments gone — but what waited ahead would need them.
expense:1.line: 'The *expense* is high, but altitude travel leaves no room for spoiled food.'

sentences.en: The market on Windmere Street was busy and loud.
sentences.cn: 风梅尔街上的市集人声鼎沸。

sentences.en: Old Helm bought three jars of cloud-salt, a rare seasoning that keeps food fresh at high altitude.
sentences.cn: 老舵买了三罐云盐，这是一种在高空中能保鲜食物的稀有调味品。

sentences.en: The *expense* was steep — two full word-fragments traded away.
He tucked the jars under his arm without a word.
sentences.cn: 他把罐子夹在腋下，无言地走了。

toward:1.en: The stone path outside the camp curved gently *toward* a gap in the clouds. Bell stood at the far end, her lantern swinging in the breeze. She did not look back, but raised one hand — a quiet signal. The troupe picked up their packs and followed.
toward:1.cnHint: 营地外的石路弯向云层缺口，小铃举手示意大家朝____那个方向出发。
toward:1.hook: Past the gap, no path was marked on any map.
toward:1.line: 'We move *toward* the light, and trust the words to guide us.'

sentences.en: The stone path outside the camp curved gently *toward* a gap in the clouds.
Bell stood at the far end, her lantern swinging in the breeze.
sentences.cn: 小铃站在远端，灯笼在微风中摇晃。

sentences.en: She did not look back, but raised one hand — a quiet signal.
sentences.cn: 她没有回头，但抬起了一只手——一个无声的信号。

sentences.en: The troupe picked up their packs and followed.
sentences.cn: 队伍背起行囊跟了上去。

track:1.en: Old Helm knelt on the open ground outside the supply tent and pressed two fingers into the soft earth. A faint *track* led away from the camp — thin, careful steps, not from any of the troupe. He looked up at the horizon without blinking.
track:1.cnHint: 老舵手在供给帐篷外发现了一条陌生的____，脚印不属于队伍中的任何人。
track:1.hook: Whoever left those steps had not wanted to be seen.
track:1.line: 'This *track* is fresh — someone was here before dawn.'

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt on the open ground outside the supply tent and pressed two fingers into the soft earth.
sentences.cn: 老舵在补给帐篷外的空地上跪下，用两根手指按入软土里。

sentences.en: A faint *track* led away from the camp — thin, careful steps, not from any of the troupe.
He looked up at the horizon without blinking.
sentences.cn: 他抬起头，眼睛一眨不眨地望向地平线。

afford:1.en: Silverfang leaned against the railing of his ship, parked at the floating pier outside town. 'You cannot *afford* to waste a single fragment on a guess,' he said, arms crossed. His voice was calm but his eyes were sharp. The troupe listened, and for once, no one argued.
afford:1.cnHint: 竞争船长在城镇外的浮动码头上警告大家，不能在猜测上____浪费任何碎片。
afford:1.hook: He knew something about the final island that he had not shared.
afford:1.line: 'We cannot *afford* to guess — not this close to the edge.'

sentences.en: Silverfang leaned against the railing of his ship, parked at the floating pier outside town.
sentences.cn: 银牙靠在停泊在镇外浮码头的船舷上。

sentences.en: 'You cannot *afford* to waste a single fragment on a guess,' he said, arms crossed.
His voice was calm but his eyes were sharp.
sentences.cn: 他的声音很平静，但眼神锐利。

sentences.en: The troupe listened, and for once, no one argued.
sentences.cn: 队伍听着，难得有人没有争辩。

feature:1.en: Bell spread the full map across the outdoor viewing platform. She pointed to one small mark near the centre. 'This *feature* appears on every fragment we have collected,' she said. It was a tiny circle with a single dot inside — simple, easy to miss, impossible to explain.
feature:1.cnHint: 小铃在观景台上展开地图，指出每块碎片上都有的一个____标记。
feature:1.hook: That tiny circle was the only thing all the fragments shared.
feature:1.line: 'Notice this *feature* — it is the one clue we keep overlooking.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the full map across the outdoor viewing platform.
sentences.cn: 小铃把完整的地图铺在室外观景台上。

sentences.en: She pointed to one small mark near the centre.
sentences.cn: 她指向靠近中心的一个小标记。

sentences.en: 'This *feature* appears on every fragment we have collected,' she said.
It was a tiny circle with a single dot inside — simple, easy to miss, impossible to explain.
sentences.cn: 那是个细小的圆圈，圆心有个点——简洁到容易忽略，却又解释不了。

innovative:1.en: Outside the word-forge at the edge of the market, a young craftsman had built something new. Old Helm studied it carefully. 'Quite *innovative*,' he said — a compass that read the hum of hidden words instead of magnetic north. The needle spun once, then pointed straight up.
innovative:1.cnHint: 在市集边缘的字炉外，老舵手称赞一位年轻工匠造出的新装置____。
innovative:1.hook: A compass pointing upward could mean only one thing.
innovative:1.line: 'This is *innovative* — I have never seen a compass read words before.'

sentences.en: Outside the word-forge at the edge of the market, a young craftsman had built something new.
sentences.cn: 在市场边缘的造词铁匠铺外，一个年轻工匠造出了什么新东西。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied it carefully.
sentences.cn: 老舵仔细研究了它。

sentences.en: 'Quite *innovative*,' he said — a compass that read the hum of hidden words instead of magnetic north.
The needle spun once, then pointed straight up.
sentences.cn: 针转了一圈，然后笔直地指向上方。

experiment:1.en: At the edge of Driftstone Market, Old Helm set up a small table covered in jars of coloured dust. 'Every new island we reach is an *experiment*,' he said, mixing two powders until a tiny spark of light floated upward. The spark traced a path across the sky and stopped — pointing straight at an island none of us had seen before.
experiment:1.cnHint: 老舵在市集边缘用彩色粉末做____，结果引出了一座新岛屿的方向。
experiment:1.hook: The spark was still moving, and it wanted us to follow.
experiment:1.line: 'Every new island we reach is an *experiment*, and tonight the sky is our result.'

sentences.en: At the edge of Driftstone Market, Old Helm set up a small table covered in jars of coloured dust.
sentences.cn: 在漂流石市集的边缘，老舵摆起了一张小桌子，上面铺满了装着彩色粉末的罐子。

sentences.en: 'Every new island we reach is an *experiment*,' he said, mixing two powders until a tiny spark of light floated upward.
The spark traced a path across the sky and stopped — pointing straight at an island none of us had seen before.
sentences.cn: 那道光迹在天空中划过一条路径，然后停了下来——正好指向我们之前从没见过的一座岛屿。

nature:1.en: Bell led us to a cliff where the wind sang through hollow stones. 'This is the *nature* of this island,' she said softly, pressing her ear to the rock as if listening to a secret. Around her feet, tiny blue flowers opened one by one in the starlight, each bloom spelling out a letter of a word we had been searching for all week.
nature:1.cnHint: 小铃在悬崖边感受这座岛的____，脚边的花朵竟拼出了一个他们寻找已久的词。
nature:1.hook: The last flower opened, and the word it spelled made Old Helm go very quiet.
nature:1.line: 'The *nature* of this place speaks — you only have to press your ear close enough.'

sentences.en: Bell led us to a cliff where the wind sang through hollow stones.
sentences.cn: 小铃带我们来到一处悬崖，风在空心的石头间唱歌。

sentences.en: 'This is the *nature* of this island,' she said softly, pressing her ear to the rock as if listening to a secret.
Around her feet, tiny blue flowers opened one by one in the starlight, each bloom spelling out a letter of a word we had been searching for all week.
sentences.cn: 在她脚边，一朵朵蓝色小花在星光下一个接一个地绽开，每朵花都拼出我们整个星期都在寻找的那个词的一个字母。

status:1.en: A gate of twisted silver stood at the centre of the market square, and carved above it were the words: 'Only those of *status* may pass.' Silverfang laughed and pulled out our worn troupe banner. The gate hummed, read the stitched insignia, and swung open without a sound, revealing a road paved with softly glowing stones.
status:1.cnHint: 市场中央的银门要求来者具备一定的____，银牙船长亮出旗帜后，门竟自己开了。
status:1.hook: Beyond the gate, the glowing road curved out of sight around a cloud.
status:1.line: 'Our *status* as travellers is written on this banner — and the gate just agreed.'

sentences.en: A gate of twisted silver stood at the centre of the market square, and carved above it were the words: 'Only those of *status* may pass.'
Silverfang laughed and pulled out our worn troupe banner.
sentences.cn: 银牙笑了笑，掏出我们破旧的队伍旗幡。

sentences.en: The gate hummed, read the stitched insignia, and swung open without a sound, revealing a road paved with softly glowing stones.
sentences.cn: 大门嗡的一声，读取了缝线上的标志，无声地开了，露出一条铺着微弱发光的石头的道路。

accident:1.en: I tripped over a loose cobblestone and knocked Old Helm's satchel off the railing. By pure *accident*, the bag burst open mid-fall and scattered a dozen collected words into the wind. For one breathless moment the words hung in the air, arranging themselves into a rough shape — a map of the islands ahead.
accident:1.cnHint: 叙述者不小心打翻了老舵的包，这场____却让散落的词语在空中拼成了一张地图。
accident:1.hook: The map shivered once, then drifted east as if pulled by an invisible string.
accident:1.line: 'A happy *accident*, I would call it — those words knew exactly where to go.'

sentences.en: I tripped over a loose cobblestone and knocked Old Helm's satchel off the railing.
sentences.cn: 我被一块松动的鹅卵石绊倒，把老舵搭在栏杆上的背包撞了下去。

sentences.en: By pure *accident*, the bag burst open mid-fall and scattered a dozen collected words into the wind.
For one breathless moment the words hung in the air, arranging themselves into a rough shape — a map of the islands ahead.
sentences.cn: 有那么一个屏息的时刻，这些词在空中悬停，自己排成了一个粗略的形状——一张前方各岛的地图。

active:1.en: Most of the island's market stalls had gone quiet for the night, but one corner stayed bright and *active*: a circle of older travellers trading small carved tiles, each tile marked with a fragment of a new word. Bell watched carefully from the edge, then stepped in and offered a tile of our own, earning a piece of the word we needed most.
active:1.cnHint: 夜晚的集市大多沉寂，但一个角落依然____热闹，小铃用一块刻字木牌换到了关键词碎片。
active:1.hook: The tile in Bell's hand glowed faintly, as though glad to be found.
active:1.line: 'Stay *active* at the edges of any market and you will always find the real trade.'

sentences.en: Most of the island's market stalls had gone quiet for the night, but one corner stayed bright and *active*: a circle of older travellers trading small carved tiles, each tile marked with a fragment of a new word.
Bell watched carefully from the edge, then stepped in and offered a tile of our own, earning a piece of the word we needed most.
sentences.cn: 小铃从边缘仔细观察，然后走了进去，拿出我们自己的一块瓷砖，换到了我们最需要的那个词的碎片。

feed:1.en: Near the docks, a child was tossing crumbs to a flock of tiny cloud-birds that hovered just above the wooden planks. 'You have to *feed* them first,' Old Helm told me, handing me a pinch of silver grain from his coat pocket. I held out my palm; the smallest bird landed, dropped a folded scrap of paper, and flew away.
feed:1.cnHint: 老舵告诉叙述者要先____这些云雀，其中最小的一只送来了一张折叠的纸条。
feed:1.hook: The scrap of paper unfolded to show three words and an arrow pointing up.
feed:1.line: '*Feed* them once with kindness and they will bring you something worth keeping.'

sentences.en: Near the docks, a child was tossing crumbs to a flock of tiny cloud-birds that hovered just above the wooden planks.
sentences.cn: 在码头附近，一个孩子在给一群悬浮在木板上方的小云鸟撒面包屑。

sentences.en: 'You have to *feed* them first,' Old Helm told me, handing me a pinch of silver grain from his coat pocket.
I held out my palm; the smallest bird landed, dropped a folded scrap of paper, and flew away.
sentences.cn: 我摊开手心；最小的那只鸟落了下来，掉下一张折叠好的纸条，然后飞走了。

principle:1.en: Silverfang haggled loudly with a merchant over a rolled-up chart, then suddenly stopped and handed the chart back. 'One *principle* I never break,' he said to me as we walked away, 'never trade a real map for a drawn one.' Two steps later he turned and showed me what he had palmed instead — the actual island seal, hidden under the merchant's counter.
principle:1.cnHint: 银牙船长在集市上坚守一条____，并机智地拿走了商人藏在柜台下的真正宝物。
principle:1.hook: The seal caught the starlight and pulsed once, warm and gold.
principle:1.line: 'A single *principle*, held firmly, will serve you better than a dozen clever tricks.'

sentences.en: Silverfang haggled loudly with a merchant over a rolled-up chart, then suddenly stopped and handed the chart back.
sentences.cn: 银牙大声地跟一个商人讨价还价一张卷起的海图，忽然停下来，把海图还给了他。

sentences.en: 'One *principle* I never break,' he said to me as we walked away, 'never trade a real map for a drawn one.'
Two steps later he turned and showed me what he had palmed instead — the actual island seal, hidden under the merchant's counter.
sentences.cn: 两步之后他转身给我看他实际上偷走的东西——藏在商人柜台下的真正的岛屿印玺。

article:1.en: On a low table near the harbour gate lay a single yellowed *article* torn from some old journal, its headline reading: 'Island of Ending Clocks Found — Then Lost.' Bell picked it up and read aloud the final line, which named the exact wind direction needed to reach it. Old Helm quietly updated the map, and our course shifted by just one degree.
article:1.cnHint: 小铃在港口附近的旧报纸____中读到了一个失落岛屿的方位线索，航线因此悄悄改变。
article:1.hook: One degree is a small change, but across a sky this wide, it leads somewhere completely new.
article:1.line: 'One *article*, kept by chance, just saved us a month of searching.'

sentences.en: On a low table near the harbour gate lay a single yellowed *article* torn from some old journal, its headline reading: 'Island of Ending Clocks Found — Then Lost.'
Bell picked it up and read aloud the final line, which named the exact wind direction needed to reach it.
sentences.cn: 小铃拿起来，大声读出了最后一行，里面写着到达它需要的准确风向。

sentences.en: Old Helm quietly updated the map, and our course shifted by just one degree.
sentences.cn: 老舵无声地更新了地图，我们的航线转移了整整一度。

digital:1.en: At the edge of the map, a stone pillar rose from the clouds. Carved into it were *digital* marks — not like letters, but sharp little symbols that flickered like a screen when the light hit them. Old Helm pressed his palm against them, and a soft hum filled the air.
digital:1.cnHint: 石柱上的____符号在光线下闪烁，老舵长将手贴上去，柱子发出嗡嗡声。
digital:1.hook: The hum grew louder, and the pillar began to sink.
digital:1.line: 'These *digital* marks are unlike anything on our old charts,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: At the edge of the map, a stone pillar rose from the clouds.
sentences.cn: 在地图的边缘，一根石柱从云层中升起。

sentences.en: Carved into it were *digital* marks — not like letters, but sharp little symbols that flickered like a screen when the light hit them.
Old Helm pressed his palm against them, and a soft hum filled the air.
sentences.cn: 老舵把手掌按在上面，空气里发出一阵低沉的嗡鸣声。

sale:1.en: A tiny market floated on a wooden platform between two islands. Banners hung from every post, and a cheerful woman called out prices to passing sky-boats. Bell tugged my sleeve and pointed to a rolled map on a small table — it was marked clearly: for *sale*, one silver coin.
sale:1.cnHint: 悬空市集上，领航员发现桌上摆着一幅标注____的地图。
sale:1.hook: Bell reached for the coin, but the map had already vanished.
sale:1.line: 'That map is for *sale* — we need it before someone else grabs it,' Bell said.

sentences.en: A tiny market floated on a wooden platform between two islands.
sentences.cn: 一个小市集浮在两座岛屿之间的木质平台上。

sentences.en: Banners hung from every post, and a cheerful woman called out prices to passing sky-boats.
sentences.cn: 旗帜从每根柱子上飘下来，一个神气的女人对着往来的天船喊价。

sentences.en: Bell tugged my sleeve and pointed to a rolled map on a small table — it was marked clearly: for *sale*, one silver coin.

contact:1.en: The bridge between the two islands was broken, leaving a long gap of open sky. Old Helm told me our only choice was to *contact* the keeper of the far tower, whose signal lamp still blinked across the clouds. I waved a bright cloth three times, heart pounding, and waited.
contact:1.cnHint: 桥断了，我们必须____对岸塔楼的守望者，老舵长让我挥动布旗发出信号。
contact:1.hook: The lamp blinked back — but the pattern was wrong.
contact:1.line: 'We must *contact* the tower keeper before the clouds roll in,' Old Helm urged.

sentences.en: The bridge between the two islands was broken, leaving a long gap of open sky.
sentences.cn: 两座岛屿之间的桥断了，留下一长段敞开的天空。

sentences.en: Old Helm told me our only choice was to *contact* the keeper of the far tower, whose signal lamp still blinked across the clouds.
I waved a bright cloth three times, heart pounding, and waited.
sentences.cn: 我挥舞着亮布三次，心跳如鼓，然后等待。

failure:1.en: We had tried twice to cross the wind gate at the island's edge, and twice the current had pushed us back. Old Helm stood quietly for a moment, studying the sky. He said that *failure* to read the wind's true direction was the only reason we kept being turned around.
failure:1.cnHint: 两次穿越风门都被气流推回，老舵长说____读懂风向才是真正的原因。
failure:1.hook: On the third attempt, the wind changed direction entirely.
failure:1.line: '*Failure* to watch the low clouds will cost us another hour,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: We had tried twice to cross the wind gate at the island's edge, and twice the current had pushed us back.
sentences.cn: 我们已经试过两次穿过岛屿边缘的风门，两次都被气流推了回来。

sentences.en: Old Helm stood quietly for a moment, studying the sky.
sentences.cn: 老舵静静地站了一会儿，观察着天空。

sentences.en: He said that *failure* to read the wind's true direction was the only reason we kept being turned around.

bird:1.en: A large, silver-feathered creature landed on the rail beside Bell and stared at her with bright yellow eyes. 'Clever *bird*,' she whispered, and it tilted its head as if it understood. Then it dropped a small folded paper at her feet and launched itself back into the open sky.
bird:1.cnHint: 一只银羽____落在领航员旁边，叼来一张折叠的纸片后飞走了。
bird:1.hook: Bell unfolded the paper and went very still.
bird:1.line: 'That *bird* has been following us since the last island,' Bell said quietly.

sentences.en: A large, silver-feathered creature landed on the rail beside Bell and stared at her with bright yellow eyes.
sentences.cn: 一只巨大的银羽生物落在小铃身边的栏杆上，用明亮的黄眼睛盯着她。

sentences.en: 'Clever *bird*,' she whispered, and it tilted its head as if it understood.
Then it dropped a small folded paper at her feet and launched itself back into the open sky.
sentences.cn: 然后它在她脚下丢下一张折好的纸片，纵身跳回开阔的天空。

official:1.en: A tall figure in a deep blue coat stood at the gate of the island's only tower. A badge on his chest caught the light. Old Helm said he was an *official* of the Sky Council — the one person who could stamp our map and let us pass to the next region.
official:1.cnHint: 塔楼门口站着天空议会的____，他是唯一能盖章放行的人。
official:1.hook: The official looked at our map and slowly shook his head.
official:1.line: 'Only an *official* of the Sky Council can open that gate,' Old Helm reminded us.

sentences.en: A tall figure in a deep blue coat stood at the gate of the island's only tower.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着深蓝色大衣的高大身影站在岛上唯一塔楼的门口。

sentences.en: A badge on his chest caught the light.
sentences.cn: 他胸口的徽章闪闪发光。

sentences.en: Old Helm said he was an *official* of the Sky Council — the one person who could stamp our map and let us pass to the next region.

confidence:1.en: My hands were shaking as I stepped up to read the carved word aloud — the gate would only open for a clear, steady voice. Bell gave me a small nod, and that simple look filled me with *confidence*. I took a breath, spoke the word firmly, and heard the lock click open.
confidence:1.cnHint: 我颤抖着走上前，领航员的一个点头给了我____，我稳稳念出了咒语。
confidence:1.hook: The gate swung open to reveal nothing but white mist.
confidence:1.line: 'A little *confidence* is all that door asks for,' Bell said with a smile.

sentences.en: My hands were shaking as I stepped up to read the carved word aloud — the gate would only open for a clear, steady voice.
sentences.cn: 我的手在发抖，一步步走上前去朗读雕刻的文字——只有清晰稳定的声音才能打开这扇门。

sentences.en: Bell gave me a small nod, and that simple look filled me with *confidence*.
I took a breath, spoke the word firmly, and heard the lock click open.
sentences.cn: 我深吸一口气，坚定地说出那个词，听到锁打开的声音。

display:1.en: At the very edge of the island, a circle of tall stones stood in the open air. Each stone began to *display* a glowing image — mountains, rivers, and paths that shifted slowly like a living painting. Old Helm walked from stone to stone, reading the route that the pictures traced together.
display:1.cnHint: 石阵中每块巨石开始____发光的图像，拼成了一条完整的路线。
display:1.hook: When Old Helm reached the last stone, his face went pale.
display:1.line: 'Watch — the stones *display* the path only for a short time,' Old Helm warned.

sentences.en: At the very edge of the island, a circle of tall stones stood in the open air.
sentences.cn: 在岛的最边缘，一圈高大的石头屹立在开阔的天空中。

sentences.en: Each stone began to *display* a glowing image — mountains, rivers, and paths that shifted slowly like a living painting.
Old Helm walked from stone to stone, reading the route that the pictures traced together.
sentences.cn: 老舵从一块石头走到另一块，读出这些图像拼在一起形成的路线。

operation:1.en: At the edge of the map, Old Helm spread a glowing chart across a flat stone. 'Every *operation* on this chart — fold, turn, mark — changes which island appears next,' he said. Bell leaned in, fingers ready. The next island was waiting to be called into existence.
operation:1.cnHint: 老舵主解释说，对地图的每一次____都会让新的岛屿浮现。
operation:1.hook: Bell's finger hovered over a mark no one had made.
operation:1.line: 'Every *operation* must be exact, or we drift into nothing.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the map, Old Helm spread a glowing chart across a flat stone.
sentences.cn: 在地图的边缘，老舵在一块平石上铺开一张发光的图表。

sentences.en: 'Every *operation* on this chart — fold, turn, mark — changes which island appears next,' he said.
Bell leaned in, fingers ready.
sentences.cn: 小铃探过身去，手指已经做好准备。

sentences.en: The next island was waiting to be called into existence.
sentences.cn: 下一座岛屿等待被唤入存在。

population:1.en: The island of Crestholm rose from the clouds like a green crown. Old Helm checked his notes. 'Small *population* — maybe two hundred souls — but every one of them is said to know a hidden word.' The troupe looked at each other. Two hundred doors to knock on.
population:1.cnHint: 老舵主说这座岛的____虽然不多，但每个人都藏着一个词。
population:1.hook: Smoke rose from only one chimney at the island's center.
population:1.line: 'A small *population* can still hold the biggest secrets.'

sentences.en: The island of Crestholm rose from the clouds like a green crown.
sentences.cn: 克雷斯特霍尔姆岛从云层中升起，像一顶绿色的王冠。

sentences.en: Old Helm checked his notes.
sentences.cn: 老舵查看了他的笔记。

sentences.en: 'Small *population* — maybe two hundred souls — but every one of them is said to know a hidden word.'
The troupe looked at each other.
sentences.cn: 队伍互相看了一眼。

sentences.en: Two hundred doors to knock on.
sentences.cn: 两百扇门要敲开。

quick:1.en: Bell called out a heading and the vessel tilted sharply left. 'We have to be *quick*,' she said, watching a wall of silver fog roll toward them. Old Helm tightened the ropes. The fog swallowed the stars one by one. There were perhaps thirty seconds before it swallowed them too.
quick:1.cnHint: 小铃警告说必须____，因为银色的雾正在迅速吞没星星。
quick:1.hook: The last star vanished, and the compass began to spin.
quick:1.line: 'Be *quick* — that fog hides things that do not sleep.'

sentences.en: Bell called out a heading and the vessel tilted sharply left.
sentences.cn: 小铃喊了一个方向，船体急剧向左倾斜。

sentences.en: 'We have to be *quick*,' she said, watching a wall of silver fog roll toward them.
Old Helm tightened the ropes.
sentences.cn: 老舵拉紧了绳索。

sentences.en: The fog swallowed the stars one by one.
sentences.cn: 雾一颗一颗地吞没了星星。

sentences.en: There were perhaps thirty seconds before it swallowed them too.
sentences.cn: 也许只剩三十秒，它就会把他们也吞没。

scale:1.en: Old Helm unrolled a new fragment of map and frowned. 'The *scale* is wrong,' he muttered. On the chart, the next island looked no bigger than a thumbnail, yet Bell swore she could already see its cliffs filling the whole horizon ahead. Something had changed the island — or the map.
scale:1.cnHint: 老舵主发现地图的____有误，眼前的岛屿比图上标示的大得多。
scale:1.hook: The cliffs kept growing, long after they should have stopped.
scale:1.line: 'Check the *scale* — what we see and what is drawn do not match.'

sentences.en: Old Helm unrolled a new fragment of map and frowned.
sentences.cn: 老舵展开一张新的地图碎片，皱起眉头。

sentences.en: 'The *scale* is wrong,' he muttered.
On the chart, the next island looked no bigger than a thumbnail, yet Bell swore she could already see its cliffs filling the whole horizon ahead.
sentences.cn: 在图表上，下一座岛屿看起来只有指甲盖那么大，可小铃发誓她已经能看到它的悬崖填满了整个前方地平线。

sentences.en: Something had changed the island — or the map.
sentences.cn: 什么东西改变了这座岛——或者改变了这张地图。

basic:1.en: The market square of Dunport was loud and bright. Silverfang bought three warm rolls and handed one to me. 'This is the *basic* rule of island travel,' she said with a grin. 'Always eat before you search for words. A hungry mind misreads everything.' I took the roll and felt wiser already.
basic:1.cnHint: 竞争船长说，吃饱饭是岛屿旅行的____原则，否则什么都看不准。
basic:1.hook: Then Silverfang's grin faded as she read the baker's sign.
basic:1.line: 'The *basic* rule: eat first, hunt words second.'

sentences.en: The market square of Dunport was loud and bright.
sentences.cn: 邦港的集市广场热闹而明亮。

sentences.en: Silverfang bought three warm rolls and handed one to me.
sentences.cn: 银牙买了三个热面包，递了一个给我。

sentences.en: 'This is the *basic* rule of island travel,' she said with a grin.
'Always eat before you search for words.
sentences.cn: 总是先吃饱再去寻找那些词汇。

sentences.en: A hungry mind misreads everything.'
sentences.cn: 饿肚子的脑子什么都读不对。

sentences.en: I took the roll and felt wiser already.
sentences.cn: 我接过面包，顿时觉得自己聪慧了许多。

constantly:1.en: Bell stood at the prow, her eyes *constantly* moving — left to the clouds, right to the stars, down to the shifting map. 'She never rests,' Old Helm told me quietly. 'The sky changes every minute. If she blinks too long, we miss the gap.' I started watching the sky too.
constantly:1.cnHint: 小铃的眼睛____扫视天空和地图，因为稍一分神就会错过航道。
constantly:1.hook: Then she went very still, staring at one fixed point.
constantly:1.line: 'I am *constantly* reading the sky — it never sends the same message twice.'

sentences.en: Bell stood at the prow, her eyes *constantly* moving — left to the clouds, right to the stars, down to the shifting map.
'She never rests,' Old Helm told me quietly.
sentences.cn: 老舵轻声告诉我。

sentences.en: 'The sky changes every minute.
sentences.cn: 天空每一分钟都在变。

sentences.en: If she blinks too long, we miss the gap.'
sentences.cn: 她要是眨眼太久，我们就会错过那个缝隙。

sentences.en: I started watching the sky too.
sentences.cn: 我也开始抬头看天空了。

favor:1.en: Two paths led away from the crossroads: one paved with white stone, one rough with roots. Silverfang studied both and then chose the rough one. 'I *favor* the harder road,' she said simply. 'Smooth paths have already given up their secrets.' Old Helm smiled and followed without a word.
favor:1.cnHint: 竞争船长说她____走崎岖的那条路，因为平坦的路早已没有秘密。
favor:1.hook: Something on the rough path glinted, half-buried in the roots.
favor:1.line: 'I *favor* the road that makes you work for what it hides.'

sentences.en: Two paths led away from the crossroads: one paved with white stone, one rough with roots.
sentences.cn: 十字路口分出两条路：一条铺着白石头，一条被树根缠绕。

sentences.en: Silverfang studied both and then chose the rough one.
sentences.cn: 银牙研究了两条路，然后选了那条崎岖的。

sentences.en: 'I *favor* the harder road,' she said simply.
'Smooth paths have already given up their secrets.'
sentences.cn: 光滑的路已经把秘密都交出来了。

sentences.en: Old Helm smiled and followed without a word.
sentences.cn: 老舵微笑着跟在她身后，没有说一句话。

absence:1.en: We reached the place marked on the map, but there was nothing — only open sky where an island should have floated. Old Helm was quiet for a long moment. 'The *absence* of a place is still a clue,' he said at last. Bell wrote the blank coordinates down carefully. Empty space had its own story.
absence:1.cnHint: 地图上标记的位置空无一物，老舵主说这种____本身就是一条线索。
absence:1.hook: Then Bell's pen stopped — the coordinates were already written in someone else's hand.
absence:1.line: 'The *absence* of an island tells us someone got here first.'

sentences.en: We reached the place marked on the map, but there was nothing — only open sky where an island should have floated.
sentences.cn: 我们到了地图上标记的地方，却什么都没有——只有空荡荡的天空，本该漂浮着一座岛屿。

sentences.en: Old Helm was quiet for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 老舵沉默了很久。

sentences.en: 'The *absence* of a place is still a clue,' he said at last.
Bell wrote the blank coordinates down carefully.
sentences.cn: 小铃小心地把这些空白的坐标记了下来。

sentences.en: Empty space had its own story.
sentences.cn: 空白的地方也有自己的故事。

character:1.en: We landed on a narrow island where every stone was carved with a different mark. Old Helm knelt and traced one slowly. 'Each *character* cut here is part of the map,' he said. The carvings glowed faintly, and the island seemed to breathe around us.
character:1.cnHint: 老头盔在石头上发现了奇特的____，据说它们是地图的一部分。
character:1.hook: One carved mark began to move on its own.
character:1.line: 'Every *character* on this stone points to a place we have not found yet.'

sentences.en: We landed on a narrow island where every stone was carved with a different mark.
sentences.cn: 我们登上了一座狭长的岛，岛上每一块石头都刻着不同的记号。

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt and traced one slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪下来，缓缓描摹其中一个。

sentences.en: 'Each *character* cut here is part of the map,' he said.
The carvings glowed faintly, and the island seemed to breathe around us.
sentences.cn: 那些刻痕微微发光，岛屿似乎在我们周围呼吸。

clean:1.en: After the storm passed, our deck was covered in silver dust from a nearby cloud. Bell handed me a brush and smiled. 'A *clean* ship finds cleaner skies,' she said. We swept together in easy silence, and slowly the next island came into view ahead.
clean:1.cnHint: 贝尔让我帮忙把船____，说这样才能看见更好的风景。
clean:1.hook: Beneath the dust lay a map none of us had drawn.
clean:1.line: 'Keep it *clean* and the sky will show us where to go next.'

sentences.en: After the storm passed, our deck was covered in silver dust from a nearby cloud.
sentences.cn: 风暴过后，我们的甲板上覆盖了来自附近云层的银色尘埃。

sentences.en: Bell handed me a brush and smiled.
sentences.cn: 小铃递给我一把刷子，笑了。

sentences.en: 'A *clean* ship finds cleaner skies,' she said.
We swept together in easy silence, and slowly the next island came into view ahead.
sentences.cn: 我们一起在静默中打扫，慢慢地，下一座岛屿出现在了前方。

convey:1.en: Old Helm held up a small stone that pulsed with soft light. He said words alone could not *convey* what it felt like to hold a piece of the edge of the world. I reached out and touched it. A warmth spread through my hand like sunlight through thin cloth.
convey:1.cnHint: 老头盔拿着发光的石头，说语言无法____那种感觉。
convey:1.hook: The stone grew warm and then showed us a face.
convey:1.line: 'No map can *convey* what waits at the edge of everything.'

sentences.en: Old Helm held up a small stone that pulsed with soft light.
sentences.cn: 老舵举起一块散发柔和光芒的小石头。

sentences.en: He said words alone could not *convey* what it felt like to hold a piece of the edge of the world.
I reached out and touched it.
sentences.cn: 我伸出手去摸它。

sentences.en: A warmth spread through my hand like sunlight through thin cloth.
sentences.cn: 一股温暖像阳光透过薄布一样在我手心蔓延开来。

distraction:1.en: Bell was steering us through a narrow gap between two cloud walls when a flock of bright birds suddenly crossed our path. Old Helm caught my arm before I could lean over the rail. 'No *distraction* now,' he said quietly. Bell guided us through without blinking.
distraction:1.cnHint: 穿越云墙时，贝尔不允许任何____打断她的专注。
distraction:1.hook: Something inside the cloud wall had been watching us pass.
distraction:1.line: 'Any *distraction* here and we miss the gap for another full season.'

sentences.en: Bell was steering us through a narrow gap between two cloud walls when a flock of bright birds suddenly crossed our path.
sentences.cn: 小铃正引导我们穿过两堵云墙之间的狭窄缝隙，突然一群闪闪发光的鸟掠过我们的路线。

sentences.en: Old Helm caught my arm before I could lean over the rail.
sentences.cn: 老舵在我还没来得及探出栏杆之前就抓住了我的手臂。

sentences.en: 'No *distraction* now,' he said quietly.
Bell guided us through without blinking.
sentences.cn: 小铃眼睛都没眨一下就引导我们通过了。

fight:1.en: The wind pushed hard against our ship as we climbed toward the highest island on the chart. Old Helm stood at the front, leaning forward, full of quiet *fight*. 'This is what we came for,' he called back to us. The island broke through the clouds above.
fight:1.cnHint: 风势凶猛，但老头盔身上有一股不服输的____。
fight:1.hook: The island above had no edges anyone could see.
fight:1.line: 'Keep your *fight* with you — the last climb is always the longest.'

sentences.en: The wind pushed hard against our ship as we climbed toward the highest island on the chart.
sentences.cn: 风猛烈地推着我们的船向着海图上最高的那座岛爬升。

sentences.en: Old Helm stood at the front, leaning forward, full of quiet *fight*.
'This is what we came for,' he called back to us.
sentences.cn: 他回头对我们喊道。

sentences.en: The island broke through the clouds above.
sentences.cn: 那座岛从云层中破出了头。

finish:1.en: We found the edge of the oldest chart tacked to a post in an empty market. The ink stopped mid-line, as if the mapmaker had simply walked away. Old Helm ran his finger along the *finish* of the last stroke. 'Someone stopped here on purpose,' he said softly.
finish:1.cnHint: 在空旷的集市上，我们发现一张地图的____处藏着某种秘密。
finish:1.hook: Behind the post was a door that matched the map exactly.
finish:1.line: 'The *finish* of this line is where our real journey begins.'

sentences.en: We found the edge of the oldest chart tacked to a post in an empty market.
sentences.cn: 我们在一个空旷的集市里发现了最古老的海图钉在一根木桩上。

sentences.en: The ink stopped mid-line, as if the mapmaker had simply walked away.
sentences.cn: 墨迹在一半处停住了，仿佛那个制图者就这样走开了。

sentences.en: Old Helm ran his finger along the *finish* of the last stroke.
'Someone stopped here on purpose,' he said softly.
sentences.cn: 他轻声说。

frequently:1.en: Silverfang's ship appeared *frequently* on islands just before we arrived, always gone by the time we landed. Bell studied the pattern on our chart and tapped it twice. 'She is not following us,' Bell said. 'She is reading the same sky.' That thought made me look up.
frequently:1.cnHint: 银牙的船____出现在我们前方，贝尔觉得对方在读同一片天空。
frequently:1.hook: This time, Silverfang's ship had not left.
frequently:1.line: 'She *frequently* reaches the word before us — that is not luck.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's ship appeared *frequently* on islands just before we arrived, always gone by the time we landed.
Bell studied the pattern on our chart and tapped it twice.
sentences.cn: 小铃研究了我们海图上的这个规律，轻轻敲了两下。

sentences.en: 'She is not following us,' Bell said.
sentences.cn: 小铃说。

sentences.en: 'She is reading the same sky.'
sentences.cn: 她在读同样的天空。

sentences.en: That thought made me look up.
sentences.cn: 这个想法让我抬起了头。

invest:1.en: Old Helm spread every coin we had on the market table and bought a single small jar of pale ink. Bell raised an eyebrow. 'We *invest* in the map,' he said simply. He opened the jar, added three new islands to our chart, and the paper glowed at the edges.
invest:1.cnHint: 老头盔把所有的钱都____在了一小罐墨水上，用来补全地图。
invest:1.hook: The new islands on the chart began drifting slowly toward each other.
invest:1.line: 'We *invest* everything in the map — that is the only rule I keep.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread every coin we had on the market table and bought a single small jar of pale ink.
sentences.cn: 老舵把我们所有的硬币都摊在市集的桌子上，只买了一个小瓶淡色的墨水。

sentences.en: Bell raised an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 小铃挑了挑眉。

sentences.en: 'We *invest* in the map,' he said simply.
He opened the jar, added three new islands to our chart, and the paper glowed at the edges.
sentences.cn: 他打开瓶子，在我们的海图上添了三座新岛屿，纸张的边缘开始闪闪发光。

institution:1.en: At the edge of the island, a carved stone arch marked the entrance to an ancient *institution* — a circle of scholars who had traded in rare words for centuries. Old Helm bowed his head with real respect. 'They kept the map alive,' he said quietly. I stepped through the arch and felt history settle on my shoulders.
institution:1.cnHint: 古老的____守护着地图的记忆，老舵主带领我们走进这片石拱之地。
institution:1.hook: Inside, one scholar held a fragment we had never seen before.
institution:1.line: 'Every great journey owes something to an *institution* older than itself,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: At the edge of the island, a carved stone arch marked the entrance to an ancient *institution* — a circle of scholars who had traded in rare words for centuries.
Old Helm bowed his head with real respect.
sentences.cn: 老舵低下头，真诚地鞠了一躬。

sentences.en: 'They kept the map alive,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "他们让地图活了下来，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: I stepped through the arch and felt history settle on my shoulders.
sentences.cn: 我穿过拱门，感觉历史落在了我的肩膀上。

outcome:1.en: Bell spread the four recovered word-fragments across the deck and studied them in silence. The rest of us held our breath. Whatever she decided, the *outcome* would set our course for the next island — or send us back to the fog. She pressed two fragments together, and they glowed gold.
outcome:1.cnHint: 领航员将碎片拼合，____将决定我们下一段旅途的方向。
outcome:1.hook: The glow slowly drew the shape of a door none of us recognised.
outcome:1.line: 'The *outcome* depends on the order we place them,' Bell said firmly.

sentences.en: Bell spread the four recovered word-fragments across the deck and studied them in silence.
sentences.cn: 小铃把四块找回来的词语碎片铺开在甲板上，沉默地研究着。

sentences.en: The rest of us held our breath.
sentences.cn: 我们其他人都屏住了呼吸。

sentences.en: Whatever she decided, the *outcome* would set our course for the next island — or send us back to the fog.
She pressed two fragments together, and they glowed gold.
sentences.cn: 她把两块碎片紧贴在一起，它们闪出了金色的光。

recognize:1.en: We landed on a pale island dusted with silver sand. A old signpost stood alone at the shore. Old Helm walked up, tilted his head, and smiled. 'I *recognize* this place,' he said softly, 'though the stars above it have shifted.' I looked around — there was no other sign of life, only wind and wonder.
recognize:1.cnHint: 老舵主____出了这座被星光改变的小岛，但岛上似乎隐藏着什么秘密。
recognize:1.hook: Then the signpost turned on its own, pointing somewhere new.
recognize:1.line: 'I *recognize* that marking — it means we are very close,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: We landed on a pale island dusted with silver sand.
sentences.cn: 我们降落在一座苍白的小岛上，铺满了银色的沙子。

sentences.en: A old signpost stood alone at the shore.
sentences.cn: 一根老旧的路标独自矗立在岸边。

sentences.en: Old Helm walked up, tilted his head, and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵走过去，歪了歪头，笑了。

sentences.en: 'I *recognize* this place,' he said softly, 'though the stars above it have shifted.'
I looked around — there was no other sign of life, only wind and wonder.
sentences.cn: 我环顾四周——没有其他生命的迹象，只有风和无尽的奇异。

safety:1.en: The bridge between the two floating rocks was no wider than my boot. Bell crossed first, arms out, eyes ahead. Silverfang went next, quick and sure. I paused, heart loud in my chest. 'Your *safety* matters more than your speed,' Old Helm called from behind me. I breathed out, took one careful step, then another.
safety:1.cnHint: 老舵主提醒我，____比速度更重要，我小心地踏上了那座细窄的桥。
safety:1.hook: Halfway across, one stone shifted beneath my foot.
safety:1.line: 'Your *safety* comes first — the word can wait one minute,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The bridge between the two floating rocks was no wider than my boot.
sentences.cn: 两块浮起的石头之间的桥不比我的靴子宽多少。

sentences.en: Bell crossed first, arms out, eyes ahead.
sentences.cn: 小铃先过去，张开双臂，目视前方。

sentences.en: Silverfang went next, quick and sure.
sentences.cn: 银牙接着过，动作敏捷而稳健。

sentences.en: I paused, heart loud in my chest.
sentences.cn: 我停顿了一下，心跳声在胸腔里震得很响。

sentences.en: 'Your *safety* matters more than your speed,' Old Helm called from behind me.
I breathed out, took one careful step, then another.
sentences.cn: 我呼出一口气，小心翼翼地迈出一步，又是一步。

collect:1.en: Every morning Bell would walk the rim of whatever island we had camped on and *collect* small things — a seed, a feather, a chip of bright stone. She pressed them into a cloth pouch she wore at her hip. 'Maps are not only words,' she told me once, holding a blue feather to the starlight.
collect:1.cnHint: 领航员每天早晨____各种小物件，她说地图不只是文字。
collect:1.hook: That morning she found something that had no name in any language we knew.
collect:1.line: 'I *collect* these so we remember every island we have touched,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Every morning Bell would walk the rim of whatever island we had camped on and *collect* small things — a seed, a feather, a chip of bright stone.
She pressed them into a cloth pouch she wore at her hip.
sentences.cn: 她把它们压进一个系在腰间的布袋里。

sentences.en: 'Maps are not only words,' she told me once, holding a blue feather to the starlight.
sentences.cn: "地图不仅仅是文字，"她曾经对我说，在星光下举着一根蓝色的羽毛。

door:1.en: The word fragment we carried that day was carved on a flat stone the shape of a *door*. When Old Helm held it up to the wind, a faint outline appeared in the air ahead — tall, narrow, trembling like a reflection in water. Silverfang took a slow step toward it. 'Careful,' I whispered.
door:1.cnHint: 老舵主举起形如____的石刻碎片，空气中浮现出一道若隐若现的轮廓。
door:1.hook: Silverfang reached out and the outline became solid under their hand.
door:1.line: 'Every *door* on these islands opens only once, so choose your moment,' Old Helm warned.

sentences.en: The word fragment we carried that day was carved on a flat stone the shape of a *door*.
When Old Helm held it up to the wind, a faint outline appeared in the air ahead — tall, narrow, trembling like a reflection in water.
sentences.cn: 老舵把它举向风中时，前方的空气里浮现出一个淡淡的轮廓——高高的、狭窄的、像水面上的倒影一样颤抖。

sentences.en: Silverfang took a slow step toward it.
sentences.cn: 银牙慢慢向它走去。

sentences.en: 'Careful,' I whispered.
sentences.cn: "小心，"我低声说。

eventually:1.en: The fog around the northern cluster had turned back three ships before ours. Silverfang pushed the vessel forward anyway, reading the currents by touch. The fog thinned, then thinned again. We *eventually* broke through into clear sky, and a whole new chain of islands hung above us like lit lanterns.
eventually:1.cnHint: 穿越重重迷雾后，我们____冲破阻碍，看见了一串如灯笼般悬挂的新岛屿。
eventually:1.hook: One of those islands was already moving slowly toward us.
eventually:1.line: 'If you keep going, you will *eventually* find the sky you are looking for,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: The fog around the northern cluster had turned back three ships before ours.
sentences.cn: 北边那片区域的雾曾经挡住了我们之前的三艘船。

sentences.en: Silverfang pushed the vessel forward anyway, reading the currents by touch.
sentences.cn: 银牙还是把船推了进去，用触觉读着水流。

sentences.en: The fog thinned, then thinned again.
sentences.cn: 雾散开了，又散开了。

sentences.en: We *eventually* broke through into clear sky, and a whole new chain of islands hung above us like lit lanterns.

match:1.en: Old Helm set two word-fragments on the stone table and asked me to find which one would *match* the symbol on the northern gate. I turned them both slowly, held them to the starlight, and felt a faint hum when I brought one close to the gate's carved edge. It locked into place with a clean, bright click.
match:1.cnHint: 老舵主让我找出能与北门符文____的碎片，我在星光下仔细辨认。
match:1.hook: The gate swung open onto a sky nobody in the troupe had ever mapped.
match:1.line: 'Find the piece that will *match* the gate, and the last island will show itself,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm set two word-fragments on the stone table and asked me to find which one would *match* the symbol on the northern gate.
I turned them both slowly, held them to the starlight, and felt a faint hum when I brought one close to the gate's carved edge.
sentences.cn: 我慢慢转动它们，举向星光，当我把其中一块靠近北门的雕刻边缘时，感到了一阵微弱的嗡鸣。

sentences.en: It locked into place with a clean, bright click.
sentences.cn: 它以清脆明亮的咔嗒声锁进了位置。

safe:1.en: At the edge of the map, Old Helm knelt beside a mossy stone wall and brushed the dirt away. Behind a loose brick sat a small iron *safe*, no bigger than a bread loaf. Inside, a folded paper glowed faintly — another word, another island waiting to be found.
safe:1.cnHint: 老舵在石墙缝里发现了一个装有发光纸片的____。
safe:1.hook: But the lock had already been broken from the inside.
safe:1.line: 'Whatever was in this *safe*, someone reached it before us,' Old Helm said quietly.

sentences.en: At the edge of the map, Old Helm knelt beside a mossy stone wall and brushed the dirt away.
sentences.cn: 在地图的边缘，老舵跪在一堵长满苔藓的石墙旁，刷去上面的土。

sentences.en: Behind a loose brick sat a small iron *safe*, no bigger than a bread loaf.
Inside, a folded paper glowed faintly — another word, another island waiting to be found.
sentences.cn: 里面放着一张折叠的纸，微微发光——又一个词语，又一座等待被发现的小岛。

speed:1.en: Bell stood at the prow of the sky-boat, eyes wide, her scarf snapping behind her. The wind had shifted, and the islands were drifting apart fast. She adjusted the sail with calm hands. 'We match the *speed* of the current,' she said, 'or we lose the passage forever.'
speed:1.cnHint: 贝尔告诉我们必须配合气流的____，否则会错失航道。
speed:1.hook: The gap between the islands was already wider than the boat was long.
speed:1.line: 'Match the *speed* of the wind, or we fall behind,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Bell stood at the prow of the sky-boat, eyes wide, her scarf snapping behind her.
sentences.cn: 小铃站在天空船的船头，眼睛睁得很大，她的围巾在身后飘舞。

sentences.en: The wind had shifted, and the islands were drifting apart fast.
sentences.cn: 风向变了，小岛在迅速漂散。

sentences.en: She adjusted the sail with calm hands.
sentences.cn: 她用平稳的手调整着船帆。

sentences.en: 'We match the *speed* of the current,' she said, 'or we lose the passage forever.'

burden:1.en: Old Helm carried the word-chest on his back all morning across the cracked stone plaza. By midday he sat down on a fountain's edge, breathing hard. I offered to carry it next. He smiled and shook his head. 'It is my *burden*,' he said, 'and also my joy.'
burden:1.cnHint: 老舵独自背着装满词语的箱子，说这份____也是他的快乐。
burden:1.hook: Then the fountain behind him began to rise, stone by stone, into the sky.
burden:1.line: 'This chest is my *burden* to carry — do not worry for me,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Old Helm carried the word-chest on his back all morning across the cracked stone plaza.
sentences.cn: 老舵整个上午都背着词语箱穿过龟裂的石头广场。

sentences.en: By midday he sat down on a fountain's edge, breathing hard.
sentences.cn: 到了中午他坐在喷泉的边缘上，呼吸沉重。

sentences.en: I offered to carry it next.
sentences.cn: 我主动要背它。

sentences.en: He smiled and shook his head.
sentences.cn: 他笑了笑，摇摇头。

sentences.en: 'It is my *burden*,' he said, 'and also my joy.'

former:1.en: Two roads crossed the open market square. One was wide and paved with white stone; the other was narrow and covered in soft grass. Bell pointed to both and asked which way we should go. Old Helm chose the *former* without hesitation, saying the stone road always leads to the next word.
former:1.cnHint: 面对两条路，老舵选择了____，也就是宽阔的石板路。
former:1.hook: But at its far end, the white road simply stopped — in mid-air.
former:1.line: 'Of the two paths, I trust the *former* — the stone one,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Two roads crossed the open market square.
sentences.cn: 两条路在开放的市场广场上交叉。

sentences.en: One was wide and paved with white stone; the other was narrow and covered in soft grass.
sentences.cn: 一条宽阔，铺着白石；另一条狭窄，覆盖着软草。

sentences.en: Bell pointed to both and asked which way we should go.
sentences.cn: 小铃指着两条路，问我们应该走哪一条。

sentences.en: Old Helm chose the *former* without hesitation, saying the stone road always leads to the next word.

oppose:1.en: Silverfang's crew had reached the market first and blocked the only gate. They crossed their arms and said no one else would pass. Old Helm walked straight toward them without slowing. 'You may *oppose* us all you like,' he said pleasantly, 'but the word has already chosen its reader.'
oppose:1.cnHint: 银牙的船员封锁了城门，但老舵毫不畏惧地____他们。
oppose:1.hook: The gate swung open on its own the moment Old Helm finished speaking.
oppose:1.line: 'You can *oppose* us, but the map does not answer to you,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Silverfang's crew had reached the market first and blocked the only gate.
sentences.cn: 银牙的船队先抵达市场，堵住了唯一的出入口。

sentences.en: They crossed their arms and said no one else would pass.
sentences.cn: 他们交叉双臂说没人能通过。

sentences.en: Old Helm walked straight toward them without slowing.
sentences.cn: 老舵笔直朝他们走去，脚步没有半分减缓。

sentences.en: 'You may *oppose* us all you like,' he said pleasantly, 'but the word has already chosen its reader.'

unable:1.en: The word-fragment hovered just above the old clock tower, spinning slowly in the morning light. I climbed every step, stretched as far as I could, and still I was *unable* to reach it. Bell watched from below, then pulled out a small silver whistle and blew one soft note. The fragment floated down.
unable:1.cnHint: 我爬上钟楼却____够到漂浮的词语碎片，最终靠贝尔的口哨解决了问题。
unable:1.hook: The whistle's note was still hanging in the air, shaped like a door.
unable:1.line: 'I was *unable* to reach it, but your whistle did what my arms could not,' I told Bell.

sentences.en: The word-fragment hovered just above the old clock tower, spinning slowly in the morning light.
sentences.cn: 那个词的碎片悬浮在老钟楼正上方，在晨光中缓缓旋转。

sentences.en: I climbed every step, stretched as far as I could, and still I was *unable* to reach it.
Bell watched from below, then pulled out a small silver whistle and blew one soft note.
sentences.cn: 小铃从下面看着，然后掏出一只小银哨吹了一声。

sentences.en: The fragment floated down.
sentences.cn: 碎片飘落下来。

unusual:1.en: The open-air market on the floating island sold things I had never seen: jars of frozen laughter, hats that changed colour with your mood, maps drawn in starlight. But the most *unusual* stall had nothing on it at all — just a sign that read: 'Bring a word, take a wonder.'
unusual:1.cnHint: 集市上有个____的摊位，空空如也，只写着用词换奇迹的告示。
unusual:1.hook: Old Helm walked straight to that empty stall without even looking at the others.
unusual:1.line: 'That empty stall is the most *unusual* thing I have seen on any island,' I said.

sentences.en: The open-air market on the floating island sold things I had never seen: jars of frozen laughter, hats that changed colour with your mood, maps drawn in starlight.
sentences.cn: 浮岛上的露天市集卖着我从未见过的东西：装着冻住的笑声的罐子、会随心情变色的帽子、用星光画成的地图。

sentences.en: But the most *unusual* stall had nothing on it at all — just a sign that read: 'Bring a word, take a wonder.'

apart:1.en: The troupe stood at the very edge of the last mapped island. Ahead, two smaller rocks drifted slowly *apart*, leaving a growing gap of open sky between them. Bell measured the distance with her eyes. 'We jump now,' she said, 'before it is too wide.' We jumped. We made it. Barely.
apart:1.cnHint: 两块小岩石渐渐____，我们必须在缝隙变大前纵身一跳。
apart:1.hook: On the far rock, scratched into the stone, was a single new word.
apart:1.line: 'They are drifting *apart* — we jump on three, and we do not look down,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The troupe stood at the very edge of the last mapped island.
sentences.cn: 队伍站在最后一座已知岛屿的边缘。

sentences.en: Ahead, two smaller rocks drifted slowly *apart*, leaving a growing gap of open sky between them.
Bell measured the distance with her eyes.
sentences.cn: 小铃用眼睛估量了距离。

sentences.en: 'We jump now,' she said, 'before it is too wide.'
sentences.cn: 她说，"我们现在跳，再晚就太宽了。"

sentences.en: We jumped.
sentences.cn: 我们跳了。

sentences.en: We made it.
sentences.cn: 我们成功了。

sentences.en: Barely.
sentences.cn: 勉强成功。

advice:1.en: The market square on Thistledown Island buzzed with traders calling from every stall. Old Helm stopped beside a lamp-post and studied the crowd. 'You look lost,' said a friendly map-seller. Old Helm smiled and asked for *advice* on which road led to the edge of the island. The seller pointed west, and a new word glowed on our map.
advice:1.cnHint: 在市集广场，老舵向一位地图商人寻求____，找到了通往岛屿边缘的道路。
advice:1.hook: But the road west ended at nothing but open sky.
advice:1.line: 'My *advice* is simple: always ask the one who sells the maps.'

sentences.en: The market square on Thistledown Island buzzed with traders calling from every stall.
sentences.cn: 蓟绒岛的市集广场里商贩们从各个摊位上叫卖声不绝。

sentences.en: Old Helm stopped beside a lamp-post and studied the crowd.
sentences.cn: 老舵停在一根灯柱旁研究着人群。

sentences.en: 'You look lost,' said a friendly map-seller.
sentences.cn: 一个友善的地图商说，"你看起来迷路了。"

sentences.en: Old Helm smiled and asked for *advice* on which road led to the edge of the island.
The seller pointed west, and a new word glowed on our map.
sentences.cn: 商人指向西方，我们的地图上浮现了一个新的词。

attempt:1.en: The wind bridge between Coral Isle and the next island swayed dangerously. Bell studied the ropes and shook her head twice. Then she took a deep breath and began to *attempt* the crossing anyway, testing each plank with one careful foot before trusting it with her full weight. By the time she reached the other side, the rest of us had already stopped breathing.
attempt:1.cnHint: 小铃面对摇晃的风桥，鼓起勇气____过桥，每一步都走得小心翼翼。
attempt:1.hook: The last plank cracked just as she stepped off it.
attempt:1.line: 'We should *attempt* the crossing before the wind gets stronger,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The wind bridge between Coral Isle and the next island swayed dangerously.
sentences.cn: 珊瑚岛和下一个岛之间的风桥危险地摇晃着。

sentences.en: Bell studied the ropes and shook her head twice.
sentences.cn: 小铃查看了绳索，摇了两次头。

sentences.en: Then she took a deep breath and began to *attempt* the crossing anyway, testing each plank with one careful foot before trusting it with her full weight.
By the time she reached the other side, the rest of us had already stopped breathing.
sentences.cn: 等她到了另一边时，我们其他人早已屏住了呼吸。

draw:1.en: After a full morning of racing clouds across the sky-lanes, Silverfang and Bell arrived at Windhook Island at exactly the same moment. Old Helm checked both anchor ropes and declared it a *draw*, then laughed so hard the whole deck shook. The tied result meant the new word on the map belonged equally to both of them, and neither could quite stop smiling.
draw:1.cnHint: 银牙和小铃同时抵达，老舵宣布比赛以____收场，两人共同获得了地图碎片。
draw:1.hook: Then the map fragment split itself cleanly in two.
draw:1.line: 'A *draw* is fair enough — you are both the best I have ever seen,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: After a full morning of racing clouds across the sky-lanes, Silverfang and Bell arrived at Windhook Island at exactly the same moment.
sentences.cn: 在天空航道上追赶了整个上午的云层后，银牙和小铃在同一时刻抵达了风钩岛。

sentences.en: Old Helm checked both anchor ropes and declared it a *draw*, then laughed so hard the whole deck shook.
The tied result meant the new word on the map belonged equally to both of them, and neither could quite stop smiling.
sentences.cn: 平局意味着地图上的新词属于他们两个，谁都停不下来地微笑。

facility:1.en: High on Amber Ridge floated a small island built entirely for learning. Every corner held a shelf, a lens, or a strange spinning tool. Bell called it the finest *facility* she had ever visited, running her fingers along a brass telescope that could read star-names from ten islands away. Old Helm found the word we needed carved above the main door.
facility:1.cnHint: 小铃参观了一座专为学习而建的岛屿____，那里的每个角落都充满了奇妙的工具。
facility:1.hook: The telescope suddenly swung on its own and pointed south.
facility:1.line: 'This *facility* has everything a navigator could ever dream of,' Bell said quietly.

sentences.en: High on Amber Ridge floated a small island built entirely for learning.
sentences.cn: 琥珀岭高处漂浮着一座完全为学习而建的小岛。

sentences.en: Every corner held a shelf, a lens, or a strange spinning tool.
sentences.cn: 每个角落都放着书架、透镜或奇异的旋转工具。

sentences.en: Bell called it the finest *facility* she had ever visited, running her fingers along a brass telescope that could read star-names from ten islands away.
Old Helm found the word we needed carved above the main door.
sentences.cn: 老舵在正门上方找到了我们需要的那个词。

firm:1.en: A sudden gust tried to push our ship off course near the Pale Cliffs. Old Helm gripped the wheel and stayed *firm*, not giving a single degree to the wind. His arms did not shake and his eyes did not move from the horizon ahead. When the gust passed, Bell marked the safe path on our map, and a new word appeared in gold beside it.
firm:1.cnHint: 狂风袭来，老舵____地握紧船轮，一步不让，引领船只安全通过。
firm:1.hook: Ahead, the Pale Cliffs were moving closer together.
firm:1.line: 'Stay *firm* at the wheel — this wind will pass in sixty seconds,' Old Helm called out.

sentences.en: A sudden gust tried to push our ship off course near the Pale Cliffs.
sentences.cn: 在苍白悬崖附近，一阵突然的狂风想把我们的船吹离航线。

sentences.en: Old Helm gripped the wheel and stayed *firm*, not giving a single degree to the wind.
His arms did not shake and his eyes did not move from the horizon ahead.
sentences.cn: 他的胳膊没有颤抖，眼睛也没有离开前方的地平线。

sentences.en: When the gust passed, Bell marked the safe path on our map, and a new word appeared in gold beside it.
sentences.cn: 狂风过去后，小铃在地图上标记了这条安全航线，一个用金色写的新词出现在它旁边。

innovation:1.en: The island of Gearlight was unlike any place we had seen. Its people had built sky-bridges out of folded paper and starlight glass. Old Helm called the whole place a wonder of *innovation*, marvelling at how simple ideas had grown into something that kept an entire island floating above the clouds. A glowing word waited for us at the centre of the bridge.
innovation:1.cnHint: 在Gearlight岛，老舵对当地人用简单材料建造天桥的____赞叹不已。
innovation:1.hook: One paper bridge was already holding three more islands above it.
innovation:1.line: 'Real *innovation* comes from asking what nobody else thought to ask,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The island of Gearlight was unlike any place we had seen.
sentences.cn: 齿轮灯岛不像我们见过的任何地方。

sentences.en: Its people had built sky-bridges out of folded paper and starlight glass.
sentences.cn: 那里的人用折纸和星光玻璃建造了天桥。

sentences.en: Old Helm called the whole place a wonder of *innovation*, marvelling at how simple ideas had grown into something that kept an entire island floating above the clouds.
A glowing word waited for us at the centre of the bridge.
sentences.cn: 桥的中心有一个发光的词在等我们。

multiple:1.en: The map showed one path to Sunspire, but Bell discovered *multiple* routes spiralling out from the same starting point, each one marked with a different star symbol. She spread them on the deck and counted seven in total. Old Helm let me choose, and the one I picked was the only route still lit by the evening star, so we followed its light north.
multiple:1.cnHint: 小铃发现地图上通往目的地的路线不止一条，而是有____条，最终由叙述者来选择。
multiple:1.hook: Six of the seven paths had been quietly crossed out in red.
multiple:1.line: 'There are *multiple* ways forward — the question is which star you trust,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The map showed one path to Sunspire, but Bell discovered *multiple* routes spiralling out from the same starting point, each one marked with a different star symbol.
She spread them on the deck and counted seven in total.
sentences.cn: 她把地图铺在甲板上数了一遍，一共七条。

sentences.en: Old Helm let me choose, and the one I picked was the only route still lit by the evening star, so we followed its light north.
sentences.cn: 老舵让我选择，我选的那条路恰好还被晚星照亮，所以我们跟着它的光向北走。

path:1.en: Fog rolled in thick across the garden island of Mossbell just as we landed. The stone *path* that cut through the flower beds was the only thing still visible, glowing faintly with a soft blue light. I followed it slowly while Old Helm and Bell waited at the ship. At the end of the path stood a small stone pillar, and a new word was carved deep into its face.
path:1.cnHint: 浓雾中，叙述者独自沿着唯一可见的发光石____前行，在终点找到了新的地图文字。
path:1.hook: The pillar had a second face, and something was already carved there too.
path:1.line: 'Every great journey is really just one *path* chosen one step at a time,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Fog rolled in thick across the garden island of Mossbell just as we landed.
sentences.cn: 雾气在我们登陆苔藓岛时滚滚而来，浓得不见五指。

sentences.en: The stone *path* that cut through the flower beds was the only thing still visible, glowing faintly with a soft blue light.
I followed it slowly while Old Helm and Bell waited at the ship.
sentences.cn: 我沿着它慢慢走，老舵和小铃在船上等待。

sentences.en: At the end of the path stood a small stone pillar, and a new word was carved deep into its face.
sentences.cn: 路的尽头竖着一根小石柱，一个新词深深地刻在它的表面。

announce:1.en: The wind carried Old Helm's voice across the whole market square. He climbed onto a crate and *announced* to every traveller and trader present: our troupe had found the edge of the map. Strangers looked up from their stalls, eyes wide, feet already turning toward us.
announce:1.cnHint: 老赫姆站在箱子上，向广场上所有人____了我们找到地图尽头的消息。
announce:1.hook: But one hooded figure did not turn — they simply smiled.
announce:1.line: 'I *announce* to all of you: the edge of the map is real!'

sentences.en: The wind carried Old Helm's voice across the whole market square.
sentences.cn: 风把老舵的声音吹过了整个集市广场。

sentences.en: He climbed onto a crate and *announced* to every traveller and trader present: our troupe had found the edge of the map.
Strangers looked up from their stalls, eyes wide, feet already turning toward us.
sentences.cn: 陌生人从摊位抬起头，眼睛睁得很大，脚已经转向我们。

appropriate:1.en: Bell spread the map across a low stone wall and studied it carefully. Old Helm wanted to fly straight into the storm clouds ahead, but Bell shook her head. 'The southern wind route is more *appropriate*,' she said, tracing a gentle arc with her finger. She always found the right path.
appropriate:1.cnHint: 贝尔认为绕行南风路线比直飞风暴更____。
appropriate:1.hook: Then the southern wind suddenly reversed direction.
appropriate:1.line: 'A slower route is *appropriate* when the sky is angry.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the map across a low stone wall and studied it carefully.
sentences.cn: 小铃把地图铺在一面低矮的石墙上，仔细研究着。

sentences.en: Old Helm wanted to fly straight into the storm clouds ahead, but Bell shook her head.
sentences.cn: 老舵想直冲前面的风暴云，但小铃摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'The southern wind route is more *appropriate*,' she said, tracing a gentle arc with her finger.
She always found the right path.
sentences.cn: 她总是能找到对的路。

chief:1.en: Silverfang's ship docked beside ours just as the sun touched the horizon. He stepped off with his crew behind him, arms crossed. His *chief* reason for following us, he admitted at last, was not the treasure — it was the word written at the very edge of the map.
chief:1.cnHint: 银牙承认，追随我们的____原因并非财宝。
chief:1.hook: He read that word aloud, and the stars above shifted.
chief:1.line: 'My *chief* reason for being here is that single word on the map.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's ship docked beside ours just as the sun touched the horizon.
sentences.cn: 银牙的船停靠在我们的船旁，正好在太阳触及地平线的时候。

sentences.en: He stepped off with his crew behind him, arms crossed.
sentences.cn: 他踏了下来，他的船员跟在身后，双臂交叉。

sentences.en: His *chief* reason for following us, he admitted at last, was not the treasure — it was the word written at the very edge of the map.

clearly:1.en: The fragment glowed the moment Old Helm placed it on the ground. Strange lines of light spread outward, forming paths and peaks none of us had seen before. *Clearly*, the map was alive in ways we had never guessed. Even Silverfang stepped back and said nothing for a full minute.
clearly:1.cnHint: 碎片散发的光芒____表明，这张地图是有生命的。
clearly:1.hook: One glowing path led straight off the island's edge.
clearly:1.line: 'This map is *clearly* trying to tell us something urgent.'

sentences.en: The fragment glowed the moment Old Helm placed it on the ground.
sentences.cn: 老舵把碎片放在地上的那一刻，它就发出了光。

sentences.en: Strange lines of light spread outward, forming paths and peaks none of us had seen before.
sentences.cn: 奇异的光线向外蔓延，形成了我们从未见过的路径和山峰。

sentences.en: *Clearly*, the map was alive in ways we had never guessed.
Even Silverfang stepped back and said nothing for a full minute.
sentences.cn: 连银牙都往后退了一步，整整一分钟没说话。

communicate:1.en: The stone pillars at the square's centre were carved with tiny pictures — ships, stars, hands reaching out. Bell knelt and touched one gently. 'These were used to *communicate* between islands long ago,' she said softly. Each picture was a message from someone who had stood here before us.
communicate:1.cnHint: 广场石柱上的图案曾被用来在各岛之间____信息。
communicate:1.hook: The last picture showed a troupe exactly like ours.
communicate:1.line: 'Ancient people used these carvings to *communicate* across the sky.'

sentences.en: The stone pillars at the square's centre were carved with tiny pictures — ships, stars, hands reaching out.
sentences.cn: 广场中心的石柱上雕刻着微小的图画——船、星星、伸出的手。

sentences.en: Bell knelt and touched one gently.
sentences.cn: 小铃跪下来，轻轻地摸了摸其中一个。

sentences.en: 'These were used to *communicate* between islands long ago,' she said softly.
Each picture was a message from someone who had stood here before us.
sentences.cn: 每一幅图画都是来自曾经站在这里的人的讯息。

emphasis:1.en: Old Helm gathered us under the lamp at the crossroads and spoke slowly. He put great *emphasis* on one rule above all others: we must never trade a word fragment away, no matter what anyone offered. His eyes moved to Silverfang's ship in the distance as he said it.
emphasis:1.cnHint: 老赫姆特别____了一条规矩：绝不能转让地图碎片。
emphasis:1.hook: A stranger was already approaching with a very generous offer.
emphasis:1.line: 'I place *emphasis* on this rule: no fragment leaves our hands.'

sentences.en: Old Helm gathered us under the lamp at the crossroads and spoke slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵在十字路口的灯下把我们聚在一起，缓缓地说。

sentences.en: He put great *emphasis* on one rule above all others: we must never trade a word fragment away, no matter what anyone offered.
His eyes moved to Silverfang's ship in the distance as he said it.
sentences.cn: 他的眼睛扫过远处银牙的船，说出这番话的时候。

emphasize:1.en: Bell drew a circle around the outermost island on the map and tapped it twice. 'I want to *emphasize* that we have very little time,' she said, looking at the pale sky. The stars were fading faster than they should. Old Helm nodded and began folding the map without another word.
emphasize:1.cnHint: 贝尔____说，留给我们到达最外岛屿的时间已经不多了。
emphasize:1.hook: The last star on the horizon blinked out.
emphasize:1.line: 'Let me *emphasize* this: the stars will not wait for us.'

sentences.en: Bell drew a circle around the outermost island on the map and tapped it twice.
sentences.cn: 小铃在地图最外层的岛屿周围画了一个圆，然后敲了两下。

sentences.en: 'I want to *emphasize* that we have very little time,' she said, looking at the pale sky.
The stars were fading faster than they should.
sentences.cn: 星星消退的速度比它们应该消退的速度快。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded and began folding the map without another word.
sentences.cn: 老舵点了点头，没再说话就开始折起地图。

england:1.en: An old trader at the corner stall smiled when he saw our map. 'I once knew a navigator from *England*,' he said, 'who drew sky-maps just like this one.' He touched the edge with a careful finger. 'She said every map has a door — you just have to find the right key.'
england:1.cnHint: 角落摊位的老商人提到，他曾认识一位来自____的绘图师。
england:1.hook: He pressed a small brass key quietly into Old Helm's hand.
england:1.line: 'A navigator from *England* once told me maps have hidden doors.'

sentences.en: An old trader at the corner stall smiled when he saw our map.
sentences.cn: 角落摊位的一个老商人看到我们的地图时笑了。

sentences.en: 'I once knew a navigator from *England*,' he said, 'who drew sky-maps just like this one.'
He touched the edge with a careful finger.
sentences.cn: 他用谨慎的手指摸了摸边缘。

sentences.en: 'She said every map has a door — you just have to find the right key.'
sentences.cn: 她说每张地图都有一扇门——你只需要找到对的钥匙。

moment:1.en: The troupe reached the edge of the last island just before sunrise. Old Helm raised one hand, and everyone stopped. For one quiet *moment*, the whole sky turned gold — stars fading, a new horizon glowing. Nobody spoke. The silence itself felt like a gift none of us expected to find here.
moment:1.cnHint: 在地图尽头，团长举手示意大家停下，天空在那一____变成金色。
moment:1.hook: Then the gold faded — and something beneath us began to move.
moment:1.line: 'Hold still — this *moment* belongs to all of us.'

sentences.en: The troupe reached the edge of the last island just before sunrise.
sentences.cn: 队伍在日出前到达了最后一个岛屿的边缘。

sentences.en: Old Helm raised one hand, and everyone stopped.
sentences.cn: 老舵抬起一只手，所有人都停了下来。

sentences.en: For one quiet *moment*, the whole sky turned gold — stars fading, a new horizon glowing.
Nobody spoke.
sentences.cn: 没有人说话。

sentences.en: The silence itself felt like a gift none of us expected to find here.
sentences.cn: 这寂静本身感觉像是我们没想到会在这里找到的礼物。

nice:1.en: Bell spread the final map fragment on a flat stone and studied it with care. The lines were so *nice* in their detail — each curve measured to a hair's width — that she used a thin stick rather than her finger to trace them, afraid even a touch might smear the truth hidden inside.
nice:1.cnHint: 领航员在石头上研究地图碎片，被其____的细节所震惊。
nice:1.hook: One line on the map led not outward, but straight down.
nice:1.line: 'Look at this — the lines are too *nice* to be made by hand.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the final map fragment on a flat stone and studied it with care.
sentences.cn: 小铃把最后的地图碎片铺在平石上，小心地研究。

sentences.en: The lines were so *nice* in their detail — each curve measured to a hair's width — that she used a thin stick rather than her finger to trace them, afraid even a touch might smear the truth hidden inside.

peer:1.en: A thick morning mist rolled across the bridge of stone connecting the last two islands. I walked to the edge and tried to *peer* through the white cloud below, searching for solid ground. There was none. Old Helm put a hand on my shoulder and said the map had never lied yet.
peer:1.cnHint: 清晨的迷雾遮住了视线，我努力____向云层下方，却看不到任何地面。
peer:1.line: '*Peer* as hard as you like — you won't see the bottom from here.'

sentences.en: A thick morning mist rolled across the bridge of stone connecting the last two islands.
sentences.cn: 厚重的晨雾滚过连接最后两个岛屿的石桥。

sentences.en: I walked to the edge and tried to *peer* through the white cloud below, searching for solid ground.
There was none.
sentences.cn: 没有。

sentences.en: Old Helm put a hand on my shoulder and said the map had never lied yet.
sentences.cn: 老舵把手放在我的肩上，说地图从来没有骗过我们。

pretty:1.en: A market had grown at the very tip of the island, where traders sold fragments of sky-glass shaped into small *pretties* — charms, pendants, and tiny stars on silver wire. Bell chose one shaped like a compass rose and held it up. Light bent through it and painted colours on the stone path.
pretty:1.cnHint: 在岛屿尽头的市集，领航员挑选了一件玻璃____，光线穿过它折射出彩色光斑。
pretty:1.hook: The colours on the path pointed in a direction no compass had ever shown.
pretty:1.line: 'This little *pretty* bends light — that is not normal glass.'

sentences.en: A market had grown at the very tip of the island, where traders sold fragments of sky-glass shaped into small *pretties* — charms, pendants, and tiny stars on silver wire.
Bell chose one shaped like a compass rose and held it up.
sentences.cn: 小铃选了一个罗盘玫瑰形的，举了起来。

sentences.en: Light bent through it and painted colours on the stone path.
sentences.cn: 光穿过它，在石头路上画出了各种颜色。

recommendation:1.en: Old Helm unrolled a note left by a traveller who had reached this island before us. It held only one *recommendation*: cross at dawn, not dusk, and carry something that makes sound. He folded the note carefully, tucked it away, and then looked at Bell's small wind-chime with a satisfied nod.
recommendation:1.cnHint: 团长读到前人留下的纸条，上面只有一条____：黎明时分穿越，并随身携带能发声的东西。
recommendation:1.hook: Bell's wind-chime rang once — though the air was perfectly still.
recommendation:1.line: 'There is only one *recommendation* on this note, so we had better follow it.'

sentences.en: Old Helm unrolled a note left by a traveller who had reached this island before us.
sentences.cn: 老舵展开了一张纸条，是比我们更早到达这座岛屿的旅人留下的。

sentences.en: It held only one *recommendation*: cross at dawn, not dusk, and carry something that makes sound.
He folded the note carefully, tucked it away, and then looked at Bell's small wind-chime with a satisfied nod.
sentences.cn: 他小心地叠好纸条，收了起来，然后满意地点了点头，看着小铃的小风铃。

strange:1.en: The fruit sold at the last market tasted like nothing I could name — not sweet, not sour, just *strange* in the way a song sounds when you almost recognise it but cannot place the memory. Silverfang bought a whole bag and said that was exactly the kind of taste worth chasing across islands.
strange:1.cnHint: 市集里的水果味道____，像一首似曾相识却无法辨认的歌，竞争船长却买了一整袋。
strange:1.hook: Silverfang offered one to Old Helm, who turned pale at the smell.
strange:1.line: 'It tastes *strange*, yes — but that is what makes it worth finding.'

sentences.en: The fruit sold at the last market tasted like nothing I could name — not sweet, not sour, just *strange* in the way a song sounds when you almost recognise it but cannot place the memory.
Silverfang bought a whole bag and said that was exactly the kind of taste worth chasing across islands.
sentences.cn: 银牙买了整整一袋，说这正是值得跨越岛屿去追寻的味道。

widespread:1.en: News of the final map fragment had become *widespread* among sky-traders long before our troupe arrived. Every stall keeper knew our name, every dockhand had a theory about what lay beyond. Silverfang walked ahead of us, visibly annoyed that the secret we had carried so far was now everyone's favourite topic.
widespread:1.cnHint: 关于最后一块地图碎片的消息已经____流传，市集里每个人都知道我们的名字。
widespread:1.hook: One trader knew a detail about the fragment that only we should have known.
widespread:1.line: 'The rumour is *widespread* — someone in our troupe has been talking.'

sentences.en: News of the final map fragment had become *widespread* among sky-traders long before our troupe arrived.
Every stall keeper knew our name, every dockhand had a theory about what lay beyond.
sentences.cn: 每个摊主都认识我们的名字，每个码头工人都对其中隐藏的东西有自己的理论。

sentences.en: Silverfang walked ahead of us, visibly annoyed that the secret we had carried so far was now everyone's favourite topic.
sentences.cn: 银牙走在我们前面，明显对我们一直守护的秘密现在成了所有人最爱谈论的话题感到烦躁。

wonderful:1.en: When Bell placed the last fragment into the map and the whole picture clicked into place, a low hum rose from the stone table. The completed map glowed soft blue. Old Helm looked at it for a long time before he spoke. 'What a *wonderful* problem,' he said, smiling. 'We have run out of edges.'
wonderful:1.cnHint: 领航员将最后的碎片拼入地图，地图发出蓝光，团长看了许久才开口说了一句____的话。
wonderful:1.hook: The map showed one more island — on the back.
wonderful:1.line: 'What a *wonderful* problem — the map has no more edges to find.'

sentences.en: When Bell placed the last fragment into the map and the whole picture clicked into place, a low hum rose from the stone table.
sentences.cn: 小铃把最后的碎片放入地图，整个图案咔哒一声拼在一起，低沉的嗡鸣声从石桌升起。

sentences.en: The completed map glowed soft blue.
sentences.cn: 完整的地图发出柔和的蓝光。

sentences.en: Old Helm looked at it for a long time before he spoke.
sentences.cn: 老舵盯着它看了很久才开口。

sentences.en: 'What a *wonderful* problem,' he said, smiling.
'We have run out of edges.'
sentences.cn: "我们已经没有边界了。"

male:1.en: At the edge of the map, a long rope bridge stretched between two islands. Old Helm checked each plank carefully. 'Only the *male* goats cross first,' he said, watching the horned animals test the bridge. 'They are heavier. If it holds them, it holds us.'
male:1.cnHint: 老舵主让____山羊先过桥，测试桥板是否牢固。
male:1.hook: The last plank cracked before the final goat stepped off.
male:1.line: 'Only *male* goats are heavy enough to test this bridge.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the map, a long rope bridge stretched between two islands.
sentences.cn: 地图的边缘，一条长长的绳桥在两座岛屿之间伸展。

sentences.en: Old Helm checked each plank carefully.
sentences.cn: 老舵仔细检查了每一块木板。

sentences.en: 'Only the *male* goats cross first,' he said, watching the horned animals test the bridge.
'They are heavier.
sentences.cn: "它们更重。

sentences.en: If it holds them, it holds us.'
sentences.cn: 如果它们能通过，我们就能通过。"

fish:1.en: The market island smelled of salt and smoke. Stalls lined the narrow path, each one piled high with the morning catch. Bell pointed at a silver pile near the end. 'That *fish* still has frost on its scales,' she said. 'Someone flew it in from the ice islands tonight.'
fish:1.cnHint: 贝儿在市场摊位上发现一条来自冰岛的____，鳞片上还带着霜。
fish:1.hook: Beneath the frost, the scales spelled out half a map.
fish:1.line: 'This *fish* came from somewhere we have never been.'

sentences.en: The market island smelled of salt and smoke.
sentences.cn: 市场岛闻起来有盐和烟的味道。

sentences.en: Stalls lined the narrow path, each one piled high with the morning catch.
sentences.cn: 狭窄的小径两旁排列着摊位，每个摊位都堆满了早晨的收获。

sentences.en: Bell pointed at a silver pile near the end.
sentences.cn: 小铃指向末尾附近的一堆银色物品。

sentences.en: 'That *fish* still has frost on its scales,' she said.
'Someone flew it in from the ice islands tonight.'
sentences.cn: "有人今晚从冰岛飞来了。"

fashion:1.en: The island tailor worked in an open courtyard. Bright cloth hung from every pole. Old Helm watched him stitch in quick, neat loops. 'He sews in the old *fashion*,' Old Helm said quietly, 'the way mapmakers once bound their charts.' I looked closer and saw thread patterns that matched our route.
fashion:1.cnHint: 老舵主发现裁缝缝制的____与地图路线惊人地吻合。
fashion:1.hook: The next stitch traced exactly where our map went blank.
fashion:1.line: 'He works in a *fashion* I have not seen for many years.'

sentences.en: The island tailor worked in an open courtyard.
sentences.cn: 岛上的裁缝在开放的院子里工作。

sentences.en: Bright cloth hung from every pole.
sentences.cn: 鲜艳的布料从每根柱子上垂下来。

sentences.en: Old Helm watched him stitch in quick, neat loops.
sentences.cn: 老舵看着他以快速、整洁的环圈缝纫。

sentences.en: 'He sews in the old *fashion*,' Old Helm said quietly, 'the way mapmakers once bound their charts.'
I looked closer and saw thread patterns that matched our route.
sentences.cn: 我凑近一看，发现了与我们路线相匹配的线纹图案。

weather:1.en: We landed on the high bridge island just before noon. The wind had turned sharp and cold. Bell spread her hands and read the air like a page. 'The *weather* here changes without warning,' she said. 'The clouds move in circles, not lines. That means the next island is hiding itself from us.'
weather:1.cnHint: 贝儿通过观察____变化，判断下一座岛屿正在刻意隐藏自己。
weather:1.hook: Then the clouds locked into a perfect ring and stopped.
weather:1.line: '*Weather* like this only appears near an island that does not want to be found.'

sentences.en: We landed on the high bridge island just before noon.
sentences.cn: 我们在正午刚过时降落在高桥岛上。

sentences.en: The wind had turned sharp and cold.
sentences.cn: 风变得尖锐而寒冷。

sentences.en: Bell spread her hands and read the air like a page.
sentences.cn: 小铃张开双手，像读书一样读懂了空气。

sentences.en: 'The *weather* here changes without warning,' she said.
'The clouds move in circles, not lines.
sentences.cn: "云朵以圆形移动，而不是直线。

sentences.en: That means the next island is hiding itself from us.'
sentences.cn: 这意味着下一座岛屿在躲避我们。"
