slightly:2.hook: The last drawing showed an island with no name at all.
slightly:2.line: '*Slightly* tip it — one wrong move and the note tears.'

sentences.en: The old bottle had been sealed for years.
sentences.cn: 那个旧瓶子已经密封多年了。

sentences.en: When Bell *slightly* tilted it, a rolled-up note slid out and landed in my palm.
The paper was thin, covered in tiny drawings of islands we had never seen.
sentences.cn: 纸很薄，上面覆满了我们从未见过的岛屿的细小绘图。

sentences.en: Old Helm leaned close, eyes wide, and whispered that this was no ordinary map.
sentences.cn: 老舵靠近了，眼睛睁得很大，低声说这不是普通的地图。

vital:2.en: Deep inside the cloud-archive, we found a locked chest. Bell read the tag aloud: the key inside was *vital* to opening the gate at the edge of the map. Without it, the final island would stay hidden forever. Old Helm pressed the chest to his coat and said we were not leaving without it.
vital:2.cnHint: 在云端档案库深处，众人发现了一把对打开地图边缘大门____的钥匙。
vital:2.hook: Someone else had already tried to open the chest — and failed.
vital:2.line: 'This key is *vital*; lose it and the gate never opens.'

sentences.en: Deep inside the cloud-archive, we found a locked chest.
sentences.cn: 在云档深处，我们找到了一个上了锁的箱子。

sentences.en: Bell read the tag aloud: the key inside was *vital* to opening the gate at the edge of the map.
Without it, the final island would stay hidden forever.
sentences.cn: 没有它，最后的岛屿将永远隐没在黑暗里。

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed the chest to his coat and said we were not leaving without it.
sentences.cn: 老舵把箱子紧紧贴住胸口，说我们不能空手离开。

rare:2.en: Bell held up the crystal she had pulled from the rock pool. Its light was soft and steady, not like anything I had seen before. Old Helm said such stones were *rare* — found only where two sky-currents crossed at midnight. He turned it slowly, and the crystal painted tiny islands across the cabin wall.
rare:2.cnHint: 小铃找到一块只在两股天空气流交汇处才能发现的____水晶，它把小岛的影像投射在船舱墙上。
rare:2.hook: One of those glowing islands was circled in what looked like red ink.
rare:2.line: 'A stone this *rare* appears maybe once in a hundred years.'

sentences.en: Bell held up the crystal she had pulled from the rock pool.
sentences.cn: 小铃举起了从岩石潭里拉出来的水晶。

sentences.en: Its light was soft and steady, not like anything I had seen before.
sentences.cn: 它的光柔和而稳定，不像我见过的任何东西。

sentences.en: Old Helm said such stones were *rare* — found only where two sky-currents crossed at midnight.
He turned it slowly, and the crystal painted tiny islands across the cabin wall.
sentences.cn: 他慢慢转动它，水晶在舱室墙上投出一个个小岛的影子。

useful:2.en: Tucked behind a loose panel near the helm, I found a notebook filled with wind patterns and current charts. Old Helm flipped through it and nodded slowly. He said it was the most *useful* thing anyone could carry across the outer islands. Bell added it to the map-bag without a word.
useful:2.cnHint: 在船舵旁的暗格里，我找到了一本记载风向与洋流的笔记，老舵说这是穿越外岛时最____的东西。
useful:2.hook: The last page had a single sentence: trust the east wind after dark.
useful:2.line: 'Keep it — nothing more *useful* exists out here on the edge.'

sentences.en: Tucked behind a loose panel near the helm, I found a notebook filled with wind patterns and current charts.
sentences.cn: 我在舵轮附近的一块松动的面板后面找到了一本笔记本，里面全是风向图和洋流图。

sentences.en: Old Helm flipped through it and nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵翻过一页，慢慢点了点头。

sentences.en: He said it was the most *useful* thing anyone could carry across the outer islands.
Bell added it to the map-bag without a word.
sentences.cn: 小铃默不作声地把它加进了地图袋。

blood:2.en: The ancient door was sealed with a lock shaped like a hand. An old note beside it said the door opened only for those who carried island *blood* — people born under a sky without ground below. Old Helm placed his palm against the stone and the lock clicked open, quiet as a held breath.
blood:2.cnHint: 古老的门只向拥有岛屿____的人开启，老舵把手掌贴上石锁，门悄然打开了。
blood:2.hook: Beyond the door, starlight fell on a staircase going up — not down.
blood:2.line: 'Island *blood* runs in my veins; I have always known this door.'

sentences.en: The ancient door was sealed with a lock shaped like a hand.
sentences.cn: 古老的门用一把手形的锁封住了。

sentences.en: An old note beside it said the door opened only for those who carried island *blood* — people born under a sky without ground below.
Old Helm placed his palm against the stone and the lock clicked open, quiet as a held breath.
sentences.cn: 老舵把手掌贴在石头上，锁咔哒一声打开了，安静得像一口憋住的气息。

fund:2.en: Inside the hollow statue, we found a small tin box. Bell counted the coins inside — enough to *fund* three more legs of the journey and still leave something for repairs. Old Helm looked relieved. He said a troupe without money is a troupe that stands still, and we had too many islands left to visit.
fund:2.cnHint: 空心雕像里的小锡盒里有足够____三段旅程的硬币，让老舵松了一口气。
fund:2.hook: Pressed beneath the coins was a note that read: spend it wisely.
fund:2.line: 'These coins will *fund* us to the edge of the sky and back.'

sentences.en: Inside the hollow statue, we found a small tin box.
sentences.cn: 在空心雕像的内部，我们找到了一个小铁盒。

sentences.en: Bell counted the coins inside — enough to *fund* three more legs of the journey and still leave something for repairs.
Old Helm looked relieved.
sentences.cn: 老舵看起来松了一口气。

sentences.en: He said a troupe without money is a troupe that stands still, and we had too many islands left to visit.
sentences.cn: 他说一支没有钱的队伍就是一支停滞不前的队伍，而我们还有太多的岛屿要去。

operation:2.en: Deep inside the archive tower, Bell spread a crumbling chart across the stone floor. 'This whole *operation* has a logic,' she said, tracing the lines with one finger. Each route connected the islands like steps in a calculation — miss one, and the path home dissolved into open sky.
operation:2.cnHint: 小铃在档案塔里发现旧地图，意识到整次旅行的____有其内在逻辑。
operation:2.hook: One step was already missing from the chart.
operation:2.line: 'This whole *operation* has a logic — follow it carefully.'

sentences.en: Deep inside the archive tower, Bell spread a crumbling chart across the stone floor.
sentences.cn: 在档案塔的深处，小铃把一张残破的地图铺在石头地面上。

sentences.en: 'This whole *operation* has a logic,' she said, tracing the lines with one finger.
Each route connected the islands like steps in a calculation — miss one, and the path home dissolved into open sky.
sentences.cn: 每条航线都像计算中的步骤一样连接着岛屿——漏掉一个，回家的路就会溶解在空旷的天空里。

population:2.en: The message arrived folded inside a seed pod. Old Helm read it aloud: the island ahead had lost its *population* long ago, every resident drawn skyward by a strange light. Only their carved words remained, pressed into the bark of silver trees, waiting for someone willing to listen.
population:2.cnHint: 一封信揭示前方岛屿的____早已消失，只留下树皮上刻满的文字。
population:2.hook: The silver trees were already glowing at the edge of the clouds.
population:2.line: 'The island's *population* vanished — only their words are left.'

sentences.en: The message arrived folded inside a seed pod.
sentences.cn: 消息是折叠在一个豆荚里送来的。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it aloud: the island ahead had lost its *population* long ago, every resident drawn skyward by a strange light.
Only their carved words remained, pressed into the bark of silver trees, waiting for someone willing to listen.
sentences.cn: 只有他们刻在银树树皮上的文字还在，等待着某个愿意倾听的人。

quick:2.en: Bell pressed a small compass into my hand without a word. The needle was *quick* — it spun, steadied, then pointed somewhere our charts had never named. Old Helm leaned over my shoulder, eyes bright. 'That direction,' he said quietly, 'is exactly where we need to go.'
quick:2.cnHint: 小铃给了我一个指针____的罗盘，它指向地图上从未标注的方向。
quick:2.hook: The compass needle trembled, then pointed straight down.
quick:2.line: 'The needle is *quick* — it already knows the way.'

sentences.en: Bell pressed a small compass into my hand without a word.
sentences.cn: 小铃默不作声地把一个小罗盘塞进我的手心。

sentences.en: The needle was *quick* — it spun, steadied, then pointed somewhere our charts had never named.
Old Helm leaned over my shoulder, eyes bright.
sentences.cn: 老舵靠向我的肩膀，眼睛亮了起来。

sentences.en: 'That direction,' he said quietly, 'is exactly where we need to go.'
sentences.cn: "那个方向，"他轻声说，"正好是我们需要去的地方。"

scale:2.en: Pinned to the mast was a map unlike any we carried. Its *scale* was enormous — one finger's width equalled a full day's flight. At that size, our entire journey so far was barely a scratch. Old Helm touched it gently, as though afraid the distances might grow even larger under his hand.
scale:2.cnHint: 船桅上钉着一幅____极大的地图，让我们意识到旅途才刚刚开始。
scale:2.hook: At that scale, the map's edge was still blank.
scale:2.line: 'At this *scale*, we have barely begun our journey.'

sentences.en: Pinned to the mast was a map unlike any we carried.
sentences.cn: 桅杆上钉着一张和我们携带的任何地图都不同的地图。

sentences.en: Its *scale* was enormous — one finger's width equalled a full day's flight.
At that size, our entire journey so far was barely a scratch.
sentences.cn: 按那个比例，我们到目前为止的整个旅程也不过是一道浅浅的划痕。

sentences.en: Old Helm touched it gently, as though afraid the distances might grow even larger under his hand.
sentences.cn: 老舵温柔地摸了摸它，仿佛害怕距离在他手下会变得更加遥远。

basic:2.en: Inside the hollow lighthouse, a single engraved tablet waited on the shelf. Bell dusted it off and read slowly. The words were plain, almost too simple — the *basics* of sky-navigation, the kind of knowledge every troupe should carry. But no one had told us. Someone had left this here on purpose.
basic:2.cnHint: 灯塔里的石刻写着航行的____知识，像是有人特意为我们留下的。
basic:2.hook: Below the basics, a second message had been scratched out.
basic:2.line: 'These are the *basics* — someone knew we would need them.'

sentences.en: Inside the hollow lighthouse, a single engraved tablet waited on the shelf.
sentences.cn: 在空心灯塔的内部，一块刻着字的石板静静地躺在架子上。

sentences.en: Bell dusted it off and read slowly.
sentences.cn: 小铃拂去灰尘，缓缓读了起来。

sentences.en: The words were plain, almost too simple — the *basics* of sky-navigation, the kind of knowledge every troupe should carry.
But no one had told us.
sentences.cn: 但没人告诉过我们。

sentences.en: Someone had left this here on purpose.
sentences.cn: 有人是特意把它留在这里的。

constantly:2.en: The word-fragment glowed *constantly*, never dimming even when I cupped my hands around it to block the starlight. Old Helm said some words refused to sleep — they kept burning because the place they unlocked was still waiting, patient and awake, somewhere beyond the last reef of clouds.
constantly:2.cnHint: 碎片文字____发光，老舵手说这意味着它指向的地方仍在等待我们。
constantly:2.hook: Its glow had just turned a deeper, warmer gold.
constantly:2.line: 'It glows *constantly* — that island is still waiting for us.'

sentences.en: The word-fragment glowed *constantly*, never dimming even when I cupped my hands around it to block the starlight.
Old Helm said some words refused to sleep — they kept burning because the place they unlocked was still waiting, patient and awake, somewhere beyond the last reef of clouds.
sentences.cn: 老舵说有些文字拒绝入睡——它们一直在燃烧，因为它们解开的地方仍在等待，耐心而清醒，在最后一道云礁的某处。

favor:2.en: Two routes branched from the ridge marker. Old Helm studied both, then tapped the narrower one. 'I *favor* this path,' he said, 'because the wind here smells of pine bark, and pine only grows where there is solid ground.' I had learned to trust his nose at least as much as any map.
favor:2.cnHint: 老舵手在两条路中____较窄的那条，因为风的气味告诉了他答案。
favor:2.hook: The wider path had just let out a low, hollow sound.
favor:2.line: 'I *favor* the narrow path — the wind already told me why.'

sentences.en: Two routes branched from the ridge marker.
sentences.cn: 两条路从岭标处分了出去。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied both, then tapped the narrower one.
sentences.cn: 老舵研究了两条，然后敲了敲那条更窄的。

sentences.en: 'I *favor* this path,' he said, 'because the wind here smells of pine bark, and pine only grows where there is solid ground.'
I had learned to trust his nose at least as much as any map.
sentences.cn: 我已经学会了相信他的鼻子，就像相信任何地图一样。

absence:2.en: The dock was full of footprints but held no people. Silverfang crouched and pressed a finger into the soft wood. 'Fresh,' he said. The *absence* of voices felt heavier than silence — it meant someone had been here moments ago and chosen, very deliberately, not to be seen by us.
absence:2.cnHint: 码头上有新鲜脚印却空无一人，这种____让竞争船长意识到有人在刻意躲避我们。
absence:2.hook: One set of footprints led directly to the edge and stopped.
absence:2.line: 'This *absence* of people is not an accident — someone hid.'

sentences.en: The dock was full of footprints but held no people.
sentences.cn: 码头上满是脚印，却不见一个人影。

sentences.en: Silverfang crouched and pressed a finger into the soft wood.
sentences.cn: 银牙蹲下身子，一根手指按进软木。

sentences.en: 'Fresh,' he said.
sentences.cn: "新鲜的。"他说。

sentences.en: The *absence* of voices felt heavier than silence — it meant someone had been here moments ago and chosen, very deliberately, not to be seen by us.

institution:2.en: At the edge of the map, we found a stone building carved with a golden compass. Old Helm ran his fingers over the symbol and smiled. 'This mark belongs to the Wayfinders,' he said, 'an *institution* older than any chart we carry — they have mapped every island that ever floated.'
institution:2.cnHint: 老船长认出了一个古老____的标志，这让整个队伍都安静下来。
institution:2.hook: But the door beneath the compass was already open.
institution:2.line: 'The *institution* has left a message — and it is meant for us.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the map, we found a stone building carved with a golden compass.
sentences.cn: 在地图的边缘，我们发现了一座石头建筑，上面雕刻着一个金色的罗盘。

sentences.en: Old Helm ran his fingers over the symbol and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵用手指摩擦那个符号，露出了笑容。

sentences.en: 'This mark belongs to the Wayfinders,' he said, 'an *institution* older than any chart we carry — they have mapped every island that ever floated.'

outcome:2.en: Bell spread the old chart across a flat rock and traced three possible routes to the next island. We debated for a long time. Old Helm finally tapped the middle path. Whatever our choice, he said, the *outcome* would teach us something the map never could — and that alone made it worth picking.
outcome:2.cnHint: 小铃研究地图后，大家对选哪条路争论不休，老船长说无论____如何都值得一试。
outcome:2.hook: The middle path disappeared into a cloud that glowed faintly green.
outcome:2.line: 'Trust the crew — the *outcome* will surprise us all.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the old chart across a flat rock and traced three possible routes to the next island.
sentences.cn: 小铃把旧地图铺在一块平坦的石头上，描绘出通往下一个岛屿的三条可能路线。

sentences.en: We debated for a long time.
sentences.cn: 我们争论了很长时间。

sentences.en: Old Helm finally tapped the middle path.
sentences.cn: 老舵最终点了点中间那条路。

sentences.en: Whatever our choice, he said, the *outcome* would teach us something the map never could — and that alone made it worth picking.

recognize:2.en: I pulled a faded tile from the rubble of a sunken arch. Strange letters covered its face. Bell leaned in close, then stepped back with wide eyes. 'I *recognize* this script,' she whispered. 'It is the oldest word-language — the one the first island-builders used to name the sky itself.'
recognize:2.cnHint: 小铃在废墟中认出了一块刻有古老文字的石板，令所有人震惊。
recognize:2.hook: The tile grew warm the moment Bell touched it again.
recognize:2.line: 'I *recognize* that symbol — we have been here before, in a dream.'

sentences.en: I pulled a faded tile from the rubble of a sunken arch.
sentences.cn: 我从一道沉没的拱门的废墟中拉出一块褪色的瓷砖。

sentences.en: Strange letters covered its face.
sentences.cn: 奇怪的字母覆盖了它的表面。

sentences.en: Bell leaned in close, then stepped back with wide eyes.
sentences.cn: 小铃靠近看了看，然后睁大眼睛退后了。

sentences.en: 'I *recognize* this script,' she whispered.
'It is the oldest word-language — the one the first island-builders used to name the sky itself.'
sentences.cn: "那是最古老的文字语言——最早的岛屿建造者用来命名天空本身的语言。"

safety:2.en: The bridge between the two islands was nothing but rope and old wood. Old Helm tested each plank before letting anyone cross. 'Your *safety* matters more than any word we might find on the other side,' he called back, voice calm against the wind roaring below us.
safety:2.cnHint: 老船长坚持逐块检查桥板，把大家的____放在寻找新词语之前。
safety:2.hook: Halfway across, one plank cracked loud as a drum.
safety:2.line: 'Move carefully — your *safety* is the only map we cannot replace.'

sentences.en: The bridge between the two islands was nothing but rope and old wood.
sentences.cn: 两个岛屿之间的桥梁只不过是绳子和老木头。

sentences.en: Old Helm tested each plank before letting anyone cross.
sentences.cn: 老舵在让任何人通过之前测试了每一块木板。

sentences.en: 'Your *safety* matters more than any word we might find on the other side,' he called back, voice calm against the wind roaring below us.

collect:2.en: The island of Ashenveil was covered in tiny blue stones, each one etched with a single letter. Old Helm handed each of us a small bag. 'We *collect* only what we can carry,' he said, 'because a word too heavy to hold is a word you will never truly learn.'
collect:2.cnHint: 在Ashenveil岛，队长让大家____刻有字母的蓝色石头，但提醒不要贪多。
collect:2.hook: At the bottom of my bag, one stone hummed softly against my palm.
collect:2.line: '*Collect* only the ones that feel right — the stones will know.'

sentences.en: The island of Ashenveil was covered in tiny blue stones, each one etched with a single letter.
sentences.cn: 灰烬面纱岛被密密麻麻的蓝色石头覆盖，每一块上面都刻着一个字母。

sentences.en: Old Helm handed each of us a small bag.
sentences.cn: 老舵给我们每个人都递了一个小袋子。

sentences.en: 'We *collect* only what we can carry,' he said, 'because a word too heavy to hold is a word you will never truly learn.'

door:2.en: We followed a thread of floating lanterns to a cliff face at the very rim of the known map. There, cut cleanly into the stone, was a single *door* — no handle, no lock, just a frame of dark wood standing alone in the rock like a quiet invitation from somewhere beyond.
door:2.cnHint: 在地图边缘的悬崖上，我们发现了一扇奇怪的____，它静静地立在那里等待着。
door:2.hook: Bell pressed her ear to the wood and then smiled without explaining why.
door:2.line: 'Every *door* at the edge of the map opens into a new chapter.'

sentences.en: We followed a thread of floating lanterns to a cliff face at the very rim of the known map.
sentences.cn: 我们追随着一条浮动灯笼的线来到了已知地图边缘的悬崖绝壁。

sentences.en: There, cut cleanly into the stone, was a single *door* — no handle, no lock, just a frame of dark wood standing alone in the rock like a quiet invitation from somewhere beyond.

eventually:2.en: The word-fragment we needed had been missing from Old Helm's collection for three full seasons. We searched ruin after ruin, island after island. Then, tucked inside a hollow star-coral on the lowest shelf of a tidal cave, there it was. '*Eventually*,' Bell said softly, 'the map always gives back what it owes.'
eventually:2.cnHint: 老船长寻找某个词语碎片长达三个季节，____在一个潮汐洞穴中找到了它。
eventually:2.hook: The fragment clicked into the map and a new island blinked into view.
eventually:2.line: '*Eventually* every lost word finds the hand that needs it most.'

sentences.en: The word-fragment we needed had been missing from Old Helm's collection for three full seasons.
sentences.cn: 老舵收集中缺少的那个词碎片已经三个整季节没有出现了。

sentences.en: We searched ruin after ruin, island after island.
sentences.cn: 我们一个废墟接一个废墟地搜索，一个岛屿接一个岛屿地搜索。

sentences.en: Then, tucked inside a hollow star-coral on the lowest shelf of a tidal cave, there it was. '*Eventually*,' Bell said softly, 'the map always gives back what it owes.'

match:2.en: Silverfang arrived just as we placed the last word-tile on the stone table. He studied our arrangement and then, reluctantly, laid his own chart beside it. The two maps were a perfect *match* — every island, every gap, every unnamed cloud lined up exactly. Neither crew could reach the next horizon alone.
match:2.cnHint: 银牙的地图和我们的地图完全吻合，两支队伍意识到必须合作才能前进。
match:2.hook: Old Helm extended his hand, and after a long pause, Silverfang took it.
match:2.line: 'A perfect *match* — it seems the sky planned this meeting for us.'

sentences.en: Silverfang arrived just as we placed the last word-tile on the stone table.
sentences.cn: 银牙恰好在我们把最后一块词砖放在石桌上时赶到了。

sentences.en: He studied our arrangement and then, reluctantly, laid his own chart beside it.
sentences.cn: 他研究了我们的排列，然后不太情愿地把他自己的地图放在了一边。

sentences.en: The two maps were a perfect *match* — every island, every gap, every unnamed cloud lined up exactly.
Neither crew could reach the next horizon alone.
sentences.cn: 两支船队都无法独自到达下一个地平线。

advice:2.en: Deep in the Archive Grotto, Old Helm unrolled a brittle scroll covered in faded ink. 'Someone left *advice* for every traveller who reaches this place,' he murmured, tracing each line with care. The words warned of a hidden current below the next island. Bell copied them down without a sound.
advice:2.cnHint: 老船长在档案洞穴里发现了一张古老的卷轴，上面写满了给旅行者的____。
advice:2.hook: But one line had been torn away, and no one knew what it warned of.
advice:2.line: 'This *advice* was written for us — read every word carefully.'

sentences.en: Deep in the Archive Grotto, Old Helm unrolled a brittle scroll covered in faded ink.
sentences.cn: 在档案岩洞深处，老舵展开了一张布满褪色墨迹的易碎卷轴。

sentences.en: 'Someone left *advice* for every traveller who reaches this place,' he murmured, tracing each line with care.
The words warned of a hidden current below the next island.
sentences.cn: 这些话语警告了下一个岛屿下方隐藏的洋流。

sentences.en: Bell copied them down without a sound.
sentences.cn: 小铃无声地把它们抄了下来。

attempt:2.en: The Crystal Bridge connecting two islands had cracked down the middle. Old Helm watched the gap, then stepped back and nodded at me. I took a breath and *attempted* to leap across, arms wide, the wind pushing hard against my chest. My boots landed on the far edge — just barely.
attempt:2.cnHint: 我____跳过那道裂缝，双脚刚好落在了桥的另一端。
attempt:2.hook: On the far side, a locked door had already been opened from within.
attempt:2.line: 'I will *attempt* the jump — hold the rope steady.'

sentences.en: The Crystal Bridge connecting two islands had cracked down the middle.
sentences.cn: 连接两个岛屿的水晶桥从中间裂开了。

sentences.en: Old Helm watched the gap, then stepped back and nodded at me.
sentences.cn: 老舵看着那道裂缝，然后退了一步，向我点了点头。

sentences.en: I took a breath and *attempted* to leap across, arms wide, the wind pushing hard against my chest.
My boots landed on the far edge — just barely.
sentences.cn: 我的靴子落在了远边的边缘——勉强着陆。

draw:2.en: At the Sky Crossroads, Silverfang and Old Helm had searched the same hidden shelf at the same moment and found the same map fragment. Neither would let go. Bell called it a *draw* and suggested they copy the fragment twice, one for each troupe. Both captains stared at her, then laughed.
draw:2.cnHint: 两位船长同时找到同一块碎片，贝尔宣布这是一场____，提议各复制一份。
draw:2.hook: Yet the two copies showed different routes — one of them had to be false.
draw:2.line: 'Call it a *draw* and we each take a copy — agreed?'

sentences.en: At the Sky Crossroads, Silverfang and Old Helm had searched the same hidden shelf at the same moment and found the same map fragment.
sentences.cn: 在天空十字路口，银牙和老舵在同一时刻搜索了同一个隐藏的架子，并找到了同样的地图碎片。

sentences.en: Neither would let go.
sentences.cn: 谁都不肯松手。

sentences.en: Bell called it a *draw* and suggested they copy the fragment twice, one for each troupe.
Both captains stared at her, then laughed.
sentences.cn: 两位船长盯着她看，然后笑了。

facility:2.en: Tucked behind a waterfall on the Island of Mists was a small stone *facility* built for mapmakers long ago: a flat table, ink wells still sealed, and shelves of blank paper. Old Helm ran his hand along the edge and whispered that someone had kept it in perfect order. But no one had lived here for years.
facility:2.cnHint: 瀑布后面藏着一处古老的制图____，桌台整洁，墨水未干。
facility:2.hook: A fresh sheet of paper lay on the table, and something was already sketched on it.
facility:2.line: 'This *facility* was built to last — and it has.'

sentences.en: Tucked behind a waterfall on the Island of Mists was a small stone *facility* built for mapmakers long ago: a flat table, ink wells still sealed, and shelves of blank paper.
Old Helm ran his hand along the edge and whispered that someone had kept it in perfect order.
sentences.cn: 老舵用手指尖沿着边缘滑过，低声说有人把这地方保护得完美无缺。

sentences.en: But no one had lived here for years.
sentences.cn: 但已经没人在这里住过好多年了。

firm:2.en: The final stepping stone before the Island of Echoes wobbled under every foot. Bell tested it twice and shook her head. Old Helm pressed his boot down slowly until the stone settled, *firm* at last, as if it had simply been waiting for the right weight to hold it in place. He waved us across one by one.
firm:2.cnHint: 老舵手用力踩稳了那块摇晃的踏脚石，它终于变得____。
firm:2.hook: The moment the last of us crossed, the stone dropped silently into the clouds.
firm:2.line: 'Keep your step *firm* — this stone will hold if you trust it.'

sentences.en: The final stepping stone before the Island of Echoes wobbled under every foot.
sentences.cn: 回声岛前最后一块踏脚石在每个人的脚下都晃晃悠悠的。

sentences.en: Bell tested it twice and shook her head.
sentences.cn: 小铃试了两次，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed his boot down slowly until the stone settled, *firm* at last, as if it had simply been waiting for the right weight to hold it in place.
He waved us across one by one.
sentences.cn: 他一个一个地挥手让我们过去。

innovation:2.en: The old bridge builders of the floating islands had left a sign near their workshop: 'Every *innovation* begins with a question no one has answered yet.' Old Helm read it aloud twice. Bell pulled out her notebook. I stood very still, feeling the words settle somewhere deep, like a word-fragment locking into a map.
innovation:2.cnHint: 工坊入口的石碑上刻着一句关于____的格言，让整个团队陷入了沉思。
innovation:2.hook: Below the motto, someone had carved a question — still unanswered after all this time.
innovation:2.line: 'True *innovation* starts the moment you ask a question no one else dared.'

sentences.en: The old bridge builders of the floating islands had left a sign near their workshop: 'Every *innovation* begins with a question no one has answered yet.'
Old Helm read it aloud twice.
sentences.cn: 老舵大声读了两遍。

sentences.en: Bell pulled out her notebook.
sentences.cn: 小铃掏出了她的笔记本。

sentences.en: I stood very still, feeling the words settle somewhere deep, like a word-fragment locking into a map.
sentences.cn: 我站得很僵硬，感受着这些词像地图碎片一样在心底咔的一声卡进去。

multiple:2.en: The Archivist's Tower held *multiple* doors, each painted a different colour and each sealed with a different riddle. Old Helm tried the blue one first, then the gold. Bell solved the riddle on the silver door in under a minute. Behind it sat a single small chest that held the next map fragment, neatly folded.
multiple:2.cnHint: 档案师塔里有____扇门，贝尔率先解开了银门上的谜题。
multiple:2.hook: The chest also held a key labelled with a door colour none of us had tried.
multiple:2.line: 'There are *multiple* doors here — we solve them one riddle at a time.'

sentences.en: The Archivist's Tower held *multiple* doors, each painted a different colour and each sealed with a different riddle.
Old Helm tried the blue one first, then the gold.
sentences.cn: 老舵先试了蓝色的门，然后是金色的。

sentences.en: Bell solved the riddle on the silver door in under a minute.
sentences.cn: 小铃不到一分钟就解开了银色门上的谜语。

sentences.en: Behind it sat a single small chest that held the next map fragment, neatly folded.
sentences.cn: 门后放着一个小箱子，里面整齐地叠着下一块地图碎片。

path:2.en: At the edge of the last charted island, the map simply ended in blank white space. Old Helm knelt and pressed the paper flat. Then Bell noticed it: a faint dotted *path* leading off the page, pressed into the paper rather than drawn in ink, as if the maker had pushed the route in by hand. We had our next direction.
path:2.cnHint: 在地图的尽头，贝尔发现了一条压印在纸上的隐秘____，指向未知之地。
path:2.hook: The dots stopped at a shape none of us recognised — an island with no name.
path:2.line: 'Follow the *path* pressed into the paper — it leads beyond the edge.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the last charted island, the map simply ended in blank white space.
sentences.cn: 在最后一个已绘制的岛屿边缘，地图就结束在空白的白色空间里。

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt and pressed the paper flat.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪下来，把纸张压平。

sentences.en: Then Bell noticed it: a faint dotted *path* leading off the page, pressed into the paper rather than drawn in ink, as if the maker had pushed the route in by hand.
We had our next direction.
sentences.cn: 我们找到了下一个方向。

safe:2.en: Deep inside the cliff tower, we found a heavy iron *safe* bolted to the stone wall. Old Helm pressed his ear against it and turned the dial slowly. When it clicked open, a folded map fragment tumbled out, glowing faintly with the name of an island none of us had ever seen. The word was ours.
safe:2.cnHint: 在峭壁塔楼深处，老舵手打开了一个铁制____，里面藏着发光的地图碎片。
safe:2.hook: But the map showed two paths, and only one led somewhere safe.
safe:2.line: 'This *safe* has been locked for a hundred years,' Old Helm said softly.

sentences.en: Deep inside the cliff tower, we found a heavy iron *safe* bolted to the stone wall.
Old Helm pressed his ear against it and turned the dial slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵把耳朵贴在上面，慢慢转动转盘。

sentences.en: When it clicked open, a folded map fragment tumbled out, glowing faintly with the name of an island none of us had ever seen.
sentences.cn: 转盘咔的一声打开时，一块折叠的地图碎片掉了出来，隐隐约约闪着光，上面是我们谁都没见过的一个岛屿的名字。

sentences.en: The word was ours.
sentences.cn: 这个词属于我们了。

speed:2.en: Bell called out the wind direction, and Old Helm adjusted the sails with quiet confidence. The island was drifting away — slowly at first, then faster. I felt the deck tremble beneath me as our vessel matched its *speed*, pulling alongside just in time for me to grab the rope ladder and climb.
speed:2.cnHint: 贝尔和老舵手驾船以极快的____追上了漂移的岛屿，我抓住绳梯爬了上去。
speed:2.hook: At the top of the ladder, something ancient was waiting.
speed:2.line: 'Match its *speed* or we lose it forever,' Bell warned.

sentences.en: Bell called out the wind direction, and Old Helm adjusted the sails with quiet confidence.
sentences.cn: 小铃喊出风的方向，老舵用平稳而自信的动作调整帆。

sentences.en: The island was drifting away — slowly at first, then faster.
sentences.cn: 岛屿在漂离——先是缓缓的，然后越来越快。

sentences.en: I felt the deck tremble beneath me as our vessel matched its *speed*, pulling alongside just in time for me to grab the rope ladder and climb.

burden:2.en: The stone door would not move. Bell and I pushed together, but it held firm. Old Helm knelt and read the carving beneath our feet: only someone willing to carry a *burden* could pass. I picked up the heavy lantern from the floor and held it to my chest. The door swung open.
burden:2.cnHint: 石门上的刻字说，只有愿意承受____的人才能通过，我抱起沉重的灯笼，门开了。
burden:2.hook: Beyond the door, the lantern's light revealed a staircase with no visible end.
burden:2.line: 'Every explorer knows the weight of a *burden*,' Old Helm said with a warm smile.

sentences.en: The stone door would not move.
sentences.cn: 石门纹丝不动。

sentences.en: Bell and I pushed together, but it held firm.
sentences.cn: 小铃和我一起推，但它牢牢地卡着。

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt and read the carving beneath our feet: only someone willing to carry a *burden* could pass.
I picked up the heavy lantern from the floor and held it to my chest.
sentences.cn: 我从地板上拿起沉重的灯笼，紧紧抱在胸口。

sentences.en: The door swung open.
sentences.cn: 门打开了。

former:2.en: Two paths split at the ridge. The *former* led down to a quiet valley full of silver grass; the latter climbed toward a crumbling bridge above the clouds. Bell studied both, then pointed downward. Old Helm agreed. We took the first path, and the valley gave us exactly what we needed: a new word carved on a stone post.
former:2.cnHint: 山脊处有两条路，贝尔选择了____，带领大家走进了刻有新词语的山谷。
former:2.hook: The stone post bore a second carving no one had noticed yet.
former:2.line: 'The *former* path is quieter, but quiet things often hide the most,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Two paths split at the ridge.
sentences.cn: 两条路在山脊处分开。

sentences.en: The *former* led down to a quiet valley full of silver grass; the latter climbed toward a crumbling bridge above the clouds.
Bell studied both, then pointed downward.
sentences.cn: 小铃研究了一会儿两条路，然后指向下面。

sentences.en: Old Helm agreed.
sentences.cn: 老舵同意。

sentences.en: We took the first path, and the valley gave us exactly what we needed: a new word carved on a stone post.
sentences.cn: 我们走了第一条路，山谷给了我们正好需要的东西：一块石柱上刻着的新词。

oppose:2.en: Silverfang's crew arrived at the bridge just as we did, and he crossed his arms. 'Turn back,' he said. 'This fragment is mine.' Old Helm stood steady. 'We do not *oppose* you, but this word belongs to the sky.' Silverfang studied Old Helm's calm face for a long moment, then stepped aside with a surprised laugh.
oppose:2.cnHint: 银牙出现并要求我们离开，但老舵手平静地表示不____他，只是坚持这个词语属于天空。
oppose:2.hook: Silverfang's laugh faded as he read what the fragment actually said.
oppose:2.line: 'I don't *oppose* fair rivals,' Silverfang said, 'only lazy ones.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's crew arrived at the bridge just as we did, and he crossed his arms.
sentences.cn: 银牙和他的船队在我们到达时也来到了桥边，他叉起了双臂。

sentences.en: 'Turn back,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他说，"回头。"

sentences.en: 'This fragment is mine.'
sentences.cn: "这块碎片是我的。"

sentences.en: Old Helm stood steady.
sentences.cn: 老舵站得很稳。

sentences.en: 'We do not *oppose* you, but this word belongs to the sky.'
Silverfang studied Old Helm's calm face for a long moment, then stepped aside with a surprised laugh.
sentences.cn: 银牙沉默地看着老舵平静的脸庞，过了好久，突然笑着退到了一边。

unable:2.en: The lock on the crystal gate had no keyhole, no handle, no dial. We circled it three times. Bell tried her compass; Old Helm tried his voice. I was nearly *unable* to hide my worry when I noticed letters carved around the frame — letters that spelled a word we had collected two islands ago. I spoke it aloud, and the gate dissolved like morning mist.
unable:2.cnHint: 水晶门没有锁孔，大家几乎____找到开门方法，直到叙述者发现了刻在门框上的字母。
unable:2.hook: Where the gate had stood, a thousand stars now shone from below.
unable:2.line: 'I was *unable* to see it at first — but you found it,' Bell said warmly.

sentences.en: The lock on the crystal gate had no keyhole, no handle, no dial.
sentences.cn: 水晶门上的锁没有钥匙孔，没有把手，也没有转盘。

sentences.en: We circled it three times.
sentences.cn: 我们绕着它走了三圈。

sentences.en: Bell tried her compass; Old Helm tried his voice.
sentences.cn: 小铃试了她的指南针；老舵试了他的声音。

sentences.en: I was nearly *unable* to hide my worry when I noticed letters carved around the frame — letters that spelled a word we had collected two islands ago.
I spoke it aloud, and the gate dissolved like morning mist.
sentences.cn: 我大声说出了这个词，门像晨雾一样消散了。

unusual:2.en: The island was quiet in an *unusual* way — no wind, no bird calls, no rustling leaves. Old Helm pressed his boot against the ground and listened. Bell held up her lantern and turned slowly. Then we all felt it: the island itself was humming, deep and steady, like something alive beneath the stone, trying to tell us where to walk.
unusual:2.cnHint: 这座岛的寂静十分____，老舵手和贝尔察觉到了大地深处传来的嗡嗡声。
unusual:2.hook: The humming grew louder the closer we got to the island's centre.
unusual:2.line: 'It is *unusual* for an island to sing,' Old Helm said, 'but not impossible.'

sentences.en: The island was quiet in an *unusual* way — no wind, no bird calls, no rustling leaves.
Old Helm pressed his boot against the ground and listened.
sentences.cn: 老舵把靴子踩进地面，仔细听。

sentences.en: Bell held up her lantern and turned slowly.
sentences.cn: 小铃举起了她的灯笼，慢慢转身。

sentences.en: Then we all felt it: the island itself was humming, deep and steady, like something alive beneath the stone, trying to tell us where to walk.
sentences.cn: 然后我们都感受到了：这个岛屿本身在发出嗡嗡声，低沉而稳定，像是石头底下什么活的东西在试图告诉我们应该往哪儿走。

character:2.en: The old bottle had washed up on the shore of a cloud island, sealed with wax. Inside was a single folded note. Bell held it to the starlight and read the words carved in neat, small letters. 'Every island has a *character* of its own,' Old Helm said softly, 'and this one is written right here.'
character:2.cnHint: 小铃在一个云岛岸边发现了一个旧瓶子，里面的纸条揭示了这座岛的____。
character:2.hook: But the wax seal bore a mark none of us had ever seen before.
character:2.line: 'Every island has a *character* of its own,' said Old Helm, tracing the carved words.

sentences.en: The old bottle had washed up on the shore of a cloud island, sealed with wax.
sentences.cn: 那只古老的玻璃瓶冲上了云岛的海滩，瓶口用蜡封得严严实实。

sentences.en: Inside was a single folded note.
sentences.cn: 里面放着一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: Bell held it to the starlight and read the words carved in neat, small letters.
sentences.cn: 小铃把纸条凑到星光下，读着那些工整细小的刻字。

sentences.en: 'Every island has a *character* of its own,' Old Helm said softly, 'and this one is written right here.'

clean:2.en: We landed on an island of white stone, scrubbed smooth by years of wind. There was not a single leaf or shadow anywhere — only open sky and bright ground. Bell laughed and spread her arms wide. 'I have never felt such a *clean* place,' she said. Old Helm smiled and pressed a new word into the map.
clean:2.cnHint: 小铃登上了一座白石岛，感受到了前所未有的____与开阔。
clean:2.hook: Then we noticed the stone was not white — it was glowing from inside.
clean:2.line: 'I have never felt such a *clean* place,' Bell said, turning slowly in the open air.

sentences.en: We landed on an island of white stone, scrubbed smooth by years of wind.
sentences.cn: 我们降落在一座白石岛上，被多年的风吹得光滑如镜。

sentences.en: There was not a single leaf or shadow anywhere — only open sky and bright ground.
sentences.cn: 岛上没有一片叶子，没有一丝阴影——只有开阔的天空和耀眼的地面。

sentences.en: Bell laughed and spread her arms wide.
sentences.cn: 小铃笑着张开双臂。

sentences.en: 'I have never felt such a *clean* place,' she said.
Old Helm smiled and pressed a new word into the map.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑了笑，在地图上又刻下了一个新词。

convey:2.en: Tucked inside a hollow tree at the centre of the island was a small wooden box. Inside lay a painted tile with no words at all — only shapes and colours. Old Helm studied it for a long moment. 'Pictures can *convey* more than letters sometimes,' he said, and held it up so we could all see what it meant.
convey:2.cnHint: 老船长在空心树中找到一块无字瓷砖，说图案能____比文字更多的信息。
convey:2.hook: The shapes on the tile shifted the moment we stepped back into the wind.
convey:2.line: 'Pictures can *convey* more than letters sometimes,' Old Helm said quietly, holding the tile to the light.

sentences.en: Tucked inside a hollow tree at the centre of the island was a small wooden box.
sentences.cn: 岛中心的一棵空心树里藏着一个小木盒。

sentences.en: Inside lay a painted tile with no words at all — only shapes and colours.
sentences.cn: 盒子里放着一块彩绘的瓷砖，上面没有任何文字——只有形状和颜色。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied it for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 老舵盯着它看了很久。

sentences.en: 'Pictures can *convey* more than letters sometimes,' he said, and held it up so we could all see what it meant.

distraction:2.en: Silverfang was circling our island on his ship, calling out riddles to slow us down. Old Helm shook his head and kept walking toward the stone arch where the next word waited. 'A little noise is only a *distraction*,' he said calmly. We reached the arch first, and the word lit up under our hands.
distraction:2.cnHint: 银牙船长故意用谜语拖延我们，但老船长说那不过是一种____，带我们抢先找到了词语。
distraction:2.hook: Silverfang went quiet after that, which felt more worrying than his riddles had.
distraction:2.line: 'A little noise is only a *distraction*,' Old Helm said, eyes fixed on the stone arch ahead.

sentences.en: Silverfang was circling our island on his ship, calling out riddles to slow us down.
sentences.cn: 银牙驾着船在我们的岛周围绕圈，不断喊出谜题来拖延我们。

sentences.en: Old Helm shook his head and kept walking toward the stone arch where the next word waited.
sentences.cn: 老舵摇摇头，继续朝那座石拱门走去，下一个词就等在那里。

sentences.en: 'A little noise is only a *distraction*,' he said calmly.
We reached the arch first, and the word lit up under our hands.
sentences.cn: 我们先到达了拱门，那个词在我们手下亮了起来。

fight:2.en: The word was locked inside a rusted iron chest bolted to the cliffside. Every pull and push did nothing. Bell sat down, chin in her hands, and thought. Then she smiled. 'The chest does not want force — it wants a key. Save your *fight* for the things that actually push back.' She found the keyhole hidden in the rock.
fight:2.cnHint: 小铃劝大家别用蛮力对付铁箱，说要把____留给真正需要的地方，随后发现了隐藏的钥匙孔。
fight:2.hook: Inside the chest was not a word — it was a tiny compass, already spinning.
fight:2.line: 'Save your *fight* for the things that actually push back,' Bell said with a calm smile.

sentences.en: The word was locked inside a rusted iron chest bolted to the cliffside.
sentences.cn: 那个词被锁在一只锈迹斑斑的铁箱里，箱子被螺栓固定在悬崖边。

sentences.en: Every pull and push did nothing.
sentences.cn: 无论怎样拉扯推动都没有用。

sentences.en: Bell sat down, chin in her hands, and thought.
sentences.cn: 小铃坐下来，托着下巴思考。

sentences.en: Then she smiled.
sentences.cn: 然后她笑了。

sentences.en: 'The chest does not want force — it wants a key.
sentences.cn: 铁箱不需要蛮力——它需要一把钥匙。

sentences.en: Save your *fight* for the things that actually push back.'
She found the keyhole hidden in the rock.
sentences.cn: 她找到了隐藏在岩石里的钥匙孔。

finish:2.en: The map showed one last mark on this island — a carved pillar at the eastern edge. When we pressed the final word-stone into its slot at the top, soft light poured down all four sides. Old Helm stepped back and crossed his arms. 'A good *finish* always looks simple from the outside,' he said. The pillar opened and showed us the next sky.
finish:2.cnHint: 我们将最后一块词石嵌入石柱，老船长感叹好的____从外面看总是简单的，随后柱子打开了新的天际。
finish:2.hook: Beyond the pillar, a whole island we had never mapped was rising toward us.
finish:2.line: 'A good *finish* always looks simple from the outside,' Old Helm said, stepping back to see the whole pillar glow.

sentences.en: The map showed one last mark on this island — a carved pillar at the eastern edge.
sentences.cn: 地图在这座岛的最后标了一处——东边边缘有一根雕刻的石柱。

sentences.en: When we pressed the final word-stone into its slot at the top, soft light poured down all four sides.
sentences.cn: 当我们把最后的词石插进顶部的卡槽时，柔和的光芒从四面八方倾泻而下。

sentences.en: Old Helm stepped back and crossed his arms.
sentences.cn: 老舵往后退了一步，抱起了双臂。

sentences.en: 'A good *finish* always looks simple from the outside,' he said.
The pillar opened and showed us the next sky.
sentences.cn: 石柱打开了，为我们展现了下一片天空。

frequently:2.en: Bell kept a small notebook where she recorded every word we found and where. I noticed she flipped back to certain pages more often than others. 'Some words come up *frequently* in the old carvings,' she explained. 'Those are the ones that point to the next island.' She tapped a page, and the air around us shifted like the world agreed.
frequently:2.cnHint: 小铃解释说某些词在古老雕刻中____出现，正是这些词指引着下一座岛屿的方向。
frequently:2.hook: The word she tapped began to glow faintly through the paper itself.
frequently:2.line: 'Some words come up *frequently* in the old carvings,' Bell said, tapping her notebook with two fingers.

sentences.en: Bell kept a small notebook where she recorded every word we found and where.
sentences.cn: 小铃用一本小笔记本记录我们找到的每一个词和它们的位置。

sentences.en: I noticed she flipped back to certain pages more often than others.
sentences.cn: 我注意到她经常翻回某些特定的页面。

sentences.en: 'Some words come up *frequently* in the old carvings,' she explained.
'Those are the ones that point to the next island.'
sentences.cn: 那些词指向下一座岛。

sentences.en: She tapped a page, and the air around us shifted like the world agreed.
sentences.cn: 她点了点那一页，我们周围的空气就像整个世界都在认可一样开始扭动。

invest:2.en: The island had a fountain at its heart, dry for many years. Old Helm reached into his coat and placed three small word-stones into the basin. 'You have to *invest* something to wake a sleeping place,' he said quietly. Water rose at once, carrying with it a folded cloth map that had been waiting at the bottom for a long time.
invest:2.cnHint: 老船长将三块词石放入干涸的喷泉，说唤醒沉睡之地需要____些什么，清水随即涌出并带出了一张地图。
invest:2.hook: The map was dated, and the date was exactly the day Old Helm was born.
invest:2.line: 'You have to *invest* something to wake a sleeping place,' Old Helm said, setting the stones gently into the basin.

sentences.en: The island had a fountain at its heart, dry for many years.
sentences.cn: 岛的中心有一座喷泉，已经干涸多年了。

sentences.en: Old Helm reached into his coat and placed three small word-stones into the basin.
sentences.cn: 老舵从外套里掏出三块小石片，放进了水池里。

sentences.en: 'You have to *invest* something to wake a sleeping place,' he said quietly.
Water rose at once, carrying with it a folded cloth map that had been waiting at the bottom for a long time.
sentences.cn: 水立刻涌了上来，带出了一张折叠的布质地图，那是在池底等待了很久的东西。

moment:2.en: The old bottle had been sealed for what felt like forever. When Bell finally pulled the cork, a single folded paper fell out. Old Helm held it under the lantern light, reading slowly. 'This is the *moment* we have been waiting for,' he said softly. The paper showed a path to an island none of us had ever seen.
moment:2.cnHint: 小铃打开一个封存已久的瓶子，里面的纸条让老船长说出了意味深长的话，那个____终于到来了。
moment:2.hook: The path on the paper led straight into a cloud no star could light.
moment:2.line: 'This is the *moment* we have been waiting for,' Old Helm said, his voice barely a whisper.

sentences.en: The old bottle had been sealed for what felt like forever.
sentences.cn: 那只古老的玻璃瓶被密封了似乎永远那么长的时间。

sentences.en: When Bell finally pulled the cork, a single folded paper fell out.
sentences.cn: 当小铃终于拔出软木塞时，一张折叠的纸从里面掉了出来。

sentences.en: Old Helm held it under the lantern light, reading slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵把纸放在灯光下，缓缓读着。

sentences.en: 'This is the *moment* we have been waiting for,' he said softly.
The paper showed a path to an island none of us had ever seen.
sentences.cn: 那张纸显示了通往一座我们从未见过的岛屿的路径。

nice:2.en: The measuring tools Bell laid out were not simple things. Each one had been carved with *nice* attention to detail — every mark exactly one hair apart, every edge perfectly flat. Old Helm said such careful work was the only reason our maps never sent us the wrong way. I ran my finger along one ruler and felt nothing but smooth, even lines.
nice:2.cnHint: 小铃展示了她那些刻度极其____、做工精密的测量工具，老船长说正是这份精密让地图从不出错。
nice:2.hook: But the finest ruler in the set was missing its last mark.
nice:2.line: 'Only *nice* work like this keeps us from flying off the edge,' Bell said, holding the tool to the light.

sentences.en: The measuring tools Bell laid out were not simple things.
sentences.cn: 小铃铺开的测量工具不是什么简单的东西。

sentences.en: Each one had been carved with *nice* attention to detail — every mark exactly one hair apart, every edge perfectly flat.
Old Helm said such careful work was the only reason our maps never sent us the wrong way.
sentences.cn: 老舵说正是这样的细致工作才让我们的地图从不指错方向。

sentences.en: I ran my finger along one ruler and felt nothing but smooth, even lines.
sentences.cn: 我用手指沿着一把尺子摸过，感受到的只有光滑均匀的线条。

peer:2.en: The message jar had been wedged into a crack in the island's stone wall for a long time. I had to *peer* into the narrow gap, pressing my cheek against the cold rock, before I could read the faded words inside. Old Helm stood behind me, quiet and patient. 'What does it say?' he asked. I read aloud: a name, a date, and a single new word.
peer:2.cnHint: 叙述者费力地____进石缝，才勉强看清了藏在里面的古老信息。
peer:2.hook: The date on the message was fifty years before Old Helm was born.
peer:2.line: 'You have to *peer* right in — the words are too faint to read from outside,' I told Old Helm.

sentences.en: The message jar had been wedged into a crack in the island's stone wall for a long time.
sentences.cn: 信息罐子已经卡在岛屿石墙的裂缝里很久了。

sentences.en: I had to *peer* into the narrow gap, pressing my cheek against the cold rock, before I could read the faded words inside.
Old Helm stood behind me, quiet and patient.
sentences.cn: 老舵站在我身后，安静而耐心。

sentences.en: 'What does it say?' he asked.
sentences.cn: 他问道，上面写的是什么？

sentences.en: I read aloud: a name, a date, and a single new word.
sentences.cn: 我大声读出来：一个名字，一个日期，还有一个新词。

pretty:2.en: Silverfang dropped a small cloth bag onto the map table. Out rolled half a dozen polished stones, each one a different colour. 'Trade goods,' he said, but Old Helm picked one up and turned it slowly. It was a *pretty*, a carved charm shaped like a flying fish, smooth and warm in the palm. Hidden under its tail was a tiny word — our next destination.
pretty:2.cnHint: 银牙带来的小饰品里藏着一个____小巧迷人的飞鱼挂件，而它的尾巴下藏着下一个目的地的线索。
pretty:2.hook: No one could explain how the word had been carved so deep without cracking the stone.
pretty:2.line: 'That one is no ordinary stone — that one is a *pretty* someone hid a secret inside,' Old Helm said quietly.

sentences.en: Silverfang dropped a small cloth bag onto the map table.
sentences.cn: 银牙把一个小布袋扔到地图桌上。

sentences.en: Out rolled half a dozen polished stones, each one a different colour.
sentences.cn: 里面滚出来半打打磨光滑的石头，每一块颜色都不同。

sentences.en: 'Trade goods,' he said, but Old Helm picked one up and turned it slowly.
sentences.cn: 他说这是贸易商品，但老舵拿起其中一块，慢慢转动着。

sentences.en: It was a *pretty*, a carved charm shaped like a flying fish, smooth and warm in the palm.
Hidden under its tail was a tiny word — our next destination.
sentences.cn: 石头尾巴底下隐藏着一个小小的词——我们的下一个目的地。

recommendation:2.en: Tucked inside the hollow post at the island's edge was a folded note. It was addressed to no one, but the handwriting matched the style Old Helm had taught me. The note was a *recommendation*: it named our troupe by description and urged whoever found it to share their star charts with us freely. Someone, somewhere, had spoken well of us before we even arrived.
recommendation:2.cnHint: 一张藏在木柱里的纸条是对我们小队的____，有人在我们到来之前就已经为我们说好话了。
recommendation:2.hook: The ink was still fresh, though no ship had docked here in weeks.
recommendation:2.line: 'A *recommendation* from a stranger — that is the best kind,' Old Helm said, folding the note with care.

sentences.en: Tucked inside the hollow post at the island's edge was a folded note.
sentences.cn: 岛屿边缘那个空心木柱里塞着一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: It was addressed to no one, but the handwriting matched the style Old Helm had taught me.
sentences.cn: 纸条没有收件人，但笔迹风格和老舵教我的一模一样。

sentences.en: The note was a *recommendation*: it named our troupe by description and urged whoever found it to share their star charts with us freely.
Someone, somewhere, had spoken well of us before we even arrived.
sentences.cn: 不知哪个什么地方的人已经在我们到来之前替我们说过好话。

strange:2.en: The object on the stone shelf was *strange* to all of us — a small box covered in marks that looked like letters but followed no pattern any of us knew. Bell turned it over twice. Old Helm pressed one side and it opened with a soft click. Inside was a folded strip of paper with a single word written in plain, clear script, as if the box had been waiting to give it to us all along.
strange:2.cnHint: 石架上有一个____的盒子，没人认识上面的符号，但老船长一按，它就打开了，里面是一个清晰的词。
strange:2.hook: The word inside was one Old Helm claimed he had forgotten years ago.
strange:2.line: '*Strange* as it looks, I think this box was made for us to find,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The object on the stone shelf was *strange* to all of us — a small box covered in marks that looked like letters but followed no pattern any of us knew.
Bell turned it over twice.
sentences.cn: 小铃翻过那只盒子两次。

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed one side and it opened with a soft click.
sentences.cn: 老舵按了一下某个面，盒子轻轻咔嗒一声打开了。

sentences.en: Inside was a folded strip of paper with a single word written in plain, clear script, as if the box had been waiting to give it to us all along.
sentences.cn: 里面是一张折叠的纸条，上面用清楚利落的字体写着一个字，仿佛这只盒子从一开始就在等着把它交给我们。

widespread:2.en: Bell unrolled the oldest chart in the trunk, and we all leaned in. Across the whole surface, a single symbol repeated itself — *widespread* across every island, every sea lane, every blank corner. Old Helm had seen it once before, on a wall deep inside a cave. 'It is a greeting,' he said. 'Whoever made these maps wanted every traveller to feel welcome.'
widespread:2.cnHint: 古老海图上一个符号____地分布在每一个角落，老船长说那是地图绘制者留给所有旅人的问候。
widespread:2.hook: The symbol appeared on the back of Bell's compass too, and she had never noticed.
widespread:2.line: 'Look how *widespread* it is — not one island on this chart without that mark,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Bell unrolled the oldest chart in the trunk, and we all leaned in.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开了箱子里最古老的星图，我们都探过身去。

sentences.en: Across the whole surface, a single symbol repeated itself — *widespread* across every island, every sea lane, every blank corner.
Old Helm had seen it once before, on a wall deep inside a cave.
sentences.cn: 老舵曾在一个很深的洞穴墙上见过它。

sentences.en: 'It is a greeting,' he said.
sentences.cn: "那是个问候，"他说。

sentences.en: 'Whoever made these maps wanted every traveller to feel welcome.'
sentences.cn: "谁绘制这些地图的人想让每个旅人都感到受欢迎。"

wonderful:2.en: The sealed jar had sat at the centre of the island for longer than any of us had been alive. When Old Helm finally lifted the lid, a warm smell rose out — something like pine and something like rain. Inside lay a short letter and a pressed flower. 'It is *wonderful*,' I said, not meaning the flower but the whole idea: that someone had left a small, careful gift for strangers not yet born.
wonderful:2.cnHint: 一个封存多年的罐子里装着信和压花，叙述者觉得有人为素未谋面的陌生人留下礼物这件事真是____。
wonderful:2.hook: The letter named an island that appeared on no chart we carried.
wonderful:2.line: 'It is *wonderful* that a stranger thought of us so far ahead,' I said, and Old Helm smiled.

sentences.en: The sealed jar had sat at the centre of the island for longer than any of us had been alive.
sentences.cn: 那只密封的罐子已经放在岛屿中心很久了——比我们任何人活过的岁月都长。

sentences.en: When Old Helm finally lifted the lid, a warm smell rose out — something like pine and something like rain.
sentences.cn: 当老舵终于打开罐子盖时，一股温暖的气味飘了出来——有点像松木，也有点像雨。

sentences.en: Inside lay a short letter and a pressed flower.
sentences.cn: 里面放着一封短信和一朵压干的花。

sentences.en: 'It is *wonderful*,' I said, not meaning the flower but the whole idea: that someone had left a small, careful gift for strangers not yet born.

announce:2.en: Deep in the chart-room, Old Helm unrolled a glowing scroll across the table. 'Listen up,' he said, and *announced* that the final island — the one at the edge of every map — had just appeared on our compass. The whole troupe went silent, breath held, eyes wide.
announce:2.cnHint: 老舵主在图室里____了一个令全团屏息的消息。
announce:2.hook: The compass needle spun once, then pointed somewhere none of us dared name.
announce:2.line: 'I *announce* it now: the last island is real, and it is waiting.'

sentences.en: Deep in the chart-room, Old Helm unrolled a glowing scroll across the table.
sentences.cn: 在深处的地图室里，老舵在桌上铺开了一卷发光的纸卷。

sentences.en: 'Listen up,' he said, and *announced* that the final island — the one at the edge of every map — had just appeared on our compass.
The whole troupe went silent, breath held, eyes wide.
sentences.cn: 整个剧团都安静了下来，屏住呼吸，睁大眼睛。

appropriate:2.en: Bell set down three sky-lanterns on the deck and studied each one carefully. Only the blue lantern, she decided, was *appropriate* for sending a signal through the dense star-fog ahead. She lit it with steady hands, and its light cut a clean path into the dark.
appropriate:2.cnHint: 领航员贝尔挑选了一盏____的天灯，点燃它向星雾深处传递信号。
appropriate:2.hook: Something in the fog answered with a light of its own.
appropriate:2.line: 'Only this one is *appropriate* — the others will mislead us entirely.'

sentences.en: Bell set down three sky-lanterns on the deck and studied each one carefully.
sentences.cn: 小铃在甲板上放下三盏天灯，仔细研究了每一盏。

sentences.en: Only the blue lantern, she decided, was *appropriate* for sending a signal through the dense star-fog ahead.
She lit it with steady hands, and its light cut a clean path into the dark.
sentences.cn: 她用稳定的手点燃了它，光线在黑暗中切出了一条清晰的路。

chief:2.en: Silverfang's ship pulled alongside ours just as the island came into view. He stepped onto the rail, grinning. His *chief* reason for following us all this way, he admitted at last, was not rivalry — it was the single word carved on his own tattered map that matched ours exactly.
chief:2.cnHint: 竞争船长银牙透露了他一路跟随我们的____原因，令人意外。
chief:2.hook: He held out his map fragment, and the two pieces trembled toward each other like magnets.
chief:2.line: 'My *chief* reason for being here? That word on your map — I have half of it.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's ship pulled alongside ours just as the island came into view.
sentences.cn: 银牙的船正好在岛屿映入眼帘时靠上了我们的船。

sentences.en: He stepped onto the rail, grinning.
sentences.cn: 他踩上栏杆，咧嘴笑着。

sentences.en: His *chief* reason for following us all this way, he admitted at last, was not rivalry — it was the single word carved on his own tattered map that matched ours exactly.

clearly:2.en: The stone archway at the island's entrance was covered in carved letters, but most were worn away by wind and rain. One word, however, stood out *clearly* above all the rest, glowing faintly gold in the starlight. Bell traced it with one finger and whispered its sound aloud.
clearly:2.cnHint: 石拱门上大多数字迹已模糊，只有一个词____地发着金光。
clearly:2.hook: The moment she spoke it, the archway began to open.
clearly:2.line: 'Look — this word shines *clearly* while everything around it has faded to nothing.'

sentences.en: The stone archway at the island's entrance was covered in carved letters, but most were worn away by wind and rain.
sentences.cn: 岛屿入口的石拱上刻满了字母，但大多被风雨磨蚀掉了。

sentences.en: One word, however, stood out *clearly* above all the rest, glowing faintly gold in the starlight.
Bell traced it with one finger and whispered its sound aloud.
sentences.cn: 小铃用一根手指描过那个字，轻轻地把它的发音说了出来。

communicate:2.en: Old Helm pressed his palm against a flat stone panel near the archway. Symbols rose across its surface, shifting and rearranging. 'The island is trying to *communicate*,' he murmured, leaning close. Each symbol matched a word our troupe had collected, as if the place had been waiting for exactly us.
communicate:2.cnHint: 石板上升起的符文似乎是小岛在试图____，而它使用的正是我们收集过的词。
communicate:2.hook: The last symbol pulsed, and below it a doorway appeared where there had been solid rock.
communicate:2.line: 'These symbols *communicate* one clear message: we were expected here all along.'

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed his palm against a flat stone panel near the archway.
sentences.cn: 老舵把手掌按在拱门旁边的一块平整的石板上。

sentences.en: Symbols rose across its surface, shifting and rearranging.
sentences.cn: 符号浮现在石板表面，不断地移动和重新排列。

sentences.en: 'The island is trying to *communicate*,' he murmured, leaning close.
Each symbol matched a word our troupe had collected, as if the place had been waiting for exactly us.
sentences.cn: 每一个符号都和我们剧团收集的一个字相吻合，好像这个地方一直在等着我们这样的人。

emphasis:2.en: Bell read the inscription above the door twice, then a third time, her voice growing slower. She placed *emphasis* on the final syllable each time, as if the word itself needed weight to become real. On her fourth reading, a soft chime rang out from somewhere deep inside the island.
emphasis:2.cnHint: 贝尔反复朗读门上的铭文，每次都在最后一个音节上加以____，直到岛内传来回响。
emphasis:2.hook: The chime faded, and in the silence we heard footsteps — coming toward us from inside.
emphasis:2.line: 'The *emphasis* belongs on the last word — say it like you mean it.'

sentences.en: Bell read the inscription above the door twice, then a third time, her voice growing slower.
sentences.cn: 小铃把拱门上方的铭文读了两遍，然后又读了第三遍，她的声音越来越缓慢。

sentences.en: She placed *emphasis* on the final syllable each time, as if the word itself needed weight to become real.
On her fourth reading, a soft chime rang out from somewhere deep inside the island.
sentences.cn: 在她第四遍诵读时，一阵轻轻的铃声从岛屿深处的某个地方响了出来。

emphasize:2.en: Old Helm drew a circle around the glowing word on his scroll and looked at each of us in turn. 'I want to *emphasize* this,' he said quietly. 'Once we carry this word through that door, there is no retracing our route. The map behind us will go dark.' No one moved for a long moment.
emphasize:2.cnHint: 老舵主用手指圈出那个词，郑重地____这一步无法回头。
emphasize:2.hook: Bell was the first to step forward, her lantern raised, her face calm and certain.
emphasize:2.line: 'I *emphasize* this once: beyond that door, the old map ends forever.'

sentences.en: Old Helm drew a circle around the glowing word on his scroll and looked at each of us in turn.
sentences.cn: 老舵在他的纸卷上圈出那个发光的字，然后依次看了我们每一个人。

sentences.en: 'I want to *emphasize* this,' he said quietly.
'Once we carry this word through that door, there is no retracing our route.
sentences.cn: "一旦我们拿着这个字穿过那扇门，就没有回头路了。

sentences.en: The map behind us will go dark.'
sentences.cn: 我们身后的地图会暗下去。"

sentences.en: No one moved for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 没人动，沉默了好久。

england:2.en: Inside a dusty chest near the archway, Bell found a faded letter sealed with wax. It was written by a navigator who had left *England* long ago, crossing sea after sea in search of islands that 'exist only where words are believed.' She read the last line aloud, and her voice caught.
england:2.cnHint: 贝尔在一封信中读到，这位航海家从____出发，毕生寻找只有相信文字才能抵达的岛屿。
england:2.hook: At the bottom of the letter, in fresh ink, was a name — Bell's own.
england:2.line: 'She left *England* with nothing but a list of words and the courage to trust them.'

sentences.en: Inside a dusty chest near the archway, Bell found a faded letter sealed with wax.
sentences.cn: 在拱门附近的一只尘封的箱子里，小铃找到了一封褪色的信，用蜡封着。

sentences.en: It was written by a navigator who had left *England* long ago, crossing sea after sea in search of islands that 'exist only where words are believed.'
She read the last line aloud, and her voice caught.
sentences.cn: 她把最后一行读了出来，声音哽咽了。

immediately:2.en: On the eastern ledge of Drift Isle, Bell found a rolled map tucked inside a hollow lantern. She opened it, and *immediately* the painted lines began to glow, tracing a path toward an island none of us had seen before. The air tasted like rain and distant bells.
immediately:2.cnHint: 小铃在悬崖边的灯笼里发现了一张地图，____亮了起来，指向未知的岛屿。
immediately:2.hook: The glowing path stopped exactly where our charts went blank.
immediately:2.line: '*Immediately* after I touched it, the map came alive,' Bell whispered.

sentences.en: On the eastern ledge of Drift Isle, Bell found a rolled map tucked inside a hollow lantern.
sentences.cn: 小铃在漂流岛的东边悬崖上，从一盏空心灯笼里找到了一卷地图。

sentences.en: She opened it, and *immediately* the painted lines began to glow, tracing a path toward an island none of us had seen before.
The air tasted like rain and distant bells.
sentences.cn: 空气里弥漫着雨水和远处铃声的味道。

improvement:2.en: Old Helm spread the newest chart across the navigation table and tapped a line with one thick finger. 'This is a real *improvement*,' he said softly. The old route had taken three days; the revised path curved through a warm wind channel and would take one. We studied it in quiet awe.
improvement:2.cnHint: 老船长看着新航线图，称赞这次的____让我们节省了大量时间。
improvement:2.hook: No one asked who had left the revised chart on our table.
improvement:2.line: 'An *improvement* this clear means someone wanted us to find it,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the newest chart across the navigation table and tapped a line with one thick finger.
sentences.cn: 老舵把最新的海图铺在导航台上，用粗壮的手指敲了敲其中一条线。

sentences.en: 'This is a real *improvement*,' he said softly.
The old route had taken three days; the revised path curved through a warm wind channel and would take one.
sentences.cn: 老路线要走三天，修改后的路线绕过一条温风通道，只需要一天。

sentences.en: We studied it in quiet awe.
sentences.cn: 我们安静地盯着它，满是敬畏。

afternoon:2.en: We drifted above the Cloud Shelf through the long *afternoon*, watching light turn from white to gold across the stone towers below. Bell marked each tower on her chart as a new word-fragment. By the time the stars appeared, she had collected seven, and the map had grown a new edge.
afternoon:2.cnHint: 整个____，小铃一直在记录云层上方的石塔，地图因此延伸出了新的边缘。
afternoon:2.hook: The seventh tower lit up before Bell even touched her pen to it.
afternoon:2.line: 'This *afternoon* alone gave us more map than the whole last week,' Bell said.

sentences.en: We drifted above the Cloud Shelf through the long *afternoon*, watching light turn from white to gold across the stone towers below.
Bell marked each tower on her chart as a new word-fragment.
sentences.cn: 小铃把每座塔楼都标注在她的图表上，当作一个新的字片段。

sentences.en: By the time the stars appeared, she had collected seven, and the map had grown a new edge.
sentences.cn: 到星星出现的时候，她已经收集了七个，地图也长出了新的边界。

expand:2.en: Old Helm pressed the word-fragment against the centre of our master map. The parchment shivered, and we watched it *expand* outward in slow ripples, like a stone dropped in still water. New coastlines appeared at the edges. I could hear the rest of the troupe hold their breath as one.
expand:2.cnHint: 老船长将词片段贴上地图，地图开始____，露出了从未见过的海岸线。
expand:2.hook: At the very new edge, something small and dark was already moving.
expand:2.line: 'Watch it *expand*—every new word makes our world a little larger,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed the word-fragment against the centre of our master map.
sentences.cn: 老舵把字片段按在我们主地图的中央。

sentences.en: The parchment shivered, and we watched it *expand* outward in slow ripples, like a stone dropped in still water.
New coastlines appeared at the edges.
sentences.cn: 新的海岸线在边缘浮现。

sentences.en: I could hear the rest of the troupe hold their breath as one.
sentences.cn: 我能感觉到整个剧团的人都屏住了呼吸。

regardless:2.en: Silverfang stood at the prow of her rival ship, close enough to shout across. She held up a word-fragment we had lost in the last storm. '*Regardless* of what happened between us before,' she called, 'you need this more than I do.' Then she tossed it across the gap without waiting for thanks.
regardless:2.cnHint: 竞争船长____过去的恩怨，把我们遗失的词片段扔了过来。
regardless:2.hook: The fragment landed in my hands, still warm from her grip.
regardless:2.line: '*Regardless* of our rivalry, the map belongs to all of us,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Silverfang stood at the prow of her rival ship, close enough to shout across.
sentences.cn: 银牙站在她那艘对立船的船首，离得近到可以喊话。

sentences.en: She held up a word-fragment we had lost in the last storm. '*Regardless* of what happened between us before,' she called, 'you need this more than I do.'
Then she tossed it across the gap without waiting for thanks.
sentences.cn: 然后她把它扔过空隙，没等道谢就转身了。

rid:2.en: The old warning sign on Fog Arch Island read: find the hidden word and *rid* this place of its endless mist. Bell located the stone tile, pressed it firmly, and spoke the word aloud. The fog peeled back in long quiet sheets, and a whole harbour appeared, waiting and still.
rid:2.cnHint: 小铃找到了隐藏的词语，念出它，终于让这座岛____了笼罩已久的迷雾。
rid:2.hook: The harbour held three ships—all flying flags we did not recognise.
rid:2.line: 'Say the word and *rid* this island of fog forever,' Bell read from the tile.

sentences.en: The old warning sign on Fog Arch Island read: find the hidden word and *rid* this place of its endless mist.
Bell located the stone tile, pressed it firmly, and spoke the word aloud.
sentences.cn: 小铃找到了那块石瓷砖，用力按下去，大声念出了那个字。

sentences.en: The fog peeled back in long quiet sheets, and a whole harbour appeared, waiting and still.
sentences.cn: 雾气无声地一层层往后退，一整个港口露了出来，静静地等待着我们。

dog:2.en: A small *dog* with silver-tipped ears was sitting on the dock of Pinwheel Isle when we arrived. It had a rolled note tied to its collar and refused to move until Bell knelt and took it gently. The note contained a single word-fragment drawn in careful ink: our next destination.
dog:2.cnHint: 到达风车岛时，一只____静静地等着我们，它的项圈上绑着指引下一站的词片段。
dog:2.hook: The dog vanished the moment Bell read the last letter aloud.
dog:2.line: 'That *dog* has been waiting for us,' Old Helm said, kneeling beside it.

sentences.en: A small *dog* with silver-tipped ears was sitting on the dock of Pinwheel Isle when we arrived.
It had a rolled note tied to its collar and refused to move until Bell knelt and took it gently.
sentences.cn: 小铃跪下身子，轻轻地从它脖子上取下那张纸条。

sentences.en: The note contained a single word-fragment drawn in careful ink: our next destination.
sentences.cn: 纸条上用笔墨工整地画了一个字片段：我们下一个要去的地方。

busy:2.en: The market island of Lantern Cross was *busy* even before sunrise—traders calling out, pulley baskets swinging between platforms, lamps swaying overhead. In all that noise, Bell spotted a single still figure holding a word-fragment out in an open palm, patient as stone, waiting for only us to notice.
busy:2.cnHint: 热闹____的集市上，小铃在人群中发现了一个安静地托着词片段等待我们的神秘人。
busy:2.hook: When I blinked, the figure was gone, but the fragment remained.
busy:2.line: 'Stay close—it is too *busy* here to lose each other,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The market island of Lantern Cross was *busy* even before sunrise—traders calling out, pulley baskets swinging between platforms, lamps swaying overhead.
In all that noise, Bell spotted a single still figure holding a word-fragment out in an open palm, patient as stone, waiting for only us to notice.
sentences.cn: 在所有这些噪声里，小铃发现了一个静止的身影，掌心摊开着一个字片段，像石头一样有耐心，只在等我们发现。

extreme:2.en: The message was carved into a stone at the very edge of the island, where the wind was so strong it nearly pulled me off my feet. Old Helm read it aloud: the next map fragment lay across a gap of *extreme* distance, far wider than any we had crossed before. Bell measured it twice and nodded slowly.
extreme:2.cnHint: 石头上的信息显示，下一块地图碎片在____远的地方，老舵手大声读了出来。
extreme:2.hook: Bell folded her measuring rope and stared at the empty sky.
extreme:2.line: 'The *extreme* cold up there will test every one of us,' Old Helm warned.

sentences.en: The message was carved into a stone at the very edge of the island, where the wind was so strong it nearly pulled me off my feet.
sentences.cn: 信息刻在岛屿最边缘的一块石头上，风大得几乎要把我吹下去。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it aloud: the next map fragment lay across a gap of *extreme* distance, far wider than any we had crossed before.
Bell measured it twice and nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 小铃量了两遍，慢慢地点了点头。

style:2.en: Tucked inside a hollow tree near the island's centre, we found a small book. Its pages were covered in drawings of clouds, each one labelled in a looping, careful hand. Old Helm smiled and said the *style* of writing matched that of a map-maker the troupe had followed years ago, long before I joined.
style:2.cnHint: 我们在树洞里发现了一本小书，老舵手认出了书中那种____的字迹。
style:2.hook: The last page held a single arrow pointing east, toward open sky.
style:2.line: 'I know this *style* — she always drew her letters like little waves,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Tucked inside a hollow tree near the island's centre, we found a small book.
sentences.cn: 在岛屿中心附近的一棵空心树里，我们找到了一本小书。

sentences.en: Its pages were covered in drawings of clouds, each one labelled in a looping, careful hand.
sentences.cn: 书的每一页都画满了云朵，每一朵都用圆润工整的笔迹标上了名字。

sentences.en: Old Helm smiled and said the *style* of writing matched that of a map-maker the troupe had followed years ago, long before I joined.

color:2.en: Bell spread the recovered fragment on the deck and we all leaned in. The ink had faded, but one detail stayed clear: a patch of vivid *color*, deep blue ringed with gold, marking what looked like a hidden harbour below the clouds. Old Helm traced it gently with one finger and let out a soft whistle.
color:2.cnHint: 贝尔展开地图碎片，上面有一块独特的____标记着隐藏的港口。
color:2.hook: Somewhere below the clouds, that harbour was waiting for us.
color:2.line: 'That *color* only appears on maps drawn by the eldest island keepers,' Bell said quietly.

sentences.en: Bell spread the recovered fragment on the deck and we all leaned in.
sentences.cn: 小铃把找到的片段铺在甲板上，我们都凑了上去。

sentences.en: The ink had faded, but one detail stayed clear: a patch of vivid *color*, deep blue ringed with gold, marking what looked like a hidden harbour below the clouds.
Old Helm traced it gently with one finger and let out a soft whistle.
sentences.cn: 老舵用一根手指轻轻地描过那个地方，发出了一声柔和的口哨声。

meeting:2.en: The fragment we found was not a map at all — it was a record of a *meeting* between two troupe leaders, held on this very island sixty years ago. They had agreed to leave a shared trail of words through the sky for anyone brave enough to follow. Old Helm read it without a word and then folded it close to his chest.
meeting:2.cnHint: 碎片记录的是六十年前两位船队领袖在这座岛上的一次____。
meeting:2.hook: Old Helm's eyes held a story he had not yet told us.
meeting:2.line: 'That *meeting* changed the course of every troupe that came after,' Old Helm said softly.

sentences.en: The fragment we found was not a map at all — it was a record of a *meeting* between two troupe leaders, held on this very island sixty years ago.
They had agreed to leave a shared trail of words through the sky for anyone brave enough to follow.
sentences.cn: 他们约定在天空中留下一条用字编织的共同路线，给任何勇敢的追随者。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it without a word and then folded it close to his chest.
sentences.cn: 老舵默默地读完，然后把它紧紧地贴在胸口。

volunteer:2.en: The rope bridge to the next island had broken in the night. Someone needed to swim a guide-line across the narrow but rushing channel below. Before Old Helm could speak, I stepped forward as the *volunteer*, surprising even myself. Silverfang raised an eyebrow, then handed me the rope without argument.
volunteer:2.cnHint: 绳桥断了，叙述者主动站出来当____，令船长们都感到意外。
volunteer:2.hook: The water below was fast, cold, and full of unknowns.
volunteer:2.line: 'A *volunteer* with no fear of cold water — I respect that,' Silverfang said with a grin.

sentences.en: The rope bridge to the next island had broken in the night.
sentences.cn: 夜里绳桥断了。

sentences.en: Someone needed to swim a guide-line across the narrow but rushing channel below.
sentences.cn: 得有人游过下面湍急的海峡，拉一根导绳到对岛去。

sentences.en: Before Old Helm could speak, I stepped forward as the *volunteer*, surprising even myself.
Silverfang raised an eyebrow, then handed me the rope without argument.
sentences.cn: 银牙扬了扬眉毛，二话不说就把绳子递给了我。

deliver:2.en: A paper bird landed on the bow railing just before dawn. Silverfang unfolded it carefully and read the single line inside: a fellow captain had kept her promise to *deliver* the last missing fragment to whoever reached this island first. It was tucked under the bird's wing, wrapped in wax cloth to keep it dry.
deliver:2.cnHint: 一只纸鸟在黎明前降落，带来了另一位船长承诺____的最后一块地图碎片。
deliver:2.hook: The wax cloth was still warm, as if the bird had only just left her hand.
deliver:2.line: 'She said she would *deliver* it on time, and she never breaks her word,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: A paper bird landed on the bow railing just before dawn.
sentences.cn: 天快亮的时候，一只纸鸟落在了船头栏杆上。

sentences.en: Silverfang unfolded it carefully and read the single line inside: a fellow captain had kept her promise to *deliver* the last missing fragment to whoever reached this island first.
It was tucked under the bird's wing, wrapped in wax cloth to keep it dry.
sentences.cn: 它夹在鸟翅膀下面，用蜡布裹着，好保持干燥。

engineering:2.en: The bridge connecting the two halves of the island was a wonder. Bell walked its length twice, studying every joint and beam with wide eyes. She said the *engineering* was unlike anything she had seen — each part fitted so perfectly that no nail had been needed, only wood and careful thought. A new word glowed at the centre of the bridge.
engineering:2.cnHint: 贝尔仔细研究这座桥，称赞其____精妙，桥的中央发光处藏着一个新词语。
engineering:2.hook: The word at the centre pulsed once, then lit the path beyond.
engineering:2.line: 'This *engineering* could hold ten ships — whoever built it knew exactly what they were doing,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The bridge connecting the two halves of the island was a wonder.
sentences.cn: 连接岛屿两半的桥是个奇迹。

sentences.en: Bell walked its length twice, studying every joint and beam with wide eyes.
sentences.cn: 小铃沿着桥走了两遍，用睁圆的眼睛研究着每个接头和横梁。

sentences.en: She said the *engineering* was unlike anything she had seen — each part fitted so perfectly that no nail had been needed, only wood and careful thought.
A new word glowed at the centre of the bridge.
sentences.cn: 桥的中央闪现出一个新的词。

tiny:2.en: Old Helm held the fragment up to the starlight and laughed quietly. In the corner, almost invisible, was a *tiny* arrow no bigger than my thumbnail, pointing to an island that appeared on none of our other pieces. Bell circled it in chalk. Silverfang leaned over and said that small signs often led to the greatest places.
tiny:2.cnHint: 老舵手发现碎片角落有一个____的箭头，指向一座从未出现过的岛屿。
tiny:2.hook: That little arrow pointed somewhere none of us had ever been.
tiny:2.line: 'A *tiny* mark like that is never an accident — someone wanted it found,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm held the fragment up to the starlight and laughed quietly.
sentences.cn: 老舵把碎片举到星光下，轻声笑了。

sentences.en: In the corner, almost invisible, was a *tiny* arrow no bigger than my thumbnail, pointing to an island that appeared on none of our other pieces.
Bell circled it in chalk.
sentences.cn: 小铃用粉笔圈了一下。

sentences.en: Silverfang leaned over and said that small signs often led to the greatest places.
sentences.cn: 银牙俯身说，细微的记号往往通往最伟大的地方。

intelligence:2.en: The old stone door would not open until we answered its riddle. Old Helm studied the carvings for a long moment. 'This door does not test strength,' he said quietly. 'It tests *intelligence*.' He traced one symbol, whispered an answer, and the door swung wide into a garden of floating lanterns.
intelligence:2.cnHint: 石门出了一道谜题，老舵主凭借____找到了答案，门后是漂浮灯笼的花园。
intelligence:2.hook: But one lantern carried a second riddle, darker than the first.
intelligence:2.line: 'This door does not test strength — it tests *intelligence*.'

sentences.en: The old stone door would not open until we answered its riddle.
sentences.cn: 那扇古老的石门要到我们答出谜语才会打开。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied the carvings for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 老舵盯着雕刻看了很久。

sentences.en: 'This door does not test strength,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "这扇门不考力气，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: 'It tests *intelligence*.'
He traced one symbol, whispered an answer, and the door swung wide into a garden of floating lanterns.
sentences.cn: 他沿着一个符号描去，低声说出答案，门就向着一座漂浮灯笼的花园打开了。

uk:2.en: Inside a brass chest we found a folded letter sealed with a small stamp. Bell held it to the starlight and read aloud: 'Sent from the *UK*, Isle of Charts, Year of the Silver Tide.' Old Helm's eyes went wide. No one had heard from the Isle of Charts in fifty years. The word 'UK' glowed briefly, then became our next map fragment.
uk:2.cnHint: 船员们在黄铜箱里发现了一封来自____的信，那是五十年来的第一封消息。
uk:2.hook: The ink on the letter was still warm.
uk:2.line: 'It says: sent from the *UK*, Isle of Charts, Year of the Silver Tide.'

sentences.en: Inside a brass chest we found a folded letter sealed with a small stamp.
sentences.cn: 在一只黄铜箱子里，我们找到了一封折好的信，用小印章封着。

sentences.en: Bell held it to the starlight and read aloud: 'Sent from the *UK*, Isle of Charts, Year of the Silver Tide.'
Old Helm's eyes went wide.
sentences.cn: 老舵的眼睛睁大了。

sentences.en: No one had heard from the Isle of Charts in fifty years.
sentences.cn: 五十年来没人听说过海图岛的消息了。

sentences.en: The word 'UK' glowed briefly, then became our next map fragment.
sentences.cn: "UK"这个词短暂地闪烁，然后成了我们下一块地图碎片。

user:2.en: We found a tall machine humming softly in a ruined tower. A dusty screen lit up and showed a single word: *user*. 'That means us,' Bell said, pressing a key. A map bloomed across the screen, marking three islands no one in our troupe had ever visited. Old Helm copied every detail before the screen went dark again.
user:2.cnHint: 废塔里的老机器亮起屏幕，提示____输入指令，地图随之显现。
user:2.hook: The third island on the map had no name — only a question mark.
user:2.line: 'The screen is waiting — we are the *user*, so let us press the key.'

sentences.en: We found a tall machine humming softly in a ruined tower.
sentences.cn: 我们在一座废弃的塔楼里找到了一台轻声嗡鸣的高大机器。

sentences.en: A dusty screen lit up and showed a single word: *user*.
'That means us,' Bell said, pressing a key.
sentences.cn: "那就是我们，"小铃说着按下了一个键。

sentences.en: A map bloomed across the screen, marking three islands no one in our troupe had ever visited.
sentences.cn: 一张地图在屏幕上绽放，标出了三座我们队伍里谁都没去过的岛屿。

sentences.en: Old Helm copied every detail before the screen went dark again.
sentences.cn: 老舵在屏幕再次变暗前把每个细节都抄了下来。

park:2.en: The island was one vast garden where clouds drifted between the trees like slow white animals. 'The old crews used to *park* their ships in the tall branches,' Old Helm said, pointing to iron rings hammered into ancient bark. We tied our own ropes to the highest ring and climbed down into the cool green shade below.
park:2.cnHint: 老舵主告诉大家，老船员们过去常把船____在这片巨树的枝丫上。
park:2.hook: Something had chewed through one of the old iron rings overnight.
