park:2.line: 'The old crews would *park* their ships right in those branches up there.'

sentences.en: The island was one vast garden where clouds drifted between the trees like slow white animals.
sentences.cn: 岛屿是一座辽阔的花园，云像缓慢移动的白色动物一样在树间飘浮。

sentences.en: 'The old crews used to *park* their ships in the tall branches,' Old Helm said, pointing to iron rings hammered into ancient bark.
We tied our own ropes to the highest ring and climbed down into the cool green shade below.
sentences.cn: 我们把自己的绳子系在最高的铁环上，爬下去进入下面凉爽的绿色阴影里。

reward:2.en: At the centre of the island stood a pedestal with a glowing word resting on it like a gift. A note beside it read: 'For those who finish the long path — a *reward*.' Bell laughed with surprise and held the word up. It pulsed warm gold in her hands, and a new route unfolded across our sky-map like a ribbon of light.
reward:2.cnHint: 走完漫长山路的旅者在石台上发现了一份____，新的航线随之展开。
reward:2.hook: The route led straight into a cloud none of us could see through.
reward:2.line: 'A note says this word is our *reward* for finishing the long path.'

sentences.en: At the centre of the island stood a pedestal with a glowing word resting on it like a gift.
sentences.cn: 岛的中央竖着一座基座，基座上闪烁着一个词，像礼物一样。

sentences.en: A note beside it read: 'For those who finish the long path — a *reward*.'
Bell laughed with surprise and held the word up.
sentences.cn: 小铃惊喜地笑了，把那个词举了起来。

sentences.en: It pulsed warm gold in her hands, and a new route unfolded across our sky-map like a ribbon of light.
sentences.cn: 它在她手心里脉动着温暖的金色，一条新的路线像一根光的丝带一样在我们的天空地图上铺展开来。

credit:2.en: The keeper of the Word Bridge checked his thick ledger before letting anyone pass. He looked at our troupe, then nodded slowly. 'You have *credit* here,' he said. 'Three words returned to the sky last season — I have it written down.' Old Helm bowed, and we crossed the bridge into the misty island beyond without paying a single coin.
credit:2.cnHint: 桥关守卫查过账本后，承认旅团凭借过去的贡献享有____，免费通行。
credit:2.hook: On the far side, the mist whispered a name none of us recognised.
credit:2.line: 'You have *credit* here — three words returned last season, I wrote it down.'

sentences.en: The keeper of the Word Bridge checked his thick ledger before letting anyone pass.
sentences.cn: 词桥的看守官翻着他厚厚的账簿，才让任何人通过。

sentences.en: He looked at our troupe, then nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 他看了看我们的队伍，然后慢慢点了点头。

sentences.en: 'You have *credit* here,' he said.
'Three words returned to the sky last season — I have it written down.'
sentences.cn: "上个季节有三个词被送回了天空——我都记下来了。"

sentences.en: Old Helm bowed, and we crossed the bridge into the misty island beyond without paying a single coin.
sentences.cn: 老舵鞠了一躬，我们就没花一个硬币地穿过桥，走进了对面雾蒙蒙的岛屿。

progress:2.en: We had been climbing the Stair of Echoes for what felt like hours, and the top was still hidden in cloud. 'Keep going,' Old Helm said each time someone slowed. 'We *progress* only by moving.' Step by step, the cloud thinned, and at last a wide platform opened above us, scattered with glowing word-stones waiting to be claimed.
progress:2.cnHint: 攀爬回音阶梯时，老舵主鼓励大家只有不断前行才能____，终于抵达顶端。
progress:2.hook: One word-stone was already cracked, as if someone had tried to take it by force.
progress:2.line: 'We *progress* only by moving — so keep your feet going, one step at a time.'

sentences.en: We had been climbing the Stair of Echoes for what felt like hours, and the top was still hidden in cloud.
sentences.cn: 我们爬回声阶梯已经有一阵子了，山顶还隐没在云里。

sentences.en: 'Keep going,' Old Helm said each time someone slowed.
sentences.cn: "继续往上，"老舵每次有人放慢步伐的时候就这样说。

sentences.en: 'We *progress* only by moving.'
Step by step, the cloud thinned, and at last a wide platform opened above us, scattered with glowing word-stones waiting to be claimed.
sentences.cn: 一步步地，云变薄了，最后一个宽阔的平台在我们上方打开，散落着等待被收集的闪烁的词石。

snack:2.en: Bell pulled a small paper bag from her coat and offered it around. 'Island seed cake,' she said cheerfully. 'Best *snack* for high altitudes.' We each took a piece as the wind carried us gently between two pearl-white clouds. Old Helm chewed thoughtfully, then pointed ahead — a new island had just drifted into view, green and bright and full of promise.
snack:2.cnHint: 贝尔分发了一种高空____，大家边吃边眺望，一座新岛屿漂入了视野。
snack:2.hook: The new island was moving — slowly, but definitely moving toward us.
snack:2.line: 'Island seed cake — best *snack* you can find at this height, trust me.'

sentences.en: Bell pulled a small paper bag from her coat and offered it around.
sentences.cn: 小铃从她的大衣里掏出一个小纸袋，递给大家。

sentences.en: 'Island seed cake,' she said cheerfully.
sentences.cn: "岛屿籽糕，"她高兴地说。

sentences.en: 'Best *snack* for high altitudes.'
We each took a piece as the wind carried us gently between two pearl-white clouds.
sentences.cn: 风温柔地托着我们在两朵珍珠白的云之间飘动时，我们每人都拿了一块。

sentences.en: Old Helm chewed thoughtfully, then pointed ahead — a new island had just drifted into view, green and bright and full of promise.
sentences.cn: 老舵若有所思地嚼着，然后指向前方——一座新的岛屿刚好飘进了视野，绿油油的，闪闪发光，充满了希望。

retire:2.en: The old lighthouse keeper handed Old Helm a rolled note before shuffling away. 'I *retire* tonight,' he said, 'but the light stays on for you.' We found his final log tucked inside — a hand-drawn map of the dark coast below the clouds, waiting to be read.
retire:2.cnHint: 老灯塔守护人把一张地图留给了老舵，然后宣布自己要____了。
retire:2.hook: The map showed a path no living sailor had taken in fifty years.
retire:2.line: 'I *retire* tonight, but everything I know now belongs to you.'

sentences.en: The old lighthouse keeper handed Old Helm a rolled note before shuffling away.
sentences.cn: 老灯塔看守人把一张卷起来的纸条递给老舵，然后蹒跚地走了。

sentences.en: 'I *retire* tonight,' he said, 'but the light stays on for you.'
We found his final log tucked inside — a hand-drawn map of the dark coast below the clouds, waiting to be read.
sentences.cn: 我们在里面发现了他最后的日志——一张手绘的暗礁海岸地图，就在云层下方，等待着被阅读。

sea:2.en: Bell pressed her ear to a giant shell on the edge of Drift Island. 'There it is,' she whispered. A low roar filled the shell — the sound of a *sea* far below the floating rocks, vast and unseen. Old Helm traced its outline on our chart with a single careful line.
sea:2.cnHint: 小铃在一枚大贝壳里听到了远方____的声音，老舵将其标注在地图上。
sea:2.hook: Whatever floated down there had not been mapped before.
sea:2.line: 'That shell holds the voice of a *sea* no one on these islands has ever touched.'

sentences.en: Bell pressed her ear to a giant shell on the edge of Drift Island.
sentences.cn: 小铃把耳朵贴在漂流岛边缘的一个巨大贝壳上。

sentences.en: 'There it is,' she whispered.
sentences.cn: "就是这个，"她低声说。

sentences.en: A low roar filled the shell — the sound of a *sea* far below the floating rocks, vast and unseen.
Old Helm traced its outline on our chart with a single careful line.
sentences.cn: 老舵用一条细线小心地在我们的地图上描出了它的轮廓。

town:2.en: Silverfang landed the ship on a wide flat rock and pointed at a cluster of tiny rooftops below — a *town* built into the cliffs of the island's underside, windows glowing warm against the dark sky. Old Helm pressed the new word-fragment to the map and smiled as a path lit up.
town:2.cnHint: 银牙发现了一座悬挂在岛屿底部的____，老舵将新词碎片贴上地图。
town:2.hook: The glowing path led straight toward the deepest part of the clouds.
town:2.line: 'Every *town* built upside-down has a secret it only shows to visitors.'

sentences.en: Silverfang landed the ship on a wide flat rock and pointed at a cluster of tiny rooftops below — a *town* built into the cliffs of the island's underside, windows glowing warm against the dark sky.
Old Helm pressed the new word-fragment to the map and smiled as a path lit up.
sentences.cn: 老舵把新的词汇碎片按在地图上，看着一条光之路径亮了起来，脸上露出了笑容。

gap:2.en: There was a *gap* in the chain of islands — a stretch of open sky where no rock floated and no star seemed to shine. Bell studied the empty space for a long moment, then slid a word-fragment into the map. A thin bridge of light slowly appeared, crossing the dark distance.
gap:2.cnHint: 小铃发现地图上有一处____，插入词语碎片后，一座光桥慢慢浮现。
gap:2.hook: The bridge hummed softly, as if it had been waiting a very long time.
gap:2.line: 'Fill the *gap* with the right word and the sky will build the rest.'

sentences.en: There was a *gap* in the chain of islands — a stretch of open sky where no rock floated and no star seemed to shine.
Bell studied the empty space for a long moment, then slid a word-fragment into the map.
sentences.cn: 小铃盯着这片空荡荡的地方看了很久，然后把一个词汇碎片滑进了地图。

sentences.en: A thin bridge of light slowly appeared, crossing the dark distance.
sentences.cn: 一道细细的光桥慢慢地出现了，跨越黑暗的距离。

generation:2.en: Inside the archive tower, shelves held jars of glowing dust — one jar for each *generation* of word-collectors before us. Old Helm lifted the newest, nearly empty jar and said our troupe's name aloud. The dust inside stirred, rose, and reshaped itself into a map fragment we had never seen.
generation:2.cnHint: 档案塔里每一____的收词者都留下了发光的尘埃，老舵念出队名后，尘埃变成了新的地图碎片。
generation:2.hook: The fragment pointed toward an island that had no name yet.
generation:2.line: 'Every *generation* of collectors leaves something behind for the next to find.'

sentences.en: Inside the archive tower, shelves held jars of glowing dust — one jar for each *generation* of word-collectors before us.
Old Helm lifted the newest, nearly empty jar and said our troupe's name aloud.
sentences.cn: 老舵拿起最新的、几乎空了的罐子，大声说出了我们剧团的名字。

sentences.en: The dust inside stirred, rose, and reshaped itself into a map fragment we had never seen.
sentences.cn: 罐子里的尘埃翻滚起来，上升，然后重新塑形成一个我们从未见过的地图碎片。

guide:2.en: A small brass compass rolled out of a cracked stone pillar and stopped at Bell's feet. Engraved on its face were the words: let wonder *guide* you. She picked it up, and the needle swung — not toward north, but toward a distant island glowing faintly gold at the horizon.
guide:2.cnHint: 一枚刻有字样的铜罗盘滚到小铃脚边，指针指向远方一座发着金光的____岛屿。
guide:2.hook: The gold glow pulsed once, as if answering the compass.
guide:2.line: 'Let wonder *guide* you, and the map will always show a next step.'

sentences.en: A small brass compass rolled out of a cracked stone pillar and stopped at Bell's feet.
sentences.cn: 一个小黄铜指南针从一根裂开的石柱里滚出来，停在小铃的脚边。

sentences.en: Engraved on its face were the words: let wonder *guide* you.
She picked it up, and the needle swung — not toward north, but toward a distant island glowing faintly gold at the horizon.
sentences.cn: 她捡了起来，指针摇晃——不是指向北方，而是指向地平线上一个远处微微闪闪发光的岛屿。

household:2.en: On Cinder Rock we found a small cave where a *household* of three had clearly lived — a table, two chairs, and a tiny stove still faintly warm. Pinned to the wall was a chart covered in handwritten word-fragments. Old Helm said quietly, 'They were collectors too.'
household:2.cnHint: 在烬岩上，我们发现一个小____留下的地图碎片，老舵轻声说他们也是收词者。
household:2.hook: One fragment on their chart matched a blank space on ours exactly.
household:2.line: 'Every *household* that ever lived here left a piece of the map behind.'

sentences.en: On Cinder Rock we found a small cave where a *household* of three had clearly lived — a table, two chairs, and a tiny stove still faintly warm.
Pinned to the wall was a chart covered in handwritten word-fragments.
sentences.cn: 钉在墙上的是一张布满手写词汇碎片的地图。

sentences.en: Old Helm said quietly, 'They were collectors too.'
sentences.cn: 老舵静静地说，"他们也是收集者。"

luxury:2.en: After weeks of hard wind and cold nights, we landed on Velvet Isle, where the grass was thick and the air smelled of warm bread. Old Helm called it a *luxury* — soft ground under our feet, clear skies above, and a whole undiscovered island spread before us like a gift.
luxury:2.cnHint: 经过几周的艰辛旅途，老舵说踏上天鹅绒岛、脚踩软草是一种难得的____。
luxury:2.hook: Beneath the soft grass, Bell's boot struck something hollow and hard.
luxury:2.line: 'Rest on real ground — that is a *luxury* every word-collector earns eventually.'

sentences.en: After weeks of hard wind and cold nights, we landed on Velvet Isle, where the grass was thick and the air smelled of warm bread.
sentences.cn: 经过几周的强风和寒冷的夜晚，我们登陆了天鹅绒岛，那里草很厚，空气里弥漫着温暖的面包味道。

sentences.en: Old Helm called it a *luxury* — soft ground under our feet, clear skies above, and a whole undiscovered island spread before us like a gift.

disadvantage:2.en: The island of Mirrored Cliffs gave us a clear *disadvantage*: our map fragment was written in fading ink, and the cliffs reflected sunlight so sharply that no one could read it. Old Helm shielded his eyes and laughed softly. 'Every hard place teaches us something,' he said.
disadvantage:2.cnHint: 镜崖岛的强烈反光让我们处于____，地图上的字迹几乎无法辨认。
disadvantage:2.hook: Behind the glare, something large was moving toward us.
disadvantage:2.line: Old Helm said, 'The light is our *disadvantage*, but also our signal.'

sentences.en: The island of Mirrored Cliffs gave us a clear *disadvantage*: our map fragment was written in fading ink, and the cliffs reflected sunlight so sharply that no one could read it.
Old Helm shielded his eyes and laughed softly.
sentences.cn: 老舵遮住眼睛，轻轻地笑了。

sentences.en: 'Every hard place teaches us something,' he said.
sentences.cn: "每个困难的地方都教会我们一些东西，"他说。

discuss:2.en: We landed on the Cloud Garden island, where flowers grew in mid-air. Bell spread the map across a floating stone and called us over. 'We need to *discuss* which path leads to the next word,' she said. The three routes ahead looked equally strange and equally beautiful.
discuss:2.cnHint: 在云花岛上，小铃把地图展开，招呼大家____下一步的路线。
discuss:2.hook: Then the stone beneath the map began to slowly sink.
discuss:2.line: Bell said, 'Let us *discuss* this before the wind changes direction.'

sentences.en: We landed on the Cloud Garden island, where flowers grew in mid-air.
sentences.cn: 我们在云花岛登陆了，那里鲜花在半空中生长。

sentences.en: Bell spread the map across a floating stone and called us over.
sentences.cn: 小铃把地图铺在一块漂浮的石头上，喊我们过来。

sentences.en: 'We need to *discuss* which path leads to the next word,' she said.
The three routes ahead looked equally strange and equally beautiful.
sentences.cn: 前面的三条路看起来同样奇异，同样美丽。

psychological:2.en: The Whispering Hollow island had no monsters, no storms — only silence that pressed against the ears. Old Helm told me the hardest challenge here was *psychological*: travellers who feared quiet often turned back before finding the word hidden at the centre. I took a slow breath and walked on.
psychological:2.cnHint: 在低语洼地，老舵主说这里最大的考验是____上的——许多旅行者因此中途折返。
psychological:2.hook: The silence then shifted, as if it had been listening all along.
psychological:2.line: Old Helm said, 'The danger here is entirely *psychological*, so breathe.'

sentences.en: The Whispering Hollow island had no monsters, no storms — only silence that pressed against the ears.
sentences.cn: 低语空心岛上没有怪物，没有风暴——只有一种压在耳朵上的寂静。

sentences.en: Old Helm told me the hardest challenge here was *psychological*: travellers who feared quiet often turned back before finding the word hidden at the centre.
I took a slow breath and walked on.
sentences.cn: 我深吸一口气，继续前进。

request:2.en: A small glowing bird landed on Bell's shoulder just after we crossed the Amber Bridge island. It carried a folded leaf — a *request* from Silverfang, asking to meet at the island's highest lamp before sunset. Bell raised an eyebrow. Old Helm simply folded the leaf back and nodded.
request:2.cnHint: 一只发光的鸟带来了竞争船长的____，邀我们在最高灯塔见面。
request:2.hook: The bird dissolved into sparks before anyone could ask it questions.
request:2.line: Silverfang had written, 'This is a *request*, not a challenge — please come.'

sentences.en: A small glowing bird landed on Bell's shoulder just after we crossed the Amber Bridge island.
sentences.cn: 在我们穿过琥珀桥岛之后不久，一只小的发光鸟停在了小铃的肩膀上。

sentences.en: It carried a folded leaf — a *request* from Silverfang, asking to meet at the island's highest lamp before sunset.
Bell raised an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 小铃扬起了眉毛。

sentences.en: Old Helm simply folded the leaf back and nodded.
sentences.cn: 老舵只是把叶子折回去，点了点头。

symptom:2.en: The word-fragment we found on Rust Reef island was cracked and cold. Old Helm said the cracking was a *symptom* of a sick sky — somewhere above, a wind channel was breaking apart. Bell checked her compass, watching the needle tremble. The island itself seemed to be holding its breath.
symptom:2.cnHint: 生锈礁的地图碎片已经开裂，老舵主说这是天空生病的____。
symptom:2.hook: The compass needle snapped clean off without warning.
symptom:2.line: Old Helm said, 'A cracked word is a *symptom* — the sky above is ill.'

sentences.en: The word-fragment we found on Rust Reef island was cracked and cold.
sentences.cn: 我们在生锈礁岛找到的字片段破裂了，冰冷冰冷的。

sentences.en: Old Helm said the cracking was a *symptom* of a sick sky — somewhere above, a wind channel was breaking apart.
Bell checked her compass, watching the needle tremble.
sentences.cn: 小铃检查了她的罗盘，看着指针颤抖。

sentences.en: The island itself seemed to be holding its breath.
sentences.cn: 岛屿本身似乎在屏住呼吸。

upon:2.en: *Upon* the highest platform of the Lantern Steps island, we found a jar sealed with golden wax. Inside was a single word written on a ribbon of silver paper. Bell held it to the light, her eyes wide. Whatever was written there made her laugh and cover her mouth at the same time.
upon:2.cnHint: 在灯阶岛最高的台子____，我们发现了一个封着金蜡的罐子。
upon:2.hook: Bell re-sealed the jar without letting the rest of us see.
upon:2.line: Bell said, '*Upon* this platform, the whole sky looks like a gift.'

sentences.en: *Upon* the highest platform of the Lantern Steps island, we found a jar sealed with golden wax.
Inside was a single word written on a ribbon of silver paper.
sentences.cn: 里面是一根银纸带上写的一个单词。

sentences.en: Bell held it to the light, her eyes wide.
sentences.cn: 小铃把它凑到光下，眼睛睁得很大。

sentences.en: Whatever was written there made her laugh and cover her mouth at the same time.
sentences.cn: 无论上面写的是什么，都让她既笑又捂住嘴。

argument:2.en: Silverfang and Old Helm stood at the edge of the Tide Bridge island, deep in *argument* about which star marked the next destination. Their voices were firm but not unkind. Bell and I watched from a distance. In the end, both of them pointed at the same star — and went quiet.
argument:2.cnHint: 在潮汐桥岛，老舵主和竞争船长为下一个目的地展开了____。
argument:2.hook: The star they both chose suddenly blinked out.
argument:2.line: Silverfang said, 'Our *argument* ends here — that star is the one.'

sentences.en: Silverfang and Old Helm stood at the edge of the Tide Bridge island, deep in *argument* about which star marked the next destination.
Their voices were firm but not unkind.
sentences.cn: 他们的声音坚定却不失温度。

sentences.en: Bell and I watched from a distance.
sentences.cn: 小铃和我在远处看着。

sentences.en: In the end, both of them pointed at the same star — and went quiet.
sentences.cn: 最后，他们俩指向了同一颗星——然后都沉默了。

crisis:2.en: The word we needed was locked inside a crystal that had begun to crack. Bell called it a *crisis*: if the crystal broke fully, the word would scatter into the wind and the map would stay incomplete. We worked quickly, cupping our hands around the crystal until it steadied and held.
crisis:2.cnHint: 装着关键词语的水晶开始碎裂，小铃说这是一场____，必须马上阻止。
crisis:2.hook: A single crack remained, fine as a hair and perfectly still.
crisis:2.line: Bell said, 'This is a *crisis* — hold it gently and do not move.'

sentences.en: The word we needed was locked inside a crystal that had begun to crack.
sentences.cn: 我们需要的字被锁在一块已经开始裂开的水晶里。

sentences.en: Bell called it a *crisis*: if the crystal broke fully, the word would scatter into the wind and the map would stay incomplete.
We worked quickly, cupping our hands around the crystal until it steadied and held.
sentences.cn: 我们快速行动，用手掌围住水晶，直到它稳定下来。

analysis:2.en: At the edge of the island, Bell spread a wide sheet of paper across a flat rock. She had mapped every star pattern we had seen for three weeks. 'This *analysis* shows a clear path north,' she said quietly. Old Helm leaned in, eyes wide. The paper glowed faintly, as if the stars agreed.
analysis:2.cnHint: 小铃将三周以来的星象数据整理成图，通过____发现了一条通往北方的航线。
analysis:2.hook: But north, the charts showed, was not on any map we carried.
analysis:2.line: 'This *analysis* of the star patterns shows exactly where we need to go next.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the island, Bell spread a wide sheet of paper across a flat rock.
sentences.cn: 在岛边，小铃把一大张纸铺在平坦的石头上。

sentences.en: She had mapped every star pattern we had seen for three weeks.
sentences.cn: 她绘制了我们三周来看到的每一个星星图案。

sentences.en: 'This *analysis* shows a clear path north,' she said quietly.
Old Helm leaned in, eyes wide.
sentences.cn: 老舵俯身看，眼睛睁得很大。

sentences.en: The paper glowed faintly, as if the stars agreed.
sentences.cn: 纸轻轻地发着光，仿佛星星也同意似的。

application:2.en: A sealed glass bottle sat wedged in a crack near the island's edge. Inside was a folded note — an *application* to join a sky troupe, written in faded ink and signed by someone who never made it. Old Helm read it twice, folded it gently, and tucked it into his coat. 'We carry them with us,' he said.
application:2.cnHint: 在岛边的石缝里，众人发现了一封尘封已久的入团____书，老舵主将它郑重收入衣袋。
application:2.hook: The signature on the note matched the name carved into our ship's oldest plank.
application:2.line: 'Someone left this *application* long ago — we honour it by flying on.'

sentences.en: A sealed glass bottle sat wedged in a crack near the island's edge.
sentences.cn: 一个密封的玻璃瓶卡在岛边缘的一道裂缝里。

sentences.en: Inside was a folded note — an *application* to join a sky troupe, written in faded ink and signed by someone who never made it.
Old Helm read it twice, folded it gently, and tucked it into his coat.
sentences.cn: 老舵读了两遍，轻轻地折好，塞进了他的外套。

sentences.en: 'We carry them with us,' he said.
sentences.cn: "我们把他们带在身边，"他说。

living:2.en: Bell found a small garden growing in a hollow near the island's centre — bright green leaves pushing through pale stone. 'Something is still *living* here,' she whispered, kneeling down. Old Helm said old maps sometimes marked such spots as rest points, places where travelers once stopped and left seeds behind. We stayed an hour longer than planned.
living:2.cnHint: 在岛屿中心的洼地里，小铃发现了仍在____的绿色植物，这让众人决定多停留一会儿。
living:2.hook: Tucked beneath the largest leaf was a folded map fragment, still warm.
living:2.line: 'Something is still *living* here — this island has not been empty for long.'

sentences.en: Bell found a small garden growing in a hollow near the island's centre — bright green leaves pushing through pale stone.
sentences.cn: 小铃在岛中心附近的一个凹陷处发现了一个小花园——鲜绿的叶子从苍白的石头里冒出来。

sentences.en: 'Something is still *living* here,' she whispered, kneeling down.
Old Helm said old maps sometimes marked such spots as rest points, places where travelers once stopped and left seeds behind.
sentences.cn: 老舵说古老的地图有时会把这样的地方标记为休息点，那是旅行者曾经停下来留下种子的地方。

sentences.en: We stayed an hour longer than planned.
sentences.cn: 我们比计划多待了一小时。

proposal:2.en: Silverfang arrived just as we were about to leave, stepping off a small side-vessel with a rolled chart under one arm. 'I have a *proposal*,' he said, spreading the chart on our deck. It showed a shorter route to the next island — through a cloud bank we had all been avoiding. Old Helm studied it carefully and said nothing for a long moment.
proposal:2.cnHint: 竞争船长带着一份新航线____出现了，建议穿越众人一直回避的云层地带。
proposal:2.hook: The cloud bank on his chart was marked with a word none of us could read.
proposal:2.line: 'My *proposal* is simple — trust the shorter path and we arrive before the stars shift.'

sentences.en: Silverfang arrived just as we were about to leave, stepping off a small side-vessel with a rolled chart under one arm.
sentences.cn: 银牙正好在我们要离开时到达，从一艘小型侧船上走下来，胳膊下夹着一张展开的海图。

sentences.en: 'I have a *proposal*,' he said, spreading the chart on our deck.
It showed a shorter route to the next island — through a cloud bank we had all been avoiding.
sentences.cn: 它显示了一条前往下一个岛屿的更短路线——穿过一片我们一直在躲避的云层。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied it carefully and said nothing for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 老舵仔细研究了它，沉默了很久。

relevant:2.en: We found a crate of old journals near the landing stone. Most were too water-damaged to read, but Bell held one up to the light. 'This page is still *relevant*,' she said firmly. It described the exact wind pattern we had struggled with all morning. Old Helm copied the key lines into his own notebook without saying a word.
relevant:2.cnHint: 在一批破损的旧航海日志中，小铃找到了一页与当前处境仍____的记录，老舵主默默将其抄下。
relevant:2.hook: The journal's last entry was dated the same day our troupe was founded.
relevant:2.line: 'Only this page is *relevant* to where we are — the rest is someone else's story.'

sentences.en: We found a crate of old journals near the landing stone.
sentences.cn: 我们在登陆石附近发现了一箱旧日记。

sentences.en: Most were too water-damaged to read, but Bell held one up to the light.
sentences.cn: 大多数已经被水泡得无法阅读，但小铃把其中一本举到光下。

sentences.en: 'This page is still *relevant*,' she said firmly.
It described the exact wind pattern we had struggled with all morning.
sentences.cn: 它描述了我们整个早上都在苦恼的确切风型。

sentences.en: Old Helm copied the key lines into his own notebook without saying a word.
sentences.cn: 老舵把关键几行抄到自己的笔记本里，一言不发。

senior:2.en: At the docking post we met an old navigator who said nothing at first, just watched us tie our ropes. Old Helm greeted him with a small bow. 'He is a *senior* among sky travelers,' Old Helm told me quietly. The old man finally smiled, pressed a small carved token into my hand, and pointed toward the far eastern clouds without a word.
senior:2.cnHint: 在停靠点，众人遇到了一位在空中旅行者中德高望重的____，他无声地为我们指引了方向。
senior:2.hook: The token he gave me was carved with the shape of the very next island on our map.
senior:2.line: 'As a *senior* of these skies, his silence tells you more than most people's words.'

sentences.en: At the docking post we met an old navigator who said nothing at first, just watched us tie our ropes.
sentences.cn: 在停靠站，我们遇到了一位年长的领航员，他起初什么也没说，只是看着我们系绳子。

sentences.en: Old Helm greeted him with a small bow.
sentences.cn: 老舵向他深深鞠了一躬。

sentences.en: 'He is a *senior* among sky travelers,' Old Helm told me quietly.
The old man finally smiled, pressed a small carved token into my hand, and pointed toward the far eastern clouds without a word.
sentences.cn: 那位老人终于笑了，把一个小雕刻令牌塞进我的手里，然后指向遥远的东方云层，一言不发。

table:2.en: In the centre of the island stood a wide flat stone that everyone in the troupe called the *table*. Bell laid our collected word-fragments across it in a rough grid. Slowly, the pieces began to connect — edges matching, colours aligning — and a new section of the sky map appeared between them, glowing just enough to read by starlight.
table:2.cnHint: 在岛中央那块被称为____的巨石上，小铃将所有词语碎片拼合，新的天空地图浮现出来。
table:2.hook: The new section pointed toward an island that none of us had ever heard named.
table:2.line: 'Lay every fragment on the *table* — the map only speaks when the pieces are together.'

sentences.en: In the centre of the island stood a wide flat stone that everyone in the troupe called the *table*.
Bell laid our collected word-fragments across it in a rough grid.
sentences.cn: 小铃把我们收集的字片段铺在上面，粗略地排成一个网格。

sentences.en: Slowly, the pieces began to connect — edges matching, colours aligning — and a new section of the sky map appeared between them, glowing just enough to read by starlight.
sentences.cn: 慢慢地，碎片开始连接——边缘吻合，颜色对齐——一个新的天空地图片段在它们之间出现，发出足以用星光读取的光。

campus:2.en: The island below was shaped like a wide ring of low buildings around an open courtyard — someone had once called it a *campus*, and the name had stuck. Desks were still inside the rooms, covered in pale dust. On the largest desk, Bell found a folded star-chart, its corners weighted down by four smooth stones as if a lesson had only just ended.
campus:2.cnHint: 这座形如庭院建筑群的岛屿曾被称为____，小铃在最大的课桌上发现了一张压着石头的星图。
campus:2.hook: The star-chart showed a constellation that only appears once every hundred years — tonight.
campus:2.line: 'This whole island was a *campus* once — someone built it just to study the sky.'

sentences.en: The island below was shaped like a wide ring of low buildings around an open courtyard — someone had once called it a *campus*, and the name had stuck.
Desks were still inside the rooms, covered in pale dust.
sentences.cn: 房间里面还有桌子，覆盖着淡淡的灰尘。

sentences.en: On the largest desk, Bell found a folded star-chart, its corners weighted down by four smooth stones as if a lesson had only just ended.
sentences.cn: 在最大的桌子上，小铃发现了一张折起来的星图，四个光滑的石头压在角上，就像一堂课刚刚结束似的。

campaign:2.en: Old Helm spread a worn chart across the deck and tapped a line of faded text. 'This whole region,' he said, 'was mapped during a great *campaign* to reach the Sky Root — a journey that took three crews and two full seasons.' The words glowed faintly, as if remembering the effort.
campaign:2.cnHint: 老舵手向我们讲述了一段用于绘制这片区域地图的伟大____的历史。
campaign:2.hook: At the bottom of the chart, one island had no name — only a question mark.
campaign:2.line: 'Every island on this chart was found during that great *campaign* — every one but the last.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread a worn chart across the deck and tapped a line of faded text.
sentences.cn: 老舵在甲板上铺开一张磨损的图表，敲了敲上面褪色的文字。

sentences.en: 'This whole region,' he said, 'was mapped during a great *campaign* to reach the Sky Root — a journey that took three crews and two full seasons.'
The words glowed faintly, as if remembering the effort.
sentences.cn: 这些字闪闪发光，仿佛还在回忆那段艰辛的旅程。

hurt:2.en: I reached for the glowing word-fragment wedged in a crack in the stone arch, but pulled my hand back fast. 'It won't *hurt* you,' Bell said softly, watching my face. 'It only stings if you try to take it before you understand it.' I took a breath, thought of its meaning, and tried again.
hurt:2.cnHint: 贝尔告诉我，只要真正理解了这个词，它就不会____你。
hurt:2.hook: The word pulsed once, twice — then lifted free into my open palm.
hurt:2.line: 'Don't worry — it won't *hurt* you if your heart is in the right place.'

sentences.en: I reached for the glowing word-fragment wedged in a crack in the stone arch, but pulled my hand back fast.
sentences.cn: 我伸手去够卡在石拱裂缝里闪烁的字片，又快速缩回了手。

sentences.en: 'It won't *hurt* you,' Bell said softly, watching my face.
'It only stings if you try to take it before you understand it.'
sentences.cn: 在你理解它之前，你试着去拿它才会刺痛。

sentences.en: I took a breath, thought of its meaning, and tried again.
sentences.cn: 我深吸一口气，想清楚了它的意思，又试了一次。

initiative:2.en: The bridge between two islands had crumbled, and we stood staring at the gap. Nobody spoke. Then, without waiting to be asked, I tied a rope to the nearest post and swung across to test the anchor stones. Old Helm nodded slowly. 'Good *initiative*,' he said. 'The troupe needs that.'
initiative:2.cnHint: 我主动采取行动修复了桥梁，老舵手称赞了我的____。
initiative:2.hook: On the other side, a locked door was already trembling, as if it knew we were coming.
initiative:2.line: 'Good *initiative* — the troupe rewards those who move first.'

sentences.en: The bridge between two islands had crumbled, and we stood staring at the gap.
sentences.cn: 两座岛屿之间的桥已经坍塌了，我们站在那里盯着这道裂口。

sentences.en: Nobody spoke.
sentences.cn: 没人说话。

sentences.en: Then, without waiting to be asked, I tied a rope to the nearest post and swung across to test the anchor stones.
sentences.cn: 然后，没等人说什么，我就系好绳子绑在最近的柱子上，荡过去检查锚石。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵缓缓点了点头。

sentences.en: 'Good *initiative*,' he said.
'The troupe needs that.'
sentences.cn: 剧团需要这种精神。

jump:2.en: The word was written on a small stone tile floating in the middle of the air, too far to reach by hand. Bell studied it a moment, then grinned. 'You have to *jump* to earn this one,' she said. I ran, leapt, and grabbed the tile — and the whole island shuddered beneath a new light.
jump:2.cnHint: 贝尔告诉我，想要得到这块词石，就必须____过去。
jump:2.hook: The moment I landed, a hidden path lit up ahead, leading somewhere no map had shown.
jump:2.line: 'You have to *jump* for it — this word was never meant to be reached easily.'

sentences.en: The word was written on a small stone tile floating in the middle of the air, too far to reach by hand.
sentences.cn: 这个字写在悬浮在空中的小石板上，手根本够不着。

sentences.en: Bell studied it a moment, then grinned.
sentences.cn: 小铃看了一会儿，然后咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: 'You have to *jump* to earn this one,' she said.
I ran, leapt, and grabbed the tile — and the whole island shuddered beneath a new light.
sentences.cn: 我跑起来，跳起来，抓住了石板——整个岛屿在新的光芒下震颤起来。

lie:2.en: The island appeared flat from above, but when we landed I could see the truth. 'The whole valley *lies* below that ridge,' Bell called from higher ground, waving us forward. From up there, a wide silver plain stretched out under the stars — nothing like the bare rock we had expected.
lie:2.cnHint: 贝尔发现整片山谷____在山脊的另一边，与我们预想的完全不同。
lie:2.hook: And at the centre of that plain, something was shining — steady and patient as a lantern.
lie:2.line: 'The real island *lies* beyond the ridge — come up here and see for yourself.'

sentences.en: The island appeared flat from above, but when we landed I could see the truth.
sentences.cn: 从上面看，这座岛是平的，但我们着陆后才看到真相。

sentences.en: 'The whole valley *lies* below that ridge,' Bell called from higher ground, waving us forward.
From up there, a wide silver plain stretched out under the stars — nothing like the bare rock we had expected.
sentences.cn: 从那儿往外看，一片宽阔的银色平原在星光下铺展开来——完全不像我们预期的那片光秃秃的岩石。

lunch:2.en: We sat on the edge of a cloud shelf and ate *lunch* together — dried fruit, flat bread, and a warm drink from Old Helm's flask. Below us, three new islands drifted slowly into view, each one trailing a ribbon of mist. It felt like the sky itself was setting the table for what came next.
lunch:2.cnHint: 我们在云端的边缘一起吃____，眼前三座新的浮岛缓缓漂来。
lunch:2.hook: Old Helm folded his map and smiled — the next island was already within reach.
lunch:2.line: 'Eat your *lunch* while you can — after this, the sky gets a great deal more interesting.'

sentences.en: We sat on the edge of a cloud shelf and ate *lunch* together — dried fruit, flat bread, and a warm drink from Old Helm's flask.
Below us, three new islands drifted slowly into view, each one trailing a ribbon of mist.
sentences.cn: 我们下方，三座新的岛屿缓缓漂入视野，每一座都拖着一条薄雾的丝带。

sentences.en: It felt like the sky itself was setting the table for what came next.
sentences.cn: 感觉像是天空本身在为接下来的事铺好了桌子。

necessarily:2.en: Silverfang examined the recovered word-fragment and frowned. 'A new word doesn't *necessarily* open the next island right away,' she said. 'Sometimes it opens a door two steps ahead — one you didn't even know was there.' She handed it back to me, and I held it more carefully after that.
necessarily:2.cnHint: 银牙船长提醒我，得到一个新词并不____意味着下一座岛马上就会开启。
necessarily:2.hook: She pointed to the horizon, where a faint outline had already begun to appear.
necessarily:2.line: 'Finding the word doesn't *necessarily* mean the path is obvious — look further ahead.'

sentences.en: Silverfang examined the recovered word-fragment and frowned.
sentences.cn: 银牙检查了回收来的字片，皱起了眉头。

sentences.en: 'A new word doesn't *necessarily* open the next island right away,' she said.
'Sometimes it opens a door two steps ahead — one you didn't even know was there.'
sentences.cn: 有时候它打开的是两步之外的门——你甚至都不知道那扇门在那儿。

sentences.en: She handed it back to me, and I held it more carefully after that.
sentences.cn: 她把它递回给我，之后我拿它更小心了。

psychologist:2.en: Among the old records in the island library was a single page from a traveller who called herself a *psychologist* — someone who studied why people feared the sky. She had written: 'The islands are not the challenge. The challenge lives in the mind.' Old Helm read it aloud twice, quietly.
psychologist:2.cnHint: 图书馆的旧档案里，一位自称____的旅行者留下了一段令人深思的文字。
psychologist:2.hook: The last line of the page had been torn away — and no one knew what her conclusion was.
psychologist:2.line: 'A *psychologist* once wrote that the sky is only as wide as what you let yourself believe.'

sentences.en: Among the old records in the island library was a single page from a traveller who called herself a *psychologist* — someone who studied why people feared the sky.
She had written: 'The islands are not the challenge.
sentences.cn: 岛屿不是挑战。

sentences.en: The challenge lives in the mind.'
sentences.cn: 挑战活在人的心里。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it aloud twice, quietly.
sentences.cn: 老舵轻声读了两遍。

male:2.en: At the centre of the island we found a carved stone tablet. Bell read the old letters aloud: every *male* figure in the carving held a lantern, guiding boats through fog. Old Helm nodded slowly. 'They were lighthouse keepers,' he said. We rubbed a copy of the image onto paper, and a new word glowed at its edge.
male:2.cnHint: 石碑上的____人物手持灯笼，小铃认出这是古老的灯塔守护者图案，拓印后新词浮现。
male:2.hook: The word at the edge pointed to an island no map had ever named.
male:2.line: 'Every *male* keeper in this carving once guided ships through the darkest fog.'

sentences.en: At the centre of the island we found a carved stone tablet.
sentences.cn: 在岛的中央，我们找到了一块雕刻的石板。

sentences.en: Bell read the old letters aloud: every *male* figure in the carving held a lantern, guiding boats through fog.
Old Helm nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵缓缓点头。

sentences.en: 'They were lighthouse keepers,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他们是灯塔看守人，他说。

sentences.en: We rubbed a copy of the image onto paper, and a new word glowed at its edge.
sentences.cn: 我们把图像的拓片拓在纸上，它的边缘泛起了新的字光。

fish:2.en: A shallow pool sat in the hollow of the island, fed by a thin waterfall. Strange pale *fish* moved beneath the surface, each one carrying a tiny glowing mark on its side. Bell leaned close and whispered that the marks looked like letters. Old Helm scooped one gently up, and there it was — a new word, clear as starlight.
fish:2.cnHint: 一个水池里的____身上发着光，每条光纹都像字母，老舵轻轻捞起一条，新词就此浮现。
fish:2.hook: The fish slipped back into the water, but the word stayed in Old Helm's palm.
fish:2.line: 'These *fish* carry letters on their sides — this pool is a living dictionary.'

sentences.en: A shallow pool sat in the hollow of the island, fed by a thin waterfall.
sentences.cn: 一个浅水池窝在岛的凹陷处，由一条细细的瀑布补充水源。

sentences.en: Strange pale *fish* moved beneath the surface, each one carrying a tiny glowing mark on its side.
Bell leaned close and whispered that the marks looked like letters.
sentences.cn: 小铃靠近了，低声说那些标记看起来像字母。

sentences.en: Old Helm scooped one gently up, and there it was — a new word, clear as starlight.
sentences.cn: 老舵轻轻舀起一条，那里面——一个新字，清晰得像星光一样。

fashion:2.en: We landed on an island carpeted in soft moss, where tall figures made of twisted wire stood like statues. Each one wore scraps of cloth pinned in an elegant *fashion*, as if dressed for a grand occasion. Tucked inside the largest figure's collar was a folded note. Bell unfolded it, and a new word fell out like a secret.
fashion:2.cnHint: 铁丝人偶以优雅的____穿戴着布片，领口藏着一张折叠纸条，小铃打开后新词飘落而出。
fashion:2.hook: The note named a place none of us had ever dared to imagine reaching.
fashion:2.line: 'Whoever built these dressed them in *fashion* fit for the sky's own festival.'

sentences.en: We landed on an island carpeted in soft moss, where tall figures made of twisted wire stood like statues.
sentences.cn: 我们着陆在一座铺满柔软苔藓的岛上，那里有用扭转的铁丝做成的高大人形，像雕像一样站立着。

sentences.en: Each one wore scraps of cloth pinned in an elegant *fashion*, as if dressed for a grand occasion.
Tucked inside the largest figure's collar was a folded note.
sentences.cn: 卷在最大人形的衣领里有一张折起的纸条。

sentences.en: Bell unfolded it, and a new word fell out like a secret.
sentences.cn: 小铃打开了它，一个新字像秘密一样掉了出来。

weather:2.en: A brass cylinder sat on a tall post at the island's peak. Old Helm explained it was a *weather* reader — built to track wind, cloud, and rain across the floating sky. We turned a small dial on its side and the cylinder clicked open, revealing a rolled map fragment inside. Outside, the clouds began to part as if on cue.
weather:2.cnHint: 山顶的黄铜筒是测量____的装置，老舵转动表盘后筒子打开，里面藏着一张地图碎片。
weather:2.hook: The map fragment showed an island that only appeared during storms.
weather:2.line: 'This *weather* reader has been waiting years for someone to turn that dial.'

sentences.en: A brass cylinder sat on a tall post at the island's peak.
sentences.cn: 岛峰上的一根高柱子上放着一个黄铜圆筒。

sentences.en: Old Helm explained it was a *weather* reader — built to track wind, cloud, and rain across the floating sky.
We turned a small dial on its side and the cylinder clicked open, revealing a rolled map fragment inside.
sentences.cn: 我们转动了它一侧的小表盘，圆筒咔嚓一声打开了，里面卷着一张地图残片。

sentences.en: Outside, the clouds began to part as if on cue.
sentences.cn: 外面，云层仿佛收到了暗示似的开始散开。

device:2.en: Half-buried in the soil we dug up a small brass *device* no bigger than my fist, covered in tiny turning wheels. Bell oiled the wheels with a drop from her bottle, and they began to spin. Each wheel clicked to a letter, spelling out a word we had never collected before. Old Helm's eyes went wide.
device:2.cnHint: 小铃给挖出的小型____注油后，齿轮转动拼出了一个从未收集过的新词，老舵惊喜万分。
device:2.hook: The final wheel stopped, and the island beneath our feet gave a gentle shudder.
device:2.line: 'This little *device* just gave us a word the whole sky seems to have been guarding.'

sentences.en: Half-buried in the soil we dug up a small brass *device* no bigger than my fist, covered in tiny turning wheels.
Bell oiled the wheels with a drop from her bottle, and they began to spin.
sentences.cn: 小铃用她瓶里的油润滑了齿轮，它们开始转动起来。

sentences.en: Each wheel clicked to a letter, spelling out a word we had never collected before.
sentences.cn: 每个齿轮咔哒一声转到一个字母，拼出了我们从未见过的新词。

sentences.en: Old Helm's eyes went wide.
sentences.cn: 老舵的眼睛睁得很大。

farm:2.en: The island was striped with neat rows of glowing plants, each one bearing a small fruit shaped like a star. A sign at the entrance called it a sky *farm*, tended by no one we could see. At the end of the longest row stood a wooden post with a letter nailed to it. We pulled the letter free and read a new word written in careful, hopeful handwriting.
farm:2.cnHint: 无人打理的天空____种满星形果实，最长一行末端的木柱上钉着一封信，里面写有新词。
farm:2.hook: The handwriting on the letter matched the style of the tablet back on the first island.
farm:2.line: 'Whoever kept this *farm* left us the next word and then simply sailed away.'

sentences.en: The island was striped with neat rows of glowing plants, each one bearing a small fruit shaped like a star.
sentences.cn: 岛上布满了整齐的行列，闪闪发光的植物，每株都结着星形的小果子。

sentences.en: A sign at the entrance called it a sky *farm*, tended by no one we could see.
At the end of the longest row stood a wooden post with a letter nailed to it.
sentences.cn: 最长的那排末端立着一根木桩，上面钉着一封信。

sentences.en: We pulled the letter free and read a new word written in careful, hopeful handwriting.
sentences.cn: 我们扯下信纸，读到了用仔细、充满希望的笔迹写下的新词。

drug:2.en: Inside a small stone hut we found a shelf of glass bottles, each labelled in faded ink. Bell held one up to the starlight. Old Helm explained that long ago healers on this island had prepared every *drug* from island plants, treating travellers who passed through. Behind the shelf, carved into the wall, was a word we had never seen — our newest fragment.
drug:2.cnHint: 石屋药架上摆满瓶子，老舵说这里曾用岛上植物制备每种____，药架后的墙上刻着新词。
drug:2.hook: The carved word on the wall still smelled faintly of the herbs that surrounded it.
drug:2.line: 'Every *drug* on this shelf once helped a tired traveller find their strength again.'

sentences.en: Inside a small stone hut we found a shelf of glass bottles, each labelled in faded ink.
sentences.cn: 在一间小石屋里，我们找到了一架玻璃瓶子，每个都用褪色的墨水标着标签。

sentences.en: Bell held one up to the starlight.
sentences.cn: 小铃举起其中一个对着星光。

sentences.en: Old Helm explained that long ago healers on this island had prepared every *drug* from island plants, treating travellers who passed through.
Behind the shelf, carved into the wall, was a word we had never seen — our newest fragment.
sentences.cn: 在架子后面，刻在墙上的是我们从未见过的词——我们最新的片段。

heat:2.en: We crossed a field of black rock where thin cracks glowed orange below. The *heat* rising from the cracks kept the whole island warm even under the coldest stars. Bell noticed the cracks formed a pattern — lines crossing like a letter. We traced the shape together, and just like that, a new word came to all three of us at once.
heat:2.cnHint: 岩缝散发的____使小岛温暖，小铃发现这些裂缝拼成了一个字母图案，三人同时认出了新词。
heat:2.hook: The pattern pointed like an arrow toward the darkest corner of the sky.
heat:2.line: 'Feel that *heat* rising — this island has been writing its name in light all along.'

sentences.en: We crossed a field of black rock where thin cracks glowed orange below.
sentences.cn: 我们穿过了一片黑石地，细细的裂缝下泛着橙色的光。

sentences.en: The *heat* rising from the cracks kept the whole island warm even under the coldest stars.
Bell noticed the cracks formed a pattern — lines crossing like a letter.
sentences.cn: 小铃注意到裂缝形成了一个图案——交叉的线条像一个字母。

sentences.en: We traced the shape together, and just like that, a new word came to all three of us at once.
sentences.cn: 我们一起描出了这个形状，就这样，一个新词同时出现在我们三个人的脑子里。

destroy:2.en: The old tower at the edge of Ashfall Island held one last warning. A carved sign read: 'Do not *destroy* the stone lantern — it is the only light the map remembers.' Old Helm traced the letters slowly. We had nearly knocked the lantern over climbing up. Now we set it straight and watched the map glow.
destroy:2.cnHint: 艾什法尔岛边缘的石灯笼差点被我们打翻，老舵手读懂了警告，我们小心地将它____了。
destroy:2.hook: Beyond the lantern's glow, a hidden passage cracked open in the stone.
destroy:2.line: 'If we *destroy* that lantern, the whole map goes dark,' Old Helm warned.

sentences.en: The old tower at the edge of Ashfall Island held one last warning.
sentences.cn: 灰烬岛边缘的老塔楼里有最后一个警告。

sentences.en: A carved sign read: 'Do not *destroy* the stone lantern — it is the only light the map remembers.'
Old Helm traced the letters slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵缓缓描过字母。

sentences.en: We had nearly knocked the lantern over climbing up.
sentences.cn: 我们爬上去的时候差点把灯笼碰倒。

sentences.en: Now we set it straight and watched the map glow.
sentences.cn: 现在我们把它扶正了，看着地图发光。

drop:2.en: Bell found it tucked inside a hollow branch: a single glass bottle with a rolled note inside. 'One *drop* of starwater on the map and a new island appears,' the note said. We only had one chance. Bell uncorked the bottle with steady hands, and the map bloomed like a flower.
drop:2.cnHint: 贝尔在树洞里找到一张字条，说只需将一____星之水滴在地图上，新的岛屿就会出现。
drop:2.hook: The new island on the map was shaped exactly like a key.
drop:2.line: 'Just one *drop*,' Bell whispered, 'so don't shake my arm.'

sentences.en: Bell found it tucked inside a hollow branch: a single glass bottle with a rolled note inside.
sentences.cn: 小铃在一根空心树枝里找到了它：一个玻璃瓶子，里面卷着一张纸条。

sentences.en: 'One *drop* of starwater on the map and a new island appears,' the note said.
We only had one chance.
sentences.cn: 我们只有一次机会。

sentences.en: Bell uncorked the bottle with steady hands, and the map bloomed like a flower.
sentences.cn: 小铃稳稳地拔开瓶塞，地图像花儿一样绽放了。

efficiency:2.en: Silverfang spread three different routes across the deck table. 'We judge by *efficiency*,' she said firmly. 'The shortest path wastes the least wind.' Old Helm disagreed — the longer route passed a word-market we needed. In the end the map chose for us: only one path glowed.
efficiency:2.cnHint: 银牙船长坚持以____为原则选路，但老舵手认为绕远路经过词市更值得。
efficiency:2.hook: The glowing path curved toward a cloud nobody in the troupe had ever crossed.
efficiency:2.line: '*Efficiency* wins every argument when the wind is this strong,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: Silverfang spread three different routes across the deck table.
sentences.cn: 银牙在甲板桌上铺开了三条不同的路线。

sentences.en: 'We judge by *efficiency*,' she said firmly.
'The shortest path wastes the least wind.'
sentences.cn: "最短的路线浪费最少的风。"

sentences.en: Old Helm disagreed — the longer route passed a word-market we needed.
sentences.cn: 老舵不同意——更长的路线会经过我们需要的词语市场。

sentences.en: In the end the map chose for us: only one path glowed.
sentences.cn: 最后地图替我们选择了：只有一条路线发着光。

italian:2.en: Tucked under a loose tile on Mossvault Island was a folded page covered in neat, looping script. 'That looks like *Italian*,' I said, surprised. Old Helm laughed softly. 'No — it is the island's own tongue. But the curves do remind me of far-away places.' We copied every word carefully onto our map.
italian:2.cnHint: 在苔穹岛的松动地砖下，我们发现了一张用弯曲文字写成的纸页，我猜是____语，但老舵手说那是岛屿自己的文字。
italian:2.hook: One copied word began to pulse with a faint golden light.
italian:2.line: 'It looks *Italian* to me,' I said, 'but the map seems to understand it.'

sentences.en: Tucked under a loose tile on Mossvault Island was a folded page covered in neat, looping script.
sentences.cn: 苔地岛上一块松动的瓷砖下塞着一张折叠的纸，上面写满了整齐、卷曲的笔迹。

sentences.en: 'That looks like *Italian*,' I said, surprised.
Old Helm laughed softly.
sentences.cn: 老舵轻轻笑了。

sentences.en: 'No — it is the island's own tongue.
sentences.cn: "不——这是岛屿自己的语言。

sentences.en: But the curves do remind me of far-away places.'
sentences.cn: 但这些曲线确实让我想起了远方的地方。"

sentences.en: We copied every word carefully onto our map.
sentences.cn: 我们小心地把每一个字都抄到了地图上。

newspaper:2.en: A stack of thin, yellowed sheets lay pinned under a rock on Driftledge Island. Bell held one up. 'A *newspaper*,' she said, delighted. 'From a troupe that passed here long ago.' The top headline read: THIRD WORD FOUND — EASTERN ARCH UNLOCKED. We looked at each other and grinned.
newspaper:2.cnHint: 在漂岩岛上，贝尔发现了一叠古老的____，记载着前人找到第三个词、打开东拱门的消息。
newspaper:2.hook: The date on the paper was exactly one hundred years ago today.
newspaper:2.line: 'This *newspaper* is older than our ship,' Bell said, eyes wide.

sentences.en: A stack of thin, yellowed sheets lay pinned under a rock on Driftledge Island.
sentences.cn: 一沓又薄又泛黄的纸张被压在漂流崖岛的一块石头下。

sentences.en: Bell held one up.
sentences.cn: 小铃举起一张。

sentences.en: 'A *newspaper*,' she said, delighted.
'From a troupe that passed here long ago.'
sentences.cn: "来自很久前经过这里的一支剧团。"

sentences.en: The top headline read: THIRD WORD FOUND — EASTERN ARCH UNLOCKED.
sentences.cn: 头条新闻读着：第三个词被找到——东拱门已解锁。

sentences.en: We looked at each other and grinned.
sentences.cn: 我们互相看了看，咧嘴笑了。

piece:2.en: The map had a gap right at its centre — a small blank space no word had filled. Old Helm pulled a worn tile from his coat pocket. 'The missing *piece*,' he said quietly, setting it down. It clicked into place like it had always been there, and a soft chime rang across the whole deck.
piece:2.cnHint: 老舵手从口袋里取出一块旧瓦片，将它嵌入地图中央的空白处，那正是缺失的____。
piece:2.hook: Where the gap had been, a name appeared in letters made of starlight.
piece:2.line: 'Every map has one missing *piece*,' Old Helm said, 'and patience finds it.'

sentences.en: The map had a gap right at its centre — a small blank space no word had filled.
sentences.cn: 地图的正中央有个空白——一个没有词填补的小空隙。

sentences.en: Old Helm pulled a worn tile from his coat pocket.
sentences.cn: 老舵从他的大衣口袋里掏出一块磨损的瓷砖。

sentences.en: 'The missing *piece*,' he said quietly, setting it down.
It clicked into place like it had always been there, and a soft chime rang across the whole deck.
sentences.cn: 它咔哒一声就位，就像它一直都在那儿一样，整个甲板上响起了一声柔和的铃声。

target:2.en: Bell drew a neat circle on the map with her compass. 'That peak is our *target* for tomorrow,' she said. 'If we reach it before the morning star fades, the word inside will still be warm.' Silverfang nodded without argument, which meant she agreed. I started packing before anyone asked me to.
target:2.cnHint: 贝尔用圆规在地图上画出明天的____，那座山峰里的词语只在晨星消失前依然温热。
target:2.hook: Somewhere on that peak, a light blinked once, then went dark.
target:2.line: 'Mark that peak as our *target*,' Bell said, 'and we move at first light.'

sentences.en: Bell drew a neat circle on the map with her compass.
sentences.cn: 小铃用她的圆规在地图上画了一个整齐的圆圈。

sentences.en: 'That peak is our *target* for tomorrow,' she said.
'If we reach it before the morning star fades, the word inside will still be warm.'
sentences.cn: "如果我们在晨星褪去之前到达那里，里面的词还会是温热的。"

sentences.en: Silverfang nodded without argument, which meant she agreed.
sentences.cn: 银牙没有异议地点了点头，这意味着她同意了。

sentences.en: I started packing before anyone asked me to.
sentences.cn: 我还没等任何人问我，就开始收拾东西了。

actual:2.en: We had imagined the Library of Winds as a grand hall of stone. The *actual* place was a single small room carved into a cloud, walls lined with humming glass jars. Each jar held a word, buzzing softly like a caught firefly. Old Helm spread his arms wide and laughed. 'Better,' he said.
actual:2.cnHint: 我们想象中的风之图书馆是宏伟大厅，但____的地方是一间刻在云层里的小屋，墙上满是装着词语的玻璃罐。
actual:2.hook: One jar in the corner had no label — and it hummed the loudest of all.
actual:2.line: 'The *actual* library is better than any story we told about it,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: We had imagined the Library of Winds as a grand hall of stone.
sentences.cn: 我们曾想象风之图书馆是一间宽敞的石头大厅。

sentences.en: The *actual* place was a single small room carved into a cloud, walls lined with humming glass jars.
Each jar held a word, buzzing softly like a caught firefly.
sentences.cn: 每个罐子里装着一个词，轻轻嗡鸣着，像被捕住的萤火虫。

sentences.en: Old Helm spread his arms wide and laughed.
sentences.cn: 老舵张开双臂，笑了。

sentences.en: 'Better,' he said.
sentences.cn: "更好，"他说。

pursue:2.en: The old map showed a faint trail leading off the edge of our last island. 'We must *pursue* every lead,' Old Helm said, rolling the parchment with care. Bell plotted a new heading before the stars could shift. By morning, a silver thread of light stretched across the sky, pointing somewhere none of us had ever been.
pursue:2.cnHint: 老舵手说，我们必须____每一条线索，领航员随即定好了新航向。
pursue:2.hook: The silver thread was moving, and it seemed to know we were following.
pursue:2.line: 'We must *pursue* every lead, no matter how faint it looks.'

sentences.en: The old map showed a faint trail leading off the edge of our last island.
sentences.cn: 破旧的地图上显示出一条模糊的踪迹，延伸到我们最后一座岛屿的边缘之外。

sentences.en: 'We must *pursue* every lead,' Old Helm said, rolling the parchment with care.
Bell plotted a new heading before the stars could shift.
sentences.cn: 小铃在星辰移动之前就绘制了新的航向。

sentences.en: By morning, a silver thread of light stretched across the sky, pointing somewhere none of us had ever been.
sentences.cn: 到了天亮时分，天空中伸展出一条银色的光线，指向我们从未到过的某个地方。

site:2.en: Bell unfolded a cloth etched with tiny symbols and pointed to a circle near its centre. 'This *site* was marked by the first troupe,' she said softly. We landed on a flat, mossy island where old stone pillars still stood in a ring. Old Helm walked among them slowly, and I could tell the place meant something deep to him.
site:2.cnHint: 领航员指着地图上的一个圆圈说，这个____是第一支队伍留下的标记。
site:2.hook: Between two pillars, a new symbol had been carved — and it was still warm.
site:2.line: 'This *site* was marked long before any of us were born.'

sentences.en: Bell unfolded a cloth etched with tiny symbols and pointed to a circle near its centre.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开了一块布料，上面刻着细小的符号，她指向布料中心附近的一个圆圈。

sentences.en: 'This *site* was marked by the first troupe,' she said softly.
We landed on a flat, mossy island where old stone pillars still stood in a ring.
sentences.cn: 我们在一座长满苔藓的平坦岛屿上着陆，古老的石柱仍然成环形矗立。

sentences.en: Old Helm walked among them slowly, and I could tell the place meant something deep to him.
sentences.cn: 老舵在石柱间缓缓行走，我能看出这个地方对他意义深远。

absorb:2.en: The word we found that morning glowed like a small lamp in my palm. Old Helm told me to hold it close and let my mind *absorb* every detail — the shape, the colour, the faint hum it gave off. I stood still for a long moment. When I opened my eyes, a new island had risen on the horizon, pale and quiet and waiting.
absorb:2.cnHint: 老舵手让我静下心来，用心____这个发光词语的每一个细节。
absorb:2.hook: The island on the horizon blinked once, as if it had seen me too.
absorb:2.line: 'Let your mind *absorb* it fully — only then will the map respond.'

sentences.en: The word we found that morning glowed like a small lamp in my palm.
sentences.cn: 那天早上我们找到的这个词在我的掌心里闪闪发光，如同一盏小灯。

sentences.en: Old Helm told me to hold it close and let my mind *absorb* every detail — the shape, the colour, the faint hum it gave off.
I stood still for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 我静静地站了很久。

sentences.en: When I opened my eyes, a new island had risen on the horizon, pale and quiet and waiting.
sentences.cn: 当我睁开眼睛时，地平线上升起了一座新的岛屿，苍白而寂静，等待着我们。

advance:2.en: Silverfang's ship pulled alongside ours just as we prepared to move on. 'You think your little troupe can *advance* past the Drift Gate before I do?' he called out with a grin that was more fun than threat. Old Helm simply raised one hand in a quiet wave. Bell had already set our course, and we were moving before Silverfang finished laughing.
advance:2.cnHint: 竞争船长笑着问我们是否能在他之前____越过漂流之门。
advance:2.hook: Behind us, Silverfang's ship suddenly went very quiet.
advance:2.line: 'You think you can *advance* past the Drift Gate before my crew?'

sentences.en: Silverfang's ship pulled alongside ours just as we prepared to move on.
sentences.cn: 银牙的船恰好在我们准备启程时靠了过来。

sentences.en: 'You think your little troupe can *advance* past the Drift Gate before I do?' he called out with a grin that was more fun than threat.
Old Helm simply raised one hand in a quiet wave.
sentences.cn: 老舵只是静静地抬起一只手挥了挥。

sentences.en: Bell had already set our course, and we were moving before Silverfang finished laughing.
sentences.cn: 小铃已经设定好了航线，在银牙笑声还未消散前我们就驶离了。

capable:2.en: I almost dropped the word-fragment when the wind picked up, but Bell caught my wrist with one steady hand. 'You are more *capable* than you know,' she said, and something in her voice made me believe it. I gripped the fragment tight, and it sang a single clear note that spread across the clouds like a ripple on still water.
capable:2.cnHint: 领航员握住我的手腕，说我比自己想象的更____。
capable:2.hook: The note from the fragment had not faded — it was growing louder.
capable:2.line: 'You are far more *capable* than you give yourself credit for.'

sentences.en: I almost dropped the word-fragment when the wind picked up, but Bell caught my wrist with one steady hand.
sentences.cn: 风吹起时我几乎要掉落这个词的碎片，但小铃用她稳定的一只手抓住了我的手腕。

sentences.en: 'You are more *capable* than you know,' she said, and something in her voice made me believe it.
I gripped the fragment tight, and it sang a single clear note that spread across the clouds like a ripple on still water.
sentences.cn: 我紧紧握住这个碎片，它发出了一个清晰的音符，如同静水上的涟漪一样在云朵间扩散开去。

dollar:2.en: On the market island of Thresh, a merchant held out a single worn coin and called it a *dollar* of the old sky-trade, worth one true word in exchange. Old Helm studied it without touching it. Bell leaned in and whispered that the last troupe to accept such a coin had never found their way home. We smiled politely and moved on.
dollar:2.cnHint: 商人拿出一枚旧硬币，说这枚____可以换一个真正的词语碎片。
dollar:2.hook: The merchant watched us leave with an expression that was not quite a smile.
dollar:2.line: 'One *dollar* of sky-trade, and I will give you a word you cannot find elsewhere.'

sentences.en: On the market island of Thresh, a merchant held out a single worn coin and called it a *dollar* of the old sky-trade, worth one true word in exchange.
Old Helm studied it without touching it.
sentences.cn: 老舵研究了它，但没有去触碰它。

sentences.en: Bell leaned in and whispered that the last troupe to accept such a coin had never found their way home.
sentences.cn: 小铃靠近过来，低声说上一支队伍接受过这样的硬币后就再也没找到回家的路。

sentences.en: We smiled politely and moved on.
sentences.cn: 我们礼貌地笑了笑，继续往前走。

double:2.en: The passage through the Arch Clouds took *double* the time Bell had planned — the winds kept folding back on themselves, pushing us gently in circles. Old Helm brewed tea and said nothing, which I had learned meant everything was fine. When we finally broke through, the sky ahead held two islands side by side, mirror-close, like a gift waiting to be opened.
double:2.cnHint: 穿越云拱花了预计____的时间，但突破之后，前方出现了两座并排的岛屿。
double:2.hook: The two islands were identical in every way — except one had no shadow.
double:2.line: 'It took *double* the time, but look at what we found waiting for us.'

sentences.en: The passage through the Arch Clouds took *double* the time Bell had planned — the winds kept folding back on themselves, pushing us gently in circles.
Old Helm brewed tea and said nothing, which I had learned meant everything was fine.
sentences.cn: 老舵泡了茶，什么也没说，这我已经学会了意味着一切都很好。

sentences.en: When we finally broke through, the sky ahead held two islands side by side, mirror-close, like a gift waiting to be opened.
sentences.cn: 当我们终于冲破云层时，前方的天空里并排浮着两座岛屿，镜像般地靠近，就像一份在等待被打开的礼物。

federal:2.en: The island had a carved stone gate with words in an old script above it. Bell translated slowly: it had once been a *federal* meeting ground, where every floating island sent one voice to speak for its people. Old Helm touched the stone and smiled. 'Somewhere, that agreement still holds,' he said. I wrote the word down, and the gate creaked open on its own.
federal:2.cnHint: 领航员翻译石碑文字，说这里曾是各岛派代表集会的____议事之地。
federal:2.hook: Beyond the open gate, every island we had ever visited glittered on the horizon at once.
federal:2.line: 'This was a *federal* ground — every island once had a voice here.'

sentences.en: The island had a carved stone gate with words in an old script above it.
sentences.cn: 岛屿上有一道刻着字的石门，上面是古老文字的铭文。

sentences.en: Bell translated slowly: it had once been a *federal* meeting ground, where every floating island sent one voice to speak for its people.
Old Helm touched the stone and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵摸了摸石头，笑了。

sentences.en: 'Somewhere, that agreement still holds,' he said.
sentences.cn: "这份协议仍然有效，在某个地方，"他说。

sentences.en: I wrote the word down, and the gate creaked open on its own.
sentences.cn: 我把这个词写了下来，石门自己咔嗒一声打开了。

gather:2.en: At the edge of the map, where the last island floated above empty sky, the troupe found a stone bowl. Strange lights began to *gather* around it — soft, slow, like fireflies answering a call. Old Helm held out his hand, and the lights settled on his palm, forming a shape none of us had seen before.
gather:2.cnHint: 在地图边缘，奇异的光芒在石碗周围____，落在团长手心，拼成一个神秘形状。
gather:2.hook: The shape in his palm was not a symbol — it was a door.
gather:2.line: 'Watch how they *gather*, one by one, as if they remember this place,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: At the edge of the map, where the last island floated above empty sky, the troupe found a stone bowl.
sentences.cn: 在地图的边缘，在最后一座岛屿悬浮在空荡荡的天空上方，队伍找到了一只石碗。

sentences.en: Strange lights began to *gather* around it — soft, slow, like fireflies answering a call.
Old Helm held out his hand, and the lights settled on his palm, forming a shape none of us had seen before.
sentences.cn: 老舵伸出了他的手，光点落在他的掌心，形成了一个我们都没见过的形状。

imagine:2.en: Bell unrolled the blank half of the map on a flat stone and stared at it for a long time. 'You have to *imagine* what is not yet drawn,' she said quietly. She closed her eyes, and when she opened them, a faint line had appeared on the paper — a path none of us had walked.
imagine:2.cnHint: 领航员盯着空白地图，说你必须____出尚未绘制的地方，随后纸上浮现出一条从未走过的路。
imagine:2.hook: The line on the map was still moving, slowly, toward the stars.
imagine:2.line: '*Imagine* the next island before it appears, and it will come,' Bell said softly.

sentences.en: Bell unrolled the blank half of the map on a flat stone and stared at it for a long time.
sentences.cn: 小铃在一块平石上展开了地图的空白部分，盯着看了很长时间。

sentences.en: 'You have to *imagine* what is not yet drawn,' she said quietly.
She closed her eyes, and when she opened them, a faint line had appeared on the paper — a path none of us had walked.
sentences.cn: 她闭上眼睛，当她睁开眼睛时，纸上出现了一条模糊的线——一条我们还没有走过的路。

instance:2.en: Old Helm pulled a small glass jar from his coat. Inside it floated a single word, glowing faintly. 'Every *instance* of a word we collect becomes part of the map,' he explained, placing the jar beside six others on the stone shelf carved into the cliff. Each jar held a different colour of light.
instance:2.cnHint: 团长向我们解释，每一个被收集的词语____都会成为地图的一部分，他把玻璃瓶排列在石架上。
instance:2.hook: But one jar was empty — and it was labelled with our next destination.
instance:2.line: 'This *instance* is rare — a word that opens rather than marks,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm pulled a small glass jar from his coat.
sentences.cn: 老舵从他的外套里掏出了一个小玻璃罐。

sentences.en: Inside it floated a single word, glowing faintly.
sentences.cn: 里面漂浮着一个词，微弱地闪闪发光。

sentences.en: 'Every *instance* of a word we collect becomes part of the map,' he explained, placing the jar beside six others on the stone shelf carved into the cliff.
Each jar held a different colour of light.
sentences.cn: 每个罐子里都装着不同颜色的光。

numerous:2.en: The archive room inside the cliff held *numerous* small drawers, each carved with a word in a script I could not read. Bell moved through the rows quickly, as if she had been here before. When I pulled one drawer open by mistake, a sound like wind through tall grass filled the whole room.
numerous:2.cnHint: 悬崖内部的档案室里有____个小抽屉，我不小心拉开一个，整个房间里响起了风吹草地的声音。
numerous:2.hook: Bell froze and whispered, 'Close it — that word is not ready yet.'
numerous:2.line: 'There are *numerous* words still sleeping here — do not wake them all,' Bell warned.

sentences.en: The archive room inside the cliff held *numerous* small drawers, each carved with a word in a script I could not read.
Bell moved through the rows quickly, as if she had been here before.
sentences.cn: 小铃快速穿过那一排排抽屉，仿佛她曾经来过这里。

sentences.en: When I pulled one drawer open by mistake, a sound like wind through tall grass filled the whole room.
sentences.cn: 当我不小心打开其中一个抽屉时，整个房间里充满了似风吹过高草的声音。

puzzle:2.en: A flat stone near the cliff edge was covered in carved circles and lines that overlapped in strange ways. It was clearly a *puzzle*, but touching one circle made another shift, and soon I had no idea what the original shape had been. Silverfang arrived, studied it for one second, and pressed the centre.
puzzle:2.cnHint: 悬崖边有一块刻满圆圈和线条的石板，这个____让我越弄越乱，竞争船长却只用一秒就找到了解法。
puzzle:2.hook: Under the stone, something was breathing.
puzzle:2.line: 'Every *puzzle* here has one still point — find it first,' said Silverfang calmly.

sentences.en: A flat stone near the cliff edge was covered in carved circles and lines that overlapped in strange ways.
sentences.cn: 悬崖边的一块平石上刻满了圆圈和线条，它们以奇异的方式交叠在一起。

sentences.en: It was clearly a *puzzle*, but touching one circle made another shift, and soon I had no idea what the original shape had been.
Silverfang arrived, studied it for one second, and pressed the centre.
sentences.cn: 银牙走过来，看了一秒钟，然后按下了中心。

remind:2.en: Tucked into a crack in the cliff wall was a folded piece of cloth. On it, in careful ink, someone had written a short message. The words were faded, but they seemed to *remind* Old Helm of something — he went very quiet, folded the cloth twice, and placed it inside his coat without a word.
remind:2.cnHint: 藏在石缝里的布条上有一段字迹，它似乎____了团长什么，他沉默地把它折好收进了外套。
remind:2.hook: Whatever it said, it changed the direction we were heading.
remind:2.line: 'These words *remind* me that someone else reached the edge before us,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Tucked into a crack in the cliff wall was a folded piece of cloth.
sentences.cn: 悬崖墙的裂缝里塞着一块折起来的布料。

sentences.en: On it, in careful ink, someone had written a short message.
sentences.cn: 上面用工整的墨迹写着一条短讯息。

sentences.en: The words were faded, but they seemed to *remind* Old Helm of something — he went very quiet, folded the cloth twice, and placed it inside his coat without a word.

truly:2.en: The final marker on our portion of the map was a small tower of stacked stones. When I placed my hand on the top stone, the whole stack lit up from inside. Bell laughed softly. 'Now you are *truly* part of the troupe,' she said. Above us, a new island had appeared out of the dark sky.
truly:2.cnHint: 当我触碰石塔时它从内部发光，领航员说我现在____成为了队伍的一员，天空中出现了新的岛屿。
truly:2.hook: The new island was already drifting closer, and it carried a sound like music.
truly:2.line: 'You are *truly* part of this journey now — the map knows you,' Bell said warmly.

sentences.en: The final marker on our portion of the map was a small tower of stacked stones.
sentences.cn: 我们这段地图上最后的标记是一个小小的石头堆。

sentences.en: When I placed my hand on the top stone, the whole stack lit up from inside.
sentences.cn: 我把手放在顶部的石头上，整个石堆从里面亮了起来。

sentences.en: Bell laughed softly.
sentences.cn: 小铃轻声笑了。

sentences.en: 'Now you are *truly* part of the troupe,' she said.
Above us, a new island had appeared out of the dark sky.
sentences.cn: 我们上空，一座新的岛屿从黑暗的天空中浮现出来。

valuable:2.en: Silverfang set a small chest on the ground near the cliff edge and opened it without ceremony. Inside was not gold or jewels. 'These are the *valuable* things,' he said, pointing to the worn notebooks, old maps, and tiny jars of ink nested in the chest. 'Ideas travel farther than any coin.'
valuable:2.cnHint: 竞争船长打开小箱子，里面装的不是金银，而是笔记本和旧地图——他说这些才是真正____的东西。
valuable:2.hook: At the bottom of the chest lay a map with no edges at all.
valuable:2.line: 'The most *valuable* thing we carry is what we have learned, not what we own,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: Silverfang set a small chest on the ground near the cliff edge and opened it without ceremony.
sentences.cn: 银牙在悬崖边放下一个小箱子，随意地打开了它。

sentences.en: Inside was not gold or jewels.
sentences.cn: 里面没有金子也没有珠宝。

sentences.en: 'These are the *valuable* things,' he said, pointing to the worn notebooks, old maps, and tiny jars of ink nested in the chest.
'Ideas travel farther than any coin.'
sentences.cn: '想法的传播范围比任何金币都远。'

writer:2.en: Near the edge of the last island, I found a small stone tablet half-buried in moss. The name carved on it belonged to the *writer* of our oldest map — someone Old Helm had searched for across many skies. The letters were worn, but the final word was clear: 'onward.'
writer:2.cnHint: 在最后一座岛的边缘，我发现了一块石碑，上面刻着我们最古老地图的____的名字。
writer:2.hook: But the tablet was still warm, as if someone had just left it.
writer:2.line: 'The *writer* of this map was here not long ago,' Old Helm said softly.

sentences.en: Near the edge of the last island, I found a small stone tablet half-buried in moss.
sentences.cn: 在最后一座岛的边缘，我发现了一块半埋在苔藓里的小石碑。

sentences.en: The name carved on it belonged to the *writer* of our oldest map — someone Old Helm had searched for across many skies.
The letters were worn, but the final word was clear: 'onward.'
sentences.cn: 字迹磨损了，但最后一个词清晰可辨：'继续前行'。

addition:2.en: Bell spread the recovered map across the floor of the ship. In *addition* to the six islands we already knew, three new ones glowed at the edges, drawn in silver ink we had never seen before. Old Helm touched one gently and smiled without a word.
addition:2.cnHint: 小铃展开地图，发现除了已知岛屿之外，还有____的三座新岛屿发着银光。
addition:2.hook: The silver ink was still wet.
addition:2.line: 'In *addition* to what we know, the map shows three more islands,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Bell spread the recovered map across the floor of the ship.
sentences.cn: 小铃把找回来的地图铺在船舱的地板上。

sentences.en: In *addition* to the six islands we already knew, three new ones glowed at the edges, drawn in silver ink we had never seen before.
Old Helm touched one gently and smiled without a word.
sentences.cn: 老舵轻轻碰了碰其中一个，无言地微笑了。

alternative:2.en: The bridge ahead had crumbled away. Old Helm studied the gap, then looked left — a narrow rope path stretched between two rocks. 'There is always an *alternative*,' he said. We crossed single file, the wind pulling at our coats, the stars watching from above.
alternative:2.cnHint: 桥断了，老舵发现了另一条绳索小路，他说总有____可以选择。
alternative:2.hook: Halfway across, the rope gave a single, sharp creak.
alternative:2.line: 'There is always an *alternative* if you look carefully enough,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The bridge ahead had crumbled away.
sentences.cn: 前面的桥已经坍塌了。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied the gap, then looked left — a narrow rope path stretched between two rocks.
sentences.cn: 老舵研究着这道裂口，然后朝左看了看——一条狭窄的绳索小径在两块岩石之间延伸。

sentences.en: 'There is always an *alternative*,' he said.
We crossed single file, the wind pulling at our coats, the stars watching from above.
sentences.cn: 我们排成一队穿过去，风拉扯着我们的外套，星星在上方注视着我们。

amazing:2.en: Silverfang pulled a glass bottle from a crevice in the cliff wall. Inside was a rolled note and a tiny glowing stone. 'This is *amazing*,' Bell whispered, holding it up to the starlight. The stone pulsed like a slow heartbeat, and the note inside showed a path none of us had mapped.
amazing:2.cnHint: 银牙在峭壁缝隙中找到一个装有发光石头的瓶子，小铃觉得这真是太____了。
amazing:2.hook: The glowing stone suddenly blinked twice — as if answering a question.
amazing:2.line: 'It is *amazing* that something so small could hold an entire path,' Bell whispered.

sentences.en: Silverfang pulled a glass bottle from a crevice in the cliff wall.
sentences.cn: 银牙从悬崖墙的一道缝隙里拉出一个玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: Inside was a rolled note and a tiny glowing stone.
sentences.cn: 里面是一张卷起的纸条和一块微微发光的小石头。

sentences.en: 'This is *amazing*,' Bell whispered, holding it up to the starlight.
The stone pulsed like a slow heartbeat, and the note inside showed a path none of us had mapped.
sentences.cn: 那块石头像缓慢的心跳一样跳动，里面的纸条显示出了一条我们都没有绘过的路径。

ease:2.en: After days of stormy skies, we landed on a small warm island where soft grass covered everything. Old Helm sat down and breathed out slowly. The *ease* in his face was something I had not seen before — no map to read, no wind to fight, just still air and starlight.
ease:2.cnHint: 在平静小岛上休息时，我第一次看到老舵脸上流露出真正的____与放松。
ease:2.hook: Then Bell spotted footprints in the grass — too small to be ours.
ease:2.line: 'Let this *ease* stay with you; there are harder islands still ahead,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: After days of stormy skies, we landed on a small warm island where soft grass covered everything.
sentences.cn: 经过几天暴风雨天气后，我们登陆了一座温暖的小岛，柔软的草覆盖了一切。

sentences.en: Old Helm sat down and breathed out slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵坐下来，缓缓呼出一口气。

sentences.en: The *ease* in his face was something I had not seen before — no map to read, no wind to fight, just still air and starlight.

frequent:2.en: Bell noticed that one star above us had grown brighter. She checked her notes and said our ship had made *frequent* passes over this spot without stopping — six times in two seasons. 'We kept missing something,' she said, pointing down at a faint door-shaped outline in the rock below.
frequent:2.cnHint: 小铃发现我们的船曾____多次经过这个地点，而每次都错过了岩石上那扇隐约的门。
frequent:2.hook: The door-shaped outline began to fill with soft gold light.
frequent:2.line: 'Our *frequent* visits here were never a mistake — we were being led,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Bell noticed that one star above us had grown brighter.
sentences.cn: 小铃注意到我们上方的一颗星星变得更亮了。

sentences.en: She checked her notes and said our ship had made *frequent* passes over this spot without stopping — six times in two seasons.
'We kept missing something,' she said, pointing down at a faint door-shaped outline in the rock below.
sentences.cn: '我们一直在错过什么，'她指着下方岩石上一个模糊的门形轮廓说。

hope:2.en: The last fragment of the chapter map was missing. We searched every pocket and bag until I remembered the torn piece I had kept since my first day with the troupe. I pressed it into place, and the whole map lit up. Old Helm looked at me with quiet *hope* — the kind that asks nothing back.
hope:2.cnHint: 地图最后一块碎片找不到了，直到我拼上了自己保存的那片，老舵眼中流露出温柔的____。
hope:2.hook: The completed map showed an island no one had ever named.
hope:2.line: 'You carried more *hope* with you than you knew,' Old Helm told me.

sentences.en: The last fragment of the chapter map was missing.
sentences.cn: 章节地图的最后一片碎片不见了。

sentences.en: We searched every pocket and bag until I remembered the torn piece I had kept since my first day with the troupe.
sentences.cn: 我们搜遍了每个口袋和包，直到我想起了从加入队伍第一天就留着的那张撕破的纸片。

sentences.en: I pressed it into place, and the whole map lit up.
sentences.cn: 我把它拼了上去，整张地图亮了起来。

sentences.en: Old Helm looked at me with quiet *hope* — the kind that asks nothing back.

imply:2.en: Silverfang handed me a folded page he had taken from the cliff archive. The symbols did not say anything directly, but their arrangement seemed to *imply* that the edge of the chapter map was not an ending — it was a door. I read it twice to be sure I was not imagining it.
imply:2.cnHint: 银牙交给我一页档案，上面的符号没有明说，但似乎____地图的尽头其实是一扇门。
imply:2.hook: Old Helm read over my shoulder and said only: 'Yes.'
imply:2.line: 'These signs *imply* something the writer did not wish to say aloud,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Silverfang handed me a folded page he had taken from the cliff archive.
sentences.cn: 银牙递给我一页他从悬崖档案里取出的折叠纸张。

sentences.en: The symbols did not say anything directly, but their arrangement seemed to *imply* that the edge of the chapter map was not an ending — it was a door.
I read it twice to be sure I was not imagining it.
sentences.cn: 我读了两遍，确保自己没有想象出来。

pose:2.en: At the edge of Cloudbreak Island, we found a stone figure frozen mid-step, arms wide, chin lifted. 'Someone carved their captain in a proud *pose*,' Old Helm said softly. Tucked beneath the statue's foot was a folded map fragment, still dry after what must have been many, many years.
pose:2.cnHint: 我们在石像脚下发现了一张地图碎片，石像摆出一个骄傲的____。
pose:2.hook: The map showed an island that none of our charts had ever named.
pose:2.line: 'Someone carved their captain in a proud *pose*,' Old Helm said softly.

sentences.en: At the edge of Cloudbreak Island, we found a stone figure frozen mid-step, arms wide, chin lifted.
sentences.cn: 云端岛的边缘，我们发现了一尊石像，冻结在迈步的姿态中，双臂张开，下巴昂起。

sentences.en: 'Someone carved their captain in a proud *pose*,' Old Helm said softly.
Tucked beneath the statue's foot was a folded map fragment, still dry after what must have been many, many years.
sentences.cn: 雕像脚下塞着一张折叠的地图碎片，历经了似乎许多许多年，纸张依然干燥。

stimulate:2.en: Bell pressed the glowing word-crystal against the iron door and a low hum filled the passage. 'The vibration will *stimulate* the lock mechanism,' she said, eyes bright. Gears turned, dust fell, and the door swung wide onto a room full of floating lanterns that had been waiting, it seemed, just for us.
stimulate:2.cnHint: 小铃用晶石的振动____了铁门的机关，门后是一屋子漂浮的灯笼。
stimulate:2.hook: One lantern drifted toward me and stopped, as if choosing.
stimulate:2.line: 'The vibration will *stimulate* the lock mechanism,' she said, eyes bright.

sentences.en: Bell pressed the glowing word-crystal against the iron door and a low hum filled the passage.
sentences.cn: 小铃把发光的文字晶体按在铁门上，一声低沉的嗡鸣在通道里回荡。

sentences.en: 'The vibration will *stimulate* the lock mechanism,' she said, eyes bright.
Gears turned, dust fell, and the door swung wide onto a room full of floating lanterns that had been waiting, it seemed, just for us.
sentences.cn: 齿轮转动，尘埃飘落，门猛地打开，露出一间满是悬浮灯笼的房间，那些灯笼仿佛早已在等待，就为了我们的到来。

switch:2.en: The bridge ahead split into two paths. Old Helm studied the worn lever between them. 'We need to *switch* to the lower road,' he said, pulling it firm. The left path folded away like a closing hand, and the right one lit up with soft blue stones all the way to the next island.
switch:2.cnHint: 老舵拉动拉杆，____到另一条路，蓝色石头照亮了通往下一座岛的方向。
switch:2.hook: Something on that lower road was already moving toward us.
switch:2.line: 'We need to *switch* to the lower road,' he said, pulling it firm.

sentences.en: The bridge ahead split into two paths.
sentences.cn: 前方的桥分成了两条路。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied the worn lever between them.
sentences.cn: 老舵研究着它们之间那根磨损的杠杆。

sentences.en: 'We need to *switch* to the lower road,' he said, pulling it firm.
The left path folded away like a closing hand, and the right one lit up with soft blue stones all the way to the next island.
sentences.cn: 左边的路像合拢的手一样褶皱消失了，右边的路被柔和的蓝石点亮，一直通向下一个岛。

treatment:2.en: We found a wounded sky-bird resting on a warm ledge near the island's centre. Bell opened her small pack and began her careful *treatment* of its bent wing with soft cloth and a thin wooden brace. The bird stayed still, watching her with one gold eye, as if it understood every gentle move.
treatment:2.cnHint: 小铃对受伤的天空鸟进行了细心的____，鸟儿安静地望着她。
treatment:2.hook: When it finally spread its wings, a tiny scroll fell from its feathers.
treatment:2.line: 'A little patience is all good *treatment* needs,' Bell said quietly.

sentences.en: We found a wounded sky-bird resting on a warm ledge near the island's centre.
sentences.cn: 我们在岛中心附近的一处温暖的岩架上发现了一只受伤的天空鸟。
