sentences.en: Bell opened her small pack and began her careful *treatment* of its bent wing with soft cloth and a thin wooden brace.
The bird stayed still, watching her with one gold eye, as if it understood every gentle move.
sentences.cn: 那只鸟静静地躺着，用一只金色的眼睛看着她，仿佛理解她每一个温柔的动作。

union:2.en: Two rival word-keepers had etched their names on the same stone tablet, side by side. 'A *union* of enemies,' Silverfang read aloud, tracing the carved letters slowly. Below the names was a shared map fragment, split cleanly down the middle, as though neither side had been willing to give the other the whole thing.
union:2.cnHint: 两位曾是对手的守词人在同一块石板上留下了他们____的印记和地图碎片。
union:2.hook: The two halves, pressed together, showed a path none of us had imagined.
union:2.line: 'A *union* of enemies — now that is worth reading,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Two rival word-keepers had etched their names on the same stone tablet, side by side.
sentences.cn: 两个对立的文字守护者在同一块石碑上并排刻下了各自的名字。

sentences.en: 'A *union* of enemies,' Silverfang read aloud, tracing the carved letters slowly.
Below the names was a shared map fragment, split cleanly down the middle, as though neither side had been willing to give the other the whole thing.
sentences.cn: 名字下方是一张共享的地图碎片，沿中线整齐地裂开，仿佛双方都不愿意把完整的东西给对方。

acknowledge:2.en: Old Helm stood before the island's elder, hat in hand. He spoke our troupe's name and, one by one, listed every member. The elder gave a slow nod to *acknowledge* each name, as if each of us were being written into the island's memory. I felt a small, warm pride when she nodded at mine.
acknowledge:2.cnHint: 长老郑重地点头____了我们每一位成员的名字，仿佛把我们写进了岛屿的记忆里。
acknowledge:2.hook: Then she handed Old Helm a map fragment nobody had asked for.
acknowledge:2.line: 'I *acknowledge* your troupe and welcome every name on it,' the elder said.

sentences.en: Old Helm stood before the island's elder, hat in hand.
sentences.cn: 老舵站在岛上长者的面前，帽子握在手中。

sentences.en: He spoke our troupe's name and, one by one, listed every member.
sentences.cn: 他说出了我们剧团的名字，然后逐一列举了每个成员。

sentences.en: The elder gave a slow nod to *acknowledge* each name, as if each of us were being written into the island's memory.
I felt a small, warm pride when she nodded at mine.
sentences.cn: 当她点到我的名字时，我感到一股小小的、温暖的骄傲。

alike:2.en: The twin towers at the island's north end looked exactly *alike* — same stone, same height, same cracked window on the left side. But Bell noticed that one cast its shadow east and the other cast it west. 'Two suns,' she whispered. We looked up and saw, for the first time, the second small star rising.
alike:2.cnHint: 两座看起来____的塔楼投下方向相反的影子，小铃由此发现了天空中的第二颗星。
alike:2.hook: And if there were two suns, how many islands were still hidden in the light?
alike:2.line: 'They look *alike*, but shadows never lie,' Bell whispered.

sentences.en: The twin towers at the island's north end looked exactly *alike* — same stone, same height, same cracked window on the left side.
But Bell noticed that one cast its shadow east and the other cast it west.
sentences.cn: 但小铃注意到一座向东投影，另一座向西投影。

sentences.en: 'Two suns,' she whispered.
sentences.cn: "两个太阳。"她低声说。

sentences.en: We looked up and saw, for the first time, the second small star rising.
sentences.cn: 我们抬起头，第一次看到第二颗小星星升起。

analyze:2.en: Silverfang spread three word-fragments on the ship's table and began to *analyze* the faint lines printed across each one. 'Each line is a wind current,' he said at last, sitting back. When he laid them edge to edge in the right order, the currents formed a single arrow pointing straight toward the edge of every map we owned.
analyze:2.cnHint: 银牙仔细____了三块碎片上的纹路，拼出了一个指向地图边缘的方向。
analyze:2.hook: Whatever waited at that edge, it had been drawing us there all along.
analyze:2.line: 'Let me *analyze* these lines before we guess our way off a cliff,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Silverfang spread three word-fragments on the ship's table and began to *analyze* the faint lines printed across each one.
'Each line is a wind current,' he said at last, sitting back.
sentences.cn: "每条线都是一股风流。"他最后说道，靠回椅子上。

sentences.en: When he laid them edge to edge in the right order, the currents formed a single arrow pointing straight toward the edge of every map we owned.
sentences.cn: 当他把它们按正确的顺序边对边排放时，这些风流形成了一支单独的箭头，指向我们所有地图的边缘。

belong:2.en: At the edge of the island, we found a stone chest half-buried in silver moss. Inside lay a folded map covered in tiny handwriting. Old Helm ran his finger along the border and said every fragment we had collected seemed to *belong* here, fitting together like pieces of a puzzle waiting years to be solved.
belong:2.cnHint: 在小岛边缘，老舵手发现一个石箱，里面的地图碎片似乎____于同一个更大的整体。
belong:2.hook: But one corner of the map showed an island none of us had ever seen.
belong:2.line: 'These pieces *belong* together — someone planned this long before us.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the island, we found a stone chest half-buried in silver moss.
sentences.cn: 在岛的边缘，我们发现了一只半埋在银色苔藓中的石头箱子。

sentences.en: Inside lay a folded map covered in tiny handwriting.
sentences.cn: 箱子里放着一张覆满细密笔迹的折叠地图。

sentences.en: Old Helm ran his finger along the border and said every fragment we had collected seemed to *belong* here, fitting together like pieces of a puzzle waiting years to be solved.

beneficial:2.en: Bell spread a strange blue moss across the cracked hull of our sky-boat. She explained that the moss was *beneficial* to old wood, feeding it moisture from the clouds and sealing every gap without a single nail. Within an hour the boards had stopped groaning, and the boat felt almost new beneath our feet.
beneficial:2.cnHint: 小铃用一种蓝色苔藓修复了船体，并解释这种苔藓对旧木材非常____。
beneficial:2.hook: Old Helm stared at the healed wood and quietly asked where Bell had learned that trick.
beneficial:2.line: 'Trust me, this moss is *beneficial* — the clouds have been feeding it for centuries.'

sentences.en: Bell spread a strange blue moss across the cracked hull of our sky-boat.
sentences.cn: 小铃在我们天空船的裂纹船体上铺开了一种奇异的蓝色苔藓。

sentences.en: She explained that the moss was *beneficial* to old wood, feeding it moisture from the clouds and sealing every gap without a single nail.
Within an hour the boards had stopped groaning, and the boat felt almost new beneath our feet.
sentences.cn: 一小时内，木板停止了呻吟，船在我们脚下感觉几乎崭新。

characteristic:2.en: We landed on an island that smelled of warm cinnamon and rain. Old Helm told us the sweet scent was a *characteristic* of islands formed near the eastern star-streams, a sign that the soil below was rich with minerals found nowhere else. I breathed it in and felt, somehow, that we had arrived somewhere important.
characteristic:2.cnHint: 老舵手告诉我们，这座岛上的肉桂香气是东部星流附近岛屿的____之一。
characteristic:2.hook: Silverfang knelt and pressed a coin into the soft soil, and it glowed faint gold.
characteristic:2.line: 'That sweet smell is a *characteristic* of the rarest islands on any map.'

sentences.en: We landed on an island that smelled of warm cinnamon and rain.
sentences.cn: 我们降落在一个闻起来像温暖肉桂和雨水的岛。

sentences.en: Old Helm told us the sweet scent was a *characteristic* of islands formed near the eastern star-streams, a sign that the soil below was rich with minerals found nowhere else.
I breathed it in and felt, somehow, that we had arrived somewhere important.
sentences.cn: 我吸了吸气，不知怎的，感到我们抵达了某个重要的地方。

director:2.en: Tucked inside a hollow tree we found a small notebook. The cover read: Notes of the *director* of the First Sky Survey. Every page held careful drawings of islands we had already visited, each one labelled with a word. Old Helm held the book with both hands, as though it might float away if he let go.
director:2.cnHint: 我们在空心树里发现了一本笔记本，封面写着第一次天空勘探的____的记录。
director:2.hook: The last page showed our exact boat, drawn as if someone had been watching us all along.
director:2.line: 'The *director* of this survey knew every island we would ever find.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside a hollow tree we found a small notebook.
sentences.cn: 在一个树洞里面，我们发现了一本小笔记本。

sentences.en: The cover read: Notes of the *director* of the First Sky Survey.
Every page held careful drawings of islands we had already visited, each one labelled with a word.
sentences.cn: 每一页都装满了我们已经访问过的岛屿的精细素描，每一个都标记着一个词。

sentences.en: Old Helm held the book with both hands, as though it might float away if he let go.
sentences.cn: 老舵用双手握着这本书，仿佛如果他放开就会飘走。

emerge:2.en: We waited beside a dark pool at the centre of a cloud island. Slowly, letters of light began to *emerge* from the water, rising to the surface one by one until they formed a complete word. Bell read it aloud in a whisper. The word hummed in the air for a moment, then settled into our map like a key turning in a lock.
emerge:2.cnHint: 我们守在云雾岛中央的水池旁，发光的字母从水中____，最终拼成一个新词。
emerge:2.hook: The pool went dark the instant the last letter rose, and somewhere far below us, thunder rolled.
emerge:2.line: 'Watch — the next word is about to *emerge* from the water.'

sentences.en: We waited beside a dark pool at the centre of a cloud island.
sentences.cn: 我们在云岛中心的黑池边等候。

sentences.en: Slowly, letters of light began to *emerge* from the water, rising to the surface one by one until they formed a complete word.
Bell read it aloud in a whisper.
sentences.cn: 小铃轻声读了出来。

sentences.en: The word hummed in the air for a moment, then settled into our map like a key turning in a lock.
sentences.cn: 那个词在空中嗡鸣了一刻，然后沉入了我们的地图，就像钥匙转进锁里一样。

exact:2.en: Silverfang stood over our spread-out map and tapped one blank corner with two fingers. She said she needed the *exact* position of the northern star-current to plot a safe path, and that even one degree of error could carry us three islands off course. Old Helm handed her a small brass instrument without a word.
exact:2.cnHint: 银牙船长说她需要北部星流的____位置，差一点点就会偏航好几座岛。
exact:2.hook: The brass instrument showed a reading no one in the troupe had ever seen before.
exact:2.line: 'I need the *exact* number — close enough will get us lost out here.'

sentences.en: Silverfang stood over our spread-out map and tapped one blank corner with two fingers.
sentences.cn: 银牙站在摊开的地图上方，用两根手指点了点某个空白的角落。

sentences.en: She said she needed the *exact* position of the northern star-current to plot a safe path, and that even one degree of error could carry us three islands off course.
Old Helm handed her a small brass instrument without a word.
sentences.cn: 老舵递给她一个小黄铜仪器，什么话都没说。

guest:2.en: On a pale island ringed by slow-drifting lanterns, a door stood open in a rock face. Inside, a table was set for four. A card on the table read: You are a *guest* of this island. Please eat. The soup was warm, the bread was soft, and when we finished, a new map fragment lay folded under the empty bread basket.
guest:2.cnHint: 一扇石门里摆着一张桌子，桌上的卡片写着：你是这座岛的____，请用餐。
guest:2.hook: None of us could explain who had set the table or how they had known we were coming.
guest:2.line: 'Every *guest* who eats here leaves with something they needed.'

sentences.en: On a pale island ringed by slow-drifting lanterns, a door stood open in a rock face.
sentences.cn: 在一座环绕着缓缓漂流灯笼的苍白岛屿上，岩石面孔上开着一扇门。

sentences.en: Inside, a table was set for four.
sentences.cn: 里面摆了一张四人的饭桌。

sentences.en: A card on the table read: You are a *guest* of this island.
Please eat.
sentences.cn: 请吃。

sentences.en: The soup was warm, the bread was soft, and when we finished, a new map fragment lay folded under the empty bread basket.
sentences.cn: 汤是温的，面包是软的，等我们吃完，一个折好的地图碎片就躺在空的面包篮下面。

massive:2.en: At the edge of our charts we found it: a *massive* island, wider than ten of the ones we had crossed, its cliffs wrapped in cloud and its peaks lost in stars. Old Helm said nothing for a long moment. Then he smiled, folded the newest map fragment into place, and said this was what the whole journey had been pointing toward.
massive:2.cnHint: 在地图的边缘，我们发现了一座____的岛屿，比我们之前经过的所有岛加起来还要宽阔。
massive:2.hook: Bell raised her lantern, and somewhere high above us, a light answered back.
massive:2.line: 'I always suspected something this *massive* was waiting at the end of the map.'

sentences.en: At the edge of our charts we found it: a *massive* island, wider than ten of the ones we had crossed, its cliffs wrapped in cloud and its peaks lost in stars.
Old Helm said nothing for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 老舵沉默了很久。

sentences.en: Then he smiled, folded the newest map fragment into place, and said this was what the whole journey had been pointing toward.
sentences.cn: 然后他笑了，把最新的地图碎片折进去，说这就是整个旅程一直指向的地方。

insist:2.en: The old chest sat at the edge of the island, half-buried in silver moss. Bell said we should leave it alone. But Old Helm would *insist* — he knelt down, brushed the moss aside, and lifted the lid. Inside, folded like a sleeping bird, was a map fragment with a single word glowing at its centre.
insist:2.cnHint: 老舵____要打开那个旧箱子，里面藏着发光的地图碎片。
insist:2.hook: The glowing word began to rise, drifting slowly toward the open sky.
insist:2.line: 'I *insist* we open it — maps do not bury themselves for nothing,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The old chest sat at the edge of the island, half-buried in silver moss.
sentences.cn: 那只老箱子坐在岛边，半埋在银色苔藓里。

sentences.en: Bell said we should leave it alone.
sentences.cn: 小铃说我们应该不去碰它。

sentences.en: But Old Helm would *insist* — he knelt down, brushed the moss aside, and lifted the lid.
Inside, folded like a sleeping bird, was a map fragment with a single word glowing at its centre.
sentences.cn: 里面折得像睡着的鸟一样，是一张地图碎片，中心闪烁着一个词。

investigation:2.en: A ring of burned stones near the island's edge caught Bell's eye. She circled them twice, reading the ash like a page. 'This calls for a proper *investigation*,' she said, and pulled out her brass compass. By the time the stars shifted, she had found a hidden word pressed into the rock beneath the largest stone.
investigation:2.cnHint: 小铃对那圈烧焦的石头展开了____，最终在石头下发现了隐藏的词语。
investigation:2.hook: The word she uncovered was not one any of us had seen before.
investigation:2.line: 'A proper *investigation* always starts with the ground, not the sky,' Bell said quietly.

sentences.en: A ring of burned stones near the island's edge caught Bell's eye.
sentences.cn: 岛边的一圈烧焦的石头吸引了小铃的注意。

sentences.en: She circled them twice, reading the ash like a page.
sentences.cn: 她绕着它们转了两圈，像读书一样读着灰烬。

sentences.en: 'This calls for a proper *investigation*,' she said, and pulled out her brass compass.
By the time the stars shifted, she had found a hidden word pressed into the rock beneath the largest stone.
sentences.cn: 到星星移位的时候，她在最大的石头下面压进岩石里找到了一个隐藏的词。

limited:2.en: Our supply of starlight ink — the only thing that could copy a map fragment — was *limited* to three drops. Old Helm held the tiny bottle up to the night sky and frowned. We had five fragments to trace. Silverfang crossed his arms and said we had better choose wisely, or we would lose two islands forever.
limited:2.cnHint: 我们的星光墨水____，只够复制三份地图碎片，必须做出选择。
limited:2.hook: Two islands would stay blank on our map unless someone found another answer.
limited:2.line: 'Our ink is *limited*, so every drop must count,' said Old Helm, still frowning at the bottle.

sentences.en: Our supply of starlight ink — the only thing that could copy a map fragment — was *limited* to three drops.
Old Helm held the tiny bottle up to the night sky and frowned.
sentences.cn: 老舵把那只小瓶子举向夜空，皱起了眉头。

sentences.en: We had five fragments to trace.
sentences.cn: 我们有五张碎片要描摹。

sentences.en: Silverfang crossed his arms and said we had better choose wisely, or we would lose two islands forever.
sentences.cn: 银牙交叉起双臂，说我们最好选对，不然就会永远失去两个岛屿。

listen:2.en: The island was perfectly quiet — no wind, no birds, nothing. Bell pressed her ear to the warm ground. 'You have to *listen*,' she whispered, 'really listen.' I knelt beside her and did the same. Deep below the rock, something was humming, slow and even, like a word being sounded out by the island itself.
listen:2.cnHint: 小铃让大家____大地的声音，那里似乎藏着一个被岛屿低声诵读的词。
listen:2.hook: The humming grew louder, shaping itself into something almost readable.
listen:2.line: '*Listen* to the ground before you trust the sky,' Bell whispered.

sentences.en: The island was perfectly quiet — no wind, no birds, nothing.
sentences.cn: 这个岛完全安静——没有风，没有鸟，什么都没有。

sentences.en: Bell pressed her ear to the warm ground.
sentences.cn: 小铃把耳朵贴在温暖的地面上。

sentences.en: 'You have to *listen*,' she whispered, 'really listen.'
I knelt beside her and did the same.
sentences.cn: 我跪在她身边，也做了同样的事。

sentences.en: Deep below the rock, something was humming, slow and even, like a word being sounded out by the island itself.
sentences.cn: 在岩石深处，什么东西在嗡鸣，缓慢而均匀，就像岛屿本身在发音一样。

master:2.en: The small temple at the island's centre had one room and one table. On the table lay a letter sealed with gold wax. Old Helm broke the seal and read aloud: the letter was addressed to the *master* of the troupe, and it named a place none of our maps had ever shown. We looked at each other in the warm amber light.
master:2.cnHint: 神庙里的信是写给船队____的，信中提到了一个从未出现在地图上的地方。
master:2.hook: The place the letter named had no star above it — at least, not yet.
master:2.line: 'This letter is for the *master* of this troupe, and that is you,' Bell said, sliding it toward Old Helm.

sentences.en: The small temple at the island's centre had one room and one table.
sentences.cn: 岛中心的小庙只有一间房和一张桌子。

sentences.en: On the table lay a letter sealed with gold wax.
sentences.cn: 桌上放着一封用金蜡封好的信。

sentences.en: Old Helm broke the seal and read aloud: the letter was addressed to the *master* of the troupe, and it named a place none of our maps had ever shown.
We looked at each other in the warm amber light.
sentences.cn: 我们在温暖的琥珀色灯光下互相看着。

newly:2.en: The island appeared on our chart overnight — *newly* marked in pale blue ink that no one had written. Bell traced its outline with one finger, her eyes wide. Old Helm said some islands only become real once you collect the right word. We had found the word 'horizon' the evening before, and now, here was the proof.
newly:2.cnHint: 一座____出现在地图上的岛屿，似乎是因为我们昨晚找到了正确的词语才变得真实。
newly:2.hook: Its shape was unlike any island we had ever sailed toward.
newly:2.line: 'A *newly* drawn island means our last word was the right one,' said Old Helm with a slow smile.

sentences.en: The island appeared on our chart overnight — *newly* marked in pale blue ink that no one had written.
Bell traced its outline with one finger, her eyes wide.
sentences.cn: 小铃用一根手指描绘着它的轮廓，眼睛睁得很大。

sentences.en: Old Helm said some islands only become real once you collect the right word.
sentences.cn: 老舵说有些岛屿只有在你集齐了正确的词之后才会真正存在。

sentences.en: We had found the word 'horizon' the evening before, and now, here was the proof.
sentences.cn: 我们在前一天晚上找到了"地平线"这个词，现在，证据就在眼前。

north:2.en: Every compass on the ship stopped at the same moment. All three needles swung away from *north* and pointed straight down, toward the clouds below. Silverfang tapped his glass face twice and raised an eyebrow. Bell pulled out her old paper chart and found a small note in the margin: 'Here, north is where you have already been.'
north:2.cnHint: 所有指南针同时偏离了____方，小铃在地图边缘发现了一行神秘的注释。
north:2.hook: If north was behind us, then where exactly were we heading?
north:2.line: 'When every needle leaves *north*, the island is trying to tell you something,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Every compass on the ship stopped at the same moment.
sentences.cn: 船上的每一个罗盘都在同一时刻停了下来。

sentences.en: All three needles swung away from *north* and pointed straight down, toward the clouds below.
Silverfang tapped his glass face twice and raised an eyebrow.
sentences.cn: 银牙敲了敲它的玻璃面，扬起一条眉毛。

sentences.en: Bell pulled out her old paper chart and found a small note in the margin: 'Here, north is where you have already been.'
sentences.cn: 小铃拿出她的旧纸质地图，在边缘找到了一句小注记："这儿，北方就是你已经去过的地方。"

obviously:2.en: The word fragment was carved right across the doorway of the stone shelter — at eye level, in letters as wide as my hand. Silverfang stared at it and then at us. 'It is *obviously* meant to be found,' he said, sounding almost annoyed. Old Helm laughed and said that the best secrets were always the ones hiding in plain sight.
obviously:2.cnHint: 那个词就刻在石屋门口最显眼的地方，银牙觉得这____是故意让人发现的。
obviously:2.hook: But if it was meant to be found, who had put it there, and when?
obviously:2.line: 'This was *obviously* left for us — nothing else explains the height of those letters,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: The word fragment was carved right across the doorway of the stone shelter — at eye level, in letters as wide as my hand.
sentences.cn: 这个词碎片刻在石头庇护所的门口——在眼睛高度，字母宽得像我的手。

sentences.en: Silverfang stared at it and then at us.
sentences.cn: 银牙盯着它，然后看向我们。

sentences.en: 'It is *obviously* meant to be found,' he said, sounding almost annoyed.
Old Helm laughed and said that the best secrets were always the ones hiding in plain sight.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑了，说最好的秘密总是那些躲在显眼处的。

content:2.en: On Pale Ledge Island, Old Helm unrolled a recovered chart across a flat stone. Every recovered fragment now lay in its proper place. He studied it in silence, then sat back with a slow smile. He looked *content* — as if the long search had finally given him exactly what he needed.
content:2.cnHint: 老舵手把所有碎片拼好后，露出了____的神情。
content:2.hook: But one corner of the chart still showed only blank white.
content:2.line: 'I am *content* with what we have found here, for now.'

sentences.en: On Pale Ledge Island, Old Helm unrolled a recovered chart across a flat stone.
sentences.cn: 苍白礁岛上，老舵展开一张打捞来的海图在平坦的石头上。

sentences.en: Every recovered fragment now lay in its proper place.
sentences.cn: 现在每一片打捞到的碎片都各归其位。

sentences.en: He studied it in silence, then sat back with a slow smile.
sentences.cn: 他沉默地研究了一阵，然后缓缓向后靠去，脸上浮起了一丝笑容。

sentences.en: He looked *content* — as if the long search had finally given him exactly what he needed.

divide:2.en: Bell led us to the Ridge of Two Winds, where a sharp spine of rock ran straight across the island. Warm air rose from the south face; cold air fell from the north. That single ridge seemed to *divide* the whole sky in two, as if the world itself had chosen sides.
divide:2.cnHint: 贝尔带我们来到一道山脊，它像刀刃一样____了两片天空。
divide:2.hook: Something small and bright rolled along the ridge-line toward us.
divide:2.line: 'This ridge will *divide* our path — choose your side carefully.'

sentences.en: Bell led us to the Ridge of Two Winds, where a sharp spine of rock ran straight across the island.
sentences.cn: 小铃领着我们来到了两风岭，一条尖锐的石脊直直横跨过整个岛屿。

sentences.en: Warm air rose from the south face; cold air fell from the north.
sentences.cn: 南面升起温暖的气流；北面坠下冰冷的寒风。

sentences.en: That single ridge seemed to *divide* the whole sky in two, as if the world itself had chosen sides.

generate:2.en: Deep in the Engine Grotto, a cluster of spinning copper wheels hummed without pause. Old Helm touched one gently and nodded. 'Ancient craft,' he murmured. The wheels seemed to *generate* a soft golden light that fed into the veins of crystal running through the cave walls, keeping the whole island aloft.
generate:2.cnHint: 古老的铜轮在洞窟里转动，____着让岛屿漂浮的金色光芒。
generate:2.hook: Then one wheel slowed, and the light began to flicker.
generate:2.line: 'These wheels *generate* the only power keeping us in the sky.'

sentences.en: Deep in the Engine Grotto, a cluster of spinning copper wheels hummed without pause.
sentences.cn: 在引擎石窟的深处，一簇铜制转轮无休无止地嗡鸣着。

sentences.en: Old Helm touched one gently and nodded.
sentences.cn: 老舵轻轻摸了摸其中一个，点了点头。

sentences.en: 'Ancient craft,' he murmured.
sentences.cn: "古代工艺，"他低声说道。

sentences.en: The wheels seemed to *generate* a soft golden light that fed into the veins of crystal running through the cave walls, keeping the whole island aloft.

operate:2.en: Silverfang found a locked iron panel near the island's edge. Bell knelt before it and studied the levers. 'I know this kind,' she said quietly. She began to *operate* the levers one by one, each click sending a low vibration through the stone, until a hidden door swung open before us.
operate:2.cnHint: 贝尔找到铁板上的机关，小心地____它，直到暗门打开。
operate:2.hook: Cold wind poured out from the darkness beyond the door.
operate:2.line: 'Watch closely while I *operate* this — one wrong move seals it forever.'

sentences.en: Silverfang found a locked iron panel near the island's edge.
sentences.cn: 银牙在岛屿边缘发现了一块上锁的铁制面板。

sentences.en: Bell knelt before it and studied the levers.
sentences.cn: 小铃跪在它面前仔细研究了那些杠杆。

sentences.en: 'I know this kind,' she said quietly.
sentences.cn: "我认识这种，"她轻声说。

sentences.en: She began to *operate* the levers one by one, each click sending a low vibration through the stone, until a hidden door swung open before us.

properly:2.en: I tried to read the star-script on the obelisk, but the symbols kept blurring. Bell placed her hand on my shoulder. 'Hold the lens *properly*,' she said, tilting it to catch the starlight at exactly the right angle. The symbols sharpened at once, and a new island name appeared before my eyes.
properly:2.cnHint: 贝尔提醒我____地拿好镜片，星文才终于变得清晰可读。
properly:2.hook: The name on the obelisk matched no island on our chart.
properly:2.line: 'Hold the lens *properly* — only then will the sky show you its secrets.'

sentences.en: I tried to read the star-script on the obelisk, but the symbols kept blurring.
sentences.cn: 我试图解读方尖塔上的星文，但符号一直在模糊闪烁。

sentences.en: Bell placed her hand on my shoulder.
sentences.cn: 小铃把手放在我的肩上。

sentences.en: 'Hold the lens *properly*,' she said, tilting it to catch the starlight at exactly the right angle.
The symbols sharpened at once, and a new island name appeared before my eyes.
sentences.cn: 符号立刻变得清晰起来，一个陌生的岛屿名字出现在我眼前。

render:2.en: As dawn broke over Drift Cove, a thin mist rose from the water below the island's rim. The pale light and soft fog together seemed to *render* the whole landscape weightless, as if the rocks and trees had forgotten they were solid. Old Helm simply stood and stared, unable to speak.
render:2.cnHint: 晨雾与光线共同____了一幅失重般的奇异景象，令老舵手无言以对。
render:2.hook: Then the mist parted, and something enormous moved beneath it.
render:2.line: 'This light can *render* even stone as soft as a dream.'

sentences.en: As dawn broke over Drift Cove, a thin mist rose from the water below the island's rim.
sentences.cn: 曙光降临漂流湾时，薄雾从岛屿边缘下方的水面升起。

sentences.en: The pale light and soft fog together seemed to *render* the whole landscape weightless, as if the rocks and trees had forgotten they were solid.
Old Helm simply stood and stared, unable to speak.
sentences.cn: 老舵只是站着凝视，无言以对。

resolve:2.en: Silverfang stared at the broken bridge stretching toward the next island. No rope, no plank remained. The gap was wide. He crossed his arms, jaw set. His *resolve* was clear — not a word of doubt crossed his face. He turned to us and began measuring rope from the supply pack without asking.
resolve:2.cnHint: 面对断裂的桥，竞争船长的____清晰地写在脸上，他默默拿起绳索。
resolve:2.hook: The far island began drifting slowly away from us.
resolve:2.line: 'My *resolve* is fixed — we cross tonight, wind or no wind.'

sentences.en: Silverfang stared at the broken bridge stretching toward the next island.
sentences.cn: 银牙盯着那座通往下一座岛屿的断桥。

sentences.en: No rope, no plank remained.
sentences.cn: 没有绳索，没有木板留下。

sentences.en: The gap was wide.
sentences.cn: 缝隙很宽。

sentences.en: He crossed his arms, jaw set.
sentences.cn: 他双臂交叉，下颌紧绷。

sentences.en: His *resolve* was clear — not a word of doubt crossed his face.
He turned to us and began measuring rope from the supply pack without asking.
sentences.cn: 他转身面向我们，开始从补给包里取出绳子丈量，没有多问一句。

seemingly:2.en: The cave entrance looked *seemingly* ordinary — low, narrow, framed by grey stone like a hundred others we had passed. But Bell paused and pressed her ear to the wall. A distant hum answered her. Old Helm marked it on the chart. Ordinary caves do not hum with purpose.
seemingly:2.cnHint: 那个____普通的洞口让贝尔停下了脚步，因为里面传来了奇异的嗡鸣声。
seemingly:2.hook: Whatever hummed inside had been waiting a very long time.
seemingly:2.line: 'It looks *seemingly* safe, but trust the hum, not your eyes.'

sentences.en: The cave entrance looked *seemingly* ordinary — low, narrow, framed by grey stone like a hundred others we had passed.
But Bell paused and pressed her ear to the wall.
sentences.cn: 但小铃停了下来，把耳朵贴在了岩壁上。

sentences.en: A distant hum answered her.
sentences.cn: 一阵遥远的嗡鸣声回应了她。

sentences.en: Old Helm marked it on the chart.
sentences.cn: 老舵在海图上标记了这个位置。

sentences.en: Ordinary caves do not hum with purpose.
sentences.cn: 普通的洞穴不会发出这样有目的的嗡鸣声。

mix:2.en: Bell spread the recovered map pieces across the stone table. 'These fragments come from three different islands,' she said, studying the edges. The *mix* of paper textures and ink colours told a story all on its own — someone had torn this map apart on purpose. Old Helm pressed two pieces together, and a new coastline appeared.
mix:2.cnHint: 小铃发现地图碎片是来自三座岛屿的____，拼合之后露出了一段新海岸线。
mix:2.hook: The hidden coastline pointed toward an island no one had named.
mix:2.line: 'This *mix* of inks and paper means the map was split by different hands.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the recovered map pieces across the stone table.
sentences.cn: 小铃把打捞来的地图碎片铺开在石桌上。

sentences.en: 'These fragments come from three different islands,' she said, studying the edges.
sentences.cn: "这些碎片来自三个不同的岛屿，"她边说边研究着边缘。

sentences.en: The *mix* of paper textures and ink colours told a story all on its own — someone had torn this map apart on purpose.
Old Helm pressed two pieces together, and a new coastline appeared.
sentences.cn: 老舵把两块碎片拼在一起，一条新的海岸线出现了。

necessity:2.en: The bridge between the two stone platforms had crumbled away. I looked at the gap, then at the rope in my pack. Old Helm said nothing, only watched. I understood the *necessity* of crossing without being told — the word we needed was glowing faintly on the far ledge. I threw the rope and climbed.
necessity:2.cnHint: 通往发光文字的桥断了，叙述者意识到渡过去的____，独自搭绳越过了断桥。
necessity:2.hook: My hands were still shaking when I read what the word said.
necessity:2.line: 'The *necessity* of the crossing is clear — that word won't wait for us.'

sentences.en: The bridge between the two stone platforms had crumbled away.
sentences.cn: 两个石平台之间的桥已经崩塌了。

sentences.en: I looked at the gap, then at the rope in my pack.
sentences.cn: 我看看缝隙，再看看背包里的绳子。

sentences.en: Old Helm said nothing, only watched.
sentences.cn: 老舵什么也没说，只是看着。

sentences.en: I understood the *necessity* of crossing without being told — the word we needed was glowing faintly on the far ledge.
I threw the rope and climbed.
sentences.cn: 我扔出了绳子并爬了上去。

stuff:2.en: Inside the hollow tree we found a leather bag left by some earlier traveller. Bell emptied it carefully: three dried berries, a cracked compass, and a folded note. 'Ordinary *stuff*,' she said, but Old Helm picked up the note and smiled. The handwriting matched the map fragments exactly.
stuff:2.cnHint: 空心树里藏着一个旅行者留下的袋子，里面装着些普通____，但那张纸条却意外关键。
stuff:2.hook: The note ended with a single word that made Old Helm go pale.
stuff:2.line: 'Looks like ordinary *stuff*, but every piece in here was chosen on purpose.'

sentences.en: Inside the hollow tree we found a leather bag left by some earlier traveller.
sentences.cn: 在中空的树干里，我们发现了某个早期旅人遗留的一只皮袋。

sentences.en: Bell emptied it carefully: three dried berries, a cracked compass, and a folded note.
sentences.cn: 小铃小心翼翼地倒空了它：三颗干果子、一个裂纹指南针，还有一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: 'Ordinary *stuff*,' she said, but Old Helm picked up the note and smiled.
The handwriting matched the map fragments exactly.
sentences.cn: 笔迹与地图碎片完全一致。

translate:2.en: The stone arch was carved with a script none of us could read. I pressed my palm against the surface and felt a faint hum. Then the word in my pocket — the one we had collected on the previous island — began to glow. Somehow it could *translate* the old marks into a path we understood.
translate:2.cnHint: 石拱上的古文字无人能读，但叙述者口袋里收集的词语竟能将它____成一条可识别的路径。
translate:2.hook: The path led straight down, into a cloud we could not see through.
translate:2.line: 'Let me try — I think this word can *translate* the carvings for us.'

sentences.en: The stone arch was carved with a script none of us could read.
sentences.cn: 石拱被刻上了我们都无法辨识的古老文字。

sentences.en: I pressed my palm against the surface and felt a faint hum.
sentences.cn: 我把手掌按在表面上，感受到了微弱的嗡鸣。

sentences.en: Then the word in my pocket — the one we had collected on the previous island — began to glow.
sentences.cn: 然后我口袋里的那个词——我们从前一座岛屿上收集的那个词——开始发光。

sentences.en: Somehow it could *translate* the old marks into a path we understood.

wander:2.en: Old Helm told me the islands shift position every few nights. 'If you *wander* without a word to guide you,' he said, tapping the map, 'you will step onto a cloud bridge that leads nowhere and spend a week going in circles.' I tucked our newest word carefully into the front of my coat.
wander:2.cnHint: 老舵警告说，如果没有词语引路而随意____，就会在消失的云桥上迷失一周。
wander:2.hook: That night the islands moved, and I was very glad I had listened.
wander:2.line: '*Wander* out there without a guide-word and the islands will lose you.'

sentences.en: Old Helm told me the islands shift position every few nights.
sentences.cn: 老舵告诉我那些岛屿每隔几个晚上就会改变位置。

sentences.en: 'If you *wander* without a word to guide you,' he said, tapping the map, 'you will step onto a cloud bridge that leads nowhere and spend a week going in circles.'
I tucked our newest word carefully into the front of my coat.
sentences.cn: 我小心翼翼地把我们最新收集的词语塞进了大衣前面的口袋里。

warn:2.en: Silverfang's ship pulled alongside ours just before we reached the Amber Shelf. He leaned over the rail and shouted across the gap. 'I'm here to *warn* you — the shelf tilts at dawn and swallows anything left on its surface.' He looked almost cheerful about it. Bell had us moving before he finished the sentence.
warn:2.cnHint: 银牙特意靠近来____叙述者一行：琥珀礁架在黎明时会倾斜，把一切东西吞入其中。
warn:2.hook: Silverfang waved goodbye and sailed away before we could thank him.
warn:2.line: 'I came to *warn* you — that shelf tips at first light, every single time.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's ship pulled alongside ours just before we reached the Amber Shelf.
sentences.cn: 银牙的船在我们快要到达琥珀浅滩时靠了过来。

sentences.en: He leaned over the rail and shouted across the gap.
sentences.cn: 他靠在栏杆上，隔着间隙喊话。

sentences.en: 'I'm here to *warn* you — the shelf tilts at dawn and swallows anything left on its surface.'
He looked almost cheerful about it.
sentences.cn: 他看起来倒是挺高兴的。

sentences.en: Bell had us moving before he finished the sentence.
sentences.cn: 小铃还没等他说完就让我们动身了。

advocate:2.en: At the Council of Winds, three island elders argued over which path the troupe should take. Old Helm stood quietly until they finished, then spoke. 'I am an *advocate* for the southern route,' he said, placing our map on the table. Every fragment pointed the same way. The elders fell silent and nodded.
advocate:2.cnHint: 在风之议会上，老舵作为南路的____，用地图碎片说服了沉默的长老们。
advocate:2.hook: The southern route was the only one that had no name yet.
advocate:2.line: 'I am an *advocate* for the south — the map makes the argument better than I can.'

sentences.en: At the Council of Winds, three island elders argued over which path the troupe should take.
sentences.cn: 在风之议会上，三位岛屿长者争论着车队应该走哪条路。

sentences.en: Old Helm stood quietly until they finished, then spoke.
sentences.cn: 老舵安静地站着，直到他们说完，然后才开口。

sentences.en: 'I am an *advocate* for the southern route,' he said, placing our map on the table.
Every fragment pointed the same way.
sentences.cn: 每个碎片都指向了同一个方向。

sentences.en: The elders fell silent and nodded.
sentences.cn: 长者们沉默了，点了点头。

cite:2.en: Bell kept a small notebook of every word the troupe had ever collected. When Silverfang challenged our claim to the Crystal Atoll, she opened it without hesitation. 'I can *cite* six words that together form its exact location,' she said calmly. Silverfang read the list, closed his mouth, and sailed away.
cite:2.cnHint: 银牙质疑我们对水晶环礁的权利，小铃从笔记本中____了六个词语作为精确坐标证据。
cite:2.hook: Six words, and the atoll was ours without a single argument.
cite:2.line: 'I can *cite* every word that proves this atoll belongs to our route.'

sentences.en: Bell kept a small notebook of every word the troupe had ever collected.
sentences.cn: 小铃有个小笔记本，记下了车队收集过的每一个词语。

sentences.en: When Silverfang challenged our claim to the Crystal Atoll, she opened it without hesitation.
sentences.cn: 当银牙对我们声称拥有水晶环礁的权利时，她毫不犹豫地翻了开来。

sentences.en: 'I can *cite* six words that together form its exact location,' she said calmly.
Silverfang read the list, closed his mouth, and sailed away.
sentences.cn: 银牙读完了清单，闭上嘴，扬帆离开了。

therefore:2.en: The old map ended at a blank edge. Old Helm traced the empty space with one finger and said nothing for a long moment. We had followed every road marked on it, and *therefore* the next island had to lie somewhere beyond sight, hidden by clouds we had not yet crossed.
therefore:2.cnHint: 地图上所有的路都走完了，老舵手认为____还有未知的岛屿在云雾之外。
therefore:2.hook: The clouds ahead flickered with a strange, cold light.
therefore:2.line: 'We have seen every marked path, *therefore* the real journey starts now.'

sentences.en: The old map ended at a blank edge.
sentences.cn: 老地图在空白的边缘处结束了。

sentences.en: Old Helm traced the empty space with one finger and said nothing for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 老舵用一根手指描过那片空白的地方，沉默了很久。

sentences.en: We had followed every road marked on it, and *therefore* the next island had to lie somewhere beyond sight, hidden by clouds we had not yet crossed.

truth:2.en: Deep inside the Library Isle, Bell found a stone tablet half-buried in moss. The words carved on it were old, but clear. She read them aloud slowly, and the *truth* they carried was simple: every island on the map was once a dream someone refused to give up.
truth:2.cnHint: 小铃在图书馆岛发现了一块石碑，上面刻着关于这片群岛起源的____。
truth:2.hook: Below the last carved line, a new word was still being formed.
truth:2.line: 'The *truth* on this stone is older than any map we carry.'

sentences.en: Deep inside the Library Isle, Bell found a stone tablet half-buried in moss.
sentences.cn: 在图书馆岛的深处，小铃发现了一块半埋在苔藓里的石板。

sentences.en: The words carved on it were old, but clear.
sentences.cn: 刻在上面的字很古老，但很清晰。

sentences.en: She read them aloud slowly, and the *truth* they carried was simple: every island on the map was once a dream someone refused to give up.

protein:2.en: On Harvest Isle, the troupe discovered a field of strange blue pods. Old Helm cracked one open and sniffed it carefully. 'High in *protein*,' he said with approval. We filled our bags, grateful, because the next crossing was long and we needed every bit of strength we could carry.
protein:2.cnHint: 在丰收岛，大家发现了一种富含____的蓝色豆荚，可以补充长途旅行所需的体力。
protein:2.hook: One pod at the edge of the field glowed faintly in the dark.
protein:2.line: 'Eat well — this *protein* will keep you strong for the crossing.'

sentences.en: On Harvest Isle, the troupe discovered a field of strange blue pods.
sentences.cn: 在收获岛上，车队发现了一片奇异的蓝色豆荚。

sentences.en: Old Helm cracked one open and sniffed it carefully.
sentences.cn: 老舵打开其中一个，仔细地嗅了嗅。

sentences.en: 'High in *protein*,' he said with approval.
We filled our bags, grateful, because the next crossing was long and we needed every bit of strength we could carry.
sentences.cn: 我们装满了背包，心存感激，因为下一段航程很长，我们需要尽可能多的力量。

traffic:2.en: Cloud Crossing Bridge connected six islands at once, and the *traffic* on it was unlike anything I had seen: traders, wanderers, and tiny messenger birds all moving in every direction. Bell laughed and pulled me aside before I was swept along. 'Stay close,' she said, 'or the crowd will carry you off the edge.'
traffic:2.cnHint: 云桥上____繁忙，小铃提醒我紧跟着她，以免被人流冲走。
traffic:2.hook: Somewhere in the crowd, someone was calling Old Helm's name.
traffic:2.line: 'The *traffic* on this bridge never stops, day or night.'

sentences.en: Cloud Crossing Bridge connected six islands at once, and the *traffic* on it was unlike anything I had seen: traders, wanderers, and tiny messenger birds all moving in every direction.
Bell laughed and pulled me aside before I was swept along.
sentences.cn: 小铃笑着把我拉到一边，免得我被人群冲走。

sentences.en: 'Stay close,' she said, 'or the crowd will carry you off the edge.'
sentences.cn: 她说，'靠近我，不然人群会把你推下去。'

cat:2.en: Perched on a broken signpost at the edge of Lantern Isle sat a silver *cat* with eyes like two small moons. It watched us arrive without blinking, then turned and walked into the fog. Old Helm nodded as if he had expected this. 'Follow it,' he said quietly. 'It knows the way.'
cat:2.cnHint: 灯笼岛边缘坐着一只银色的____，它起身走进雾中，老舵手让大家跟上它。
cat:2.hook: The fog grew warmer, not colder, the further we followed.
cat:2.line: 'That *cat* has led lost travellers home before — trust it.'

sentences.en: Perched on a broken signpost at the edge of Lantern Isle sat a silver *cat* with eyes like two small moons.
It watched us arrive without blinking, then turned and walked into the fog.
sentences.cn: 它目不转睛地看着我们到来，然后转身走进了雾里。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded as if he had expected this.
sentences.cn: 老舵点了点头，好像他早就预料到了。

sentences.en: 'Follow it,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: 他轻声说，'跟着它。'

sentences.en: 'It knows the way.'
sentences.cn: '它知道怎么走。'

sugar:2.en: At the market on Sweet Crag Isle, an old woman pressed a small paper packet into my hand. Inside was pale *sugar* that smelled of night flowers. 'One pinch in your lantern flame,' she whispered, 'and it will burn blue and guide you through any dark.' I held the packet very carefully.
sugar:2.cnHint: 在甜崖岛的集市上，一位老妇人送给我一包特别的____，据说放入灯中能发出蓝光引路。
sugar:2.hook: My lantern flame already seemed to lean toward the packet.
sugar:2.line: 'This *sugar* is not for eating — it is for finding your way.'

sentences.en: At the market on Sweet Crag Isle, an old woman pressed a small paper packet into my hand.
sentences.cn: 在甜脆岛的集市上，一个老女人把一个小纸包塞进了我的手里。

sentences.en: Inside was pale *sugar* that smelled of night flowers.
'One pinch in your lantern flame,' she whispered, 'and it will burn blue and guide you through any dark.'
sentences.cn: '在你的灯火上撒一小撮，'她低声说，'它就会烧成蓝色，在任何黑暗中为你指路。'

sentences.en: I held the packet very carefully.
sentences.cn: 我小心翼翼地握着那个纸包。

balance:2.en: The bridge to Mirror Isle was no wider than my foot. Bell went first, arms out, moving with quiet grace. I stepped on and felt the whole thing sway. 'Don't look down,' Bell called back. 'Just *balance* your breath and your body at the same time.' I took one slow breath and walked.
balance:2.cnHint: 通往镜岛的窄桥摇摇晃晃，小铃告诉我要同时____呼吸和身体才能走过去。
balance:2.hook: Halfway across, I saw something moving in the clouds below.
balance:2.line: '*Balance* your breath first — your body will follow on its own.'

sentences.en: The bridge to Mirror Isle was no wider than my foot.
sentences.cn: 通往镜岛的桥宽度只有我的脚那么宽。

sentences.en: Bell went first, arms out, moving with quiet grace.
sentences.cn: 小铃先走了，张开双臂，步伐平稳而优雅。

sentences.en: I stepped on and felt the whole thing sway.
sentences.cn: 我踩了上去，感觉整个桥都在摇晃。

sentences.en: 'Don't look down,' Bell called back.
sentences.cn: '别往下看，'小铃回头喊道。

sentences.en: 'Just *balance* your breath and your body at the same time.'
I took one slow breath and walked.
sentences.cn: 我深吸一口气，走了过去。

baby:2.en: Tucked in a basket near the warmest vent on Steam Isle, we found a tiny creature no bigger than a fist, covered in soft gold feathers. Old Helm knelt down and smiled. 'A *baby* sky-bird,' he said gently. 'It must have fallen from a nest above the clouds. We cannot leave it here alone.'
baby:2.cnHint: 在蒸汽岛最暖的地方，大家发现了一只掉落的____天空鸟，老舵手决定不能丢下它不管。
baby:2.hook: The tiny creature opened one bright eye and looked straight at me.
baby:2.line: 'A *baby* this small should not be out here without its flock.'

sentences.en: Tucked in a basket near the warmest vent on Steam Isle, we found a tiny creature no bigger than a fist, covered in soft gold feathers.
sentences.cn: 在蒸汽岛最温暖的通风口附近的一个篮子里，我们发现了一个小生物，拳头那么大，浑身被柔软的金色羽毛覆盖。

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt down and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪了下来，笑了。

sentences.en: 'A *baby* sky-bird,' he said gently.
'It must have fallen from a nest above the clouds.
sentences.cn: '它一定是从云上的巢里掉下来的。

sentences.en: We cannot leave it here alone.'
sentences.cn: 我们不能丢下它一个人在这里。'

childhood:2.en: Inside a hollow tree near the edge of the map, Bell found a small tin box. She opened it slowly. Inside lay a pressed flower and a folded note in faded ink. 'This place smells like *childhood*,' she said softly, 'like something warm you can almost remember.'
childhood:2.cnHint: 小铃在地图边缘的空心树里发现了一个铁盒，里面的气息让她想起了____。
childhood:2.hook: The note was addressed to someone with Bell's exact name.
childhood:2.line: 'This place smells like *childhood* — like something warm you almost remember.'

sentences.en: Inside a hollow tree near the edge of the map, Bell found a small tin box.
sentences.cn: 小铃在地图边缘的一棵空心树里找到了一个小铁盒。

sentences.en: She opened it slowly.
sentences.cn: 她慢慢打开了盒子。

sentences.en: Inside lay a pressed flower and a folded note in faded ink.
sentences.cn: 里面躺着一朵压干的花和一张褪色的纸条。

sentences.en: 'This place smells like *childhood*,' she said softly, 'like something warm you can almost remember.'

equal:2.en: Old Helm spread the new map fragment across a flat stone. The left half showed a sky route; the right half showed a sea route. He studied both for a long moment. 'Neither path is easy,' he said. 'But the danger is *equal*, so we choose by heart, not by fear.'
equal:2.cnHint: 老舵研究新地图碎片，发现两条路的风险____，他决定凭心而非恐惧来选择。
equal:2.hook: Then a wind came and lifted the map right out of his hands.
equal:2.line: 'The danger on both roads is *equal*, so we choose by heart.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the new map fragment across a flat stone.
sentences.cn: 老舵把新地图碎片铺展在一块平坦的石头上。

sentences.en: The left half showed a sky route; the right half showed a sea route.
sentences.cn: 左半边显示的是空中路线，右半边显示的是海上路线。

sentences.en: He studied both for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 他盯着两条路线看了很久。

sentences.en: 'Neither path is easy,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他说："两条路都不好走。"

sentences.en: 'But the danger is *equal*, so we choose by heart, not by fear.'

inspire:2.en: At the rim of a crumbling island, we found letters carved into the stone — names of travellers who had passed through before us. Old Helm traced one name with his finger. 'They found a way forward,' he said quietly. 'Let their courage *inspire* us to find ours.'
inspire:2.cnHint: 在破碎岛的边缘，前人留下的名字____了老舵，也激励着整个旅团继续前行。
inspire:2.hook: One of the carved names matched a name on Bell's tin-box note.
inspire:2.line: 'Let their courage *inspire* us to find our own way forward.'

sentences.en: At the rim of a crumbling island, we found letters carved into the stone — names of travellers who had passed through before us.
sentences.cn: 在一座摇摇欲坠的岛屿边缘，我们发现了刻在石头上的字母——那些在我们之前经过这里的旅人们的名字。

sentences.en: Old Helm traced one name with his finger.
sentences.cn: 老舵用手指追过其中一个名字。

sentences.en: 'They found a way forward,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: 他轻声说："他们找到了前进的路。"

sentences.en: 'Let their courage *inspire* us to find ours.'

narrow:2.en: The bridge between the two floating islands was very old — a single plank wide, swaying in the high wind. Bell went first, arms out, steps careful. 'It's *narrow*,' she called back, 'but every step holds. Trust the plank.' One by one, we crossed into the unknown.
narrow:2.cnHint: 两座浮岛之间有一座____的摇晃木桥，小铃率先过桥，鼓励众人跟上。
narrow:2.hook: Halfway across, the plank let out a long, low crack.
narrow:2.line: 'It is *narrow*, but every step holds — trust the plank.'

sentences.en: The bridge between the two floating islands was very old — a single plank wide, swaying in the high wind.
sentences.cn: 两座浮岛之间的桥非常古老——只有一块木板宽，在强风中摇晃。

sentences.en: Bell went first, arms out, steps careful.
sentences.cn: 小铃走在前面，两臂张开，脚步谨慎。

sentences.en: 'It's *narrow*,' she called back, 'but every step holds.
Trust the plank.'
sentences.cn: 相信这块木板。

sentences.en: One by one, we crossed into the unknown.
sentences.cn: 我们一个接一个地踏入了未知。

quantity:2.en: Silverfang's ship carried a surprising *quantity* of bottled star-light — dozens of small glass jars glowing softly in the hold. 'Each jar lights one hour of flight,' he explained, counting them with quick fingers. 'We have enough to reach the edge of the known sky, and no further.'
quantity:2.cnHint: 银牙的船上存有大____的星光瓶，但只够飞到已知天空的边缘。
quantity:2.hook: Old Helm asked what lay beyond the known sky, and Silverfang said nothing.
quantity:2.line: 'The *quantity* of light we carry is enough for the known sky only.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's ship carried a surprising *quantity* of bottled star-light — dozens of small glass jars glowing softly in the hold.
'Each jar lights one hour of flight,' he explained, counting them with quick fingers.
sentences.cn: 他解释说："每罐灯光能照亮一小时的飞行，"他用敏捷的手指数着，

sentences.en: 'We have enough to reach the edge of the known sky, and no further.'
sentences.cn: "我们有足够的灯光到达已知天空的边缘，再远就没有了。"

sustainable:2.en: We landed on a small island where people grew everything they needed in tall spiral gardens. An elder showed us how each layer fed the next, water cycling round and round. 'Nothing is wasted,' she said proudly. 'A *sustainable* home means the island lives as long as we do.'
sustainable:2.cnHint: 一座螺旋花园岛上的长者向我们展示了____的生活方式，这里的一切循环往复、毫不浪费。
sustainable:2.hook: She then asked if our troupe's journey was as careful as her garden.
sustainable:2.line: 'A *sustainable* home means the island lives as long as we do.'

sentences.en: We landed on a small island where people grew everything they needed in tall spiral gardens.
sentences.cn: 我们降落在一座小岛上，那里的人们在高高的螺旋形花园里种植着他们需要的一切。

sentences.en: An elder showed us how each layer fed the next, water cycling round and round.
sentences.cn: 一位长者向我们展示了每一层如何为下一层提供养分，水在其中循环往复。

sentences.en: 'Nothing is wasted,' she said proudly.
sentences.cn: 她骄傲地说："什么都不会被浪费。"

sentences.en: 'A *sustainable* home means the island lives as long as we do.'

delay:2.en: A thick cloud of silver fog had settled over the next island, making the air too dense to fly through. Old Helm folded his arms and watched it drift. 'We cannot push through that,' he said. 'Any *delay* frustrates me, but a broken ship frustrates me more. We wait.'
delay:2.cnHint: 银雾封锁了前方的岛屿，老舵决定____出发，等待雾气散去，而非强行穿越。
delay:2.hook: By nightfall the fog had not thinned even by one breath.
delay:2.line: 'Any *delay* frustrates me, but a broken ship frustrates me more.'

sentences.en: A thick cloud of silver fog had settled over the next island, making the air too dense to fly through.
sentences.cn: 一层厚厚的银色雾气笼罩了下一个岛屿，空气浓得飞不过去。

sentences.en: Old Helm folded his arms and watched it drift.
sentences.cn: 老舵交叉双臂，看着雾气飘动。

sentences.en: 'We cannot push through that,' he said.
sentences.cn: 他说，我们冲不过那个。

sentences.en: 'Any *delay* frustrates me, but a broken ship frustrates me more.
We wait.'
sentences.cn: 我们等着。

identity:2.en: The gate to the final island on the map would not open for just anyone. It asked each of us to place a hand on a glowing stone and speak our name aloud. 'Your *identity* is your key here,' Bell said, 'not your rank, not your ship — only who you truly are.'
identity:2.cnHint: 地图尽头的大门要求每个人以自己的____作为钥匙，小铃第一个走上前，平静地说出自己的名字。
identity:2.hook: When my turn came, the stone flickered and went cold.
identity:2.line: 'Your *identity* is the only key this gate will ever accept.'

sentences.en: The gate to the final island on the map would not open for just anyone.
sentences.cn: 地图上最后一座岛屿的大门不会为任何人打开。

sentences.en: It asked each of us to place a hand on a glowing stone and speak our name aloud.
sentences.cn: 它要求我们每个人都把手放在一块发光的石头上，大声说出自己的名字。

sentences.en: 'Your *identity* is your key here,' Bell said, 'not your rank, not your ship — only who you truly are.'

store:2.en: We landed on a wide shelf of rock where an old *store* sat at the edge, its wooden shelves still holding jars of dried herbs and folded maps. Bell brushed dust from a small jar and held it to the starlight. Inside, a tiny rolled note curled like a sleeping worm.
store:2.cnHint: 在悬崖边的____里，小铃发现了一张藏在药草罐中的神秘纸条。
store:2.hook: The note named a place none of us had ever heard.
store:2.line: 'This *store* has been waiting for us, not for customers,' Bell whispered.

sentences.en: We landed on a wide shelf of rock where an old *store* sat at the edge, its wooden shelves still holding jars of dried herbs and folded maps.
Bell brushed dust from a small jar and held it to the starlight.
sentences.cn: 小铃拂去小罐子上的灰尘，把它举向星光。

sentences.en: Inside, a tiny rolled note curled like a sleeping worm.
sentences.cn: 里面，一张细小的卷纸像一条沉睡的虫子一样蜷缩着。

budget:2.en: Old Helm spread our coins on the map table and counted twice. Our *budget* for supplies was almost gone, yet three islands still lay ahead on the route. Bell pointed to a cluster of lights below — a floating market, open and bright. We had just enough.
budget:2.cnHint: 老舵清点旅费，发现____所剩无几，但小铃指出了一个希望。
budget:2.hook: The market bell rang once, and a door swung open.
budget:2.line: 'Our *budget* is thin, but our luck,' said Old Helm, 'is full.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread our coins on the map table and counted twice.
sentences.cn: 老舵把我们的硬币铺在地图桌上，数了两遍。

sentences.en: Our *budget* for supplies was almost gone, yet three islands still lay ahead on the route.
Bell pointed to a cluster of lights below — a floating market, open and bright.
sentences.cn: 小铃指向下方一簇灯光——一个浮动集市，开放而明亮。

sentences.en: We had just enough.
sentences.cn: 我们钱刚好够。

grant:2.en: At the archive island, a keeper in a grey coat read our letter of passage and nodded slowly. She would *grant* us access to the lower shelves, where the oldest word-maps were kept behind glass. Bell reached out a careful hand as the keeper turned the key.
grant:2.cnHint: 档案岛的管理员决定____我们进入存放古老文字地图的密室。
grant:2.hook: Behind the glass, one map glowed faintly on its own.
grant:2.line: 'I will *grant* you one hour,' the keeper said, 'not a minute more.'

sentences.en: At the archive island, a keeper in a grey coat read our letter of passage and nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 在档案岛上，一位穿着灰色大衣的守卷人读了我们的通行证，慢慢点了点头。

sentences.en: She would *grant* us access to the lower shelves, where the oldest word-maps were kept behind glass.
Bell reached out a careful hand as the keeper turned the key.
sentences.cn: 小铃小心翼翼地伸出手，守卷人转动了钥匙。

hospital:2.en: The island of Mend was shaped like a crescent, and at its heart stood a bright *hospital* built from pale stone. Old Helm had heard that healers there kept a record of every traveller who passed through — names, words carried, and roads taken. We knocked at the wide front door.
hospital:2.cnHint: 在弯月形的小岛上，老舵带我们去____寻找一份记录旅人踪迹的名册。
hospital:2.hook: A healer opened the door and said, 'We wondered when you'd arrive.'
hospital:2.line: 'The *hospital* holds more than medicines,' Old Helm told us quietly.

sentences.en: The island of Mend was shaped like a crescent, and at its heart stood a bright *hospital* built from pale stone.
Old Helm had heard that healers there kept a record of every traveller who passed through — names, words carried, and roads taken.
sentences.cn: 老舵听说那里的治疗师们保存着每一位经过这里的旅人的记录——姓名、携带的话语和走过的道路。

sentences.en: We knocked at the wide front door.
sentences.cn: 我们敲响了宽大的前门。

island:2.en: From the crow's nest I could count seven peaks rising through the clouds below, each one a separate *island* drifting on the wind like a slow thought. Bell marked them one by one with a grease pencil. At the seventh mark, the pencil stopped — that one was not on any map.
island:2.cnHint: 小铃在标记七座____时，发现第七座根本不在任何地图上。
island:2.hook: The unmarked island turned, slowly, as if watching us back.
island:2.line: 'Every *island* has a name,' Bell said, 'even the ones that hide.'

sentences.en: From the crow's nest I could count seven peaks rising through the clouds below, each one a separate *island* drifting on the wind like a slow thought.
Bell marked them one by one with a grease pencil.
sentences.cn: 小铃用油笔把它们一个一个标记下来。

sentences.en: At the seventh mark, the pencil stopped — that one was not on any map.
sentences.cn: 标到第七座山峰时，笔停住了——那座山不在任何地图上。

native:2.en: An old woman met us at the dock of Greenveil. She was *native* to the island, born before the first rope bridge was built, and she still remembered the original name of the highest peak — a name no written map carried. She smiled and asked what we would trade for it.
native:2.cnHint: 一位土生土长的老婆婆记得最高峰的原始名字，她问我们拿什么来交换。
native:2.hook: She held out her hand and waited in the warm dark.
native:2.line: 'A *native* eye sees what maps always miss,' she said with a smile.

sentences.en: An old woman met us at the dock of Greenveil.
sentences.cn: 一个老妇人在绿林港的码头等着我们。

sentences.en: She was *native* to the island, born before the first rope bridge was built, and she still remembered the original name of the highest peak — a name no written map carried.
She smiled and asked what we would trade for it.
sentences.cn: 她笑着问我们愿意用什么来换这个名字。

tradition:2.en: On the Ember Shelf, every troupe that passed left a single stone at the entrance arch — it was a *tradition* so old no one recalled who started it. Old Helm chose our stone with care: flat, grey, and smooth. He set it down and stood still for a moment longer than usual.
tradition:2.cnHint: 老舵按照古老的____，为旅队挑选了一块石头放在拱门前。
tradition:2.hook: Beneath our stone lay a folded scrap of paper, still warm.
tradition:2.line: '*Tradition* is just memory asking to be kept alive,' Old Helm said softly.

sentences.en: On the Ember Shelf, every troupe that passed left a single stone at the entrance arch — it was a *tradition* so old no one recalled who started it.
Old Helm chose our stone with care: flat, grey, and smooth.
sentences.cn: 老舵精心挑选了我们的石头：平坦、灰色、光滑。

sentences.en: He set it down and stood still for a moment longer than usual.
sentences.cn: 他放下石头，站了一会儿，比平时久了些。

africa:2.en: Inside the archive dome, one shelf held maps copied from travellers who claimed their home sky looked nothing like ours. The label on the oldest copy read: origin unknown, possibly *Africa*. Bell traced the coastline with one finger, eyes wide, as if touching the edge of a different world entirely.
africa:2.cnHint: 档案馆里最古老的地图副本标注着可能来自____，小铃轻轻描摹着那片遥远的海岸线。
africa:2.hook: The coastline matched a shape drawn on our newest word-fragment.
africa:2.line: '*Africa*,' Bell read aloud, 'and yet here it is, above the clouds.'

sentences.en: Inside the archive dome, one shelf held maps copied from travellers who claimed their home sky looked nothing like ours.
sentences.cn: 档案馆里的一个架子上放着从旅人那里抄来的地图，他们声称自己家乡的天空看起来完全不一样。

sentences.en: The label on the oldest copy read: origin unknown, possibly *Africa*.
Bell traced the coastline with one finger, eyes wide, as if touching the edge of a different world entirely.
sentences.cn: 小铃用一根手指描着海岸线，眼睛睁得很大，仿佛在触碰一个完全不同的世界的边缘。

teenager:2.en: Tucked between two mossy stones, I found a rolled note. The handwriting was unsteady but eager — the kind a *teenager* might leave, full of big dreams and shaky spelling. It named an island no map had ever shown. Old Helm read it twice, then smiled like he recognised the dream.
teenager:2.cnHint: 石缝里的纸条出自一个____之手，上面写着从未出现在地图上的岛屿名字。
teenager:2.hook: Old Helm's smile faded the moment he flipped it over.
teenager:2.line: 'A *teenager* wrote this — but the island is very real,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Tucked between two mossy stones, I found a rolled note.
sentences.cn: 我在两块长满苔藓的石头之间找到了一卷纸条。

sentences.en: The handwriting was unsteady but eager — the kind a *teenager* might leave, full of big dreams and shaky spelling.
It named an island no map had ever shown.
sentences.cn: 它标注了一座任何地图上都没有出现过的岛屿。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it twice, then smiled like he recognised the dream.
sentences.cn: 老舵读了两遍，然后笑了，就像认出了那个梦想。

patient:2.en: The old compass dial had not moved in hours. Bell crouched beside it, watching. She was *patient* in a way the rest of us were not — still and quiet while the needle trembled, choosing its direction the way a shy creature picks a path. At last it swung north, toward the edge of the chart.
patient:2.cnHint: 贝尔____地等待旧罗盘指针转动，终于指向了地图的边缘。
patient:2.hook: North led straight off the edge of every map we owned.
patient:2.line: 'Be *patient* — the compass always finds its truth,' Bell said softly.

sentences.en: The old compass dial had not moved in hours.
sentences.cn: 那个古老的罗盘指针已经好几个小时没动了。

sentences.en: Bell crouched beside it, watching.
sentences.cn: 小铃蹲在它旁边，看着它。

sentences.en: She was *patient* in a way the rest of us were not — still and quiet while the needle trembled, choosing its direction the way a shy creature picks a path.
At last it swung north, toward the edge of the chart.
sentences.cn: 最后它转向了北方，指向图表的边缘。

classroom:2.en: The hollow tower on Ashveil Isle had once been a *classroom*: a chalkboard still clung to the curved wall, covered in lessons about wind, current, and the language of clouds. Silverfang traced a diagram with one finger and went quiet. Someone had been teaching navigation here long before any of us were born.
classroom:2.cnHint: 灰帆岛的高塔里曾是一间____，黑板上的航海课字迹至今未散。
classroom:2.hook: The final lesson on the board ended mid-sentence, abruptly.
classroom:2.line: 'This *classroom* held secrets older than our troupe,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: The hollow tower on Ashveil Isle had once been a *classroom*: a chalkboard still clung to the curved wall, covered in lessons about wind, current, and the language of clouds.
Silverfang traced a diagram with one finger and went quiet.
sentences.cn: 银牙用一根手指描着一张图，然后沉默了。

sentences.en: Someone had been teaching navigation here long before any of us were born.
sentences.cn: 在我们任何人出生之前，有人就在这里教过航海了。

vehicle:2.en: Drifting below the island's rim was a small pod — round, sealed, cushioned inside with old velvet. Old Helm called it a *vehicle* for carrying single words across great distances: you placed a written word inside, sealed it, and the wind did the rest. This one still held a word. We had not yet dared open it.
vehicle:2.cnHint: 悬崖下漂浮着一个密封舱，老舵说这是传送____"词语"的____。
vehicle:2.hook: The word sealed inside had been travelling for a hundred years.
vehicle:2.line: 'Every *vehicle* like this carried one word, one secret,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Drifting below the island's rim was a small pod — round, sealed, cushioned inside with old velvet.
sentences.cn: 岛屿边缘下方漂浮着一个小舱——圆形的、密封的，内部用旧天鹅绒垫着。

sentences.en: Old Helm called it a *vehicle* for carrying single words across great distances: you placed a written word inside, sealed it, and the wind did the rest.
This one still held a word.
sentences.cn: 这个舱里面还装着一个字。

sentences.en: We had not yet dared open it.
sentences.cn: 我们还没敢打开它。

remote:2.en: The signal fire burned on an island so *remote* that even Old Helm's oldest chart showed it only as a faint smudge. Yet someone had lit it — deliberately, in a pattern. Three short bursts, one long. Bell said that pattern was an old call for 'come and find us.' We changed course before she finished speaking.
remote:2.cnHint: 在一座极为____的小岛上，有人点燃了求援信号火。
remote:2.hook: No one had visited that island for over sixty years.
remote:2.line: 'It is *remote*, yes — but that fire was lit for us,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The signal fire burned on an island so *remote* that even Old Helm's oldest chart showed it only as a faint smudge.
Yet someone had lit it — deliberately, in a pattern.
sentences.cn: 但有人点燃了它——故意地，按照某种图案。

sentences.en: Three short bursts, one long.
sentences.cn: 三短一长。

sentences.en: Bell said that pattern was an old call for 'come and find us.'
sentences.cn: 小铃说那个图案是求救的古老信号。

sentences.en: We changed course before she finished speaking.
sentences.cn: 她话还没说完我们就改变了航向。

zoo:2.en: One island kept living creatures in glass domes arranged like a garden — a floating *zoo* of animals from islands long since lost to storm. A small fox with silver ears pressed its nose against the glass and stared at me. Pinned to its dome was a card that read: 'Keeper, please come back.'
zoo:2.cnHint: 一座浮空____里关着许多已消失岛屿的生灵，狐狸鼻子贴着玻璃望着我们。
zoo:2.hook: The keeper's logbook lay open to the very last page.
zoo:2.line: 'This *zoo* has been waiting for its keeper,' Bell said gently.

sentences.en: One island kept living creatures in glass domes arranged like a garden — a floating *zoo* of animals from islands long since lost to storm.
A small fox with silver ears pressed its nose against the glass and stared at me.
sentences.cn: 一只银耳小狐狸把鼻子贴在玻璃上，盯着我看。

sentences.en: Pinned to its dome was a card that read: 'Keeper, please come back.'
sentences.cn: 玻璃罩上钉着一张卡片，写着："管理员，请回来。"

card:2.en: Slipped under the door of our rest-hut was a small *card*, no bigger than a palm. On one side was a single drawn star; on the other, five words: 'The map is not finished.' There was no name, no seal, no clue about who had left it — only the faint smell of pine and high wind.
card:2.cnHint: 休息小屋门缝里塞着一张____，上面写着"地图还未完成"。
card:2.hook: The pine scent was still fresh — left within the last hour.
card:2.line: 'Whoever left this *card* is still on this island,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Slipped under the door of our rest-hut was a small *card*, no bigger than a palm.
On one side was a single drawn star; on the other, five words: 'The map is not finished.'
sentences.cn: 另一面写着五个字："地图还没完成。"

sentences.en: There was no name, no seal, no clue about who had left it — only the faint smell of pine and high wind.
sentences.cn: 没有名字、没有印章、没有任何线索能看出是谁留下的——只有淡淡的松木和高空风的气味。

gene:2.en: The old botanist's journal, buried in a seed chest, claimed that every sky-flower carried a *gene* for direction — a hidden code that made the bloom always face the nearest uncharted land. Bell held a pressed flower to the light, and its petals swung east, toward blank sky. Our compasses showed nothing. The flower did.
gene:2.cnHint: 古老日志说天空花朵携带一种____，能指向最近的未知陆地，贝尔手中的花瓣转向了东方。
gene:2.hook: East on every chart was nothing — just open, unmarked sky.
gene:2.line: 'This *gene* makes the flower a better compass than ours,' Bell said.

sentences.en: The old botanist's journal, buried in a seed chest, claimed that every sky-flower carried a *gene* for direction — a hidden code that made the bloom always face the nearest uncharted land.
Bell held a pressed flower to the light, and its petals swung east, toward blank sky.
sentences.cn: 小铃把一朵压干的花举向光线，花瓣转向东方，指向空白的天空。

sentences.en: Our compasses showed nothing.
sentences.cn: 我们的罗盘什么都没显示。

sentences.en: The flower did.
sentences.cn: 但花朵显示了。

modern:2.en: The cloud-chart Bell unrolled was unlike any I had seen. Its lines were clean, its colours bright, and tiny lights blinked where old maps showed only blank sky. 'This is *modern* navigation,' she said softly, tracing a glowing path toward the island at the edge of the known world.
modern:2.cnHint: 小铃展开一张与旧地图截然不同的云图，引领众人走向未知的____航路。
modern:2.hook: One blinking light on the chart had no name at all.
modern:2.line: 'This *modern* chart shows paths no old map ever dared to draw.'

sentences.en: The cloud-chart Bell unrolled was unlike any I had seen.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开的云图与我见过的任何地图都不一样。

sentences.en: Its lines were clean, its colours bright, and tiny lights blinked where old maps showed only blank sky.
sentences.cn: 线条清晰，色彩鲜艳，在那些老地图只显示空白天空的地方，闪烁着细小的光点。

sentences.en: 'This is *modern* navigation,' she said softly, tracing a glowing path toward the island at the edge of the known world.

officer:2.en: A figure in a grey coat stood at the gate of the Archive Isle, arms folded. Bell whispered that he was a sky-guild *officer*, one of the people who decided which travellers could enter and which had to turn back. Old Helm stepped forward, calm as stone, to speak with him.
officer:2.cnHint: 档案岛门口站着一名____，决定着旅人的去留。
officer:2.hook: The officer's eyes moved slowly from Old Helm to me.
officer:2.line: 'I am the *officer* here, and no one passes without a word-seal.'

sentences.en: A figure in a grey coat stood at the gate of the Archive Isle, arms folded.
sentences.cn: 一个穿着灰色大衣的身影站在档案岛的门口，双臂交叉。

sentences.en: Bell whispered that he was a sky-guild *officer*, one of the people who decided which travellers could enter and which had to turn back.
Old Helm stepped forward, calm as stone, to speak with him.
sentences.cn: 老舵平静得像块石头，向前走去与他说话。

convince:2.en: The gate would not move. Old Helm laid our collected words on the stone counter one by one, telling the story behind each. I watched the guard's hard face soften degree by degree. It took every story we had to *convince* him that our troupe belonged on the other side.
convince:2.cnHint: 老舵主用一个个字词的故事，费尽心思____守门人放行。
convince:2.hook: As the gate creaked open, I noticed the guard slip one word into his own pocket.
convince:2.line: 'Nothing will *convince* me faster than a word earned by honest travel.'

sentences.en: The gate would not move.
sentences.cn: 门纹丝不动。

sentences.en: Old Helm laid our collected words on the stone counter one by one, telling the story behind each.
sentences.cn: 老舵一张张地把我们收集的词语放在石头柜台上，讲述每个词语背后的故事。

sentences.en: I watched the guard's hard face soften degree by degree.
sentences.cn: 我看着卫兵那张冷硬的脸逐渐柔和起来。

sentences.en: It took every story we had to *convince* him that our troupe belonged on the other side.

directly:2.en: Most travellers climbed the long outer stairs to reach the Lantern Deck. Bell said there was a shorter way. She walked *directly* to a small iron panel in the wall, pressed a carved word into its slot, and a hidden lift hummed to life, carrying us straight up through the heart of the island.
directly:2.cnHint: 小铃找到一条____通往灯台甲板的秘密通道，省去了漫长的阶梯。
directly:2.hook: The lift stopped one floor higher than it should have.
directly:2.line: 'Go *directly* to the top — the longer path is a trap left for the careless.'

sentences.en: Most travellers climbed the long outer stairs to reach the Lantern Deck.
sentences.cn: 大多数旅人都要爬上漫长的外部阶梯才能到达灯塔甲板。

sentences.en: Bell said there was a shorter way.
sentences.cn: 小铃说有条更近的路。

sentences.en: She walked *directly* to a small iron panel in the wall, pressed a carved word into its slot, and a hidden lift hummed to life, carrying us straight up through the heart of the island.

extend:2.en: The rope bridge between Thorn Isle and Pale Isle was three boards short of the far platform. Old Helm studied it, then drew a word card from his coat. He pressed it to the last post, and the bridge began to *extend*, plank by plank, until it touched solid ground ahead of us.
extend:2.cnHint: 老舵主用一张字词卡让断桥自行____，跨越了最后的空缺。
extend:2.hook: The final plank locked into place with a sound like a held breath released.
extend:2.line: 'One strong word can *extend* a bridge further than ten planks of wood.'

sentences.en: The rope bridge between Thorn Isle and Pale Isle was three boards short of the far platform.
sentences.cn: 荆棘岛和苍白岛之间的绳桥距离对面的平台还差三块板。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied it, then drew a word card from his coat.
sentences.cn: 老舵研究了一下，然后从外套里抽出一张词卡。

sentences.en: He pressed it to the last post, and the bridge began to *extend*, plank by plank, until it touched solid ground ahead of us.

rat:2.en: Something small darted under the shelf in the word-vault. Bell held up her lantern and there, gnawing the corner of an old map, sat a pale *rat* with ink-black eyes. Its teeth had already eaten through two letters of the word we needed most. Old Helm sighed and knelt very slowly.
rat:2.cnHint: 在字词库里，一只____正在啃食我们最需要的那张地图残片。
rat:2.hook: The rat looked up at Old Helm as though it understood every word.
rat:2.line: 'That *rat* has eaten half our route — and it does not look sorry at all.'

sentences.en: Something small darted under the shelf in the word-vault.
sentences.cn: 词汇库的架子下有什么东西窜过。

sentences.en: Bell held up her lantern and there, gnawing the corner of an old map, sat a pale *rat* with ink-black eyes.
Its teeth had already eaten through two letters of the word we needed most.
sentences.cn: 它的牙齿已经咬穿了我们最需要的那个词的两个字母。

sentences.en: Old Helm sighed and knelt very slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵叹了口气，非常缓慢地跪了下去。

saturday:2.en: The harbour master's log lay open on the desk. Bell ran her finger down the dates until she stopped with a sharp breath. The last ship to visit the far island had docked on a *Saturday* in early spring, two years ago, and its captain had never signed out. No one had gone back since.
saturday:2.cnHint: 航务日志显示，上一艘访问远岛的船在一个____靠港后，船长就再未出现过。
saturday:2.hook: Below that Saturday entry someone had drawn a small, unfinished map.
saturday:2.line: 'It was a *Saturday* when they left — and a Saturday when the silence began.'

sentences.en: The harbour master's log lay open on the desk.
sentences.cn: 港口长的日志打开放在书桌上。

sentences.en: Bell ran her finger down the dates until she stopped with a sharp breath.
sentences.cn: 小铃用手指沿着日期向下滑，突然停住了，倒吸一口冷气。

sentences.en: The last ship to visit the far island had docked on a *Saturday* in early spring, two years ago, and its captain had never signed out.
No one had gone back since.
sentences.cn: 从那以后就没人回去过。

april:2.en: Tucked inside the hollow of the speaking-stone was a folded note, brittle at the edges. The date at the top read the third of *April*, three years past. The handwriting was hurried, the message short: the next island only appears when two sworn travellers call its name together under a new moon.
april:2.cnHint: 石洞里藏着一张三年前____留下的字条，记录着下一座岛屿出现的秘密条件。
april:2.hook: Neither of us knew whether we still had time to reach it before the new moon passed.
april:2.line: 'Every *April* the stone hides a new note — this one was meant for us.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside the hollow of the speaking-stone was a folded note, brittle at the edges.
sentences.cn: 折成一半的纸条塞在说话石的空心里，边缘都脆了。

sentences.en: The date at the top read the third of *April*, three years past.
The handwriting was hurried, the message short: the next island only appears when two sworn travellers call its name together under a new moon.
sentences.cn: 笔迹很匆促，信息很短：只有当两个发了誓的旅人在新月下一起呼唤岛屿的名字时，下一个岛屿才会出现。

artificial:2.en: Deep inside the hollow mountain, we found a garden where every flower glowed with a pale blue light. Old Helm knelt and touched a petal. 'These are *artificial*,' he said quietly. 'Someone built this place to look alive.' The air smelled of cold metal, not soil.
artificial:2.cnHint: 在空心山腹中，老船长发现花园里的花朵并非天然，而是____的。
artificial:2.hook: But the garden had a door, and the door was warm.
artificial:2.line: Old Helm: 'Every bloom here is *artificial* — yet something tends them still.'

sentences.en: Deep inside the hollow mountain, we found a garden where every flower glowed with a pale blue light.
sentences.cn: 在空心山的深处，我们发现了一个花园，那里的每朵花都闪烁着苍白的蓝光。

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt and touched a petal.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪下，触摸了一片花瓣。

sentences.en: 'These are *artificial*,' he said quietly.
'Someone built this place to look alive.'
sentences.cn: "有人建造了这个地方，让它看起来活生生的。"

sentences.en: The air smelled of cold metal, not soil.
sentences.cn: 空气里闻不到泥土的味道，只有冷金属的气味。

confirm:2.en: Bell unrolled the old map and held it against the stone wall. The carvings matched perfectly. She traced each line with one finger, then looked up with bright eyes. 'This does *confirm* it,' she said. 'The next island is real, and we are standing at its front door.'
confirm:2.cnHint: 领航员将地图与石壁上的刻纹对比，终于____了下一座岛屿的存在。
confirm:2.hook: The wall then shuddered, as though it had heard her.
confirm:2.line: Bell: 'The carvings *confirm* every word on this map — we found it.'

sentences.en: Bell unrolled the old map and held it against the stone wall.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开那张旧地图，贴在石墙上。

sentences.en: The carvings matched perfectly.
sentences.cn: 雕刻完美地吻合。

sentences.en: She traced each line with one finger, then looked up with bright eyes.
sentences.cn: 她用一根手指沿着每条线描过，然后抬头看我，眼睛闪闪发亮。

sentences.en: 'This does *confirm* it,' she said.
'The next island is real, and we are standing at its front door.'
sentences.cn: "下一个岛屿是真实存在的，我们正站在它的前门。"

context:2.en: I handed the torn page to Old Helm. Alone, the words meant nothing. He placed it beside two other fragments on the table, and suddenly the *context* was clear: the symbols formed a name, the name of an island no one in the troupe had ever visited.
context:2.cnHint: 单独一页残纸毫无意义，但结合其他碎片，老船长读懂了____，发现了一座无人知晓的岛屿名称。
context:2.hook: Old Helm folded the fragments and said nothing for a long time.
context:2.line: Old Helm: 'Without *context*, even the truest clue is just noise.'

sentences.en: I handed the torn page to Old Helm.
sentences.cn: 我把撕破的纸页递给老舵。

sentences.en: Alone, the words meant nothing.
sentences.cn: 单独一张，这些字词什么都说不了。

sentences.en: He placed it beside two other fragments on the table, and suddenly the *context* was clear: the symbols formed a name, the name of an island no one in the troupe had ever visited.

date:2.en: On the underside of a wind-dial we found carved numbers: a *date* more than three hundred years old. Bell whispered that no map in our collection was half that age. Old Helm rubbed the dust away slowly. Whoever left this message had been waiting a very long time for us to arrive.
date:2.cnHint: 风向仪背面刻着一个____，距今已逾三百年，比船队所有地图都要古老。
date:2.hook: Below the date was a single instruction, still perfectly clear.
date:2.line: Bell: 'This *date* is older than any record we carry — who left it?'

sentences.en: On the underside of a wind-dial we found carved numbers: a *date* more than three hundred years old.
Bell whispered that no map in our collection was half that age.
sentences.cn: 小铃低声说，我们收藏中没有一张地图有那么久远。

sentences.en: Old Helm rubbed the dust away slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵慢慢擦去灰尘。

sentences.en: Whoever left this message had been waiting a very long time for us to arrive.
sentences.cn: 无论是谁留下这条信息，都已经等了很久，等我们的到来。

flexible:2.en: The bridge between the two peaks was made of woven reeds, and it swayed with every step. Silverfang crossed first, light and quick. 'Stay *flexible*,' he called back, bending his knees as the bridge dipped. 'Fight the swing and you fall. Move with it and you fly.' I believed him.
flexible:2.cnHint: 银牙船长告诉大家，过吊桥时要____，顺势而动，否则会坠落。
flexible:2.hook: Halfway across, one reed snapped beneath my foot.
flexible:2.line: Silverfang: 'Stay *flexible* — the bridge decides nothing, your body decides everything.'

sentences.en: The bridge between the two peaks was made of woven reeds, and it swayed with every step.
sentences.cn: 两座山峰之间的桥用编织的芦苇做成，每踏一步都摇晃。

sentences.en: Silverfang crossed first, light and quick.
sentences.cn: 银牙先过去，轻快得很。

sentences.en: 'Stay *flexible*,' he called back, bending his knees as the bridge dipped.
'Fight the swing and you fall.
sentences.cn: 逆着摇晃对抗，你就会掉下去。

sentences.en: Move with it and you fly.'
sentences.cn: 顺着它摇，你就能飞起来。

sentences.en: I believed him.
sentences.cn: 我相信他。

fly:2.en: Old Helm opened a small glass box and out rose a paper crane that moved on its own. It circled the room once, then hovered before me. 'Let it go,' Bell said softly. I opened the window, and with one clean *fly* it was gone, carrying our reply into the open sky.
fly:2.cnHint: 老船长放出一只会自行移动的纸鹤，让它____着带走了我们的回信。
fly:2.hook: We watched until the crane became a star, then winked out.
fly:2.line: Bell: 'One clean *fly* and our message is on its way — trust it.'

sentences.en: Old Helm opened a small glass box and out rose a paper crane that moved on its own.
sentences.cn: 老舵打开一个小玻璃盒，里面飞出一只会自己活动的纸鹤。

sentences.en: It circled the room once, then hovered before me.
sentences.cn: 它在房间里转了一圈，然后停在我面前。

sentences.en: 'Let it go,' Bell said softly.
sentences.cn: 小铃轻声说。

sentences.en: I opened the window, and with one clean *fly* it was gone, carrying our reply into the open sky.

judge:2.en: At the island's market, a woman sat behind a high desk covered in small stones. Each trader placed an object before her; she studied it in silence and set a stone beside it. Silverfang leaned close to me. 'She is the *judge* here,' he murmured. 'Her word sets every price.'
judge:2.cnHint: 集市上有一位女____，用石头为所有交易品定价，一言九鼎。
judge:2.hook: Then she looked up and fixed her eyes on our troupe.
judge:2.line: Silverfang: 'In this market the *judge* speaks once, and no one argues twice.'

sentences.en: At the island's market, a woman sat behind a high desk covered in small stones.
sentences.cn: 在岛屿的市集里，一个女人坐在堆满小石头的高桌后。

sentences.en: Each trader placed an object before her; she studied it in silence and set a stone beside it.
sentences.cn: 每个商人都在她面前放一件东西；她默默地研究，然后在它旁边放一块石头。

sentences.en: Silverfang leaned close to me.
sentences.cn: 银牙靠近我。
