sentences.en: 'She is the *judge* here,' he murmured.
'Her word sets every price.'
sentences.cn: 她说了算，每样东西的价格都由她决定。

oil:2.en: The old lighthouse had not turned in years. Bell found a rusted gear at its base and tried to force it by hand. I passed her a small bottle from Old Helm's pack. She poured a few drops of *oil* onto the joint, waited, then pushed again. The great light slowly began to turn.
oil:2.cnHint: 领航员用一小瓶____润滑了锈死的齿轮，让沉寂多年的灯塔重新转动。
oil:2.hook: As the beam swept out, it lit something far below the clouds.
oil:2.line: Bell: 'A little *oil* and three hundred years of rust give way at last.'

sentences.en: The old lighthouse had not turned in years.
sentences.cn: 那座老灯塔多年没有转过了。

sentences.en: Bell found a rusted gear at its base and tried to force it by hand.
sentences.cn: 小铃在它底部找到一个生锈的齿轮，试图用手强行转动。

sentences.en: I passed her a small bottle from Old Helm's pack.
sentences.cn: 我从老舵的背包里拿出一个小瓶子递给她。

sentences.en: She poured a few drops of *oil* onto the joint, waited, then pushed again.
The great light slowly began to turn.
sentences.cn: 那盏巨大的灯慢慢开始转动了。

passion:2.en: Deep inside the Archive Island, we found a sealed chest. Inside lay hundreds of hand-drawn maps, each one signed by the same explorer. Old Helm held one up to the lantern light and smiled. 'Whoever made these had a real *passion* for discovery,' he said. The word glowed on the page, and a new path opened on our own map.
passion:2.cnHint: 在档案岛的密室里，老舵找到了一批手绘地图，感受到制图者对探索的____。
passion:2.hook: But the last map showed an island none of us had ever heard of.
passion:2.line: 'Whoever made these had a real *passion* for discovery.'

sentences.en: Deep inside the Archive Island, we found a sealed chest.
sentences.cn: 在档案岛的深处，我们发现了一个密闭的箱子。

sentences.en: Inside lay hundreds of hand-drawn maps, each one signed by the same explorer.
sentences.cn: 里面放着数百张手绘地图，每一张都由同一个探险家签名。

sentences.en: Old Helm held one up to the lantern light and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵把其中一张举到灯光下，笑了。

sentences.en: 'Whoever made these had a real *passion* for discovery,' he said.
The word glowed on the page, and a new path opened on our own map.
sentences.cn: 这个词在纸页上闪闪发光，我们自己的地图上也随之显现了一条新的路线。

temperature:2.en: The Cloud-Well Island was wrapped in thick white mist. Bell checked a small glass instrument hanging from the ship's rail and frowned. 'The *temperature* is dropping fast,' she said, tapping the glass. 'That means the well is still active.' Sure enough, warm light pulsed below the mist, and the word rose to meet us like a lantern lifted by a friendly hand.
temperature:2.cnHint: 贝尔在云井岛测量____，发现气温骤降，说明井中仍有神秘活动。
temperature:2.hook: Then the mist parted, revealing a staircase spiralling straight down into the clouds.
temperature:2.line: 'The *temperature* is dropping fast — the well is still active.'

sentences.en: The Cloud-Well Island was wrapped in thick white mist.
sentences.cn: 云井岛被厚重的白雾笼罩。

sentences.en: Bell checked a small glass instrument hanging from the ship's rail and frowned.
sentences.cn: 小铃查看了挂在船栏杆上的小玻璃仪器，皱起了眉头。

sentences.en: 'The *temperature* is dropping fast,' she said, tapping the glass.
'That means the well is still active.'
sentences.cn: 这说明那口井仍然活跃着。

sentences.en: Sure enough, warm light pulsed below the mist, and the word rose to meet us like a lantern lifted by a friendly hand.
sentences.cn: 果然，温暖的光在雾下脉动，那个词升起来迎接我们，就像被友好的手举起的灯笼。

board:2.en: We found the message on a wide, flat piece of driftwood half-buried in the sand of Tide-Stop Island. Someone had carved words into the *board* with great care, and the final line read: 'Follow the three bright stars.' Old Helm brushed away the sand and read it twice, quietly, as if he were afraid the words might vanish.
board:2.cnHint: 在潮停岛，众人在一块____上发现了刻字留言，最后一行指向三颗星。
board:2.hook: Old Helm looked up at the sky, and there they were — three stars in a perfect line.
board:2.line: 'Someone carved this message into the *board* by hand — it must matter.'

sentences.en: We found the message on a wide, flat piece of driftwood half-buried in the sand of Tide-Stop Island.
sentences.cn: 我们在退潮岛的沙地里发现了那条讯息，刻在一块宽阔平坦的漂木上。

sentences.en: Someone had carved words into the *board* with great care, and the final line read: 'Follow the three bright stars.'
Old Helm brushed away the sand and read it twice, quietly, as if he were afraid the words might vanish.
sentences.cn: 老舵拂去沙子，轻声读了两遍，仿佛担心这些词会消失。

handle:2.en: The old signal box on Copper-Peak Island was rusted shut. I grabbed the iron *handle* and pulled with both hands until it gave way with a groan. Inside was a rolled note and a small glowing stone. Bell read the note aloud: 'Leave the stone; take the word.' We took the word. The stone kept shining, as if saying goodbye.
handle:2.cnHint: 在铜峰岛，叙述者拉开信号箱的____，发现里面藏有纸条和发光石。
handle:2.hook: The glowing stone slowly rolled to the edge of the shelf, paused, and stopped.
handle:2.line: 'Grab the *handle* with both hands — it looks like it has not moved in years.'

sentences.en: The old signal box on Copper-Peak Island was rusted shut.
sentences.cn: 铜峰岛上的那个老信号箱生了锈，紧紧关闭着。

sentences.en: I grabbed the iron *handle* and pulled with both hands until it gave way with a groan.
Inside was a rolled note and a small glowing stone.
sentences.cn: 里面是一张卷起的纸条和一块会发光的小石头。

sentences.en: Bell read the note aloud: 'Leave the stone; take the word.'
sentences.cn: 小铃大声读出纸条：放下石头，拿走这个词。

sentences.en: We took the word.
sentences.cn: 我们拿走了那个词。

sentences.en: The stone kept shining, as if saying goodbye.
sentences.cn: 石头继续闪闪发光，仿佛在说再见。

ideal:2.en: Lens Island had clear skies, calm winds, and a flat stone terrace perfect for reading maps. Old Helm spread our charts across the stone and nodded with satisfaction. 'This is the *ideal* spot,' he said. 'We can see every island from here.' And he was right — for the first time, the whole floating world lay before us, bright and ordered as a dream we had all shared.
ideal:2.cnHint: 镜片岛视野开阔，老舵认为这里是查看地图的____地点，众人第一次看清了整片浮岛世界。
ideal:2.hook: Then a cloud drifted past and cast a shadow shaped exactly like an arrow.
ideal:2.line: 'This is the *ideal* spot — we can see every island from here.'

sentences.en: Lens Island had clear skies, calm winds, and a flat stone terrace perfect for reading maps.
sentences.cn: 镜头岛天空晴朗，风平浪静，有一个平坦的石头平台非常适合看地图。

sentences.en: Old Helm spread our charts across the stone and nodded with satisfaction.
sentences.cn: 老舵在石头上展开我们的图表，满意地点了点头。

sentences.en: 'This is the *ideal* spot,' he said.
'We can see every island from here.'
sentences.cn: 我们能从这里看到每一个岛屿。

sentences.en: And he was right — for the first time, the whole floating world lay before us, bright and ordered as a dream we had all shared.
sentences.cn: 他说得没错——第一次，整个漂浮的世界就展现在我们眼前，明亮得像一个我们都共同做过的梦。

ride:2.en: The sky-current above Drift Island moved like a quiet river of wind. Silverfang said we could let it carry us if we raised the soft sail. It was a slow, gentle *ride*, almost like floating on a calm sea, and the stars drifted by overhead like old friends walking past. At the far end of the current, a new island appeared, wrapped in golden morning light.
ride:2.cnHint: 在漂流岛上方，船队借助天流扬帆，享受了一段平稳的____，最终发现了沐浴晨光的新岛。
ride:2.hook: The golden light then shifted, and the island's outline changed into something like a door.
ride:2.line: 'Raise the soft sail and enjoy the *ride* — the current will take us right to it.'

sentences.en: The sky-current above Drift Island moved like a quiet river of wind.
sentences.cn: 漂流岛上方的天流像一条安静的风河一样流动。

sentences.en: Silverfang said we could let it carry us if we raised the soft sail.
sentences.cn: 银牙说如果我们升起软帆，可以让它带着我们。

sentences.en: It was a slow, gentle *ride*, almost like floating on a calm sea, and the stars drifted by overhead like old friends walking past.
At the far end of the current, a new island appeared, wrapped in golden morning light.
sentences.cn: 在气流的另一端，一个新的岛屿出现了，沐浴在金色的晨光中。

adjust:2.en: The star-chart Bell had drawn was almost right, but the northern corner was off by a small angle. She sat cross-legged on the deck, pencil moving steadily, careful to *adjust* each line until it matched the sky above us. When she finished, the chart lit up along its edges with a soft blue glow, and three new islands appeared where blank space had been.
adjust:2.cnHint: 贝尔在甲板上仔细____星图中偏差的角度，修正后地图边缘发出蓝光，新岛随之浮现。
adjust:2.hook: The middle of the three new islands pulsed once, then went completely dark.
adjust:2.line: 'I need to *adjust* this angle — even a small error will send us the wrong way.'

sentences.en: The star-chart Bell had drawn was almost right, but the northern corner was off by a small angle.
sentences.cn: 小铃画的星图几乎是对的，但北角偏离了一个小角度。

sentences.en: She sat cross-legged on the deck, pencil moving steadily, careful to *adjust* each line until it matched the sky above us.
When she finished, the chart lit up along its edges with a soft blue glow, and three new islands appeared where blank space had been.
sentences.cn: 当她完成时，星图的边缘亮起了柔和的蓝光，之前空白的地方出现了三个新岛屿。

basis:2.en: Old Helm would not choose our next island at random. He spread the collected word-fragments on the deck and studied them one by one. 'We move on a solid *basis*,' he said, 'not on guesses.' He arranged the fragments into a pattern, and they locked together with a soft click, forming a complete map that pointed clearly to the east.
basis:2.cnHint: 老舵将收集到的词语碎片逐一研究，认为行动要有充分的____，拼合后地图指向了东方。
basis:2.hook: The completed map then began to fold itself, slowly, into the shape of a ship.
basis:2.line: 'We move on a solid *basis* — never on guesses alone.'

sentences.en: Old Helm would not choose our next island at random.
sentences.cn: 老舵不会随意选择我们的下一个岛屿。

sentences.en: He spread the collected word-fragments on the deck and studied them one by one.
sentences.cn: 他把收集到的词片段铺在甲板上，一个一个地研究。

sentences.en: 'We move on a solid *basis*,' he said, 'not on guesses.'
He arranged the fragments into a pattern, and they locked together with a soft click, forming a complete map that pointed clearly to the east.
sentences.cn: 他把这些片段排成一个图案，它们咔哒一声锁在了一起，形成一张完整的地图，清楚地指向东方。

comfortable:2.en: We found the message tucked inside an old wooden chest near the edge of Driftstone Isle. Old Helm spread a worn *comfortable* quilt over the chest's lid and smoothed it flat, then lifted a folded note hidden beneath — a map fragment with words we had never seen before.
comfortable:2.cnHint: 老舵在漂石岛边缘的旧木箱里发现了一张纸条，纸条下藏着新的地图碎片。
comfortable:2.hook: The words on the fragment glowed faintly, then went dark.
comfortable:2.line: 'Lay it flat on something *comfortable*, or the ink will crack,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: We found the message tucked inside an old wooden chest near the edge of Driftstone Isle.
sentences.cn: 我们在漂流石岛边缘的一只老木箱里找到了那条信息。

sentences.en: Old Helm spread a worn *comfortable* quilt over the chest's lid and smoothed it flat, then lifted a folded note hidden beneath — a map fragment with words we had never seen before.

conclusion:2.en: Bell studied the three stone markers on the ridge of Windhollow Peak for a long moment, moving her lantern slowly from left to right. She drew a quiet breath and announced her *conclusion*: the markers formed an arrow pointing straight toward the unmapped eastern cloud.
conclusion:2.cnHint: 小铃在风谷峰的山脊上仔细观察三块石碑，得出了指向东方未知云海的____。
conclusion:2.hook: No island had ever been charted that far east before.
conclusion:2.line: 'My *conclusion* is simple — someone wanted us to follow this path,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Bell studied the three stone markers on the ridge of Windhollow Peak for a long moment, moving her lantern slowly from left to right.
sentences.cn: 小铃在风谷峰的山脊上盯着那三块石头标记看了很久，缓缓地把灯笼从左移到右。

sentences.en: She drew a quiet breath and announced her *conclusion*: the markers formed an arrow pointing straight toward the unmapped eastern cloud.

formal:2.en: A sealed letter waited on the helm post of an abandoned sky-skiff drifting near Amber Shelf. The handwriting inside was neat and *formal*, each word pressed firmly into the paper — unlike the hurried scrawl we had grown used to from our own troupe's notes.
formal:2.cnHint: 在琥珀礁附近漂流的废弃飞舟上，我们发现了一封字迹____的密封信件。
formal:2.hook: The letter was addressed to a name none of us recognised.
formal:2.line: 'This is too *formal* to be friendly — someone powerful wrote this,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: A sealed letter waited on the helm post of an abandoned sky-skiff drifting near Amber Shelf.
sentences.cn: 一封密信在靠近琥珀礁的一艘废弃天船的舵柱上等着我们。

sentences.en: The handwriting inside was neat and *formal*, each word pressed firmly into the paper — unlike the hurried scrawl we had grown used to from our own troupe's notes.

happiness:2.en: Carved into the bark of the great silver tree at the centre of Lantern Drift was a single sentence left by an earlier traveller: true *happiness*, it read, is the moment a new word opens a door you forgot was locked. Old Helm touched the letters gently and smiled.
happiness:2.cnHint: 在灯漂岛中央的银树树皮上，前人刻下了一句关于____的话，令老舵深受触动。
happiness:2.hook: Beneath the carving, a hollow in the bark held one more fragment.
happiness:2.line: '*Happiness* is carved right here — and so is our next clue,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Carved into the bark of the great silver tree at the centre of Lantern Drift was a single sentence left by an earlier traveller: true *happiness*, it read, is the moment a new word opens a door you forgot was locked.
Old Helm touched the letters gently and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵轻轻摸了摸那些字，笑了。

intelligent:2.en: The puzzle lock on the vault door at Stormcrest Crossing had twelve rotating rings covered in symbols. Bell crouched before it with calm eyes. 'Whoever built this was deeply *intelligent*,' she murmured, and within minutes her careful hands had turned each ring to the right position.
intelligent:2.cnHint: 在风冠渡口的金库门前，小铃赞叹设计者的____，随后冷静地解开了十二环谜题锁。
intelligent:2.hook: The door swung open onto a room full of floating, glowing letters.
intelligent:2.line: 'An *intelligent* builder always leaves one shortcut hidden inside,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The puzzle lock on the vault door at Stormcrest Crossing had twelve rotating rings covered in symbols.
sentences.cn: 风暴岭交叉口保险库的门上有一把谜题锁，十二个旋转的环上刻满了符号。

sentences.en: Bell crouched before it with calm eyes.
sentences.cn: 小铃蹲在它面前，眼神平静。

sentences.en: 'Whoever built this was deeply *intelligent*,' she murmured, and within minutes her careful hands had turned each ring to the right position.

novel:2.en: Among the scattered objects on the shelf of the Pale Harbour lighthouse stood a thin *novel* bound in pale blue cloth, its pages filled not with a story but with hand-drawn charts of islands no official map had ever named. Silverfang lifted it with both hands.
novel:2.cnHint: 在白港灯塔的书架上，银牙发现了一本蓝布封面的____，里面全是从未被官方标注的海岛图。
novel:2.hook: The last page showed an island shaped exactly like a key.
novel:2.line: 'This *novel* holds more secrets than any map I have sailed by,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: Among the scattered objects on the shelf of the Pale Harbour lighthouse stood a thin *novel* bound in pale blue cloth, its pages filled not with a story but with hand-drawn charts of islands no official map had ever named.
Silverfang lifted it with both hands.
sentences.cn: 银牙用双手捧起了它。

political:2.en: The fragment we recovered from Greywood Station was wrapped in a broadsheet covered in bold headlines. Old Helm skimmed it once and set it aside; he had no interest in *political* arguments between distant councils. The fragment beneath it, though, made his eyes go wide.
political:2.cnHint: 老舵对包裹地图碎片的报纸上那些____争论毫无兴趣，却被碎片本身的内容惊住了。
political:2.hook: The fragment named a place even Old Helm had thought was only legend.
political:2.line: 'Leave the *political* noise aside — look at what was hidden underneath,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The fragment we recovered from Greywood Station was wrapped in a broadsheet covered in bold headlines.
sentences.cn: 我们从灰林站找到的碎片被包在一张大字标题的报纸里。

sentences.en: Old Helm skimmed it once and set it aside; he had no interest in *political* arguments between distant councils.
The fragment beneath it, though, made his eyes go wide.
sentences.cn: 但下面那块碎片让他睁大了眼睛。

property:2.en: A brass plate fixed to the gate of the empty garden on Cinderveil Ridge read: private *property* — entry forbidden by order of the Sky Council. Bell tilted her head at the sign, then pointed to the gap in the hedge just wide enough for one person to slip through.
property:2.cnHint: 在煤纱岭的空花园门上，天空议会的牌子写着此处为私人____，禁止入内，但小铃已发现了一条缝隙。
property:2.hook: Inside the garden, something was already waiting for us.
property:2.line: 'A *property* this well-guarded must be hiding something worth finding,' said Bell.

sentences.en: A brass plate fixed to the gate of the empty garden on Cinderveil Ridge read: private *property* — entry forbidden by order of the Sky Council.
Bell tilted her head at the sign, then pointed to the gap in the hedge just wide enough for one person to slip through.
sentences.cn: 小铃歪了歪头看着那块牌子，然后指向树篱上那个刚好够一个人钻过去的缝隙。

relative:2.en: Old Helm spread the old chart across a flat stone and pointed to two islands. 'The distance between them is *relative*,' he said quietly, 'depending on which wind you trust.' Bell studied the gap and began sketching a new path. The chart seemed to breathe under her pencil.
relative:2.cnHint: 老舵主指着地图上两座岛屿，说它们之间的距离取决于你信任哪种风，小铃开始重新绘制路线。
relative:2.hook: But the wind Bell trusted had never blown before.
relative:2.line: 'The distance is *relative*, Bell — trust the wind, not the ruler.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the old chart across a flat stone and pointed to two islands.
sentences.cn: 老舵把那张旧图铺在平石上，指向两座岛屿。

sentences.en: 'The distance between them is *relative*,' he said quietly, 'depending on which wind you trust.'
Bell studied the gap and began sketching a new path.
sentences.cn: 小铃研究了那片区域，开始画起一条新路线。

sentences.en: The chart seemed to breathe under her pencil.
sentences.cn: 在她的铅笔下，图纸像是活了过来。

rent:2.en: We landed on a small market island where a sign above a wooden dock read: 'Storage *rent* due at dawn.' Inside one locked crate, someone had tucked a rolled map page. Whoever left it could no longer afford to keep it. Their loss had become our direction.
rent:2.cnHint: 在一座市集岛上，一个欠了____的储物箱里藏着一张地图残片，失主的损失成了我们的方向。
rent:2.hook: The dock-keeper's lantern swung closer in the dark.
rent:2.line: 'The *rent* was unpaid — so the map became ours tonight.'

sentences.en: We landed on a small market island where a sign above a wooden dock read: 'Storage *rent* due at dawn.'
Inside one locked crate, someone had tucked a rolled map page.
sentences.cn: 在一只上了锁的木箱里，有人塞进了一页卷起来的地图。

sentences.en: Whoever left it could no longer afford to keep it.
sentences.cn: 留下它的人已经付不起保管费了。

sentences.en: Their loss had become our direction.
sentences.cn: 他们的失落成了我们的方向。

round:2.en: The ancient lighthouse ran on a single *round* of gears that clicked once every hour, each click releasing a small drawer. Bell had been counting clicks since midnight. On the seventh, a drawer slid open and offered us a folded slip of paper holding three new words.
round:2.cnHint: 古老灯塔的齿轮完成一次____后，第七个抽屉弹开，里面藏着写有新词语的纸条。
round:2.hook: Three words, but only one of them pointed upward.
round:2.line: 'One full *round* of the gears, and the island reveals its secret.'

sentences.en: The ancient lighthouse ran on a single *round* of gears that clicked once every hour, each click releasing a small drawer.
Bell had been counting clicks since midnight.
sentences.cn: 小铃从午夜开始就在数秒针声。

sentences.en: On the seventh, a drawer slid open and offered us a folded slip of paper holding three new words.
sentences.cn: 第七声响起时，一个抽屉滑开了，递给我们一张折叠的纸条，上面写着三个陌生的字。

structure:2.en: The ruins rose from the mist like a ribcage: tall arches and stone ribs curving inward. 'The *structure* tells you its purpose,' Old Helm said, walking its outline slowly. He stopped at the centre, knelt, and lifted a loose tile. Beneath it lay a shallow box sealed with wax.
structure:2.cnHint: 老舵主通过遗迹的____判断出它的用途，并在中央的活动地砖下发现了一个蜡封的小盒子。
structure:2.hook: The wax seal carried a symbol none of us recognised.
structure:2.line: 'Read the *structure* first — it always hides its treasure at the centre.'

sentences.en: The ruins rose from the mist like a ribcage: tall arches and stone ribs curving inward.
sentences.cn: 那些废墟从雾气中升起，像一副肋骨：高耸的拱门和向内弯曲的石肋。

sentences.en: 'The *structure* tells you its purpose,' Old Helm said, walking its outline slowly.
He stopped at the centre, knelt, and lifted a loose tile.
sentences.cn: 他走到中央，跪下身，掀开了一块松动的瓷砖。

sentences.en: Beneath it lay a shallow box sealed with wax.
sentences.cn: 瓷砖下压着一只用蜡封住的浅盒子。

typical:2.en: This was not a *typical* island stop. There were no traders, no lanterns, no noise — only a ring of white stones and a single wooden post with a name carved into it. Bell whispered the name aloud and the post glowed faintly. A new path lit up on our chart.
typical:2.cnHint: 这不是____的停靠岛，没有商贩也没有灯光，小铃轻声念出木桩上的名字，地图上亮起了新路线。
typical:2.hook: The name Bell whispered matched no island we had ever named.
typical:2.line: 'This is not a *typical* stop — the island is waiting to be called.'

sentences.en: This was not a *typical* island stop.
There were no traders, no lanterns, no noise — only a ring of white stones and a single wooden post with a name carved into it.
sentences.cn: 没有商人，没有灯笼，没有喧哗——只有一圈白石和一根木桩，上面刻着一个名字。

sentences.en: Bell whispered the name aloud and the post glowed faintly.
sentences.cn: 小铃轻声念出那个名字，木桩泛起微弱的光芒。

sentences.en: A new path lit up on our chart.
sentences.cn: 我们的航图上亮起了一条新的路线。

vacation:2.en: Silverfang leaned against his mast, boots off, hat over his eyes. 'Consider this a short *vacation*,' he said with a lazy grin. But his fingers were busy unfolding a water-stained note his crew had found wedged inside the anchor chain. Rest, for Silverfang, always had a purpose.
vacation:2.cnHint: 竞争船长假装在____，却悄悄展开从锚链里找到的一张浸水字条。
vacation:2.hook: The note was addressed to someone who had vanished ten years ago.
vacation:2.line: 'Call it a *vacation* if you like — I call it listening carefully.'

sentences.en: Silverfang leaned against his mast, boots off, hat over his eyes.
sentences.cn: 银牙靠在桅杆上，脱去了靴子，帽子盖在眼睛上。

sentences.en: 'Consider this a short *vacation*,' he said with a lazy grin.
But his fingers were busy unfolding a water-stained note his crew had found wedged inside the anchor chain.
sentences.cn: 但他的手指忙着展开一张水渍斑驳的纸条，是船员们从锚链里夹出来的。

sentences.en: Rest, for Silverfang, always had a purpose.
sentences.cn: 对银牙来说，休息总得有个目的。

acquire:2.en: Old Helm told me that every word we *acquire* changes the shape of our map a little. We had just pressed the word into the soft wax of the record stone, and the island's outline shifted — an extra cove appeared to the east, narrow and bright, as if it had always been waiting.
acquire:2.cnHint: 老舵主说每____到一个新词，地图的形状就会改变，刻入词语后，东边果然多出了一个明亮的海湾。
acquire:2.hook: The new cove was too small for any ship — except ours.
acquire:2.line: 'Every word we *acquire* opens a door the map had kept shut.'

sentences.en: Old Helm told me that every word we *acquire* changes the shape of our map a little.
We had just pressed the word into the soft wax of the record stone, and the island's outline shifted — an extra cove appeared to the east, narrow and bright, as if it had always been waiting.
sentences.cn: 我们刚把那个词按进记录石的软蜡里，岛的轮廓就移动了——东边多出了一个狭长明亮的小海湾，仿佛它一直在那儿等着似的。

adequate:2.en: Bell checked our supplies against the new route. Water, bread, rope — all *adequate* for three days. 'Enough to reach the edge,' she said, tapping the chart. Old Helm nodded and rolled it up. On the final island at the map's end, the stars were said to touch the ground.
adequate:2.cnHint: 小铃确认了补给____以支撑三天行程，老舵主点头收起地图，传说终点岛屿上星辰会触碰地面。
adequate:2.hook: No one had ever said what happened when you touched them back.
adequate:2.line: 'Supplies are *adequate*, Old Helm — we can reach the edge by dawn.'

sentences.en: Bell checked our supplies against the new route.
sentences.cn: 小铃拿着新路线对照补给清单。

sentences.en: Water, bread, rope — all *adequate* for three days.
'Enough to reach the edge,' she said, tapping the chart.
sentences.cn: "够到达地图边缘，"她敲了敲航图说。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded and rolled it up.
sentences.cn: 老舵点点头，把它卷了起来。

sentences.en: On the final island at the map's end, the stars were said to touch the ground.
sentences.cn: 据说在地图末尾的最后一个岛上，星星是触地的。

attribute:2.en: Inside the hollow tree at the edge of the map, I found a carved tablet. Old Helm studied it closely. 'Every island has one quality we can *attribute* to its founding word,' he said, tracing the lines. 'This one belongs to the island of Patience.' A new path lit up beneath our feet.
attribute:2.cnHint: 老舵在地图尽头的空树里发现了一块刻有文字的石板，他将岛屿的特质____于其创始词语。
attribute:2.hook: But the path led somewhere none of us had chosen.
attribute:2.line: 'We can *attribute* this island's stillness to the word carved here.'

sentences.en: Inside the hollow tree at the edge of the map, I found a carved tablet.
sentences.cn: 在地图边缘那棵中空的树里，我找到了一块雕刻的石板。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied it closely.
sentences.cn: 老舵仔细研究了它。

sentences.en: 'Every island has one quality we can *attribute* to its founding word,' he said, tracing the lines.
'This one belongs to the island of Patience.'
sentences.cn: "这个岛属于耐心之岛。"

sentences.en: A new path lit up beneath our feet.
sentences.cn: 我们脚下亮起了一条新的路线。

badly:2.en: Bell pressed her ear against the old stone door at the map's edge. 'I want to open this *badly*,' she whispered, eyes bright with longing. The door had no handle, only a single word carved above the frame. I read it aloud, and the stone trembled, then swung wide into golden light.
badly:2.cnHint: 小铃____想打开地图尽头那扇石门，她大声读出门框上的词语后，门终于打开了。
badly:2.hook: What waited inside was too still to be empty.
badly:2.line: 'I want to find what is behind this door so *badly*.'

sentences.en: Bell pressed her ear against the old stone door at the map's edge.
sentences.cn: 小铃把耳朵贴在地图边缘的古老石门上。

sentences.en: 'I want to open this *badly*,' she whispered, eyes bright with longing.
The door had no handle, only a single word carved above the frame.
sentences.cn: 门上没有把手，只在门框上方刻了一个词。

sentences.en: I read it aloud, and the stone trembled, then swung wide into golden light.
sentences.cn: 我大声读出那个词，石头颤动，然后向着金色的光芒打了开来。

bridge:2.en: A gap split the last island in two — wide, windy, and deep. Old Helm pulled a folded word-card from his coat and pressed it against the air. The word on it glowed, and a stone *bridge* grew from one edge to the other, solid under our boots. He smiled like it was nothing.
bridge:2.cnHint: 老舵用一张词卡在地图尽头的断裂处召唤出了一座____，让众人得以通过。
bridge:2.hook: Something carved into the bridge stones was still moving.
bridge:2.line: 'The word on this card will *bridge* the gap — step forward.'

sentences.en: A gap split the last island in two — wide, windy, and deep.
sentences.cn: 最后一个岛被一条裂隙分成了两半——宽阔、呼啸、深邃。

sentences.en: Old Helm pulled a folded word-card from his coat and pressed it against the air.
sentences.cn: 老舵从外套里掏出一张折叠的词卡，贴在空气上。

sentences.en: The word on it glowed, and a stone *bridge* grew from one edge to the other, solid under our boots.
He smiled like it was nothing.
sentences.cn: 他笑得像是无关紧要的事。

casual:2.en: Silverfang leaned against the rusted gate at the world's edge with a *casual* air, as though he had been waiting there for years. He tossed us a small glass bottle without looking up. Inside it was a folded map fragment, still warm. 'Found it floating,' he said. 'Thought you might need it.'
casual:2.cnHint: 银牙用____的姿态靠在地图尽头的铁门旁，随手递给我们一个装有地图碎片的玻璃瓶。
casual:2.hook: The fragment showed an island none of our maps had named.
casual:2.line: '*Casual* as it looks, that bottle crossed three sky-storms to reach us.'

sentences.en: Silverfang leaned against the rusted gate at the world's edge with a *casual* air, as though he had been waiting there for years.
He tossed us a small glass bottle without looking up.
sentences.cn: 他没抬头就朝我们扔过一个小玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: Inside it was a folded map fragment, still warm.
sentences.cn: 瓶子里装着一片还热乎的折叠地图碎片。

sentences.en: 'Found it floating,' he said.
sentences.cn: "在海上漂来的，"他说。

sentences.en: 'Thought you might need it.'
sentences.cn: "想你们可能用得上。"

closely:2.en: The final marker on our map was a lantern hanging from a cloud-rock. I held the map and studied the lantern *closely*, matching every line and shadow to the drawing. Old Helm stood quiet behind me. When I found the hidden latch on the lantern's base, a small drawer popped open with a soft click.
closely:2.cnHint: 我____仔细观察地图尽头的灯笼，终于找到了隐藏的暗格。
closely:2.hook: The drawer held a key and no lock to match it.
closely:2.line: 'Look *closely* at the base — something there is not just decoration.'

sentences.en: The final marker on our map was a lantern hanging from a cloud-rock.
sentences.cn: 我们地图上最后的标记是一盏悬在云石上的灯笼。

sentences.en: I held the map and studied the lantern *closely*, matching every line and shadow to the drawing.
Old Helm stood quiet behind me.
sentences.cn: 老舵无声地站在我身后。

sentences.en: When I found the hidden latch on the lantern's base, a small drawer popped open with a soft click.
sentences.cn: 当我找到灯笼底部隐藏的卡扣时，一个小抽屉弹了开来，发出轻轻的咔哒声。

commit:2.en: Bell stood at the last stepping-stone, wind pulling at her coat. The next island was barely visible through the mist. 'Once we step off, we *commit* to the crossing — no turning back,' she said. We looked at each other, then at the word glowing in our shared map. We stepped off together.
commit:2.cnHint: 小铃提醒大家，一旦踏出这一步就____无法回头，但众人还是一起跨了出去。
commit:2.hook: The stepping-stone sank the moment the last boot left it.
commit:2.line: 'If we *commit* to this path, the map will show us the rest.'

sentences.en: Bell stood at the last stepping-stone, wind pulling at her coat.
sentences.cn: 小铃站在最后的踏脚石上，风吹扯着她的外套。

sentences.en: The next island was barely visible through the mist.
sentences.cn: 下一个岛在雾霭中隐约可见。

sentences.en: 'Once we step off, we *commit* to the crossing — no turning back,' she said.
We looked at each other, then at the word glowing in our shared map.
sentences.cn: 我们互相看了一眼，又看了看共同航图中泛光的那个词。

sentences.en: We stepped off together.
sentences.cn: 我们一起踏了出去。

concentrate:2.en: The star above the final island pulsed like a slow heartbeat. Old Helm told me to *concentrate* on the word at the map's centre, to hold it clearly in my mind and let nothing else in. I did. The clouds parted. A new island drifted into view, steady and unhurried, as if it had always been there.
concentrate:2.cnHint: 老舵让我____注意力于地图中心的词语，随后一座新岛屿缓缓出现在云层之外。
concentrate:2.hook: The island had a door, and the door was already open.
concentrate:2.line: '*Concentrate* on the word — let every other thought go quiet.'

sentences.en: The star above the final island pulsed like a slow heartbeat.
sentences.cn: 最后那个岛上空的星星像缓慢的心跳一样脉动着。

sentences.en: Old Helm told me to *concentrate* on the word at the map's centre, to hold it clearly in my mind and let nothing else in.
I did.
sentences.cn: 我照做了。

sentences.en: The clouds parted.
sentences.cn: 云散开了。

sentences.en: A new island drifted into view, steady and unhurried, as if it had always been there.
sentences.cn: 一个新的岛漂浮进了视野，平稳而不急不躁，仿佛它一直都在那儿。

conscious:2.en: When I touched the final stone at the edge of the map, I became *conscious* of every word our troupe had ever collected — all of them humming softly inside me at once. Old Helm watched with calm eyes. 'Now you understand,' he said. 'The words were never just a map. They were the journey.'
conscious:2.cnHint: 触摸到地图尽头的石头时，我____意识到我们收集的所有词语都在心中轻声回响。
conscious:2.hook: Old Helm's next words rewrote everything I thought I knew.
conscious:2.line: 'Be *conscious* of each word we carry — they are listening too.'

sentences.en: When I touched the final stone at the edge of the map, I became *conscious* of every word our troupe had ever collected — all of them humming softly inside me at once.
Old Helm watched with calm eyes.
sentences.cn: 老舵用平静的眼神看着我。

sentences.en: 'Now you understand,' he said.
sentences.cn: "现在你明白了，"他说。

sentences.en: 'The words were never just a map.
sentences.cn: "这些词从来不只是一份地图。

sentences.en: They were the journey.'
sentences.cn: 它们就是这段旅程。"

obvious:2.en: The old map chest had been locked for years, but tonight its latch hung open. Inside, a folded note rested on top of a dried flower. The message written there was *obvious*: three arrows pointing toward the edge of the world, and a single word — 'Come.'
obvious:2.cnHint: 箱子里的纸条让大家一眼就看出了____的指引。
obvious:2.hook: Someone had been here before us, and recently.
obvious:2.line: Old Helm said, 'The meaning is *obvious* — we leave at dawn.'

sentences.en: The old map chest had been locked for years, but tonight its latch hung open.
sentences.cn: 这只老地图箱被锁了好多年，但今晚它的闩子却开着了。

sentences.en: Inside, a folded note rested on top of a dried flower.
sentences.cn: 里面压着一张折好的纸条，上面放着一朵干花。

sentences.en: The message written there was *obvious*: three arrows pointing toward the edge of the world, and a single word — 'Come.'

ordinary:2.en: Bell picked up a small stone from the island's edge and turned it slowly in her hand. To anyone else it would seem *ordinary* — round, grey, worn smooth. But when she held it to the starlight, thin golden lines appeared across its surface, like a map waiting to be read.
ordinary:2.cnHint: 小铃手中那块看似____的石头，在星光下藏着秘密。
ordinary:2.hook: The lines shifted, and a new island appeared.
ordinary:2.line: Bell whispered, 'This is no *ordinary* stone, trust me.'

sentences.en: Bell picked up a small stone from the island's edge and turned it slowly in her hand.
sentences.cn: 小铃从岛边捡起一块小石头，在手里慢慢转动。

sentences.en: To anyone else it would seem *ordinary* — round, grey, worn smooth.
But when she held it to the starlight, thin golden lines appeared across its surface, like a map waiting to be read.
sentences.cn: 但她把它对着星光一照，石头表面就浮现出细细的金色纹路，像一份等着被读懂的地图。

pace:2.en: Old Helm began to *pace* the length of the deck, three steps forward, three steps back, while the rest of us waited in silence. He had found a sealed jar with a torn letter inside, and none of the words made sense yet. We watched his boots until he stopped.
pace:2.cnHint: 团长在甲板上____，手里握着一封看不懂的信。
pace:2.hook: Then he smiled, and that was more worrying than the letter.
pace:2.line: Old Helm muttered, 'Let me *pace* and think — I almost have it.'

sentences.en: Old Helm began to *pace* the length of the deck, three steps forward, three steps back, while the rest of us waited in silence.
He had found a sealed jar with a torn letter inside, and none of the words made sense yet.
sentences.cn: 他找到了一只密封的罐子，里面有一封撕破的信，可字都还看不明白。

sentences.en: We watched his boots until he stopped.
sentences.cn: 我们盯着他的靴子看，直到他停下来。

participate:2.en: A glowing board had appeared overnight at the centre of our camp, covered in small tiles, each one a letter. A note pinned beside it said that only those who *participate* in solving the puzzle will see the next island rise from the clouds below.
participate:2.cnHint: 营地里出现的谜题板要求大家____，才能解锁下一座岛屿。
participate:2.hook: One tile was already missing, and no one admitted taking it.
participate:2.line: Silverfang called out, 'Everyone must *participate* — even the new one!'

sentences.en: A glowing board had appeared overnight at the centre of our camp, covered in small tiles, each one a letter.
sentences.cn: 营地中央一夜间出现了一块发光的木板，上面铺满了小瓷砖，每一块都是一个字母。

sentences.en: A note pinned beside it said that only those who *participate* in solving the puzzle will see the next island rise from the clouds below.

pilot:2.en: Tucked inside the hollow of the signal tree, we found a worn leather badge. Bell read the faded letters aloud: *pilot* of the First Sky Route, retired. Whoever left it here had once led ships through the oldest path in the sky, and they wanted us to find this.
pilot:2.cnHint: 信号树的树洞里藏着一枚徽章，属于一位退休的____。
pilot:2.hook: On the back of the badge was our troupe's own symbol.
pilot:2.line: Bell said quietly, 'A *pilot* of the First Route left this for us.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside the hollow of the signal tree, we found a worn leather badge.
sentences.cn: 在信号树的空心处，我们找到了一枚磨损的皮制徽章。

sentences.en: Bell read the faded letters aloud: *pilot* of the First Sky Route, retired.
Whoever left it here had once led ships through the oldest path in the sky, and they wanted us to find this.
sentences.cn: 留下这东西的人曾经领航过天空中最古老的路线，他们想让我们找到这个。

primary:2.en: The fragment we recovered was small, but Bell explained that it was the *primary* piece — the one all other map sections connect to. Without it, the rest of the chart was just scattered shapes. She placed it at the centre of the table and the whole map shivered into focus.
primary:2.cnHint: 小铃说找到的碎片是____的那一块，整张地图因此变得清晰。
primary:2.hook: At the very centre of the map burned a tiny, steady light.
primary:2.line: Bell said, 'This piece is *primary* — everything else follows from it.'

sentences.en: The fragment we recovered was small, but Bell explained that it was the *primary* piece — the one all other map sections connect to.
Without it, the rest of the chart was just scattered shapes.
sentences.cn: 没有它，剩下的图就只是一堆散碎的形状。

sentences.en: She placed it at the centre of the table and the whole map shivered into focus.
sentences.cn: 她把它放在桌子中央，整张地图突然聚焦成了一个整体。

priority:2.en: Silverfang arrived at the dock before sunrise, arms full of supply bags. She said there had been a signal from the far island during the night — two long flashes, one short. Reaching that signal was now our *priority*, and she had already charted the fastest wind path to get there.
priority:2.cnHint: 远岛传来信号，银牙说这是目前最重要的____。
priority:2.hook: Two long flashes, one short — a call for help.
priority:2.line: Silverfang said firmly, 'That signal is our *priority* above all else.'

sentences.en: Silverfang arrived at the dock before sunrise, arms full of supply bags.
sentences.cn: 银牙在日出前赶到了码头，怀里堆满了补给袋。

sentences.en: She said there had been a signal from the far island during the night — two long flashes, one short.
sentences.cn: 她说昨晚远岛传来过信号——两长一短的闪光。

sentences.en: Reaching that signal was now our *priority*, and she had already charted the fastest wind path to get there.

throughout:2.en: *Throughout* the night, small lights had drifted up from the valley below — not fireflies, but folded paper lanterns, each one carrying a single written word. By morning they had gathered against our hull like quiet visitors. Old Helm collected every one and spread them across the floor like a second sky.
throughout:2.cnHint: 整整一夜____，纸灯笼从山谷里飘来，每盏都写着一个词。
throughout:2.hook: Laid together, the words formed one long, urgent sentence.
throughout:2.line: Old Helm said, '*Throughout* the night they came — read every one.'

sentences.en: *Throughout* the night, small lights had drifted up from the valley below — not fireflies, but folded paper lanterns, each one carrying a single written word.
By morning they had gathered against our hull like quiet visitors.
sentences.cn: 到了早上，它们就像安静的访客一样贴在我们的船舱边。

sentences.en: Old Helm collected every one and spread them across the floor like a second sky.
sentences.cn: 老舵把每一盏都收起来，像铺展第二片天空一样把它们摊在地板上。

conventional:2.en: At the edge of the last island, Old Helm unrolled a map unlike any I had seen before. It was not drawn in the *conventional* way — no lines, no compass rose — just scattered words glowing like embers. 'Each word is a door,' he said softly. I reached out and touched the nearest one. The air shivered.
conventional:2.cnHint: 老舵手展开一张地图，和____的地图完全不同，上面只有发光的文字。
conventional:2.hook: The word I touched began to rise off the page.
conventional:2.line: 'This is nothing like a *conventional* map — and that is exactly the point.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the last island, Old Helm unrolled a map unlike any I had seen before.
sentences.cn: 在最后一个岛的边缘，老舵展开了一张我从没见过的地图。

sentences.en: It was not drawn in the *conventional* way — no lines, no compass rose — just scattered words glowing like embers.
'Each word is a door,' he said softly.
sentences.cn: "每个字都是一扇门，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: I reached out and touched the nearest one.
sentences.cn: 我伸手去碰最近的那个字。

sentences.en: The air shivered.
sentences.cn: 空气颤动了。

disappear:2.en: Bell held the compass flat and watched the needle spin. Then, without a sound, the nearest island began to *disappear* — its edges dissolving into starlight like sugar in warm tea. 'It only hides,' Bell said, calm as ever. 'Find the right word and it comes back.' I searched my coat pocket and found one.
disappear:2.cnHint: 小铃看着最近的岛屿慢慢____，她平静地说找到合适的词就能让它回来。
disappear:2.hook: My fingers closed around a folded scrap of glowing paper.
disappear:2.line: 'Don't worry — islands don't truly *disappear*, they just wait to be named.'

sentences.en: Bell held the compass flat and watched the needle spin.
sentences.cn: 小铃把罗盘放平，看着指针转动。

sentences.en: Then, without a sound, the nearest island began to *disappear* — its edges dissolving into starlight like sugar in warm tea.
'It only hides,' Bell said, calm as ever.
sentences.cn: "它只是躲起来了，"小铃平静地说。

sentences.en: 'Find the right word and it comes back.'
sentences.cn: "找到对的字，它就会出现。"

sentences.en: I searched my coat pocket and found one.
sentences.cn: 我在外套口袋里摸索，找到了一个。

district:2.en: The old chart called this stretch of sky the Amber *District* — a region of islands where every stone glowed faintly gold at dusk. Silverfang had sailed here once before and left in a hurry, he said, without explaining why. I copied the name into my notebook. Old Helm gave a quiet nod, as if a door had just unlocked.
district:2.cnHint: 旧海图把这片天空称为琥珀____，每块石头在黄昏时都发出金色的光。
district:2.hook: Silverfang's jaw tightened the moment he heard the name aloud.
district:2.line: 'Mark it down — the Amber *District* is where our next word is waiting.'

sentences.en: The old chart called this stretch of sky the Amber *District* — a region of islands where every stone glowed faintly gold at dusk.
Silverfang had sailed here once before and left in a hurry, he said, without explaining why.
sentences.cn: 银牙说他以前来过这里一次，然后匆匆离开了，但没有解释原因。

sentences.en: I copied the name into my notebook.
sentences.cn: 我把这个名字抄进了笔记本。

sentences.en: Old Helm gave a quiet nod, as if a door had just unlocked.
sentences.cn: 老舵静静地点了点头，仿佛一扇门刚刚打开了。

greatly:2.en: When I read the recovered word aloud, the fog that had wrapped our ship for two days lifted all at once. Bell laughed — a bright, surprised sound. Old Helm said the word had *greatly* widened the map, adding three new islands along the eastern edge where before there had been only blank sky. I stared at the fresh outline and felt something warm open in my chest.
greatly:2.cnHint: 当我大声念出找回的词后，迷雾散去，地图____扩展了，东边多出三座新岛屿。
greatly:2.hook: One of the new islands had a light blinking on its shore.
greatly:2.line: 'Reading that word has *greatly* changed what we thought was the edge of the world.'

sentences.en: When I read the recovered word aloud, the fog that had wrapped our ship for two days lifted all at once.
sentences.cn: 我大声读出那个找到的字时，缠绕我们船两天的雾一下子散开了。

sentences.en: Bell laughed — a bright, surprised sound.
sentences.cn: 小铃笑了——一声明亮、惊喜的笑。

sentences.en: Old Helm said the word had *greatly* widened the map, adding three new islands along the eastern edge where before there had been only blank sky.
I stared at the fresh outline and felt something warm open in my chest.
sentences.cn: 我盯着这份新的轮廓，感觉胸口有什么温暖的东西打开了。

imitate:2.en: Tucked inside a hollow tree on the Isle of Echoes, we found a brass bird that could *imitate* any sound it heard. Old Helm whispered a word into its beak — a word from the map. The bird repeated it perfectly, and a hidden door in the bark swung open. Inside was a lantern and another fragment. Bell grinned. 'Nature is the best teacher,' she said.
imitate:2.cnHint: 在回声岛的空心树里，我们发现了一只能____任何声音的铜鸟，它帮我们打开了藏着地图碎片的暗门。
imitate:2.hook: The lantern inside was already lit, as if someone had just left.
imitate:2.line: 'It can *imitate* any sound — so whisper the word clearly and only once.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside a hollow tree on the Isle of Echoes, we found a brass bird that could *imitate* any sound it heard.
Old Helm whispered a word into its beak — a word from the map.
sentences.cn: 老舵在它的喙里低声说了一个词——地图上的一个词。

sentences.en: The bird repeated it perfectly, and a hidden door in the bark swung open.
sentences.cn: 鸟完美地重复了这个词，树皮里的一扇隐门吱呀一声打开了。

sentences.en: Inside was a lantern and another fragment.
sentences.cn: 里面是一盏灯笼和另一片碎片。

sentences.en: Bell grinned.
sentences.cn: 小铃咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: 'Nature is the best teacher,' she said.
sentences.cn: "大自然是最好的老师，"她说。

implement:2.en: Hanging on the wall of the sky-market stall was every *implement* a navigator could want — bone needles for stitching charts, copper gauges for measuring wind, and tiny ink-pots that never ran dry. Bell picked up a slender silver pen and held it to the light. 'This is how we write the next word properly,' she said. Old Helm paid with a single glowing syllable.
implement:2.cnHint: 天空集市的摊位上挂满了各种导航____，小铃挑了一支银笔，说这才是正确书写下一个词的工具。
implement:2.hook: The ink inside the pen was the color of the night sky.
implement:2.line: 'Every *implement* here was made for one purpose — finding what comes next.'

sentences.en: Hanging on the wall of the sky-market stall was every *implement* a navigator could want — bone needles for stitching charts, copper gauges for measuring wind, and tiny ink-pots that never ran dry.
Bell picked up a slender silver pen and held it to the light.
sentences.cn: 小铃拿起一支纤细的银笔，举到光下。

sentences.en: 'This is how we write the next word properly,' she said.
sentences.cn: "就是用这个来正确地写下一个词，"她说。

sentences.en: Old Helm paid with a single glowing syllable.
sentences.cn: 老舵用一个闪闪发光的音节付了钱。

mood:2.en: A soft rain had settled over the deck, and with it came a strange *mood* — quiet, a little heavy, as if the sky itself was thinking. Old Helm set down his tea and looked out at the grey horizon. Then he smiled and pointed. Far off, catching the last light, a new island had surfaced right where the map said it would. The heavy feeling lifted all at once.
mood:2.cnHint: 甲板上笼罩着一种奇异的____，就连老舵手也沉默下来，直到他发现地图上预言的新岛屿出现了。
mood:2.hook: The island was shaped exactly like the word Old Helm had been holding all week.
mood:2.line: 'The sky has a *mood* today — and I think it is trying to show us something.'

sentences.en: A soft rain had settled over the deck, and with it came a strange *mood* — quiet, a little heavy, as if the sky itself was thinking.
Old Helm set down his tea and looked out at the grey horizon.
sentences.cn: 老舵放下茶杯，看着灰蒙蒙的地平线。

sentences.en: Then he smiled and pointed.
sentences.cn: 然后他笑了，指向远方。

sentences.en: Far off, catching the last light, a new island had surfaced right where the map said it would.
sentences.cn: 远处，接住最后的光线，一个新的岛屿正好出现在地图所说的地方。

sentences.en: The heavy feeling lifted all at once.
sentences.cn: 那沉重的感觉一下子消散了。

motivation:2.en: Silverfang had raced us to the Isle of First Light before, and I asked Bell why he kept chasing the same map we did. She thought for a moment. 'His *motivation* is not the words,' she said. 'It is the proof that they exist.' That answer surprised me. It also made me look at the next fragment in my hand with much gentler eyes.
motivation:2.cnHint: 小铃解释说，银牙追逐地图的____并不是为了那些词本身，而是为了证明它们真实存在。
motivation:2.hook: Silverfang's ship was already a bright speck on the horizon ahead.
motivation:2.line: 'His *motivation* matters — understanding it might be the only way we reach the next island first.'

sentences.en: Silverfang had raced us to the Isle of First Light before, and I asked Bell why he kept chasing the same map we did.
sentences.cn: 银牙之前就比我们先冲到了第一束光的岛屿，我问小铃为什么他还在追我们同样的地图。

sentences.en: She thought for a moment.
sentences.cn: 她想了一会儿。

sentences.en: 'His *motivation* is not the words,' she said.
'It is the proof that they exist.'
sentences.cn: "这些词确实存在的证明。"

sentences.en: That answer surprised me.
sentences.cn: 那个回答让我吃了一惊。

sentences.en: It also made me look at the next fragment in my hand with much gentler eyes.
sentences.cn: 它也让我用更温柔的眼光看着我手里的下一片碎片。

worldwide:2.en: Old Helm unrolled the oldest chart in his pack. It showed not one island or one sea, but a *worldwide* web of floating lands, each dot connected by lines of light. 'This map was drawn by every troupe that ever sailed,' he said softly. I traced one line with my finger and felt the whole sky hum.
worldwide:2.cnHint: 老舵手展开一张古老地图，上面记录着____范围内所有浮岛的位置，我轻轻触碰，感受到整片天空的震动。
worldwide:2.hook: One line on the map still had no end.
worldwide:2.line: 'This *worldwide* map belongs to every troupe that ever sailed these skies.'

sentences.en: Old Helm unrolled the oldest chart in his pack.
sentences.cn: 老舵展开了他背包里最古老的海图。

sentences.en: It showed not one island or one sea, but a *worldwide* web of floating lands, each dot connected by lines of light.
'This map was drawn by every troupe that ever sailed,' he said softly.
sentences.cn: "这张地图是由每一支曾经航过的船队绘制的，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: I traced one line with my finger and felt the whole sky hum.
sentences.cn: 我用手指追踪了一条线，感到整个天空都在嗡嗡作响。

accomplish:2.en: The sealed door had beaten every troupe before us. Bell studied the carvings for an hour, then smiled and pressed three stones in order. The lock clicked open. 'We *accomplished* what no one else could,' she said, stepping through into a room full of soft golden light. I could barely breathe.
accomplish:2.cnHint: 贝尔研究门上的刻纹后，终于打开了这扇难倒所有人的门，她说我们____了别人未能做到的事。
accomplish:2.hook: Beyond the door, something was still moving in the dark.
accomplish:2.line: 'We *accomplished* what every troupe before us could not.'

sentences.en: The sealed door had beaten every troupe before us.
sentences.cn: 那扇密封的门已经击败了我们之前的每一支船队。

sentences.en: Bell studied the carvings for an hour, then smiled and pressed three stones in order.
sentences.cn: 小铃研究了雕刻一个小时，然后笑了，按下了三块石头。

sentences.en: The lock clicked open.
sentences.cn: 锁咔嗒一声打开了。

sentences.en: 'We *accomplished* what no one else could,' she said, stepping through into a room full of soft golden light.
I could barely breathe.
sentences.cn: 我几乎喘不过气来。

address:2.en: Tucked inside a hollow stone was a small folded note. Bell read it aloud: it was an *address* — not a street, but a set of star angles and wind counts that pointed to an island no chart had named. Old Helm copied it into his log with steady hands. I felt a door opening in my chest.
address:2.cnHint: 一块空心石里藏着一张字条，上面写着一个____——用星角和风速指向一座无名浮岛。
address:2.hook: The star angles on the note matched tonight's sky exactly.
address:2.line: 'This *address* will lead us somewhere no map has ever shown.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside a hollow stone was a small folded note.
sentences.cn: 藏在一块中空的石头里是一张小小的折叠纸条。

sentences.en: Bell read it aloud: it was an *address* — not a street, but a set of star angles and wind counts that pointed to an island no chart had named.
Old Helm copied it into his log with steady hands.
sentences.cn: 老舵用稳定的手把它抄进了他的航海日志。

sentences.en: I felt a door opening in my chest.
sentences.cn: 我感到一扇门在我的胸口打开了。

barely:2.en: The bridge between the two islands was a single rope, worn thin by years of wind. I crossed it one careful step at a time, arms out wide. I *barely* made it to the far side before the last thread snapped behind me. Silverfang caught my arm. The new island smelled of pine and rain.
barely:2.cnHint: 我小心翼翼地踩过一根细绳索，____勉强抵达对岸，身后绳索随即断裂。
barely:2.hook: Silverfang looked back at the broken rope and said nothing.
barely:2.line: 'You *barely* made it — next time, let me cross first.'

sentences.en: The bridge between the two islands was a single rope, worn thin by years of wind.
sentences.cn: 两个岛屿之间的桥是一根单独的绳子，被多年的风吹得很薄。

sentences.en: I crossed it one careful step at a time, arms out wide.
sentences.cn: 我一步一步谨慎地越过它，两臂张开。

sentences.en: I *barely* made it to the far side before the last thread snapped behind me.
Silverfang caught my arm.
sentences.cn: 银牙抓住了我的胳膊。

sentences.en: The new island smelled of pine and rain.
sentences.cn: 新的岛屿闻起来像松树和雨水。

blame:2.en: The word-fragment we needed was gone — the pedestal empty, the dust disturbed. Silverfang crossed his arms. 'Don't look at me,' he said. Old Helm raised a hand: 'No *blame* yet. Something took it recently. That means it is close.' He pointed to a trail of faint sparks drifting toward the east cliff.
blame:2.cnHint: 碎片不翼而飞，老舵手阻止大家互相____，指出有人刚刚带走了它，线索还在。
blame:2.hook: The sparks were moving faster now, toward the cliff edge.
blame:2.line: 'There is no *blame* here — only a trail we need to follow.'

sentences.en: The word-fragment we needed was gone — the pedestal empty, the dust disturbed.
sentences.cn: 我们需要的词碎片消失了——基座是空的，尘埃被扰动过。

sentences.en: Silverfang crossed his arms.
sentences.cn: 银牙交叉双臂。

sentences.en: 'Don't look at me,' he said.
sentences.cn: "别看我，"他说。

sentences.en: Old Helm raised a hand: 'No *blame* yet.
Something took it recently.
sentences.cn: 有什么东西最近拿走了它。

sentences.en: That means it is close.'
sentences.cn: 这意味着它很近。"

sentences.en: He pointed to a trail of faint sparks drifting toward the east cliff.
sentences.cn: 他指向一条微弱的火花尾迹漂向东悬崖。

chat:2.en: While Bell fixed the compass, Silverfang and I sat on the edge of the island and let our feet hang over the stars below. We began to *chat* — quietly at first, then laughing about wrong turns and strange skies. By the time Bell called us back, I felt less like a new member and more like someone who belonged.
chat:2.cnHint: 贝尔修理罗盘时，我和银牙坐在岛边____，笑谈一路上的弯路与奇景，我渐渐有了归属感。
chat:2.hook: Bell's voice cut through our laughter with sudden urgency.
chat:2.line: 'Let's *chat* while we wait — there is time, and I want to know your story.'

sentences.en: While Bell fixed the compass, Silverfang and I sat on the edge of the island and let our feet hang over the stars below.
sentences.cn: 小铃修理指南针的时候，银牙和我坐在岛屿的边缘，让我们的脚悬在下面的星星上。

sentences.en: We began to *chat* — quietly at first, then laughing about wrong turns and strange skies.
By the time Bell called us back, I felt less like a new member and more like someone who belonged.
sentences.cn: 等小铃把我们叫回来的时候，我感觉不像一个新成员，更像一个真正属于这里的人。

combat:2.en: The wind-beast was only fog and sound, but it pressed hard against our little ship. Old Helm took the wheel and set the sails at a sharp angle. He said the best *combat* against a storm is not force — it is a smarter path. The beast thinned, the stars returned, and ahead shone a light we had not seen before.
combat:2.cnHint: 面对呼啸的风兽，老舵主说对抗它最好的____不是蛮力，而是更聪明的航线。
combat:2.hook: The new light ahead was blinking in a pattern.
combat:2.line: 'The only *combat* worth winning out here is fought with a clever course.'

sentences.en: The wind-beast was only fog and sound, but it pressed hard against our little ship.
sentences.cn: 风兽只是雾和声音，但它使劲压着我们小小的船。

sentences.en: Old Helm took the wheel and set the sails at a sharp angle.
sentences.cn: 老舵把握盘，以一个尖锐的角度张开了帆。

sentences.en: He said the best *combat* against a storm is not force — it is a smarter path.
The beast thinned, the stars returned, and ahead shone a light we had not seen before.
sentences.cn: 怪兽消散了，星星回来了，前面闪耀着我们从未见过的光。

danger:2.en: Bell held up her hand and we all stopped. A soft crack ran across the stone path ahead — the island's edge was breaking away. 'Real *danger*,' she said quietly, not in fear but in respect, the way you speak to something large. We backed up, found another route, and arrived at the far tower just as the sun touched the horizon.
danger:2.cnHint: 贝尔发现石路前方出现裂缝，轻声说出____，我们随即退后另寻路线，有惊无险地抵达远塔。
danger:2.hook: The far tower door was already open, waiting for someone.
danger:2.line: 'This kind of *danger* asks for patience, not speed — step back.'

sentences.en: Bell held up her hand and we all stopped.
sentences.cn: 小铃抬起手，我们都停了下来。

sentences.en: A soft crack ran across the stone path ahead — the island's edge was breaking away.
sentences.cn: 一道细小的裂缝穿过前面的石头路——岛屿的边缘正在崩裂。

sentences.en: 'Real *danger*,' she said quietly, not in fear but in respect, the way you speak to something large.
We backed up, found another route, and arrived at the far tower just as the sun touched the horizon.
sentences.cn: 我们退了回去，找到了另一条路，正好在太阳接触地平线时到达了远处的塔。

partly:2.en: The old chest we found on Driftmoss Island was *partly* buried under pale roots, as if the island itself had been slowly swallowing it for years. Bell brushed the soil away with careful hands. Inside lay a folded page, and on it, one glowing word — our next destination, waiting all along.
partly:2.cnHint: 贝尔在浮岛上发现了一只____被埋住的旧箱子，里面藏着一张发光的地图碎片。
partly:2.hook: The word on the page pulsed once, then pointed due north.
partly:2.line: 'This box is *partly* open — something inside is still breathing.'

sentences.en: The old chest we found on Driftmoss Island was *partly* buried under pale roots, as if the island itself had been slowly swallowing it for years.
Bell brushed the soil away with careful hands.
sentences.cn: 小铃用细心的双手刷去泥土。

sentences.en: Inside lay a folded page, and on it, one glowing word — our next destination, waiting all along.
sentences.cn: 里面放着一张折叠的纸，上面闪闪发光的一个词——我们的下一个目的地，一直在那里等着。

practical:2.en: Old Helm spread the recovered fragments across the deck and frowned. Most maps showed pretty pictures of clouds and dragons. 'A *practical* map,' he said firmly, 'tells you wind speed, landing depth, and where the roots are weak.' He kept only three fragments and let the rest sail away on the breeze.
practical:2.cnHint: 老舵手挑选地图碎片时，只留下____的那几张，其余全部放走。
practical:2.hook: The three chosen fragments clicked together like old friends.
practical:2.line: 'We keep only what is *practical* — beauty without use is just weight.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the recovered fragments across the deck and frowned.
sentences.cn: 老舵把找回来的碎片铺满了甲板，皱起了眉头。

sentences.en: Most maps showed pretty pictures of clouds and dragons.
sentences.cn: 大多数地图画的是云和龙的漂亮图案。

sentences.en: 'A *practical* map,' he said firmly, 'tells you wind speed, landing depth, and where the roots are weak.'
He kept only three fragments and let the rest sail away on the breeze.
sentences.cn: 他只留下了三片碎片，让其余的随风飘去。

profit:2.en: Silverfang once told me she had sailed these skies purely for *profit* — rare stones, glowing seeds, bottled starlight. But on the morning we found the word carved into the bark of a sky-cedar, she stood very still and said nothing about prices at all.
profit:2.cnHint: 竞争船长过去航行是为了____，但那天早晨她在天杉树前沉默了。
profit:2.hook: She reached out and touched the carving as if it were an old name.
profit:2.line: 'I used to count every find as *profit*, but this one feels different.'

sentences.en: Silverfang once told me she had sailed these skies purely for *profit* — rare stones, glowing seeds, bottled starlight.
But on the morning we found the word carved into the bark of a sky-cedar, she stood very still and said nothing about prices at all.
sentences.cn: 但在我们发现那个词刻在一棵空中雪松树皮上的那个早晨，银牙静静地站在那里，一句关于价格的话都没说。

promise:2.en: The word was sealed inside a hollow stone, wrapped in a leaf with writing on it: 'To whoever finds this — keep going.' Old Helm read it aloud twice. He called it a *promise* left by some earlier traveller, proof that this sky-road had been walked before and was worth walking still.
promise:2.cnHint: 老舵手在中空石头里发现了一片叶子，他说那是前人留下的一个____。
promise:2.hook: Somewhere ahead, that earlier traveller might have left another.
promise:2.line: 'This note is a *promise* that the road ahead is real.'

sentences.en: The word was sealed inside a hollow stone, wrapped in a leaf with writing on it: 'To whoever finds this — keep going.'
sentences.cn: 这个词被封在一块中空的石头里，包裹在一片有字迹的叶子中：「无论谁找到这个——继续前进。」

sentences.en: Old Helm read it aloud twice.
sentences.cn: 老舵大声读了两遍。

sentences.en: He called it a *promise* left by some earlier traveller, proof that this sky-road had been walked before and was worth walking still.

rarely:2.en: Bell said she *rarely* felt nervous reading a navigation word for the first time, but her voice was a half-step higher than usual as she lifted the glowing shard from the pool of still water. The word lit her face blue. She smiled anyway, and read it clearly into the night air.
rarely:2.cnHint: 贝尔____会紧张，但这次从水池中取出发光碎片时，她的声音有些不一样。
rarely:2.hook: The word she read sent every compass needle spinning at once.
rarely:2.line: 'I *rarely* shake like this — this word must be something special.'

sentences.en: Bell said she *rarely* felt nervous reading a navigation word for the first time, but her voice was a half-step higher than usual as she lifted the glowing shard from the pool of still water.
The word lit her face blue.
sentences.cn: 这个词用蓝光照亮了她的脸。

sentences.en: She smiled anyway, and read it clearly into the night air.
sentences.cn: 她还是笑了，清晰地把它读到了夜空中。

severe:2.en: The storm over Ashveil Island had been *severe* enough to crack three of the lower deck boards, and it had driven our target word deep into a sea-cave behind the falls. We climbed in anyway, dripping and laughing, and Bell held the word up like a small torch in the dark.
severe:2.cnHint: 阿什维尔岛的风暴十分____，但大家还是爬进海洞找到了那个词。
severe:2.hook: The word glowed brighter the deeper into the cave we went.
severe:2.line: 'The damage is *severe*, but we got what we came for.'

sentences.en: The storm over Ashveil Island had been *severe* enough to crack three of the lower deck boards, and it had driven our target word deep into a sea-cave behind the falls.
We climbed in anyway, dripping and laughing, and Bell held the word up like a small torch in the dark.
sentences.cn: 我们还是爬了进去，湿漉漉的，笑声不止，小铃高举着那个词，像夜幕中的一支小火把。

smell:2.en: The word was hidden inside a bunch of dried silver-herbs hanging from the roof of an abandoned sky-cottage. I knew we were close because of the *smell* — sweet and a little sharp, like starlight pressed into a flower. Old Helm said only the right island grows herbs that glow and scent at the same time.
smell:2.cnHint: 我们靠着一种特殊的____找到了藏在废弃小屋里的词语碎片。
smell:2.hook: Old Helm said only two islands in all the sky could grow those herbs.
smell:2.line: 'Follow the *smell* — if it sharpens, the word is very near.'

sentences.en: The word was hidden inside a bunch of dried silver-herbs hanging from the roof of an abandoned sky-cottage.
sentences.cn: 这个词藏在挂在一间废弃空中小屋屋顶上的一束干银草里。

sentences.en: I knew we were close because of the *smell* — sweet and a little sharp, like starlight pressed into a flower.
Old Helm said only the right island grows herbs that glow and scent at the same time.
sentences.cn: 老舵说只有对的岛才能长出既闪闪发光又有香气的草。

socialize:2.en: Every time the troupe arrives at a sky-market island, Bell is the first off the ship. She will *socialize* with anyone — traders, cloud-fishers, children with star-nets — and somehow, within an hour, she always learns exactly which vendor is hiding a map fragment under their counter.
socialize:2.cnHint: 贝尔每次靠港都会主动____，然后总能打听到藏着地图碎片的摊主。
socialize:2.hook: This time she came back grinning, holding something that glowed gold.
socialize:2.line: 'You have to *socialize* — the best maps are never on display.'

sentences.en: Every time the troupe arrives at a sky-market island, Bell is the first off the ship.
sentences.cn: 每次船队到达空中集市岛，小铃总是第一个下船的。

sentences.en: She will *socialize* with anyone — traders, cloud-fishers, children with star-nets — and somehow, within an hour, she always learns exactly which vendor is hiding a map fragment under their counter.

dinner:2.en: At the edge of the map, we found a long stone table set among the clouds. Old Helm lit the lanterns without a word. 'Every journey deserves a proper *dinner*,' he said, placing the last word-fragment at the centre like a dish. The stars leaned in, as if hungry too.
dinner:2.cnHint: 在地图的尽头，老舵主摆好石桌，为大家举办了一场____。
dinner:2.hook: But the table had been set for one more person than we were.
dinner:2.line: 'Every journey deserves a proper *dinner*, even at the edge of the map.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the map, we found a long stone table set among the clouds.
sentences.cn: 在地图的边缘，我们找到了一张长长的石桌，就放在云雾中。

sentences.en: Old Helm lit the lanterns without a word.
sentences.cn: 老舵默不作声地点亮了灯笼。

sentences.en: 'Every journey deserves a proper *dinner*,' he said, placing the last word-fragment at the centre like a dish.
The stars leaned in, as if hungry too.
sentences.cn: 星星们凑了过来，好像也饿了似的。

embrace:2.en: The fog at the map's edge was thick and cold. I almost turned back. Then Bell reached out and gave my shoulder a quick, firm *embrace*. 'The fog is part of the path,' she said. I stepped forward, and the clouds parted to reveal a whole new island glowing below.
embrace:2.cnHint: 贝尔给了叙述者一个____，鼓励他迈出踏入迷雾的那一步。
embrace:2.hook: The new island below was shaped exactly like the word in my hand.
embrace:2.line: 'The fog is cold, but let it *embrace* you — it means you are close.'

sentences.en: The fog at the map's edge was thick and cold.
sentences.cn: 地图边缘的雾很浓很冷。

sentences.en: I almost turned back.
sentences.cn: 我差点转身回头。

sentences.en: Then Bell reached out and gave my shoulder a quick, firm *embrace*.
'The fog is part of the path,' she said.
sentences.cn: 「雾是路的一部分，」她说。

sentences.en: I stepped forward, and the clouds parted to reveal a whole new island glowing below.
sentences.cn: 我向前走去，云雾散开了，下面露出了一整座闪闪发光的新岛屿。

explanation:2.en: Old Helm handed me a glass bottle sealed with wax. Inside was a single folded note. I opened it carefully. The only thing written on it was a new word and a map marking — no *explanation* at all. Bell laughed. 'He never explains. The road does that for him.'
explanation:2.cnHint: 瓶中纸条只有一个词和一处标记，完全没有____，贝尔却觉得这很正常。
explanation:2.hook: The map marking pointed somewhere none of us had ever dared to sail.
explanation:2.line: 'There is no *explanation* — the island will answer your questions itself.'

sentences.en: Old Helm handed me a glass bottle sealed with wax.
sentences.cn: 老舵递给我一个蜡封的玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: Inside was a single folded note.
sentences.cn: 里面是一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: I opened it carefully.
sentences.cn: 我小心地打开了它。

sentences.en: The only thing written on it was a new word and a map marking — no *explanation* at all.
Bell laughed.
sentences.cn: 小铃笑了。

sentences.en: 'He never explains.
sentences.cn: 「他从不解释。

sentences.en: The road does that for him.'
sentences.cn: 路会替他解释的。」

intend:2.en: I spread the old word-fragments on the deck and tried to match their edges. Silverfang watched with crossed arms. 'What do you *intend* to find out there?' she asked. I told her: the place where the map ends and something new begins. She uncrossed her arms. 'Fair enough,' she said.
intend:2.cnHint: 银牙问叙述者____做什么，得到答案后她的态度改变了。
intend:2.hook: She then pulled out a fragment none of us had ever seen before.
intend:2.line: 'Tell me what you *intend* to do, and I will tell you if the wind agrees.'

sentences.en: I spread the old word-fragments on the deck and tried to match their edges.
sentences.cn: 我把那些旧词碎片铺在甲板上，试图对上它们的边缘。

sentences.en: Silverfang watched with crossed arms.
sentences.cn: 银牙双臂交叉，看着我。

sentences.en: 'What do you *intend* to find out there?' she asked.
I told her: the place where the map ends and something new begins.
sentences.cn: 我告诉她：那个地图结束、新的东西开始的地方。

sentences.en: She uncrossed her arms.
sentences.cn: 她放下了双臂。

sentences.en: 'Fair enough,' she said.
sentences.cn: 「也行，」她说。

leadership:2.en: When the clouds closed in and our compass spun without purpose, the troupe looked at Old Helm. He said nothing for a long moment. Then, quietly, he turned the ship three degrees left. That calm, unhurried *leadership* was worth more than any shouted order. The clouds opened like a door.
leadership:2.cnHint: 在迷失方向的时候，老舵主平静的____让船找到了出路。
leadership:2.hook: Through the gap in the clouds, we saw lights that no map had ever named.
leadership:2.line: 'Good *leadership* is mostly listening — to the wind, and to the crew.'

sentences.en: When the clouds closed in and our compass spun without purpose, the troupe looked at Old Helm.
sentences.cn: 乌云压低了，罗盘转得没了方向，整个剧团都看向了老舵。

sentences.en: He said nothing for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 他沉默了很久。

sentences.en: Then, quietly, he turned the ship three degrees left.
sentences.cn: 然后，他静静地把船向左转了三度。

sentences.en: That calm, unhurried *leadership* was worth more than any shouted order.
The clouds opened like a door.
sentences.cn: 乌云像门一样裂开了。

locate:2.en: The newest word-fragment glowed faintly in my palm: a gold shape like a leaf. Bell leaned over the navigation table and traced three routes before she could *locate* the matching island. It sat just beyond a ring of slow spinning clouds, patient as if it had always been waiting for us.
locate:2.cnHint: 贝尔在航海图上努力____与碎片形状匹配的那座岛屿。
locate:2.hook: The island had no name on any chart, only a small hand-drawn star.
locate:2.line: 'Give me an hour and I will *locate* it — no island hides from a good navigator.'

sentences.en: The newest word-fragment glowed faintly in my palm: a gold shape like a leaf.
sentences.cn: 最新的词根在我掌心里闪闪发光——一个金色的叶子形状。

sentences.en: Bell leaned over the navigation table and traced three routes before she could *locate* the matching island.
It sat just beyond a ring of slow spinning clouds, patient as if it had always been waiting for us.
sentences.cn: 它就躺在缓缓转动的云环外，像一直在耐心地等我们来。

original:2.en: Bell unrolled a very old chart, its edges brown and soft. 'This is the *original* map,' she said, 'before anyone added the new islands.' I compared it with our current one. Half the places we had already visited were not on it. We had gone further than anyone before us.
original:2.cnHint: 贝尔展示了____地图，叙述者发现他们已经走到了前人从未到达之处。
original:2.hook: One blank space on the original map matched perfectly with the word in my hand.
original:2.line: 'The *original* map ends here — what comes next is ours to draw.'

sentences.en: Bell unrolled a very old chart, its edges brown and soft.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开了一份很旧的图，边缘已经泛黄变软。

sentences.en: 'This is the *original* map,' she said, 'before anyone added the new islands.'
I compared it with our current one.
sentences.cn: 我把它和现在的图对比了一下。

sentences.en: Half the places we had already visited were not on it.
sentences.cn: 我们已经走过的地方，一半都不在上面。

sentences.en: We had gone further than anyone before us.
sentences.cn: 我们走得比任何人都远。

overcome:2.en: The final gap in the map was a wide stretch of sky with no island, no star, and no wind. The ship drifted. Old Helm sat still with his eyes closed for a long minute. Then he smiled. 'Every map has one blank place to *overcome*,' he said, and set the sails toward the dark.
overcome:2.cnHint: 面对地图上最后的空白，老舵主鼓励大家____眼前这片无路可走的虚空。
overcome:2.hook: A faint light blinked once, far ahead, exactly where the map showed nothing.
overcome:2.line: 'We will *overcome* this empty sky the same way we overcame all the others — together.'

sentences.en: The final gap in the map was a wide stretch of sky with no island, no star, and no wind.
sentences.cn: 图上最后的空白是一大片天空，没有岛，没有星，也没有风。

sentences.en: The ship drifted.
sentences.cn: 船漂流了。

sentences.en: Old Helm sat still with his eyes closed for a long minute.
sentences.cn: 老舵闭着眼睛坐了很久。

sentences.en: Then he smiled.
sentences.cn: 然后他笑了。

sentences.en: 'Every map has one blank place to *overcome*,' he said, and set the sails toward the dark.

threaten:2.en: The edge of the map island crumbled beneath our feet. Dark clouds began to *threaten* the sky above the stone bridge, and Old Helm pulled us back with one firm hand. 'Not yet,' he said quietly. Bell held up a glowing word-fragment, and the clouds slowly parted, revealing a pale silver path ahead.
threaten:2.cnHint: 乌云____着通往石桥的天空，老舵手把大家拉了回来。
threaten:2.hook: The silver path led somewhere no map had ever shown.
threaten:2.line: 'Those clouds *threaten* the crossing — we wait for Bell's word.'

sentences.en: The edge of the map island crumbled beneath our feet.
sentences.cn: 图的边缘在我们脚下碎裂。

sentences.en: Dark clouds began to *threaten* the sky above the stone bridge, and Old Helm pulled us back with one firm hand.
'Not yet,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "还不是时候，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: Bell held up a glowing word-fragment, and the clouds slowly parted, revealing a pale silver path ahead.
sentences.cn: 小铃举起闪闪发光的词根，乌云慢慢散开，露出前面一条苍白的银色小径。

throw:2.en: Bell found the sealed jar buried under a pile of old star-charts. Inside was a rolled note and a single word-fragment. 'Opening it is a *throw*,' Old Helm admitted, turning the jar slowly in his rough hands. 'But every island we have ever found began with someone being brave enough to try.' I cracked the seal.
throw:2.cnHint: 打开那只神秘罐子是一次____，但老舵手说每座岛都需要勇气。
throw:2.hook: The note inside named a place none of us had ever heard.
throw:2.line: 'Opening this jar is a *throw*, but I say we do it.'

sentences.en: Bell found the sealed jar buried under a pile of old star-charts.
sentences.cn: 小铃在一堆旧星图下面找到了密封的罐子。

sentences.en: Inside was a rolled note and a single word-fragment.
sentences.cn: 里面是一张卷起的纸条和一个词根。

sentences.en: 'Opening it is a *throw*,' Old Helm admitted, turning the jar slowly in his rough hands.
'But every island we have ever found began with someone being brave enough to try.'
sentences.cn: "但我们找到的每一个岛，都始于有人鼓起勇气去尝试。"

sentences.en: I cracked the seal.
sentences.cn: 我打破了封印。

unlike:2.en: Silverfang's ship carried a large iron chest that was *unlike* anything in our troupe's small wagon — its lid was covered in tiny carved words, each one a place already visited. Old Helm traced them with one finger, smiling. 'Every mark is a door we opened,' he said. Bell pressed a new word-fragment into the last empty space, and the chest hummed softly.
unlike:2.cnHint: 银牙的铁箱____我们的旅行车，盖子上刻满了已探索过的地名。
unlike:2.hook: The hum grew louder as the chest pointed toward the north.
unlike:2.line: 'This chest is *unlike* any I have seen — it remembers every word.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's ship carried a large iron chest that was *unlike* anything in our troupe's small wagon — its lid was covered in tiny carved words, each one a place already visited.
Old Helm traced them with one finger, smiling.
sentences.cn: 老舵用一根手指轻轻描过它们，笑了。

sentences.en: 'Every mark is a door we opened,' he said.
sentences.cn: "每一个痕迹都是我们打开过的门，"他说。

sentences.en: Bell pressed a new word-fragment into the last empty space, and the chest hummed softly.
sentences.cn: 小铃把一个新的词根按进最后空着的地方，箱子轻轻嗡鸣起来。

vast:2.en: We landed on an island with no buildings, only an open field of pale blue grass stretching in every direction. The silence was *vast*, pressing gently against my ears like soft cloth. Old Helm knelt and pressed his palm to the ground. Somewhere beneath us, a word-fragment glowed faintly, and the grass bent toward it like a quiet invitation.
vast:2.cnHint: 那座岛上一片____的寂静，老舵手跪地感受到了埋藏其中的词语碎片。
vast:2.hook: The ground itself seemed to be waiting for us to listen.
vast:2.line: 'The silence here is *vast* — the island is trying to speak.'

sentences.en: We landed on an island with no buildings, only an open field of pale blue grass stretching in every direction.
sentences.cn: 我们登陆了一个岛，没有建筑，只有苍蓝色的草无尽地向四周铺展。

sentences.en: The silence was *vast*, pressing gently against my ears like soft cloth.
Old Helm knelt and pressed his palm to the ground.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪下来，把手掌按在地上。

sentences.en: Somewhere beneath us, a word-fragment glowed faintly, and the grass bent toward it like a quiet invitation.
sentences.cn: 我们下面的某处，一个词根在幽幽地闪光，草像接到了轻声邀请一样向它弯去。

absolutely:2.en: Bell laid three word-fragments on the table and studied them for a long time. 'I am *absolutely* certain these fit together,' she said at last, pressing them edge to edge. The pieces locked with a soft click, and a new shape appeared — a small island drawn in faint gold light, floating just beyond the edge of our current chart. Old Helm laughed with quiet delight.
absolutely:2.cnHint: 贝尔____确定三块词语碎片能拼在一起，果然拼出了一座新岛屿的轮廓。
absolutely:2.hook: The gold island on the chart had no name — yet.
absolutely:2.line: 'I am *absolutely* certain — press them together and you will see.'

sentences.en: Bell laid three word-fragments on the table and studied them for a long time.
sentences.cn: 小铃在桌上铺开三个词根，久久地研究着。

sentences.en: 'I am *absolutely* certain these fit together,' she said at last, pressing them edge to edge.
The pieces locked with a soft click, and a new shape appeared — a small island drawn in faint gold light, floating just beyond the edge of our current chart.
sentences.cn: 碎片咔哒一声锁在了一起，一个新的形状出现了——一个岛屿，画在淡金色的光里，浮在我们现在的图表边缘外。

sentences.en: Old Helm laughed with quiet delight.
sentences.cn: 老舵安静地笑出声来。

accumulate:2.en: Our map-chest had grown heavy. Over many journeys, word-fragments begin to *accumulate* in ways you do not notice until you try to lift the lid. Silverfang counted them aloud while Bell wrote each one down. Old Helm watched from his chair and smiled at me. 'That weight,' he said, 'is everywhere we have ever been brave enough to go.'
accumulate:2.cnHint: 旅行途中，词语碎片悄悄地____在地图箱里，直到沉得难以抬盖。
accumulate:2.hook: Bell's list ended with a name no one had spoken aloud before.
accumulate:2.line: 'Words *accumulate* faster than you think — count them with me.'

sentences.en: Our map-chest had grown heavy.
sentences.cn: 我们的图箱变沉了。

sentences.en: Over many journeys, word-fragments begin to *accumulate* in ways you do not notice until you try to lift the lid.
Silverfang counted them aloud while Bell wrote each one down.
sentences.cn: 银牙大声数着，小铃把每一个都记下来。

sentences.en: Old Helm watched from his chair and smiled at me.
sentences.cn: 老舵坐在椅子里看着我笑。

sentences.en: 'That weight,' he said, 'is everywhere we have ever been brave enough to go.'
sentences.cn: "那份沉，"他说，"就是我们每一次鼓起勇气去的地方。"

breakfast:2.en: We had planned to leave at first light, but Old Helm insisted we *breakfast* together on the warm deck first. He set out bread and dried fruit while the stars above us slowly faded. Bell found a word-fragment hidden inside the bread basket, wrapped in a dry leaf. 'Someone left it here for us,' she said softly, holding it up to the last of the starlight.
breakfast:2.cnHint: 出发前大家在甲板上____，贝尔在面包篮里发现了一块被藏起来的词语碎片。
breakfast:2.hook: The leaf it was wrapped in showed a tiny map drawn in ink.
breakfast:2.line: 'We *breakfast* first — the stars will still be there when we are ready.'

sentences.en: We had planned to leave at first light, but Old Helm insisted we *breakfast* together on the warm deck first.
He set out bread and dried fruit while the stars above us slowly faded.
sentences.cn: 他在温暖的甲板上摆出了面包和干果，头上的星星一点点褪去。

sentences.en: Bell found a word-fragment hidden inside the bread basket, wrapped in a dry leaf.
sentences.cn: 小铃在面包篮里找到了一个词根，用干叶子包着。

sentences.en: 'Someone left it here for us,' she said softly, holding it up to the last of the starlight.
sentences.cn: "有人把它留在这里给我们，"她轻声说，举起来对着最后的星光。

capacity:2.en: Silverfang's old ship had a hidden lower deck we had never entered. 'Its *capacity* surprised even me,' he admitted, pushing open the narrow door. Inside, row after row of shelves held sealed jars, each one glowing faintly with a stored word-fragment. Old Helm looked at Bell, then at me. 'Well,' he said warmly, 'it seems our map just grew a great deal larger.'
capacity:2.cnHint: 银牙船的隐藏底舱____惊人，里面藏着一排排盛有词语碎片的罐子。
capacity:2.hook: One jar near the back glowed brighter than all the others.
capacity:2.line: 'The *capacity* of this deck is larger than the whole ship above — come and see.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's old ship had a hidden lower deck we had never entered.
sentences.cn: 银牙的老船有个我们从没进去过的隐藏下层甲板。

sentences.en: 'Its *capacity* surprised even me,' he admitted, pushing open the narrow door.
Inside, row after row of shelves held sealed jars, each one glowing faintly with a stored word-fragment.
sentences.cn: 里面一排排的架子上放着密封的罐子，每一个都闪着存储的词根的微光。

sentences.en: Old Helm looked at Bell, then at me.
sentences.cn: 老舵看了看小铃，又看了看我。

sentences.en: 'Well,' he said warmly, 'it seems our map just grew a great deal larger.'
sentences.cn: "嗯，"他温暖地说，"看起来我们的图刚变大了不少。"

disaster:2.en: Tucked inside a cracked lantern near the island's edge, I found a folded note. Old Helm read it aloud: the troupe before ours had tried to cross the Voidrift without a full word-map. The result was a *disaster* — their ship came apart between islands, and only one member reached the other side. Old Helm folded the note carefully and said nothing for a while.
disaster:2.cnHint: 一张旧便条记录了上一支队伍的____，老舵读完后陷入了沉默。
disaster:2.hook: He tucked the note into his coat, and I wondered if he recognized the handwriting.
disaster:2.line: 'That crossing was a *disaster* — we will not repeat their mistake.'
