sentences.cn: 老舵微微一笑，拎着灯笼径直走了进去。

cook:2.en: On the island of Ember Shelf, we found a clay kitchen floating all on its own, no walls, just a stove under open stars. Old Helm sat down and began to *cook* a pot of something thick and golden. The smell alone made the next map fragment glow brighter in Bell's hand.
cook:2.cnHint: 老舵在漂浮的厨房里____了一锅食物，地图碎片竟然发出了光。
cook:2.hook: The pot held one ingredient none of us could name.
cook:2.line: 'Let me *cook* — hunger makes brave people foolish,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: On the island of Ember Shelf, we found a clay kitchen floating all on its own, no walls, just a stove under open stars.
sentences.cn: 在余烬架岛上，我们发现了一个浮动的泥土厨房，没有墙，只有一个炉灶在开阔的星空下。

sentences.en: Old Helm sat down and began to *cook* a pot of something thick and golden.
The smell alone made the next map fragment glow brighter in Bell's hand.
sentences.cn: 仅仅是那股味道就让小铃手里的下一块地图碎片闪得更亮了。

corporate:2.en: Bell pulled a brass plate from the ruins and read it aloud. 'A *corporate* seal,' she said, 'meaning this island once belonged to a whole group, not one person.' The crest showed seven hands joined in a circle. Old Helm copied it into his notebook. Seven islands. Seven hands.
corporate:2.cnHint: 小铃发现了一块____印章，说明这座岛曾属于某个团体。
corporate:2.hook: Six of those seven islands had already vanished from every known map.
corporate:2.line: 'A *corporate* seal this old means someone shared a very big secret,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Bell pulled a brass plate from the ruins and read it aloud.
sentences.cn: 小铃从废墟里拔出一块黄铜板，大声读了出来。

sentences.en: 'A *corporate* seal,' she said, 'meaning this island once belonged to a whole group, not one person.'
The crest showed seven hands joined in a circle.
sentences.cn: 盾徽上显示七只手在圆圈里紧紧相握。

sentences.en: Old Helm copied it into his notebook.
sentences.cn: 老舵把它抄进了他的笔记本。

sentences.en: Seven islands.
sentences.cn: 七座岛屿。

sentences.en: Seven hands.
sentences.cn: 七只手。

dangerous:2.en: The rope bridge to Fog Notch swayed hard even with no wind. 'It is *dangerous*,' Silverfang said, testing one plank with his boot, 'but the word we need is on the other side.' He tied a guide rope to my wrist before stepping forward, which told me everything about how serious he was.
dangerous:2.cnHint: 银牙警告说前方的吊桥____，但他们必须过去取得地图碎片。
dangerous:2.hook: Halfway across, two planks dropped silently into the cloud below.
dangerous:2.line: '*Dangerous* is just the cost of finding something worth finding,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: The rope bridge to Fog Notch swayed hard even with no wind.
sentences.cn: 通往雾口的绳桥即使没有风也在猛烈摇晃。

sentences.en: 'It is *dangerous*,' Silverfang said, testing one plank with his boot, 'but the word we need is on the other side.'
He tied a guide rope to my wrist before stepping forward, which told me everything about how serious he was.
sentences.cn: 他在我的手腕上系了一根导引绳才向前踏去，这告诉我他有多么认真。

debt:2.en: The keeper of Pale Shelf Island offered us the map fragment freely. 'No payment,' she said. Old Helm bowed low. 'Then we owe you a *debt* of kindness,' he told her. She shook her head and pointed at the stars. 'Pay it forward to the next troupe that comes lost through here.'
debt:2.cnHint: 地图保管人免费给出了碎片，老舵说他们欠了她一份____。
debt:2.hook: She watched us leave as though she had been waiting a very long time for us.
debt:2.line: 'A *debt* of kindness is the only kind worth carrying,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The keeper of Pale Shelf Island offered us the map fragment freely.
sentences.cn: 苍白架岛的守护者免费给了我们地图碎片。

sentences.en: 'No payment,' she said.
sentences.cn: "不要报酬，"她说。

sentences.en: Old Helm bowed low.
sentences.cn: 老舵深深地鞠了一躬。

sentences.en: 'Then we owe you a *debt* of kindness,' he told her.
She shook her head and pointed at the stars.
sentences.cn: 她摇摇头，指向星空。

sentences.en: 'Pay it forward to the next troupe that comes lost through here.'
sentences.cn: "把这份恩情转给下一支迷路来这里的队伍吧。"

discipline:2.en: Bell made us practice reading star-charts every morning before the ship moved one inch. 'This *discipline* will save your life someday,' she said, tapping the chart. Silverfang grumbled. I grumbled too. But on the third morning I spotted the hidden current that would have sent us straight into the rock shelf.
discipline:2.cnHint: 小铃坚持每天早上练习读星图，她说这种____有一天会救大家的命。
discipline:2.hook: The rock shelf had no name on any map — because no one had survived it before.
discipline:2.line: '*Discipline* now means choices later — that is the whole deal,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Bell made us practice reading star-charts every morning before the ship moved one inch.
sentences.cn: 小铃让我们每天在船动一寸之前都要练习读星图。

sentences.en: 'This *discipline* will save your life someday,' she said, tapping the chart.
Silverfang grumbled.
sentences.cn: 银牙抱怨。

sentences.en: I grumbled too.
sentences.cn: 我也抱怨。

sentences.en: But on the third morning I spotted the hidden current that would have sent us straight into the rock shelf.
sentences.cn: 但到了第三个早上，我发现了那道暗流，它本来会把我们直接送进岩石架。

error:2.en: The new map fragment showed a path curving left around the Moon Tooth peaks. I copied it carefully, but made one small *error* — I drew the curve right. We flew an hour the wrong way before Bell noticed. Old Helm did not scold me. He just said, 'Good. Now you will never make that one again.'
error:2.cnHint: 叙述者在抄写地图时犯了一个____，导致飞船偏离了方向。
error:2.hook: The wrong path had led us straight above an island that appeared on no chart at all.
error:2.line: 'One *error* is a lesson — the same error twice is a choice,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: The new map fragment showed a path curving left around the Moon Tooth peaks.
sentences.cn: 新地图碎片显示了一条在月牙峰左侧弯曲的路径。

sentences.en: I copied it carefully, but made one small *error* — I drew the curve right.
We flew an hour the wrong way before Bell noticed.
sentences.cn: 我们飞错方向飞了一个小时才被小铃发现。

sentences.en: Old Helm did not scold me.
sentences.cn: 老舵没有责骂我。

sentences.en: He just said, 'Good.
sentences.cn: 他只是说，"很好。

sentences.en: Now you will never make that one again.'
sentences.cn: 现在你这辈子都不会再犯这个错了。"

gym:2.en: At the center of Spring-Lock Island stood a round stone hall the locals called the *gym* — not for strength, but for sharpening the mind through movement and balance. Bell walked its beams without looking down. Old Helm said the founders believed a still body made a still imagination, and a still imagination could never read the sky.
gym:2.cnHint: 岛上有一座石制____，当地人在这里通过运动来锻炼思维和平衡力。
gym:2.hook: The final beam led to a hidden door, and behind it was exactly what we had come for.
gym:2.line: 'Every *gym* I have seen on these islands teaches the same thing: pay attention,' said Bell.

sentences.en: At the center of Spring-Lock Island stood a round stone hall the locals called the *gym* — not for strength, but for sharpening the mind through movement and balance.
Bell walked its beams without looking down.
sentences.cn: 小铃在横梁上行走，眼睛都不往下看。

sentences.en: Old Helm said the founders believed a still body made a still imagination, and a still imagination could never read the sky.
sentences.cn: 老舵说创建者相信静止的身体会导致停滞的想象，停滞的想象永远读不懂天空。

strength:2.en: Deep in the map room, Old Helm unrolled a canvas covered in tiny marks. 'Each island has a garrison,' he said quietly. 'Look at these numbers — their *strength* grows the closer we sail to the edge.' Bell traced the figures with one finger, eyes wide.
strength:2.cnHint: 老舵手在地图室里发现，越靠近地图边缘，岛屿守卫的____越强大。
strength:2.hook: Whatever waited at the edge, we were already outnumbered.
strength:2.line: 'Their *strength* doubles on every island past the third.' — Old Helm

sentences.en: Deep in the map room, Old Helm unrolled a canvas covered in tiny marks.
sentences.cn: 在地图室深处，老舵铺开了一张布满细小标记的画布。

sentences.en: 'Each island has a garrison,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "每个岛屿都有一座驻地，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: 'Look at these numbers — their *strength* grows the closer we sail to the edge.'
Bell traced the figures with one finger, eyes wide.
sentences.cn: 小铃用一根手指描摹着数字，眼睛睁得很大。

survive:2.en: We found a glass bottle wedged in a crack between two sky-stones. Inside was a note, blurred by rain but still readable: 'Only those who share their last lantern will *survive* the dark passage ahead.' Old Helm held it up to the starlight and said nothing for a long moment.
survive:2.cnHint: 一个漂流瓶里的字条警告大家，只有懂得分享的人才能____那片黑暗通道。
survive:2.hook: Our lantern had just enough oil for one person.
survive:2.line: 'Together we *survive*; alone we simply drift.' — Old Helm

sentences.en: We found a glass bottle wedged in a crack between two sky-stones.
sentences.cn: 我们在两块天空石之间的裂缝里发现了一个玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: Inside was a note, blurred by rain but still readable: 'Only those who share their last lantern will *survive* the dark passage ahead.'
Old Helm held it up to the starlight and said nothing for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 老舵把它举到星光下，沉默了很久。

touch:2.en: Bell handed me a small stone carved into the shape of a compass. The moment my fingers closed around it, a quiet warmth spread up my arm — a strange *touch* that felt like a welcome from the island itself. 'It chooses its keeper,' Bell said with a soft smile.
touch:2.cnHint: 领航员交给我一块雕刻罗盘，那种奇异的____让我感觉整座岛屿在欢迎我。
touch:2.hook: The stone pulsed once, then pointed somewhere no map showed.
touch:2.line: 'That *touch* means the island trusts you now.' — Bell

sentences.en: Bell handed me a small stone carved into the shape of a compass.
sentences.cn: 小铃递给我一块雕成罗盘形状的小石头。

sentences.en: The moment my fingers closed around it, a quiet warmth spread up my arm — a strange *touch* that felt like a welcome from the island itself.
'It chooses its keeper,' Bell said with a soft smile.
sentences.cn: "它会选择自己的主人，"小铃轻声笑着说。

trap:2.en: Old Helm stopped us at a glowing archway. Vines had been twisted into a neat path leading through it — too neat. 'Classic *trap*,' he muttered, kneeling to inspect the stones. 'Someone wants us to step inside before we read the word carved above the door.' We all stepped back.
trap:2.cnHint: 老舵手识破了发光拱门下的____，提醒大家先读门上的刻字再行动。
trap:2.hook: The word above the door began to slowly fade away.
trap:2.line: 'A pretty path is the oldest *trap* there is.' — Old Helm

sentences.en: Old Helm stopped us at a glowing archway.
sentences.cn: 老舵在一扇发光的拱门前把我们拦住了。

sentences.en: Vines had been twisted into a neat path leading through it — too neat.
sentences.cn: 藤蔓被缠绕成一条整洁的小径穿过它——太整洁了。

sentences.en: 'Classic *trap*,' he muttered, kneeling to inspect the stones.
'Someone wants us to step inside before we read the word carved above the door.'
sentences.cn: "有人想让我们踏进去，好在我们读门上刻的字之前。"

sentences.en: We all stepped back.
sentences.cn: 我们都往后退了。

tv:2.en: On a forgotten island shaped like a crescent, we discovered a rusted metal box with a cracked glass front. Bell cleaned the glass and recognised it at once. 'A *tv*,' she said. 'Islanders once gathered around it every evening to receive news from the capital, before the sky-roads broke apart.'
tv:2.cnHint: 在一座废弃的岛上，领航员认出了一台旧____，那是岛民昔日接收消息的设备。
tv:2.hook: The screen flickered, and a single word appeared.
tv:2.line: 'They watched this *tv* the night the last bridge fell.' — Bell

sentences.en: On a forgotten island shaped like a crescent, we discovered a rusted metal box with a cracked glass front.
sentences.cn: 在一座形如新月的被遗忘的岛屿上，我们发现了一个生锈的金属箱子，玻璃面裂开了。

sentences.en: Bell cleaned the glass and recognised it at once.
sentences.cn: 小铃清洁了玻璃，立刻认出了它。

sentences.en: 'A *tv*,' she said.
'Islanders once gathered around it every evening to receive news from the capital, before the sky-roads broke apart.'
sentences.cn: "岛民们曾经每晚聚在它周围收听来自首都的新闻，在天空之路断裂之前。"

victim:2.en: Tucked under a loose floor stone we found a journal. The final page read: 'I was not the first *victim* of this island's illusions — the mist shows you what you most want, then leads you off the edge.' Old Helm closed the journal gently and marked the island on our chart in red.
victim:2.cnHint: 一本日记揭示，失踪的旅人是这座岛屿幻象的____，迷雾会诱人走向边缘。
victim:2.hook: Red marks already covered a third of our chart.
victim:2.line: 'Let this be the last *victim* this mist ever claims.' — Old Helm

sentences.en: Tucked under a loose floor stone we found a journal.
sentences.cn: 我们在一块松动的地板石下找到了一本日记。

sentences.en: The final page read: 'I was not the first *victim* of this island's illusions — the mist shows you what you most want, then leads you off the edge.'
Old Helm closed the journal gently and marked the island on our chart in red.
sentences.cn: 老舵轻轻合上日记，在我们的图表上用红笔标记了这个岛屿。

zone:2.en: Bell spread the newest map fragment across the deck. A wide band of cloud stretched across the centre, marked with diagonal lines. 'That shaded strip is a wind *zone*,' she explained. 'Air currents there spin in every direction. Entering without the right word-key means being thrown miles off course.'
zone:2.cnHint: 领航员在新地图碎片上发现了一片危险的风力____，进入那里需要特殊的词语钥匙。
zone:2.hook: We had the map, but not yet the word.
zone:2.line: 'No ship crosses that *zone* without the right word.' — Bell

sentences.en: Bell spread the newest map fragment across the deck.
sentences.cn: 小铃在甲板上铺开了最新的地图碎片。

sentences.en: A wide band of cloud stretched across the centre, marked with diagonal lines.
sentences.cn: 中央横跨着一条宽阔的云带，上面画着斜线。

sentences.en: 'That shaded strip is a wind *zone*,' she explained.
'Air currents there spin in every direction.
sentences.cn: "那里的气流向四面八方旋转。

sentences.en: Entering without the right word-key means being thrown miles off course.'
sentences.cn: 没有正确的密语进入就会被吹飞好几英里。"

afraid:2.en: Silverfang's vessel pulled alongside ours just as the stars began to dim. He leaned over the rail and called across the gap. 'I know you are not *afraid* of the dark passage,' he said, 'but I am — and I have sailed these skies twice as long as Old Helm.' The honesty surprised everyone.
afraid:2.cnHint: 竞争船长靠近我们，坦白说自己对黑暗通道感到____，这份诚实让所有人都愣住了。
afraid:2.hook: An honest rival is far more dangerous than a proud one.
afraid:2.line: 'Even I am *afraid* of what waits past the last star.' — Silverfang

sentences.en: Silverfang's vessel pulled alongside ours just as the stars began to dim.
sentences.cn: 银牙的船在星星开始暗淡时驶过来靠上了我们的船。

sentences.en: He leaned over the rail and called across the gap.
sentences.cn: 他靠在栏杆上，隔着间隙喊了过来。

sentences.en: 'I know you are not *afraid* of the dark passage,' he said, 'but I am — and I have sailed these skies twice as long as Old Helm.'
The honesty surprised everyone.
sentences.cn: 这份坦诚让每个人都吃了一惊。

couple:2.en: At the edge of the map, Bell found a stone post with two lanterns hanging side by side. 'A *couple* of lights always marks a safe harbour,' she said softly. She pressed both lanterns at once, and a hidden door in the cliff swung open, revealing a stairway that spiralled up into the stars.
couple:2.cnHint: 小铃发现石柱上挂着的一____灯笼，同时按下后，悬崖上的暗门开启了。
couple:2.hook: The stairway had no ceiling — only endless, breathing dark.
couple:2.line: 'A *couple* of lights always marks a safe harbour,' Bell said softly.

sentences.en: At the edge of the map, Bell found a stone post with two lanterns hanging side by side.
sentences.cn: 在地图边缘，小铃发现了一根石柱，上面并排挂着两盏灯笼。

sentences.en: 'A *couple* of lights always marks a safe harbour,' she said softly.
She pressed both lanterns at once, and a hidden door in the cliff swung open, revealing a stairway that spiralled up into the stars.
sentences.cn: 她同时按下两盏灯笼，悬崖里的一扇隐门嘎吱一声打开了，露出一条螺旋向上通往星空的楼梯。

definition:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a faded scroll on the navigator's table. Every island on the map had a name, but one square was blank. 'Without a *definition*, a place cannot be found,' he muttered. He dipped his pen and wrote one careful word, and the blank square slowly filled with the shape of a brand-new island.
definition:2.cnHint: 老舵在地图上一片空白的区域写下____，那块空白随即浮现出一座新岛屿的轮廓。
definition:2.hook: The ink was still wet when the island groaned and rose from the clouds.
definition:2.line: 'Without a *definition*, a place cannot be found,' Old Helm muttered.

sentences.en: Old Helm unrolled a faded scroll on the navigator's table.
sentences.cn: 老舵在领航员的桌子上铺开了一张褪色的卷轴。

sentences.en: Every island on the map had a name, but one square was blank.
sentences.cn: 地图上的每个岛屿都有一个名字，但有一个方格是空白的。

sentences.en: 'Without a *definition*, a place cannot be found,' he muttered.
He dipped his pen and wrote one careful word, and the blank square slowly filled with the shape of a brand-new island.
sentences.cn: 他蘸了笔，仔细地写下一个单词，空白的方格慢慢填满了一座全新岛屿的形状。

imagination:2.en: Deep in the island's crystal cave, the walls showed scenes from nowhere — cities of cloud, rivers of light, creatures with a hundred wings. Bell whispered that the cave fed on *imagination*, growing new pictures from every visitor's mind. I thought of home, and a small warm window appeared, glowing gently among the crystals.
imagination:2.cnHint: 水晶洞穴以访客的____为食，我一想起家，墙上便浮现出温暖的窗户光芒。
imagination:2.hook: Then the window opened, and something beyond it waved back.
imagination:2.line: 'This cave feeds on *imagination* — think carefully about what you picture,' Bell warned.

sentences.en: Deep in the island's crystal cave, the walls showed scenes from nowhere — cities of cloud, rivers of light, creatures with a hundred wings.
sentences.cn: 深入岛屿的水晶洞穴，洞壁映现着无处之景——云城、光河、长着百般翅膀的生物。

sentences.en: Bell whispered that the cave fed on *imagination*, growing new pictures from every visitor's mind.
I thought of home, and a small warm window appeared, glowing gently among the crystals.
sentences.cn: 我想起家乡，一扇温暖的小窗户就在晶体间闪闪发光。

journey:2.en: Silverfang spread a new chart across the ship's deck and traced a long curve with one finger. 'This *journey* will take us past the Rim Rocks and beyond the last marked star,' he said, and there was no fear in his voice, only hunger. Old Helm nodded once, and Bell set the compass to a heading nobody had ever sailed before.
journey:2.cnHint: 银牙描述这段____将带领船队驶过边界岩礁，抵达最后标记星球的彼端。
journey:2.hook: Beyond the last star, the chart was perfectly, terrifyingly blank.
journey:2.line: 'This *journey* will take us past every place we have ever known,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Silverfang spread a new chart across the ship's deck and traced a long curve with one finger.
sentences.cn: 银牙在船甲板上铺开一张新海图，用一根手指沿着长长的弧线描过去。

sentences.en: 'This *journey* will take us past the Rim Rocks and beyond the last marked star,' he said, and there was no fear in his voice, only hunger.
Old Helm nodded once, and Bell set the compass to a heading nobody had ever sailed before.
sentences.cn: 老舵点了点头，小铃把罗盘转向一个从没人航过的方向。

nearby:2.en: The word we sought was carved not in some grand tower but in a mossy stone *nearby*, half-hidden under a flowering vine. I almost walked past it. Old Helm laughed and said the best discoveries always hide in plain sight. I brushed away the vine, and the carved letters glowed gold, adding one more island to our growing map.
nearby:2.cnHint: 我们寻找的词语就刻在____一块长满苔藓的石头上，险些被忽视。
nearby:2.hook: The gold glow spread outward and outlined a whole archipelago no one had mapped.
nearby:2.line: 'Check the stone *nearby* before you look to the horizon,' Old Helm advised.

sentences.en: The word we sought was carved not in some grand tower but in a mossy stone *nearby*, half-hidden under a flowering vine.
I almost walked past it.
sentences.cn: 我差点就走过去了。

sentences.en: Old Helm laughed and said the best discoveries always hide in plain sight.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑着说最好的发现总是藏在最显眼的地方。

sentences.en: I brushed away the vine, and the carved letters glowed gold, adding one more island to our growing map.
sentences.cn: 我拨开藤蔓，刻着的字母闪闪发金光，又给我们成长中的地图加上了一座岛屿。

perspective:2.en: From the ground, the island looked like a tangle of broken rock. But Bell climbed the signal mast and called down that the *perspective* up there was completely different — the rocks formed a perfect arrow pointing north. We had been reading the map from the wrong angle the whole morning. I climbed up too, and everything clicked into place.
perspective:2.cnHint: 从高处望去，小铃发现____截然不同——乱石其实构成了一个指向北方的箭头。
perspective:2.hook: North, the arrow pointed at an island none of our charts had ever named.
perspective:2.line: 'Change your *perspective* and the whole island tells a different story,' Bell called down.

sentences.en: From the ground, the island looked like a tangle of broken rock.
sentences.cn: 从地面看，岛屿像一堆破碎的石头。

sentences.en: But Bell climbed the signal mast and called down that the *perspective* up there was completely different — the rocks formed a perfect arrow pointing north.
We had been reading the map from the wrong angle the whole morning.
sentences.cn: 我们整个上午都是用错的角度读的地图。

sentences.en: I climbed up too, and everything clicked into place.
sentences.cn: 我也爬了上去，一切都对上了。

requirement:2.en: The gate to the inner island bore an inscription in clear letters: one spoken word is the only *requirement* for entry. Silverfang tried three clever phrases and the gate stayed shut. I stepped forward, thought of the word we had found that morning, and said it quietly. The gate sighed open like it had been waiting all its life for exactly that.
requirement:2.cnHint: 内岛大门的铭文写明入场只有一个____：说出一个特定的词语。
requirement:2.hook: Inside, the air smelled of rain and something older than rain.
requirement:2.line: 'One spoken word is the only *requirement* — choose it well,' the inscription read.

sentences.en: The gate to the inner island bore an inscription in clear letters: one spoken word is the only *requirement* for entry.
Silverfang tried three clever phrases and the gate stayed shut.
sentences.cn: 银牙试了三个巧妙的短语，大门没动。

sentences.en: I stepped forward, thought of the word we had found that morning, and said it quietly.
sentences.cn: 我走上前，想起了那天上午找到的那个词，轻声说了出来。

sentences.en: The gate sighed open like it had been waiting all its life for exactly that.
sentences.cn: 大门叹了一口气，像打开了一生都在等待的东西。

signal:2.en: Bell stood at the bow and raised the blue lantern three times — the agreed sign that we had found the edge of the map. Far below, through the clouds, a second light *signalled* back: another troupe, on another vessel, had reached the same edge from the other side. Old Helm spread his arms wide and said the world was suddenly twice as large.
signal:2.cnHint: 小铃举起蓝色灯笼发出____，云层下方竟有另一支船队从对面抵达了地图的尽头。
signal:2.hook: The other vessel rose slowly through the clouds, and it was beautiful and strange.
signal:2.line: 'When you reach the edge, *signal* with the blue lantern so others can find you,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Bell stood at the bow and raised the blue lantern three times — the agreed sign that we had found the edge of the map.
sentences.cn: 小铃站在船首，把蓝灯笼举起来三次——这是我们约定好的信号，表示找到了地图的边缘。

sentences.en: Far below, through the clouds, a second light *signalled* back: another troupe, on another vessel, had reached the same edge from the other side.
Old Helm spread his arms wide and said the world was suddenly twice as large.
sentences.cn: 老舵张开双臂说世界一下子变大了一倍。

salary:2.en: Tucked inside a hollow post on Amber Isle, we found a rolled-up notice. It listed every job on the old sky-fleet — cook, rigger, cloud-reader — along with each worker's *salary* paid in star-coins. Old Helm read it twice, then smiled. 'Someone valued their crew well,' he said, and added the word to our map.
salary:2.cnHint: 在一根空心柱子里，我们发现了一份记录各岗位____的旧告示。
salary:2.hook: But one name on the list matched the carving above our own ship's door.
salary:2.line: 'A fair *salary* means a loyal crew,' Old Helm said softly.

sentences.en: Tucked inside a hollow post on Amber Isle, we found a rolled-up notice.
sentences.cn: 我们在琥珀岛一根空心柱子里找到了一张卷起来的告示。

sentences.en: It listed every job on the old sky-fleet — cook, rigger, cloud-reader — along with each worker's *salary* paid in star-coins.
Old Helm read it twice, then smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵读了两遍，然后笑了。

sentences.en: 'Someone valued their crew well,' he said, and added the word to our map.
sentences.cn: "有人把他们的船员看得很值钱，"他说，把这个词加到了我们的地图上。

shopping:2.en: The market island of Tinspar hung low in the clouds, its stalls bright with lanterns. Bell dragged me from booth to booth — *shopping* for a new compass needle, a spool of silver thread, and a jar of dried sky-berries. She found all three, then held up the jar with a grin. 'Navigation fuel,' she said.
shopping:2.cnHint: 小铃带我在云端集市上____，寻找指南针针头和其他补给。
shopping:2.hook: Then she spotted a vendor selling something that had no name — yet.
shopping:2.line: 'I love *shopping* on a new island,' Bell said, eyes wide.

sentences.en: The market island of Tinspar hung low in the clouds, its stalls bright with lanterns.
sentences.cn: 锡花岛市集悬在云层下方，摊位上灯笼明亮。

sentences.en: Bell dragged me from booth to booth — *shopping* for a new compass needle, a spool of silver thread, and a jar of dried sky-berries.
She found all three, then held up the jar with a grin.
sentences.cn: 她找齐了三样，然后举起那罐子咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: 'Navigation fuel,' she said.
sentences.cn: "航海燃料，"她说。

tendency:2.en: Old Helm spread the star-charts across the deck. 'Every sky-current has a *tendency* to pull west near the solstice,' he told me, tracing a slow arc with his finger. 'Fight it and you drift. Follow it and you glide.' I wrote the word down, and the chart shimmered — a new island blinked into view.
tendency:2.cnHint: 老舵解释说，天空气流有向西偏移的____，顺势而行才能找到新岛屿。
tendency:2.hook: The island at the edge of the arc had no name on any chart we owned.
tendency:2.line: 'Clouds have a *tendency* to hide the best islands,' Old Helm said with a wink.

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the star-charts across the deck.
sentences.cn: 老舵在甲板上铺开星图。

sentences.en: 'Every sky-current has a *tendency* to pull west near the solstice,' he told me, tracing a slow arc with his finger.
'Fight it and you drift.
sentences.cn: "对着它就会漂移。

sentences.en: Follow it and you glide.'
sentences.cn: 顺着它就会滑行。"

sentences.en: I wrote the word down, and the chart shimmered — a new island blinked into view.
sentences.cn: 我把这个词写下来，海图闪了闪——一座新岛屿出现了。

tough:2.en: The rope bridge to Cinder Ledge was *tough* work — planks missing, wind howling, the whole thing swaying like a slow pendulum. Silverfang crossed first, made it look easy, then called back: 'Fastest way earns the word!' I gritted my teeth and kept moving. The ledge on the other side held a glowing stone carved with our next destination.
tough:2.cnHint: 通往Cinder Ledge的绳桥摇摇晃晃，过桥是一件____的事，但终点藏着下一个目的地。
tough:2.hook: The glowing stone was still warm, as if someone had just set it down.
tough:2.line: 'The path is *tough*, but the view makes it worth it,' Silverfang called out.

sentences.en: The rope bridge to Cinder Ledge was *tough* work — planks missing, wind howling, the whole thing swaying like a slow pendulum.
Silverfang crossed first, made it look easy, then called back: 'Fastest way earns the word!'
sentences.cn: 银牙先过去了，看起来很轻松，然后喊回来："最快过去的人赢得这个词！"

sentences.en: I gritted my teeth and kept moving.
sentences.cn: 我咬紧牙关继续前进。

sentences.en: The ledge on the other side held a glowing stone carved with our next destination.
sentences.cn: 另一边的峭壁上有一块闪闪发光的石头，上面刻着我们的下一个目的地。

tour:2.en: Bell suggested a slow *tour* of Spiral Atoll before we anchored — one full loop around its five connected islands to read the wind and mark the safe coves. We drifted in silence, watching fireflies trace the cliff edges. By the time we completed the circle, I had filled two whole pages with sketches and the map had grown a new ring.
tour:2.cnHint: 小铃建议先绕旋形环礁____一圈，观察风向，记录安全的停泊地。
tour:2.hook: On the final stretch, a second ship appeared, following our exact path.
tour:2.line: 'Every good *tour* teaches you something you did not plan to learn,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Bell suggested a slow *tour* of Spiral Atoll before we anchored — one full loop around its five connected islands to read the wind and mark the safe coves.
We drifted in silence, watching fireflies trace the cliff edges.
sentences.cn: 我们默默地飘行，看着萤火虫沿着悬崖边缘飞舞。

sentences.en: By the time we completed the circle, I had filled two whole pages with sketches and the map had grown a new ring.
sentences.cn: 等我们绕完一圈，我已经填满了两整页的素描，地图又增长了一圈。

wake:2.en: We dropped anchor at dusk and held a quiet *wake* for the word 'horizon' — a fragment lost when our old chart tore in the storm. Old Helm set a single lantern on the water and we watched it float away, carrying the memory. Then he pulled out a new chart and said, 'Grief done. Now we find it again.'
wake:2.cnHint: 我们为一块在风暴中丢失的地图碎片举行了简短的____仪式，然后重新出发。
wake:2.hook: The floating lantern stopped — and slowly turned back toward us.
wake:2.line: 'A *wake* reminds us what mattered,' Old Helm said, voice gentle.

sentences.en: We dropped anchor at dusk and held a quiet *wake* for the word 'horizon' — a fragment lost when our old chart tore in the storm.
Old Helm set a single lantern on the water and we watched it float away, carrying the memory.
sentences.cn: 老舵在水面上放了一盏灯笼，我们看着它漂走，承载着记忆。

sentences.en: Then he pulled out a new chart and said, 'Grief done.
sentences.cn: 然后他拿出一张新海图说，"悲伤完了。

sentences.en: Now we find it again.'
sentences.cn: 现在我们再找一遍。"

annual:2.en: Carved into the wall of the Tidestone Cave was a record of the troupe's *annual* journey — one line per year, each ending with how many words the team had collected. This year's line was still blank. Silverfang ran a finger along the empty space. 'Our turn to write something worth reading,' they said, and handed me the chisel.
annual:2.cnHint: 山洞石壁上刻着每年____的航行记录，今年那行还空着，等待我们来填写。
annual:2.hook: The chisel was heavier than it looked, and my hand would not stop shaking.
annual:2.line: 'The *annual* record never lies about how hard you worked,' Silverfang said.

sentences.en: Carved into the wall of the Tidestone Cave was a record of the troupe's *annual* journey — one line per year, each ending with how many words the team had collected.
This year's line was still blank.
sentences.cn: 今年这一行还是空白的。

sentences.en: Silverfang ran a finger along the empty space.
sentences.cn: 银牙用手指沿着空白处划过。

sentences.en: 'Our turn to write something worth reading,' they said, and handed me the chisel.
sentences.cn: "该轮到我们写点值得一读的东西了，"他们说，把凿子递给了我。

charity:2.en: At the Gate of Echoes, a keeper stopped us. 'No coin, no passage,' she said. Old Helm reached into his pack and gave her our spare star-map — pure *charity*, nothing asked in return. She studied it for a long moment, then stepped aside and pressed a small glass word into his palm. It spelled out our next island's name in light.
charity:2.cnHint: 在回声之门，老舵出于____之心将备用地图送给守门人，换来了下一座岛屿的名字。
charity:2.hook: The glass word was still warm, and it hummed like it was alive.
charity:2.line: 'True *charity* asks for nothing back,' Old Helm said, smiling at the keeper.

sentences.en: At the Gate of Echoes, a keeper stopped us.
sentences.cn: 在回声门，一个守卫挡住了我们。

sentences.en: 'No coin, no passage,' she said.
sentences.cn: "没有硬币，不让过，"她说。

sentences.en: Old Helm reached into his pack and gave her our spare star-map — pure *charity*, nothing asked in return.
She studied it for a long moment, then stepped aside and pressed a small glass word into his palm.
sentences.cn: 她盯着看了很久，然后让到一边，把一个小玻璃字放进了他的手心。

sentences.en: It spelled out our next island's name in light.
sentences.cn: 它用光芒拼出了我们下一个岛屿的名字。

behave:2.en: The Ink Isle librarian watched us with narrow eyes as we searched the shelves. Old Helm whispered that the word we needed was sealed inside a glass case. 'Touch nothing,' he murmured. I tried hard to *behave*, keeping my hands behind my back, even when a glowing page fluttered right past my nose.
behave:2.cnHint: 在墨水岛图书馆里，老舵提醒大家要注意____，因为我们要找的词藏在玻璃柜里。
behave:2.hook: The glass case creaked open on its own.
behave:2.line: 'You must *behave* in here, or the shelves will seal themselves forever.'

sentences.en: The Ink Isle librarian watched us with narrow eyes as we searched the shelves.
sentences.cn: 墨岛的图书管理员用狭长的眼睛盯着我们搜索书架。

sentences.en: Old Helm whispered that the word we needed was sealed inside a glass case.
sentences.cn: 老舵低声说我们需要的那个字被锁在一个玻璃柜里。

sentences.en: 'Touch nothing,' he murmured.
sentences.cn: "什么都别碰，"他低声说。

sentences.en: I tried hard to *behave*, keeping my hands behind my back, even when a glowing page fluttered right past my nose.

cent:2.en: At the sky market above Cloud-Nine Island, Bell found a coin half-buried in the wooden floor. She held it up: one copper *cent*, stamped with a tiny island on both sides. Old Helm squinted and smiled. 'That is no ordinary coin,' he said. 'That is the map fragment we have been searching for all week.'
cent:2.cnHint: 小铃在天空集市的地板上发现了一枚铜____，老舵认出它其实是一块地图碎片。
cent:2.hook: The coin began to spin on its own.
cent:2.line: 'One *cent* can open a door that gold cannot,' Old Helm said softly.

sentences.en: At the sky market above Cloud-Nine Island, Bell found a coin half-buried in the wooden floor.
sentences.cn: 在九云岛上方的天空集市里，小铃在木地板上发现了一枚半埋着的硬币。

sentences.en: She held it up: one copper *cent*, stamped with a tiny island on both sides.
Old Helm squinted and smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵眯起眼睛，笑了。

sentences.en: 'That is no ordinary coin,' he said.
sentences.cn: "那不是普通的硬币，"他说。

sentences.en: 'That is the map fragment we have been searching for all week.'
sentences.cn: "那是我们整个星期都在找的地图碎片。"

commercial:2.en: The island of Brass Quay was built for trade. Every sign, every flag, every painted wall carried some *commercial* message selling goods from across the sky. Bell said it felt like the whole island was shouting at once. But tucked behind a noisy market stall, silent and small, was the word we had come to find.
commercial:2.cnHint: 黄铜码头岛是个____气息浓厚的地方，但我们要找的词静静地藏在一个嘈杂摊位的背后。
commercial:2.hook: The word glowed faintly, waiting to be claimed.
commercial:2.line: 'This place is too *commercial*,' Bell said, 'but the word hides where no one is selling anything.'

sentences.en: The island of Brass Quay was built for trade.
sentences.cn: 铜码头岛是为了贸易而建的。

sentences.en: Every sign, every flag, every painted wall carried some *commercial* message selling goods from across the sky.
Bell said it felt like the whole island was shouting at once.
sentences.cn: 小铃说感觉整个岛都在同时大声叫喊。

sentences.en: But tucked behind a noisy market stall, silent and small, was the word we had come to find.
sentences.cn: 但在一个喧闹的市集摊位后面，悄悄地躲着一个小小的字，正是我们来要找的那个。

death:2.en: On the Isle of Still Waters, an old stone tablet stood alone in a quiet garden. It marked the spot where a great navigator had rested his final journey. Bell read the carved words aloud. The tablet spoke of *death* not as an ending but as a doorway, and below the last line, a fresh word shimmered into view, ready for us to take.
death:2.cnHint: 在静水岛的石碑上，小铃读到了一段关于____的文字，碑文下方随即浮现出我们要寻找的词。
death:2.hook: The word on the stone was still warm to the touch.
death:2.line: '*Death* is just the last island on a very long map,' Old Helm said quietly.

sentences.en: On the Isle of Still Waters, an old stone tablet stood alone in a quiet garden.
sentences.cn: 在静水岛上，一块古老的石板独自立在一个安静的花园里。

sentences.en: It marked the spot where a great navigator had rested his final journey.
sentences.cn: 它标记了一位伟大航海家最后旅程休息的地方。

sentences.en: Bell read the carved words aloud.
sentences.cn: 小铃大声读出了刻在上面的字。

sentences.en: The tablet spoke of *death* not as an ending but as a doorway, and below the last line, a fresh word shimmered into view, ready for us to take.

escape:2.en: The rope bridge to Mirror Isle snapped just as I stepped onto it. I grabbed a hanging vine and swung to the far platform, heart pounding. Old Helm called it a narrow *escape*. Bell was already laughing with relief. On the platform, carved into the railing, was the word we had come for, as if the island had tested us first.
escape:2.cnHint: 去镜子岛的绳桥断了，我勉强____成功，老舵说这真是千钧一发，而我们要找的词就刻在对面的栏杆上。
escape:2.hook: The broken bridge swayed below, and the word glowed above.
escape:2.line: 'That was a lucky *escape*,' Silverfang said, gripping the railing with wide eyes.

sentences.en: The rope bridge to Mirror Isle snapped just as I stepped onto it.
sentences.cn: 通往镜岛的绳桥在我踩上去的时候断了。

sentences.en: I grabbed a hanging vine and swung to the far platform, heart pounding.
sentences.cn: 我抓住了一根垂下来的藤条，摇晃着跳到了对面的平台，心脏砰砰直跳。

sentences.en: Old Helm called it a narrow *escape*.
Bell was already laughing with relief.
sentences.cn: 小铃已经松了口气地笑了起来。

sentences.en: On the platform, carved into the railing, was the word we had come for, as if the island had tested us first.
sentences.cn: 在平台上，刻在栏杆上的是我们来要找的那个字，仿佛这个岛先测试了我们一遍。

expose:2.en: Fog Island hid everything under a thick white mist. Silverfang said the word we needed was somewhere on the eastern cliff. Bell climbed first and pulled away a curtain of hanging moss to *expose* a wide flat rock face covered in carvings. There, among the shapes of birds and ships, was the word, clear as starlight.
expose:2.cnHint: 在雾岛，小铃拨开悬挂的苔藓，____出一整面刻满图案的岩壁，我们要找的词就在其中。
expose:2.hook: One carving was still warm, as if freshly made.
expose:2.line: 'Pull the moss aside and *expose* what the island has been hiding,' Bell called down to us.

sentences.en: Fog Island hid everything under a thick white mist.
sentences.cn: 雾岛把一切都隐藏在厚厚的白雾下。

sentences.en: Silverfang said the word we needed was somewhere on the eastern cliff.
sentences.cn: 银牙说我们需要的那个字在东边的悬崖上的某个地方。

sentences.en: Bell climbed first and pulled away a curtain of hanging moss to *expose* a wide flat rock face covered in carvings.
There, among the shapes of birds and ships, was the word, clear as starlight.
sentences.cn: 那里，在鸟和船的图案之间，那个字清晰如星光。

floor:2.en: The Crystal Cavern hung upside down beneath Lantern Isle — we had to climb down to enter it. Inside, the *floor* was smooth blue stone, so clear we could see the clouds and stars far below through it. Old Helm knelt and pressed his palm flat. The word rose up through the stone and settled in his hand like a gift.
floor:2.cnHint: 水晶洞穴的____是透明的蓝色石头，老舵跪下来触碰它，我们要找的词就从石头中浮现出来。
floor:2.hook: Below the floor, something vast moved slowly through the sky.
floor:2.line: 'Look at the *floor*,' Old Helm said, 'the word is already rising to meet us.'

sentences.en: The Crystal Cavern hung upside down beneath Lantern Isle — we had to climb down to enter it.
sentences.cn: 水晶洞穴倒悬在灯笼岛下面——我们得往下爬才能进去。

sentences.en: Inside, the *floor* was smooth blue stone, so clear we could see the clouds and stars far below through it.
Old Helm knelt and pressed his palm flat.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪下来，把掌心按在地上。

sentences.en: The word rose up through the stone and settled in his hand like a gift.
sentences.cn: 那个字从石头里升起，像礼物一样落在了他的手心。

foundation:2.en: The oldest island in the sky was barely the size of a house. Old Helm said every chain of islands we had ever visited was built outward from this one — it was the *foundation* of the whole sky map. Bell placed the last word fragment at its centre. The stone hummed, and a new cluster of islands bloomed on the horizon like morning flowers.
foundation:2.cnHint: 老舵说这座最古老的小岛是整张天空地图的____，小铃把最后一块词碎片放在它中心后，远处升起了新的岛屿群。
foundation:2.hook: The new islands were unlike any they had seen before.
foundation:2.line: 'This island is the *foundation*,' Old Helm said, 'and now you understand why we protect it.'

sentences.en: The oldest island in the sky was barely the size of a house.
sentences.cn: 天空中最古老的岛屿还不到一间房子的大小。

sentences.en: Old Helm said every chain of islands we had ever visited was built outward from this one — it was the *foundation* of the whole sky map.
Bell placed the last word fragment at its centre.
sentences.cn: 小铃把最后一个字的碎片放在了它的中心。

sentences.en: The stone hummed, and a new cluster of islands bloomed on the horizon like morning flowers.
sentences.cn: 石头发出嗡鸣声，地平线上一簇新的岛屿像晨间的花朵一样绽放开来。

frame:2.en: Inside the old lighthouse, Bell held up a wooden *frame* — four thin strips of carved driftwood, no bigger than my hand. 'Each side is a different island,' she said softly. Through the open centre, a patch of night sky looked exactly like the gap in our map. Old Helm nodded: the frame was the missing piece.
frame:2.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔里发现了一个木制____，它的形状与地图上的空缺完美吻合。
frame:2.hook: The stars inside the frame began to rearrange themselves.
frame:2.line: 'This *frame* is not decoration — it is a door.'

sentences.en: Inside the old lighthouse, Bell held up a wooden *frame* — four thin strips of carved driftwood, no bigger than my hand.
'Each side is a different island,' she said softly.
sentences.cn: "每一边都是一个不同的岛屿，"她轻声说。

sentences.en: Through the open centre, a patch of night sky looked exactly like the gap in our map.
sentences.cn: 透过开放的中心，夜空的一个角落看起来完全像我们地图上的缺口。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded: the frame was the missing piece.
sentences.cn: 老舵点了点头：这个框就是失落的碎片。

friday:2.en: A message was scratched into the stone wall of the island dock: 'Meet us on *Friday* — bring the blue word.' Old Helm studied it, then smiled. 'Someone knew we were coming,' he said. Bell checked the sky-calendar. Today was Thursday. We had exactly one night to find the blue word before the meeting.
friday:2.cnHint: 码头石壁上刻着一条神秘留言，约定在____见面。
friday:2.hook: Somewhere below the dock, a light blinked once, then twice.
friday:2.line: 'By *Friday* dawn, we either have answers — or we lose the trail.'

sentences.en: A message was scratched into the stone wall of the island dock: 'Meet us on *Friday* — bring the blue word.'
Old Helm studied it, then smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵研究了一下，然后笑了。

sentences.en: 'Someone knew we were coming,' he said.
sentences.cn: "有人知道我们要来，"他说。

sentences.en: Bell checked the sky-calendar.
sentences.cn: 小铃查了一下天空日历。

sentences.en: Today was Thursday.
sentences.cn: 今天是星期四。

sentences.en: We had exactly one night to find the blue word before the meeting.
sentences.cn: 我们还有整整一个晚上的时间来找到那个蓝字，然后赶上明天的会面。

grain:2.en: The message was hidden inside a tiny jar of sand. Bell poured it onto the chart table and each *grain* caught the starlight differently — red, gold, silver. Old Helm leaned close. 'It is not sand,' Silverfang murmured. 'Read the colours in order.' Together we spelled out the name of the next island.
grain:2.cnHint: 小铃将罐中的沙倒在地图桌上，每一____都折射出不同颜色，组成了下一座岛的名字。
grain:2.hook: One silver grain rolled to the map's edge and refused to stop.
grain:2.line: 'Every *grain* is a letter — read them before the wind does.'

sentences.en: The message was hidden inside a tiny jar of sand.
sentences.cn: 信息被藏在一个装满沙子的小罐子里。

sentences.en: Bell poured it onto the chart table and each *grain* caught the starlight differently — red, gold, silver.
Old Helm leaned close.
sentences.cn: 老舵靠得很近。

sentences.en: 'It is not sand,' Silverfang murmured.
sentences.cn: "这不是沙子，"银牙低声说。

sentences.en: 'Read the colours in order.'
sentences.cn: "按顺序读出颜色。"

sentences.en: Together we spelled out the name of the next island.
sentences.cn: 我们一起拼出了下一座岛屿的名字。

implication:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a short note left on our ship's wheel. It said only: 'The sky-door opens once.' Bell frowned. 'The *implication* is clear — if we miss the moment, the route is gone forever.' Silverfang was already pulling ropes. Nobody needed to say another word. We turned the ship toward the light on the horizon.
implication:2.cnHint: 地图上留下的短短一句话，其____让全员立刻行动起来。
implication:2.hook: The light on the horizon pulsed, as though counting down.
implication:2.line: 'The *implication* of that note is: we leave now, not tomorrow.'

sentences.en: Old Helm unrolled a short note left on our ship's wheel.
sentences.cn: 老舵展开了一张留在我们船舵上的短笺。

sentences.en: It said only: 'The sky-door opens once.'
sentences.cn: 上面只写着："天空之门只开启一次。"

sentences.en: Bell frowned.
sentences.cn: 小铃皱起了眉头。

sentences.en: 'The *implication* is clear — if we miss the moment, the route is gone forever.'
Silverfang was already pulling ropes.
sentences.cn: 银牙已经在拉绳索了。

sentences.en: Nobody needed to say another word.
sentences.cn: 没有人需要再说什么。

sentences.en: We turned the ship toward the light on the horizon.
sentences.cn: 我们把船转向地平线上的光。

incredible:2.en: We landed on an island made entirely of salt flats, white as fresh paper under the stars. In the centre sat a single stone desk with a glowing word carved deep into its top. 'This is *incredible*,' I whispered — I had never seen a word that gave off its own light. Old Helm placed his hand over it, and the whole flat island hummed gently.
incredible:2.cnHint: 我们登上一座由盐滩构成的小岛，发现了一张散发光芒的石桌，令人感到____。
incredible:2.hook: The humming grew louder the moment I reached out to touch it.
incredible:2.line: '*Incredible* — the word is warm, like it has been waiting for us.'

sentences.en: We landed on an island made entirely of salt flats, white as fresh paper under the stars.
sentences.cn: 我们降落在一座完全由盐碱地构成的岛屿上，在星光下白得像新纸一样。

sentences.en: In the centre sat a single stone desk with a glowing word carved deep into its top.
sentences.cn: 岛的中央放着一张单独的石头桌子，桌面深深刻着一个闪闪发光的字。

sentences.en: 'This is *incredible*,' I whispered — I had never seen a word that gave off its own light.
Old Helm placed his hand over it, and the whole flat island hummed gently.
sentences.cn: 老舵把手放在它上面，整个盐碱岛轻轻嗡鸣起来。

net:2.en: A silk *net* hung between two tall rocks at the island's edge, full of small glowing objects caught mid-air — each one a word-fragment from a previous troupe. Bell read them aloud one by one. Old Helm matched three of them to gaps in our map. 'Other travellers left these for whoever came next,' he said quietly. I felt like part of something much bigger.
net:2.cnHint: 两块礁石之间挂着一张丝____，网住了前人留下的发光词片。
net:2.hook: One fragment in the net was still warm, left very recently.
net:2.line: 'Pull in the *net* carefully — every piece matters to someone.'

sentences.en: A silk *net* hung between two tall rocks at the island's edge, full of small glowing objects caught mid-air — each one a word-fragment from a previous troupe.
Bell read them aloud one by one.
sentences.cn: 小铃一个一个地大声读出来。

sentences.en: Old Helm matched three of them to gaps in our map.
sentences.cn: 老舵把其中三个对应到了我们地图上的空白处。

sentences.en: 'Other travellers left these for whoever came next,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "其他旅行者留下这些给后来的人，"他轻声说。

sentences.en: I felt like part of something much bigger.
sentences.cn: 我感觉自己是某个更大事物的一部分。

obtain:2.en: The island's gate was sealed with a riddle carved above the arch: 'You may only *obtain* what you can name.' Bell thought for a moment, then spoke the word on our newest map-fragment clearly into the lock. A soft click. The gate swung open onto a garden full of floating lanterns. Old Helm patted my shoulder. 'Good things ask to be earned,' he said.
obtain:2.cnHint: 岛门上的谜语说，只有能说出名字的东西才能被____。
obtain:2.hook: Inside the garden, one lantern drifted straight toward me.
obtain:2.line: 'To *obtain* the next fragment, you must first understand what you already hold.'

sentences.en: The island's gate was sealed with a riddle carved above the arch: 'You may only *obtain* what you can name.'
Bell thought for a moment, then spoke the word on our newest map-fragment clearly into the lock.
sentences.cn: 小铃思考了片刻，然后清晰地把我们最新地图碎片上的字念进了锁里。

sentences.en: A soft click.
sentences.cn: 轻轻一声咔哒。

sentences.en: The gate swung open onto a garden full of floating lanterns.
sentences.cn: 门打开了，露出一个花园，里面飘满了发光的灯笼。

sentences.en: Old Helm patted my shoulder.
sentences.cn: 老舵拍了拍我的肩膀。

sentences.en: 'Good things ask to be earned,' he said.
sentences.cn: "好东西是要争取的，"他说。

pair:2.en: Bell spread the map and pointed to two islands close together, almost touching. 'This *pair* always moves in the same direction — if we reach one, we reach both.' Silverfang steered toward the nearer of the two. As we drew close, a narrow bridge of cloud appeared between them, solid enough to walk on. Old Helm grinned. 'Double discovery,' he said. 'Best kind of morning.'
pair:2.cnHint: 地图上紧挨着的一____小岛总是同向移动，靠近其中一座就能抵达两座。
pair:2.hook: The cloud bridge was already beginning to thin at its edges.
pair:2.line: 'Chart this *pair* together — they share one secret between them.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the map and pointed to two islands close together, almost touching.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开地图，指向两个挨得很近、几乎要碰到的岛屿。

sentences.en: 'This *pair* always moves in the same direction — if we reach one, we reach both.'
Silverfang steered toward the nearer of the two.
sentences.cn: 银牙朝其中较近的那座岛舵向转去。

sentences.en: As we drew close, a narrow bridge of cloud appeared between them, solid enough to walk on.
sentences.cn: 当我们靠近时，它们之间出现了一座窄窄的云桥，牢固得足以走过去。

sentences.en: Old Helm grinned.
sentences.cn: 老舵咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: 'Double discovery,' he said.
sentences.cn: "双重发现，"他说。

sentences.en: 'Best kind of morning.'
sentences.cn: "最棒的开场。"

persuade:2.en: The old lighthouse on Driftstone Island held a sealed door. Bell found a carved word on it — *persuade* — and said it aloud. The door hummed, then swung open, revealing a rolled map inside a glass jar. Old Helm smiled. 'Words here do not just describe things,' he said. 'They make them happen.'
persuade:2.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔门上发现了一个刻字，大声念出来后，门竟然____开了，里面藏着一张地图。
persuade:2.hook: But the map showed an island none of them had ever heard of.
persuade:2.line: 'Sometimes you have to *persuade* a door the same way you persuade a person — with the right words.'

sentences.en: The old lighthouse on Driftstone Island held a sealed door.
sentences.cn: 漂流石岛上的旧灯塔有一扇密封的门。

sentences.en: Bell found a carved word on it — *persuade* — and said it aloud.
The door hummed, then swung open, revealing a rolled map inside a glass jar.
sentences.cn: 门嗡鸣着，然后打开了，里面是一张卷起的地图，放在一个玻璃罐里。

sentences.en: Old Helm smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑了。

sentences.en: 'Words here do not just describe things,' he said.
sentences.cn: "这里的字不仅仅是描述东西，"他说。

sentences.en: 'They make them happen.'
sentences.cn: "它们让东西发生。"

preference:2.en: We reached a fork in the sky-road above Mirewend Island. Two bridges stretched ahead — one made of silver stone, one of woven cloud. Old Helm asked each of us our *preference*. Bell chose cloud. Silverfang chose stone. I said nothing, because I could not tell which path felt safer, and both looked beautiful.
preference:2.cnHint: 天空路口，老团长问大家各自的____，小铃和银牙意见不同，而叙述者无法选择。
preference:2.hook: Then the cloud bridge began to slowly dissolve at its far end.
preference:2.line: 'My *preference* is the path that leads somewhere new,' said Old Helm, stepping onto the cloud bridge first.

sentences.en: We reached a fork in the sky-road above Mirewend Island.
sentences.cn: 我们来到了泥沼地岛上空中天路的分叉口。

sentences.en: Two bridges stretched ahead — one made of silver stone, one of woven cloud.
sentences.cn: 两座桥在前方延伸——一座由银色石头造成，一座由编织的云做成。

sentences.en: Old Helm asked each of us our *preference*.
Bell chose cloud.
sentences.cn: 小铃选了云。

sentences.en: Silverfang chose stone.
sentences.cn: 银牙选了石头。

sentences.en: I said nothing, because I could not tell which path felt safer, and both looked beautiful.
sentences.cn: 我什么都没说，因为我分不清哪条路更安全，而两条看起来都很美。

reliable:2.en: Silverfang pulled a small brass compass from her coat and set it on the table. 'This is the only *reliable* thing I own,' she said quietly. The needle did not point north — it pointed toward the next word on our map. Old Helm nodded. I watched the needle tremble, then settle, aiming straight at a gap in the clouds below.
reliable:2.cnHint: 银牙拿出一个黄铜罗盘，说这是她唯一____的东西，它的指针指向下一个单词所在的方向。
reliable:2.hook: The gap in the clouds was moving, and moving fast.
reliable:2.line: 'A *reliable* tool is worth more than a dozen clever guesses,' Silverfang said, tucking the compass away.

sentences.en: Silverfang pulled a small brass compass from her coat and set it on the table.
sentences.cn: 银牙从外套里掏出一个小黄铜指南针，放在了桌子上。

sentences.en: 'This is the only *reliable* thing I own,' she said quietly.
The needle did not point north — it pointed toward the next word on our map.
sentences.cn: 指针不指向北方——它指向我们地图上的下一个字。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded.
sentences.cn: 老舵点了点头。

sentences.en: I watched the needle tremble, then settle, aiming straight at a gap in the clouds below.
sentences.cn: 我看着指针颤抖，然后稳定下来，指向下方云层中的一个缺口。

suspect:2.en: Someone had moved our word-jar in the night. Three glowing letters were missing. Old Helm looked around the camp slowly. 'I *suspect* the wind did not take them,' he said. Bell checked the edge of the island and found small boot-prints in the moss — prints none of us had made. The stars above felt suddenly closer, and colder.
suspect:2.cnHint: 营地里装字的罐子被动过，几个字母不见了，老团长____不是风干的，小铃在边缘发现了陌生的脚印。
suspect:2.hook: Whoever had been here had also left a folded note inside the empty jar.
suspect:2.line: 'I *suspect* we are not the only ones collecting words on these islands,' Old Helm said softly.

sentences.en: Someone had moved our word-jar in the night.
sentences.cn: 昨晚有人移动了我们的字罐。

sentences.en: Three glowing letters were missing.
sentences.cn: 三个闪闪发光的字母不见了。

sentences.en: Old Helm looked around the camp slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵缓缓扫视了整个营地。

sentences.en: 'I *suspect* the wind did not take them,' he said.
Bell checked the edge of the island and found small boot-prints in the moss — prints none of us had made.
sentences.cn: 小铃检查了岛的边缘，在苔藓里发现了小靴子的脚印——不是我们任何人留下的。

sentences.en: The stars above felt suddenly closer, and colder.
sentences.cn: 头顶的星星突然感觉离得更近了，也更冷了。

yield:2.en: The tall stone gate at the centre of Ashbell Island would not open to pushing or pulling. Bell read the inscription aloud: the gate would only *yield* to a word spoken with honest intent. Silverfang whispered 'trust.' The stone groaned and parted. Beyond it, a single lantern floated above a pedestal holding our next map fragment.
yield:2.cnHint: 高石门无法强行打开，门上的铭文说只有诚心说出一个词，它才会____，银牙说出了"信任"。
yield:2.hook: The lantern inside flickered once, as if it had been waiting a long time.
yield:2.line: 'Some things only *yield* when you stop forcing them,' Bell said, watching the gate slide open.

sentences.en: The tall stone gate at the centre of Ashbell Island would not open to pushing or pulling.
sentences.cn: 灰钟岛中央的高石门推不动也拉不开。

sentences.en: Bell read the inscription aloud: the gate would only *yield* to a word spoken with honest intent.
Silverfang whispered 'trust.'
sentences.cn: 银牙低声说"信任"。

sentences.en: The stone groaned and parted.
sentences.cn: 石头发出呻吟声，裂开了。

sentences.en: Beyond it, a single lantern floated above a pedestal holding our next map fragment.
sentences.cn: 在它后面，一个单独的灯笼飘浮在一个底座上方，底座上放着我们下一块地图碎片。

abandon:2.en: We found a small sky-boat tied to a post on the edge of Thornmere Island. It was full of word-jars, all empty. Old Helm knelt beside it. 'Someone chose to *abandon* this vessel — and everything they had collected,' he said. Bell counted nine empty jars. I wondered what had made the other traveller give up so close to the next island.
abandon:2.cnHint: 我们在岛边发现一艘被人____的小空船，船上有九个装词语的空罐子，不知为何主人放弃了旅程。
abandon:2.hook: At the bottom of the last jar was a single word, written in shaking handwriting: 'return.'
abandon:2.line: 'We do not *abandon* the map, no matter how tired we feel,' Old Helm said firmly but kindly.

sentences.en: We found a small sky-boat tied to a post on the edge of Thornmere Island.
sentences.cn: 我们在荆棘沼岛边缘的一根柱子上发现了一艘小小的天空船，被拴在那里。

sentences.en: It was full of word-jars, all empty.
sentences.cn: 船里装满了字罐，全都是空的。

sentences.en: Old Helm knelt beside it.
sentences.cn: 老舵在它旁边跪下。

sentences.en: 'Someone chose to *abandon* this vessel — and everything they had collected,' he said.
Bell counted nine empty jars.
sentences.cn: 小铃数了数，有九个空罐子。

sentences.en: I wondered what had made the other traveller give up so close to the next island.
sentences.cn: 我想知道是什么让那个旅行者在离下一座岛这么近的地方放弃了。

anxious:2.en: As our ship rose above the cloud-line toward the unmarked island, I felt *anxious* — the kind of nervous that sits behind your ribs and will not leave. Bell noticed and handed me a warm cup without saying anything. Old Helm looked back from the wheel and nodded once. It helped, somehow. The unknown island grew larger in the dark sky ahead.
anxious:2.cnHint: 飞船升入云层向未知岛屿驶去时，叙述者感到____，小铃默默递上一杯热饮，老团长转身点了点头。
anxious:2.hook: Then a second island appeared behind the first, and it was larger.
anxious:2.line: 'It is fine to feel *anxious*,' Bell said softly. 'It means you care about what comes next.'

sentences.en: As our ship rose above the cloud-line toward the unmarked island, I felt *anxious* — the kind of nervous that sits behind your ribs and will not leave.
Bell noticed and handed me a warm cup without saying anything.
sentences.cn: 小铃注意到了，什么也没说，递给我一杯热饮。

sentences.en: Old Helm looked back from the wheel and nodded once.
sentences.cn: 老舵从舵轮转身看了一眼，点了点头。

sentences.en: It helped, somehow.
sentences.cn: 这样不知怎的就好多了。

sentences.en: The unknown island grew larger in the dark sky ahead.
sentences.cn: 前方暗沉的天空里，那座未知的岛屿越来越大。

assess:2.en: Bell spread the new map fragment on the deck and began to *assess* it carefully — tracing the edges, checking the faint symbols, measuring the distances with her thumb. 'This piece connects to the south corner,' she said at last. Silverfang marked it on the master chart. Old Helm smiled. For the first time, more than half the map was complete.
assess:2.cnHint: 小铃仔细____新得到的地图碎片，确认它与南角相连，银牙将其标注在总图上，地图已过半完成。
assess:2.hook: The southern region of the map showed something none of them had expected: a second sky above the first.
assess:2.line: 'Before we move, we *assess* what we have,' Bell said, smoothing the map with both hands.

sentences.en: Bell spread the new map fragment on the deck and began to *assess* it carefully — tracing the edges, checking the faint symbols, measuring the distances with her thumb.
'This piece connects to the south corner,' she said at last.
sentences.cn: 她终于开口说，"这块拼图接在南角。"

sentences.en: Silverfang marked it on the master chart.
sentences.cn: 银牙在主图上标记了位置。

sentences.en: Old Helm smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑了。

sentences.en: For the first time, more than half the map was complete.
sentences.cn: 这是第一次，地图完成的部分超过了一半。

employment:2.en: Deep in the cargo hold, I found a sealed letter addressed to Old Helm. It offered *employment* to any skilled navigator willing to cross the Unmapped Edge — someone who could read star-charts no one else understood. Old Helm folded it slowly, eyes distant, as if the letter already knew his answer.
employment:2.cnHint: 船舱深处，老舵手收到一封信，信中提出了一个____的邀请。
employment:2.hook: He tucked the letter away without a single word to us.
employment:2.line: '*Employment* at the Edge? That is either great honour or great danger,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Deep in the cargo hold, I found a sealed letter addressed to Old Helm.
sentences.cn: 我在货舱深处找到了一封密封的信，收件人是老舵。

sentences.en: It offered *employment* to any skilled navigator willing to cross the Unmapped Edge — someone who could read star-charts no one else understood.
Old Helm folded it slowly, eyes distant, as if the letter already knew his answer.
sentences.cn: 老舵慢慢地折好信纸，眼神飘向远方，仿佛信已经知道了他的答案。

entire:2.en: Bell spread the new map across the deck, and we all leaned in. The *entire* island chain curved like a sleeping creature from tail to nose, every floating rock connected by thin dotted lines. No one had seen the full shape before. For a moment, none of us breathed.
entire:2.cnHint: 领航员展开地图，____的岛链第一次完整地呈现在大家眼前。
entire:2.hook: At the very centre of the map was a blank circle no one could explain.
entire:2.line: 'The *entire* chain in one view — I never thought I would see this,' said Bell.

sentences.en: Bell spread the new map across the deck, and we all leaned in.
sentences.cn: 小铃把新地图铺在甲板上，我们都凑了过去。

sentences.en: The *entire* island chain curved like a sleeping creature from tail to nose, every floating rock connected by thin dotted lines.
No one had seen the full shape before.
sentences.cn: 没人见过这样完整的全貌。

sentences.en: For a moment, none of us breathed.
sentences.cn: 那一刻，我们都屏住了呼吸。

gift:2.en: Waiting on the landing stone of Mirrow Isle was a small wooden box with no sender's name. Inside lay a compass that pointed not north, but toward the next unvisited island. Old Helm called it a *gift* from the islands themselves, as if the world wanted us to keep moving.
gift:2.cnHint: 在小岛的落脚石上，大家发现了一个无名木盒，老舵手说这是岛屿送来的____。
gift:2.hook: The compass needle began to spin the moment clouds rolled in.
gift:2.line: 'A *gift* with no giver is either kindness or a warning,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: Waiting on the landing stone of Mirrow Isle was a small wooden box with no sender's name.
sentences.cn: 在米罗岛的登陆石上等着我们的是一个没有寄件人名字的小木盒。

sentences.en: Inside lay a compass that pointed not north, but toward the next unvisited island.
sentences.cn: 盒子里装着一个指南针，但它指的不是北方，而是指向下一个未曾到访的岛屿。

sentences.en: Old Helm called it a *gift* from the islands themselves, as if the world wanted us to keep moving.

kitchen:2.en: The old waystation had been empty for years, yet when we pushed open the door the *kitchen* fire was still warm. A pot sat on the stone stove, soup inside still faintly steaming. Bell touched the wall and found a small folded note tucked between the bricks: 'Help yourself. Keep moving.'
kitchen:2.cnHint: 废弃中转站里，____的炉火还是热的，锅里的汤也冒着热气。
kitchen:2.hook: Whoever left that note could not have gone far at all.
kitchen:2.line: 'The *kitchen* was used this morning — someone was here,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The old waystation had been empty for years, yet when we pushed open the door the *kitchen* fire was still warm.
A pot sat on the stone stove, soup inside still faintly steaming.
sentences.cn: 一口锅放在石炉上，里面的汤还在微微冒气。

sentences.en: Bell touched the wall and found a small folded note tucked between the bricks: 'Help yourself.
sentences.cn: 小铃摸了摸墙，在砖缝里发现了一张折叠的纸条："随便吃。

sentences.en: Keep moving.'
sentences.cn: 继续前进。"

mystery:2.en: At the edge of Driftstone Shelf lay a door standing alone with no walls around it. Old Helm called it a *mystery* the troupe had heard of but never found. We walked around it, looked through its keyhole, and saw a view completely different from the one behind us. The stars there were wrong.
mystery:2.cnHint: 漂石台地边缘有一扇独立的门，这个____困扰着旅队很久了。
mystery:2.hook: Silverfang reached for the handle before anyone could say stop.
mystery:2.line: 'Every *mystery* has a door — we have just found ours,' said Old Helm.

sentences.en: At the edge of Driftstone Shelf lay a door standing alone with no walls around it.
sentences.cn: 在漂流石架的边缘，矗立着一扇孤独的门，周围没有任何墙壁。

sentences.en: Old Helm called it a *mystery* the troupe had heard of but never found.
We walked around it, looked through its keyhole, and saw a view completely different from the one behind us.
sentences.cn: 我们在它周围走动，往钥匙孔里看，看到的景象和我们身后的完全不同。

sentences.en: The stars there were wrong.
sentences.cn: 那里的星星都错了。

opposite:2.en: Silverfang's ship docked on the *opposite* side of the island from ours, and the two crews met at the ridge between. She laid out her half of the map; we laid out ours. Together the pieces formed one complete picture neither side had expected: a route that looped back to where everything had started.
opposite:2.cnHint: 竞争船长停在岛的____一侧，两支队伍在山脊相遇，地图碎片合二为一。
opposite:2.hook: The route on the joined map led straight back to our very first island.
opposite:2.line: '*Opposite* sides, same destination — funny how that works,' said Silverfang.

sentences.en: Silverfang's ship docked on the *opposite* side of the island from ours, and the two crews met at the ridge between.
She laid out her half of the map; we laid out ours.
sentences.cn: 她铺开了她那一半的地图；我们铺开了我们的。

sentences.en: Together the pieces formed one complete picture neither side had expected: a route that looped back to where everything had started.
sentences.cn: 拼在一起，这些碎片组成了一幅完整的图景，是两支队伍都没想到过的：一条循环的路线，通向一切的起点。

permanent:2.en: Bell discovered faint carvings along the arch of the old gate — names of crews who had passed through over centuries. She traced them with her finger and said the stone kept a *permanent* record of every journey. Old Helm added our troupe's name with a small chisel, steady and careful, letter by letter.
permanent:2.cnHint: 领航员在古门拱上发现了历代旅队的名字，石头保存着____的记录。
permanent:2.hook: The last name carved before ours had been partially scratched out.
permanent:2.line: 'A *permanent* mark means we were truly here,' said Bell softly.

sentences.en: Bell discovered faint carvings along the arch of the old gate — names of crews who had passed through over centuries.
sentences.cn: 小铃发现了古老门拱上的淡淡刻画——那是几个世纪以来经过这里的船队的名字。

sentences.en: She traced them with her finger and said the stone kept a *permanent* record of every journey.
Old Helm added our troupe's name with a small chisel, steady and careful, letter by letter.
sentences.cn: 老舵拿起小凿子，一个字一个字地仔细刻下我们船队的名字。

plenty:2.en: The harvest platform of Greencloud Isle was piled high with star-fruit, dried sky-moss, and fresh water in sealed jars. Old Helm surveyed it all and smiled for the first time in days. There was *plenty* for the entire troupe to eat well and still fill the cargo hold for the long crossing ahead.
plenty:2.cnHint: 绿云岛的收获台上物资堆积如山，老舵手说____的储备足够支撑漫长旅程。
plenty:2.hook: Then Bell noticed the supplies were sorted as if someone knew we were coming.
plenty:2.line: '*Plenty* of food means someone planned for our arrival,' said Bell.

sentences.en: The harvest platform of Greencloud Isle was piled high with star-fruit, dried sky-moss, and fresh water in sealed jars.
sentences.cn: 绿云岛的收获平台堆满了星果、晒干的天苔和密封罐装的淡水。

sentences.en: Old Helm surveyed it all and smiled for the first time in days.
sentences.cn: 老舵察看了一遍，这些天来第一次绽开了笑容。

sentences.en: There was *plenty* for the entire troupe to eat well and still fill the cargo hold for the long crossing ahead.

beautiful:2.en: At the edge of the map, where the last island floated alone, I found a glass bottle wedged between two stones. Inside was a folded note. Old Helm read it aloud, and his voice softened. 'The view from here is *beautiful*,' it said, 'and I hope whoever finds this feels it too.'
beautiful:2.cnHint: 在地图边缘的孤岛上，我们发现了一个玻璃瓶，里面藏着一张令人感动的字条。
beautiful:2.hook: But the handwriting matched someone we thought was gone.
beautiful:2.line: Old Helm said, 'Even at the world's edge, something *beautiful* finds you.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the map, where the last island floated alone, I found a glass bottle wedged between two stones.
sentences.cn: 在地图的尽头，那座孤独浮动的岛屿边缘，我在两块石头间发现了一个玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: Inside was a folded note.
sentences.cn: 瓶子里装着一张折叠的纸条。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it aloud, and his voice softened.
sentences.cn: 老舵大声读了出来，他的声音柔和了下去。

sentences.en: 'The view from here is *beautiful*,' it said, 'and I hope whoever finds this feels it too.'

combine:2.en: The old chest we pulled from the hollow tree held two halves of a torn map. Bell spread them on the ground and pressed the edges together carefully. 'If we *combine* these pieces,' she said, studying the lines, 'they show a passage no one in our troupe has ever sailed.'
combine:2.cnHint: 贝尔把两张残破的地图碎片拼在一起，发现了一条从未有人走过的航路。
combine:2.hook: The passage led straight into a cloud no star could light.
combine:2.line: Bell said, 'Let's *combine* these two halves and see what opens up.'

sentences.en: The old chest we pulled from the hollow tree held two halves of a torn map.
sentences.cn: 我们从空心树里拉出的旧木箱里装着一份被撕成两半的地图。

sentences.en: Bell spread them on the ground and pressed the edges together carefully.
sentences.cn: 小铃把它们铺在地上，小心翼翼地把边缘对齐。

sentences.en: 'If we *combine* these pieces,' she said, studying the lines, 'they show a passage no one in our troupe has ever sailed.'

complicated:2.en: The signal tower on the far island blinked in a pattern none of us recognised. Old Helm copied the flashes into his notebook and frowned. 'The code is *complicated*,' he admitted, turning the page sideways, 'but every pattern has a rhythm if you wait long enough to hear it.'
complicated:2.cnHint: 信号塔发出复杂的闪光密码，老舵手耐心地记录下来，试图找出其中的规律。
complicated:2.hook: On the third page, a single word stared back at us.
complicated:2.line: Old Helm muttered, 'This code is *complicated*, but not impossible.'

sentences.en: The signal tower on the far island blinked in a pattern none of us recognised.
sentences.cn: 远岛上的信号塔闪烁着我们都没见过的节奏。

sentences.en: Old Helm copied the flashes into his notebook and frowned.
sentences.cn: 老舵把闪光抄进笔记本里，皱起了眉头。

sentences.en: 'The code is *complicated*,' he admitted, turning the page sideways, 'but every pattern has a rhythm if you wait long enough to hear it.'

crash:2.en: We heard it before we saw it — a sharp, splitting *crash* from the lower deck. Bell rushed down and found the old navigation lantern shattered across the floor, its light still glowing faintly in the broken pieces. Resting among the glass was a tiny rolled map none of us had put there.
crash:2.cnHint: 一声巨响后，贝尔冲下甲板，发现碎裂的灯笼里藏着一张来历不明的小地图。
crash:2.hook: No one aboard had touched that lantern since dawn.
crash:2.line: Bell called up, 'There was a *crash*, and now there is a map.'

sentences.en: We heard it before we saw it — a sharp, splitting *crash* from the lower deck.
Bell rushed down and found the old navigation lantern shattered across the floor, its light still glowing faintly in the broken pieces.
sentences.cn: 小铃冲下甲板，发现老旧的导航灯碎了一地，破碎的玻璃里还透着微弱的光。

sentences.en: Resting among the glass was a tiny rolled map none of us had put there.
sentences.cn: 玻璃堆里躺着一张卷起来的小地图，我们谁都没放过那儿。

creature:2.en: Something moved at the edge of the star-pool — small, softly glowing, leaving no footprints on the silver ground. I stepped closer and the *creature* turned its wide eyes toward me, blinked once, and pressed a dry leaf into my hand before vanishing into the dark water below.
creature:2.cnHint: 一个发光的小生物在星光水池边向我递来一片干叶，随后消失在水中。
creature:2.hook: The leaf had a map burned into its surface.
creature:2.line: I whispered, 'That *creature* just gave us exactly what we needed.'

sentences.en: Something moved at the edge of the star-pool — small, softly glowing, leaving no footprints on the silver ground.
sentences.cn: 星池边缘有什么东西动了——小小的，柔和地发着光，在银色的地面上没留下脚印。

sentences.en: I stepped closer and the *creature* turned its wide eyes toward me, blinked once, and pressed a dry leaf into my hand before vanishing into the dark water below.

crime:2.en: The locked box bore a seal shaped like broken wings. Old Helm recognised it at once. 'Taking a word-fragment without the keeper's blessing,' he said quietly, 'is considered a *crime* on these islands — the kind that closes every gate ahead of you.' He put the box down without opening it.
crime:2.cnHint: 老舵手认出了封印，警告说未经许可拿走词语碎片在这些岛屿上是一种严重的过失。
crime:2.hook: Yet the box was already open when Bell found it.
crime:2.line: Old Helm warned us, 'Stealing a word-fragment is a *crime* here.'

sentences.en: The locked box bore a seal shaped like broken wings.
sentences.cn: 这只上了锁的盒子上有个断翅的印章。

sentences.en: Old Helm recognised it at once.
sentences.cn: 老舵一眼就认出来了。

sentences.en: 'Taking a word-fragment without the keeper's blessing,' he said quietly, 'is considered a *crime* on these islands — the kind that closes every gate ahead of you.'
He put the box down without opening it.
sentences.cn: 他放下盒子，没有打开。

deeply:2.en: Silverfang stood at the bow long after the others had gone inside, staring at the horizon where the last island had sunk below the cloud line. When I asked what he was thinking, he was quiet for a moment. 'I am *deeply* sorry we left that lighthouse keeper with no answer,' he said.
deeply:2.cnHint: 银牙船长独自伫立船头，对离开时未能给灯塔守护者一个答复感到深深的遗憾。
deeply:2.hook: He turned the wheel back before anyone else woke up.
deeply:2.line: Silverfang said quietly, 'I am *deeply* sorry we did not stay.'

sentences.en: Silverfang stood at the bow long after the others had gone inside, staring at the horizon where the last island had sunk below the cloud line.
sentences.cn: 银牙在船头站了很久，其他人都进屋了，他还在盯着最后一座岛沉入云线下的地平线。

sentences.en: When I asked what he was thinking, he was quiet for a moment.
sentences.cn: 我问他在想什么，他沉默了一会儿。

sentences.en: 'I am *deeply* sorry we left that lighthouse keeper with no answer,' he said.

demonstrate:2.en: Bell set the compass on the map stone and asked the youngest island-guide to watch carefully. 'I will *demonstrate* how a word-fragment sings when it finds its home,' she said. She pressed the fragment to the stone, and a soft chime rang out, drawing a glowing line to the very next island.
demonstrate:2.cnHint: 贝尔向年轻的向导演示词语碎片找到归宿时会发出声音，并点亮通往下一座岛屿的路线。
demonstrate:2.hook: The glowing line pointed somewhere none of our maps had named.
demonstrate:2.line: Bell said, 'Watch closely — let me *demonstrate* how this fragment works.'

sentences.en: Bell set the compass on the map stone and asked the youngest island-guide to watch carefully.
sentences.cn: 小铃把罗盘放在地图石上，让最年轻的岛屿向导仔细看着。

sentences.en: 'I will *demonstrate* how a word-fragment sings when it finds its home,' she said.
She pressed the fragment to the stone, and a soft chime rang out, drawing a glowing line to the very next island.
sentences.cn: 她把碎片按在石头上，一声轻轻的铃音响起，在发光的线条引导下指向了下一座岛。

strike:2.en: Deep in the map-room cave, Bell spread the newest fragment across a flat stone. 'A *strike* of luck,' she said softly — the fragment showed a path no one had walked in a hundred years. Old Helm traced the line with one finger, eyes bright with the kind of wonder only a new horizon can bring.
strike:2.cnHint: 小铃在地图室洞穴里展开碎片，发现了一条百年无人走过的路，老舵主激动地用手指描摹路线。
strike:2.hook: But the path on the fragment ended at a door with no handle.
strike:2.line: 'A *strike* of luck — this path has been waiting for us all along.'

sentences.en: Deep in the map-room cave, Bell spread the newest fragment across a flat stone.
sentences.cn: 在地图室的山洞深处，小铃把最新的碎片铺在平石上。

sentences.en: 'A *strike* of luck,' she said softly — the fragment showed a path no one had walked in a hundred years.
Old Helm traced the line with one finger, eyes bright with the kind of wonder only a new horizon can bring.
sentences.cn: 老舵用一根手指描着这条线，眼睛里闪闪发光，那是只有新地平线才能带来的惊喜。

television:2.en: At the edge of Driftwood Isle, we found an old *television* set half-buried in soft moss, its screen dark but unbroken. Old Helm knelt beside it and pressed one ear to the glass. 'It still hums,' he whispered. Bell pulled out her compass. The hum matched the frequency she had been tracking for weeks.
television:2.cnHint: 在浮木岛边缘，我们发现一台旧____，老舵主俯身一听，发现它的嗡嗡声与小铃追踪已久的频率吻合。
television:2.hook: Whatever signal the old screen carried, it was growing stronger by the minute.
television:2.line: 'This *television* is not dead — it is trying to tell us something.'

sentences.en: At the edge of Driftwood Isle, we found an old *television* set half-buried in soft moss, its screen dark but unbroken.
Old Helm knelt beside it and pressed one ear to the glass.
sentences.cn: 老舵在它边上跪下，把一只耳朵贴在玻璃上。

sentences.en: 'It still hums,' he whispered.
sentences.cn: "它还在嗡鸣，"他低声说。

sentences.en: Bell pulled out her compass.
sentences.cn: 小铃拿出她的罗盘。

sentences.en: The hum matched the frequency she had been tracking for weeks.
sentences.cn: 嗡鸣声和她追踪了好几周的频率一致。

youth:2.en: Carved into the silver archway at the island's gate were four words: 'Given to the *youth*.' Old Helm read them twice, then smiled at me in a way that felt like a gift. 'Every new member brings a fresh eye,' he said. Bell nodded and handed me the key.
youth:2.cnHint: 银色拱门上刻着"献给____"四个字，老舵主微笑着把钥匙交给了我这个新成员。
youth:2.hook: The gate swung open onto a staircase that climbed straight into the clouds.
youth:2.line: 'Given to the *youth* — and you, my friend, are exactly that.'

sentences.en: Carved into the silver archway at the island's gate were four words: 'Given to the *youth*.'
Old Helm read them twice, then smiled at me in a way that felt like a gift.
sentences.cn: 老舵读了两遍，然后用一种感觉像是礼物的方式对我微笑。

sentences.en: 'Every new member brings a fresh eye,' he said.
sentences.cn: "每个新成员都能带来新的视角，"他说。

sentences.en: Bell nodded and handed me the key.
sentences.cn: 小铃点点头，把钥匙递给了我。

alter:2.en: Bell discovered that pressing the blue stone on the map table would *alter* the shape of every island shown on it — mountains flattened, rivers shifted, whole coasts bent like soft paper. She pressed it three times before Old Helm gently caught her wrist. 'Each change is permanent,' he said quietly.
alter:2.cnHint: 小铃发现按下蓝色石块会____地图上所有岛屿的形状，老舵主轻轻拦住她，提醒每次改变都是永久的。
alter:2.hook: Two islands had already vanished from the table, and no one knew where they had gone.
alter:2.line: 'If you *alter* the map, you alter the world — choose carefully.'

sentences.en: Bell discovered that pressing the blue stone on the map table would *alter* the shape of every island shown on it — mountains flattened, rivers shifted, whole coasts bent like soft paper.
She pressed it three times before Old Helm gently caught her wrist.
sentences.cn: 她按了三次才被老舵轻轻地抓住了手腕。

sentences.en: 'Each change is permanent,' he said quietly.
sentences.cn: "每一次改变都是永久的，"他轻声说。

approximately:2.en: The message sealed inside the copper tube was short: the lost island lay *approximately* three days' sail north, past the twin lights. Old Helm pinned the note above the wheel and breathed out slowly. Bell was already adjusting our heading. I counted the stars ahead, trying to picture three days of open sky.
approximately:2.cnHint: 铜管里的信息说，失落之岛在北方____三天航程处，小铃已经开始调整航向。
approximately:2.hook: Three days felt short — unless the twin lights had moved since the note was written.
approximately:2.line: '*Approximately* three days — but the sky here has a way of stretching time.'

sentences.en: The message sealed inside the copper tube was short: the lost island lay *approximately* three days' sail north, past the twin lights.
Old Helm pinned the note above the wheel and breathed out slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵把纸条钉在舵轮上方，缓缓呼了口气。

sentences.en: Bell was already adjusting our heading.
sentences.cn: 小铃已经在调整我们的航向。

sentences.en: I counted the stars ahead, trying to picture three days of open sky.
sentences.cn: 我数着前方的星星，试图想象三天的开阔天空。

attractive:2.en: The new word-fragment glowed with a soft gold light, and its pull was *attractive* to every compass on deck — all three needles swung toward it the moment Bell set it down. Old Helm crossed his arms, impressed. 'It wants to be followed,' I said. He gave a quiet laugh. 'Then let's not keep it waiting.'
attractive:2.cnHint: 新词语碎片散发金色光芒，船上所有罗盘的指针都被它____地吸引过去。
attractive:2.hook: If every compass on the island pointed the same way, something very large was waiting there.
attractive:2.line: 'Its pull is *attractive* to every compass — that is a map fragment worth keeping.'

sentences.en: The new word-fragment glowed with a soft gold light, and its pull was *attractive* to every compass on deck — all three needles swung toward it the moment Bell set it down.
Old Helm crossed his arms, impressed.
sentences.cn: 老舵双臂交叉，印象深刻。

sentences.en: 'It wants to be followed,' I said.
sentences.cn: "它想被跟随，"我说。

sentences.en: He gave a quiet laugh.
sentences.cn: 他轻轻笑了一声。

sentences.en: 'Then let's not keep it waiting.'
sentences.cn: "那就别让它等着了。"

bag:2.en: Tucked at the very bottom of the supply *bag* was a folded note wrapped in blue thread. Old Helm lifted it out as though it might dissolve. The handwriting belonged to someone who had left the troupe long before I joined. Bell read it over his shoulder and said nothing for a long moment.
bag:2.cnHint: 在补给____的最底部，老舵主发现了一张用蓝线扎好的折叠纸条，那是一个早已离队之人的笔迹。
bag:2.hook: The note contained only coordinates — and a single word: 'hurry.'
bag:2.line: 'At the bottom of the *bag*, a note that changes everything we thought we knew.'

sentences.en: Tucked at the very bottom of the supply *bag* was a folded note wrapped in blue thread.
Old Helm lifted it out as though it might dissolve.
sentences.cn: 老舵小心翼翼地取出它，仿佛怕它会散开。

sentences.en: The handwriting belonged to someone who had left the troupe long before I joined.
sentences.cn: 笔迹属于我加入剧团之前就离开的某个人。

sentences.en: Bell read it over his shoulder and said nothing for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 小铃从他肩膀上读完，沉默了很久。

beat:2.en: We heard the island before we saw it — a slow, steady *beat* rising through the hull like a great heart below the clouds. Bell pressed her palm to the deck and counted. Old Helm trimmed the sails without a word. I leaned over the rail and watched the dark water until the first light of the new island appeared.
beat:2.cnHint: 还没看见那座岛，我们就先感受到了从船底传来的沉稳____，像云层下有一颗巨大的心脏在跳动。
beat:2.hook: The beat grew louder only when we slowed down, as though the island itself was calling us closer.
beat:2.line: 'Feel that *beat* through the hull — this island has been alive and waiting for us.'

sentences.en: We heard the island before we saw it — a slow, steady *beat* rising through the hull like a great heart below the clouds.
Bell pressed her palm to the deck and counted.
sentences.cn: 小铃把手掌贴在甲板上数着。

sentences.en: Old Helm trimmed the sails without a word.
